author: mbuzdalov
title: Bidirectional DShot telemetry probabilistically fails to start on some AM32 ESCs
body:
# Bug Report

With current master, ESC entries don't start coming in at arming in one of my copters, which prevents further spooling up via `TKOFF_RPM_MIN`. This happens with certain noticeable probability (ranging from 0.25 to 0.75), and apparently does not go away with repeated arming attempts, so power-cycling is needed.

This is bisected to commit fab4b5e65b89dffad12fa82243a9a8c622b84d65 with a change relevant to DShot ESCs.

## Bug report

### Issue details

Please describe the problem

**Version**

Reproducible starting with commit fab4b5e65b89dffad12fa82243a9a8c622b84d65.
Does not happen with the previous commit b6b4b26c12cfd578b4ad2509e9606515cdb68660.

Potentially relevant configuration features: fast rates are enabled, `SERVO_DSHOT_ESC` set to 3 "BLHeli32/AM32/Kiss+EDT". Parameters are attached to the issue.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[x] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
Quad (seemingly irrelevant).

**Hardware type**

Flight controller: FlywooF745 version 3.
ESC firmware: AM32 2.20.

**Logs**

Logs are rather irrelevant. ESC entries simply don't start coming.

Parameter dump is attached below.
[2026-03-02-0retune-again.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25704240/2026-03-02-0retune-again.txt)

author: LupusTheCanine
body: I can confirm that this happens on heli too, thankfully all motors are affected simultaneously.

author: rmackay9
body:
It must be [this 2 second delay](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/ArduCopter/esc_calibration.cpp#L25) or something in the call to "read_radio" that is required for some reason to initialise DShot.  RC input affecting output is very strange though.

In terms of timing, we have perhaps 2 days before we branch for 4.7.  I'm aiming for this Friday...

author: mbuzdalov
body:
It is interesting that @LupusTheCanine reports the issue on a Heli. The commit I have bisected to apparently saves up just a single parameter read in the case of Heli. (Unless I misunderstand something, on Heli this routine never performs this radio wait, so this may probably not be responsible for the issue.)

> For any other issues, I can (at the level of my knowledge of Ardupilot, of course) only imagine issues with:
> - `rpmdata.last_update_us` from the `AP_ESC_Telem` subsystem having a special value of 0;
> - various possible wraparound issues involving this value (e.g. I find it sketchy how `rpmdata.update_rate_hz` updates and consequently how `get_rpm` works);
> - and maybe the fact that `telemdata.last_update_ms` is also often interpreted as 0 meaning no data, but it is not set accordingly (e.g. `telemdata.last_update_ms = AP_HAL::millis();`).
> 
> These issues above might be transient in the normal use, but probably not during startup, where something may become zero in too delicate moments (probably quite an issue with the last point), and which may possibly lock the system up in an unusable state. The fact that we arrive to this code earlier in the startup with https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/commit/fab4b5e65b89dffad12fa82243a9a8c622b84d65 may increase the probability of nasty things happening. The current state feels a bit too complicated for the present me to exclude the latter with confidence.

UPD: the above is apparently unrelated to this issue, as additional investigations by inserting some logging in `AP_ESC_Telem::update()` before any filtering happens shows that no telemetry is coming in from the backend (as in: all `last_update_*` are always zeros).

author: JeyPi
title: DO_SERVO or REPEAT_SERVO during a mission not always work
body:
**Bug Report**
inconsistent results from DO_SERVO or REPEAT_SERVO commands during a mission.

 **Issue details**
I am using SERVO output 6 for a payload release mechanism.
I need the servo to work in two ways:
Proportional manual control from the RC transmitter (using a potentiometer knob) during manual flight
Automatic control from an AUTO mission at a waypoint - payload drop 
I configured SERVO6_FUNCTION = 56
RC channel assigned to a knob (proportional control works without any problem)
However, during AUTO missions the servo behaves inconsistently:
Sometimes the set PWM is executed after the command, sometimes the PWM change is executed so quickly that the servo has no time to drop the payload and there are cases when I can see the message DO_SERVO in the log after a waypoint but no PWM change at all.

I tested both mission commands:
DO_SET_SERVO
DO_REPEAT_SERVO
Both produce unreliable behaviour.

Mission behaviour observations:
The reliability strongly depends on how the mission is structured.
Best behaviour = Waypoint → DO_SET_SERVO (or DO_REPEAT_SERVO) → next Waypoint
In this case the drop works more often correctly.
Worst behaviour = Waypoint → DO_SET_SERVO → CONDITION_DELAY (2 seconds) ....
The delay is NOT respected.
The servo either does not move or immediately returns to the RC-controlled position and the 2-second delay is effectively ignored.
This makes the payload drop unreliable.

As I understand how this should work:
The pilot should be able to control the payload door proportionally from the transmitter at any time ( It would be enough to control the servo by the RC only in no auto modes)
If the command is issued it should not be possible to control the given servo output by the RC until the command lasts.
The RC input should not immediately override the mission servo command until it is finished - meaning until the condition delay expires or the next waypoint is on (which might be happening)

Actual behaviour:
AUTO mission control and RC proportional control appear to fight over the PWM output on SERVO6.
The servo sometimes ignores mission commands even though the mission continues normally.
This causes failed payload drops.

Additional observations from flight logs:
Mission command is executed (as seen in the log) but
No consistent PWM output change is visible on SERVO6
In some cases PWM briefly changes but immediately returns to RC value
This looks like RC override is blocking or overriding the mission servo command

**Version**
ARDUPLANE   4.6.2
Mission planner 1.3.83

**Platform**
Plane

**Airframe type**
Fixed wing Cessna T,R,A,E 

**Hardware type**
Pixracer,

**Logs**
[_download examples here_](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1eSy-2Zlu8tijKNW_3WjVxCtak64DkOsI?usp=sharing)


![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a051c17b-8e30-440d-bac5-5fe56fc87c7a)

The issue is due to a small change in the RC6 input. It thinks you have changed the RC input so it reverts to RC control. To fix this increase the dead-zone. `RC6_DZ` from the log 10 should be enough. That means the RC input will have to change by 10 PWM before the servo reverts to RC control.

author: hossammorayan
title: Feature Request DShot Support for ESP32 and ESP32-S3 Boards
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I am currently developing a Rover for a university graduation project using the ESP32-S3. While I understand that ESP32 is not the "gold standard" for ArduPilot compared to STM32 due to hardware timing differences, it is a highly accessible and cost-effective option for students and DIY developers in regions where specialized flight controllers are hard to source. Currently, being limited to standard PWM on the ESP32 platform makes precise brushless motor control difficult and requires manual ESC calibration which is less than ideal for modern builds.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to see basic DShot support (DShot150/300) implemented for the ESP32-S3 architecture. I believe using the ESP32 RMT peripheral could provide the necessary timing precision for DShot without placing an undue burden on the main CPU. Even if it isn't as robust as the STM32 implementation, having this "good enough" digital option would greatly expand the utility of ESP32-based ArduPilot builds for educational and prototype use.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I have considered moving to an STM32-based board, but for this specific university project and budget, the ESP32-S3's built-in Wi-Fi/Bluetooth and availability make it the primary choice.

Platform
[ ] All
[ ] AntennaTracker
[ ] Copter
[ ] Plane
[X] Rover
[ ] Submarine

**Additional context**
I recently worked through some ESP32-S3 issues in (https://github.com/ArduPilot/MissionPlanner/issues/3636), and the community was very helpful. I'd love to see this platform continue to grow. Adding DShot would make the ESP32-S3 a much more viable "entry-level" ArduPilot controller for the next generation of students.

this library (https://github.com/DrGlaucous/DShotRMT_NEO) i think can help to implement , this help me to control my brushless motor with esc by esp32s3 work in dshot (outside ardupilot by code written )

author: lthall
body:
Ok, this is a little confusing and perhaps I need to comment it better.

The voltage scaling needs to be done before the mixing is done so that the actuator limits remain -1 to 1. This is the part that does the voltage scaling:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/9c863c1a5519b143fb19d4a57fb8622bd58f9a14/libraries/AP_Motors/AP_Motors_Thrust_Linearization.cpp#L189

This is the part that does the linearisation:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/9c863c1a5519b143fb19d4a57fb8622bd58f9a14/libraries/AP_Motors/AP_Motors_Thrust_Linearization.cpp#L104

Linearisation is done over the full thrust range and therefore expo is defined for maximum battery voltage. We then need to adjust the curve for the thrust range that is available given a lower battery voltage. However we need to account for the fact that we have already done the gain scaling.

The motor mixers were really tricky to get right and it took me a few attempts before I had all the features working correctly.

Now I could probably write it to be more intuitive and easy to use.

@bnsgeyer this is consistent with the case @LupusTheCanine presented. I think he is correct saying that heli ddfp is missing the compensation gain.

author: bnsgeyer
body:
> The voltage scaling needs to be done before the mixing is done so that the actuator limits remain -1 to 1. 

@lthall it appears that we missed this crucial step when we originally set this up for heli DDFP.  we do not multiply the yaw command by the compensation gain before using the thrust_to_actuator conversion to send to the motor output.

author: bjubes
title: ArduPlane: add support for "Heading Required" parameter to LOITER_TO_ALT from common mavlink
body:
## Feature request
MAV_CMD_NAV_LOITER_TO_ALT does not currently accept the common mavlink parameter 1 - heading required. I am proposing adding support for this parameter. If set to 1, LOITER_TO_ALT would keep its current behavior of continuing to loiter until its heading is towards its next waypoint. Otherwise the waypoint would be considered "reached" once the plane is at the specified altitude and immediately continue to its next waypoint.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
- MAV_CMD_NAV_LOITER_TO_ALT accepts param1
- when param1 is 1, no change to exiting implementation
- when param1 is 0, LOITER_TO_ALT is reached when alt specified is reached, and does not continue loitering. Instead proceeds directly to next waypoint/mission item

I'm interested in implementing this solution. I have a good idea of the logical changes but would need confirmation on how best to transfer and store the parameter within `AP_Mission::Mission_Command.content`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This has the unfortunate side effect of being a breaking change, as the current behavior aligns with the value begin set to 1 in the common dialect. Inverting the flag flag where 0 is heading required, and 1 is heading not required would be backwards-compatible with ardupilot, but be inverted from common mavlink

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[x] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
Common Dialect Docs (param1 not supported): https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_LOITER_TO_ALT
Ardupilot Docs (param1 described): https://ardupilot.org/plane/docs/common-mavlink-mission-command-messages-mav_cmd.html#mav-cmd-nav-loiter-to-alt
Relevant change showing no support in docs:  https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot_wiki/pull/6535

author: Yups1337
title: Plane: Landing detection not reliable
body: # Bug Report During an accidential disarm in flight i discovered that the landing detection didn't work reliably. The plane was still moving quite fast and the "IS_FLYING" flag changed several times and the BARO_GND_PRESSURE was reset as the result. This led to the wrong assumption, that the baro was faulty. _Probably an ELRS Bug triggered the inflight disarm - this bug report is not about the disarm cause!_ ### Issue details IS_FLYING set to 0 despite plane clearly moving. It might be difficult to have all corner cases catched but this should be a solid one. **Version** Arduplane 4.6.3 **Platform** [ ] All [ ] AntennaTracker [ ] Copter [x] Plane [ ] Rover [ ] Submarine **Airframe type** Heewing T1 VTOL, 2 tilt motors, 1 hover motor **Hardware type** Speedybee F405 Wing **Logs** https://www.swisstransfer.com/d/b4733f2d-169a-4aaf-afa3-886e6af8392d online until 18.3.2026

author: LupusTheCanine
body:
I think this may be intentional. If the plane wrongly thinks it is flying and it is armed in any mode with automatic throttle control (FBWB and above) really bad things can happen, bodily harm included. It is even more dangerous with copters. 

Use of Arm/Disarm and Disarm switches is discouraged for flying vehicles as in-flight disarm is generally not recoverable.

author: IamPete1
body:
Ground pressure is updated when disarmed, it is not gated on `IS_FLYING`. 

What is the actual bug here? The vehicle was disarmed manually, it then continued flying with cut throttle. 

We have Aux-function "165: ARM/Motor Emergency Stop" if you hit it by mistake your still armed but in e-stop so still safe, but you can change your mind and un-estop with no arming checks.

author: Yups1337
body:
> Ground pressure is updated when disarmed, it is not gated on `IS_FLYING`.

Okay, shoudn't this be depending on "IS_FLYING" = 0?
 
> What is the actual bug here? The vehicle was disarmed manually, it then continued flying with cut throttle.

If you don't want to call this bug, maybe it can be tagged "improvement needed" as the "IS_FLYING" shouldn't guess around between 0 and 1. The plane is gliding in a more or less safe attitude with correct airspeed measurement so "IS_FLYING" should be zero until the plane contacts the ground.  A more conservative and reliable approach would be helpful if someone uses "IS_FLYING" for any further action. 

> We have Aux-function "165: ARM/Motor Emergency Stop" if you hit it by mistake your still armed but in e-stop so still safe, but you can change your mind and un-estop with no arming checks.

_All fine! I'am aware of the risk coming with "arming switch". The root cause wasn't my personal fault as the Radio hasn't been touched. Channel 1-5 go down simultaeously and trigger disarm. Its either ELRS V4 related or a radio (hardware?) fault. Still under investigation but not related to my point. 
I didn't even try to rearm because i was trying to establish a connection with MissionPlanner and lost the plane out of sight. Took a while to realise what happened. But it's a sub 1kg testing plane - nothing dangerous._

author: ttenterprises
title: Pixhawk 6C: SERIAL2_PROTOCOL affects SERIAL1 DMA, breaks Lua UART access and MAVLink on TELEM1 (regression after 4.3)
body:
Summary of the Issue
On Pixhawk 6C, firmware versions after 4.3 show a UART routing / DMA conflict between SERIAL1 and SERIAL2 that breaks both Lua scripting UART access and MAVLink on TELEM1.

Symptoms:
If SERIAL2_PROTOCOL = MAVLink (1 or 2):

MAVLink on TELEM1 works

Lua cannot read GNSS on TELEM2 (SERIAL1)

SERIAL1 RX appears dead or starved of DMA

GNSS replies become zeros or disappear entirely

If SERIAL2_PROTOCOL = 28 (Scripting):

Lua can read GNSS on TELEM2

MAVLink on TELEM1 becomes unstable or stops

SERIAL0 appears to lose DMA priority

TELEM1 MAVLink link drops or becomes corrupted

Lua can only open SERIAL1

serial:find_serial(1) works

serial:find_serial(0) is locked by MAVLink

serial:find_serial(2) returns nil

GPS port (SERIAL3) is not exposed to Lua at all

This behaviour does NOT occur on ArduPilot 4.3.x

TELEM1 MAVLink works

TELEM2 Lua GNSS works

SERIAL2 can be unused

No DMA conflicts

No port fighting

No need to set SERIAL2_PROTOCOL = 28

Expected Behaviour
SERIAL1 (TELEM2) should remain usable by Lua regardless of SERIAL2_PROTOCOL

SERIAL0 (TELEM1) MAVLink should not be affected by enabling scripting

SERIAL2_PROTOCOL should not steal DMA or disable SERIAL1

GPS port (SERIAL3) should be exposed to Lua if scripting is enabled

Behaviour should match ArduPilot 4.3.x

Actual Behaviour (4.4 → 4.6)
SERIAL2_PROTOCOL = MAVLink → SERIAL1 becomes unusable

SERIAL2_PROTOCOL = 28 → SERIAL0 becomes unstable

Lua can only access SERIAL1

SERIAL2 and SERIAL3 are not exposed to Lua

GNSS polling fails unless SERIAL2_PROTOCOL = 28

MAVLink fails unless SERIAL2_PROTOCOL = MAVLink

Impossible to run MAVLink on TELEM1 and Lua GNSS on TELEM2 simultaneously

Steps to Reproduce
Install ArduPilot 4.4.x or later on Pixhawk 6C

Connect GNSS module to TELEM2 (SERIAL1)

Enable Lua scripting

Set TELEM1 (SERIAL0) to MAVLink

Toggle SERIAL2_PROTOCOL between 2 and 28 

Observe:

GNSS stops working when SERIAL2 = MAVLink

MAVLink stops working when SERIAL2 = 28

Lua cannot open SERIAL2 or SERIAL3

SERIAL1 and SERIAL2 appear to share DMA or IRQ resources

Additional Notes
This appears to be a UART DMA routing regression introduced after 4.3

The Pixhawk 6C hardware uses a different UART/DMA layout than older Pixhawks

Lua UART exposure changed in 4.4 with the new scripting backend

This bug makes Lua‑based GNSS drivers impossible on 4.4+ for Pixhawk 6C

Request
Please investigate the UART/DMA routing and Lua UART exposure on Pixhawk 6C for ArduPilot 4.4+.

Specifically:

Why SERIAL2_PROTOCOL affects SERIAL1 DMA

Why SERIAL2 must be set to 28 to enable scripting

Why SERIAL0 MAVLink breaks when scripting is enabled

Why SERIAL3 (GPS port) is not exposed to Lua

Why 4.3.x does not have this issue

I can provide full UART logs, Lua scripts, and wiring diagrams if needed.

author: IamPete1
body:
I'm struggling to understand your description of the problem. What is exactly it your trying to get to work? There seems to be some confusion about which serial is which, serial 0 is the USB. See: https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-holybro-pixhawk6C.html#uart-mapping

The lua binding `serial:find_serial` only returns ports which have there protocol set to scripting. So for `serial:find_serial(1)` to work you must have two ports set to scripting, it will then return the second port. The argument is not the serial port number.

author: LuciferK47
body:
Hey @IamPete1,
Thanks for clearing up the `find_serial` issue; it does help to explain some of the confusion in the first report. I think there might still be something real here, though, if you ignore the mix-up with the serial numbers and the misunderstanding about `find_serial`. The 4.3 to 4.4 delta is what stands out to me. If TELEM2 running protocol 28 with TELEM1 MAVLink was stable in 4.3 but isn't in 4.4+, could something in the scripting backend have changed between those two versions? It could be a Pixhawk 6C HAL-specific issue with scheduler priority or DMA allocation. Not saying it is for sure, but it seems the worth looking into it.

author: LuciferK47
body:
Hey @ttenterprises,
I had a look at this and the likely potential files in the codebase ,the hwdef DMA stream assignments for the 6C and the scripting backend initialisation changes in 4.4 are the obvious places to dig. The fix itself would probably be straightforward once confirmed.
The problem is that DMA conflicts are really hard to validate without actually running it on hardware. Reading and accessing the code will only take me so far. Since I don't have a Pixhawk 6C in hand to flash and test against, I don't want to push a fix that I can't verify end-to-end.
If you're able to test builds, that would actually make this a lot more tractable ; I can point at the likely fix and you confirm whether it resolves it on real hardware.

author: ES-Alexander
title: Sub/Boat: add autotests for core features
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
ArduSub and ArduRover boat vehicles have some unique features compared to other vehicle types, and are often controlled in different ways, many of which aren't yet covered by [autotests](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/the-ardupilot-autotest-framework.html).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add autotests for the following features (where the firmware is ticked):

> Key: 
> - ✅ → autotest already available
> - ❗️ → autotest needed
> - 〰️ → maybe useful, but not essential
> - ❌ → not needed / not (currently) relevant

| Feature | Sub? | Boat? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MAVLink [`MANUAL_CONTROL`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MANUAL_CONTROL) axes | ❗️ | ❗️ | Used for GCS control by a joystick. Include roll/pitch axes |
| MAVLink [`MANUAL_CONTROL`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MANUAL_CONTROL) buttons | ❗️ | ❌ | Used for GCS control by a joystick |
| Joystick roll/pitch trim button functions | ❗️ | ❌ | joystick attitude control |
| Joystick pilot gain inc/dec button functions | ❗️ | ❌ | joystick speed control |
| [Pilot control failsafe](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/pilot-control-failsafe.html) | ❗️ | ❌ | |
| [Normal](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/parameters.html#mot-pwm-type-output-pwm-type) PWM motors | ❗️ | ❌ | `MOT_PWM_MIN`/`MAX`/`REVERSED` |
| Trimmable ([PWMAngle](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/parameters.html#mot-pwm-type-output-pwm-type)) motors | ❗️ | ❌ | `SERVOn_MIN`/`MAX`/`REVERSE` |
| Vectored 6DoF [frame](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/parameters.html#frame-config-frame-configuration) | ❗️ | ❌ | |
| [`MOTOR_DETECT`](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/modes.html) mode | ❗️ | ❌ | automatic motor reversal detection |
| [`AHRS_ORIENTATION`](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/parameters.html#ahrs-orientation-board-orientation) | ❗️ | ❗️ | accel / gyro orientation offset |
| [INS position offset](https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/parameters.html#ins-pos1-x-imu-accelerometer-x-position) | 〰️ | ❗️| |

| [compass motor compensation](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html#compassmot-compensation-for-interference-from-the-power-wires-escs-and-motors) | ❗️ | ❗️ | not (yet) frequently used |
| Leak failsafe | ❗️ | ❌ |  |
| [`VISO_ORIENT`](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/parameters.html#viso-orient-visual-odometery-camera-orientation) | ❗️ | 〰️ | DVL orientation |
| MAVLink [`GPS_INPUT`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#GPS_INPUT) | ❗️ | 〰️ | Used by some positioning systems |
| GPS heading | ✅ | ❗️ | | 
| GPS [antenna position offset](https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/parameters.html#gps1-pos-x-antenna-x-position-offset) | ❌ | ❗️ | |
| MAVLink [`AP_ADC`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/ardupilotmega.html#AP_ADC) | 〰️ | 〰️ | ADC feedback |
| EKF failsafe | 〰️ | ❗️ | |
| Lights1/2 output functions | ❗️ | ❌ | [`SERVOn_FUNCTION`](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/parameters.html#servo1-function-servo-output-function), Lights1/2 [`NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT) messages, servo PWM range, duty-cycle PWM range, joystick inc/dec buttons, [`JS_LIGHTS_STEPS`](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/parameters.html#js-lights-steps-lights-brightness-steps) param |

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Manual testing is generally possible, and should sometimes still be used as well, but is often less comprehensive and less convenient than regular automated tests which ensure features continue to work (particularly at the PR level).

**Platform**
[  ] All

List derived from a WIP [spreadsheet of features and firmware release tests](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ocXJxLq5iqt1vfY44bLjV7AJApmLLYg0DasRq-RDLMw/edit?gid=548439307#gid=548439307) from Blue Robotics, intended for testing ROVs and skid-steer boats.

author: sundar249
title: QuadPlane 4.6.3: Q_LAND_FINAL_SPD Applied From High Altitude, Q_WP_SPEED_DN Ignored During Q_LAND/Q_RTL
body:
In ArduPlane firmware 4.6.3 (QuadPlane), the parameter Q_LAND_SPEED is no longer available. Previously, this parameter allowed control of the vertical descent speed during the main VTOL descent phase, before the vehicle reached the final landing altitude defined by Q_LAND_FINAL_ALT.

Current behavior observed:

Vehicle starts Q_LAND / Q_RTL from ~100 meters altitude

Parameters set:

Q_LAND_FINAL_SPD = 0.5 m/s

Q_LAND_FINAL_ALT = 7 m

Expected behavior (based on earlier firmware logic):

Descend from 100 m → 7 m at 1 m/s (Q_LAND_SPEED)

Below 7 m descend at 0.5 m/s (Q_LAND_FINAL_SPD)

However, in 4.6.3:

The vehicle descends at 0.5 m/s from the full 100 m altitude

Q_WP_SPEED_DN (which appears to replace Q_LAND_SPEED) does not affect descent rate during Q_LAND/Q_RTL

The aircraft appears to use only Q_LAND_FINAL_SPD for the entire landing profile

Operational impact

For heavy QuadPlanes:

Very long descent time (~200 seconds from 100 m)

Excessive battery drain

Voltage sag risk

Possibility of brownout or crash before touchdown

This creates a serious safety risk, especially for:

Logistics drones

Agricultural VTOLs

Heavy-lift QuadPlanes

The absence of a parameter to control pre-final descent speed removes an important safety and endurance control previously available.

Suspected issue

Landing logic may be entering final descent mode prematurely, or the firmware may not be properly using Q_WP_SPEED_DN during Q_LAND/Q_RTL vertical descent.

Version

ArduPlane 4.6.3

Platform

[ ] All
[ ] AntennaTracker
[ ] Copter
[✔] Plane
[ ] Rover
[ ] Submarine

Airframe type

QuadPlane VTOL (multirotor + fixed wing hybrid)

Hardware type

Pixhawk-class flight controller

Logs

Logs showing descent from ~100 m at constant 0.5 m/s despite Q_WP_SPEED_DN changes can be provided upon request.

Contributor

SUNDAR C

author: sundar249
title: QuadPlane Safety Issue: RTL Enters Fixed-Wing Mode Before Q_RTL When Inside RTL_RADIUS at Low Altitude
body:
When flying a QuadPlane (Hybrid VTOL) in AUTO mission mode, switching to RTL while already inside RTL_RADIUS causes the system to first enter fixed-wing RTL logic before transitioning to Q_RTL.

This creates a delay in VTOL motor takeover. At low altitude (~15 m AGL) this delay may result in insufficient height for safe VTOL stabilization, potentially causing ground impact before Q_RTL authority is established.

Observed sequence:

AUTO → RTL (FW logic active) → position check → Q_RTL

The aircraft briefly behaves as a fixed-wing RTL vehicle even though it is already near home where immediate VTOL control would be safer.

Version
ArduPlane 4.6.3

Platform
[ ] All
[ ] AntennaTracker
[ ] Copter
[✔] Plane
[ ] Rover
[ ] Submarine

Airframe type
QuadPlane (Hybrid VTOL)

Hardware type
Pixhawk-class flight controller (Cube compatible)

Logs
Logs available and can be provided. Key indicators in logs:

MODE change: AUTO → RTL

Delay before second MODE change: RTL → QRTL

STATUSTEXT: "RTL" before VTOL entry

EV message showing Q-mode entry occurs after RTL logic

RCOU: VTOL motors idle until Q_RTL engages

Mode Transition Timeline

T0 – Aircraft in AUTO (FW)
T1 – Pilot switches to RTL
T2 – Mode = RTL (fixed-wing RTL active)
T3 – System detects aircraft inside RTL_RADIUS
T4 – Mode switches to Q_RTL
T5 – VTOL motors spool and stabilization begins

Risk Window: T1 → T4 (fixed-wing logic active at low altitude)

Parameter Interaction

RTL_RADIUS → Triggers the “already near home” logic

Q_RTL_MODE → Enables VTOL behavior during RTL

Q_RTL_ALT → Target VTOL altitude may not be reached before transition

Q_TRANSITION_MS → Adds transition delay

Q_ASSIST_SPEED → May delay VTOL dominance

Expected Behavior

If:

Vehicle = QuadPlane

RTL is triggered

Aircraft is already inside RTL_RADIUS

➡ System should immediately enter Q_RTL, skipping fixed-wing RTL logic.

Safety Impact

This affects emergency mission aborts near home at low altitude and represents a potential crash scenario due to delayed VTOL takeover.

Reporter: Sundar C

author: IamPete1

body: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1TJDGTese6_nX5Gr_z1MNgaQjiQJwMGPT/view?usp=sharing

author: IamPete1
body:
This is due to the one second delay here: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/18ced5a5f2c5033ae8e2734770c58c7cbf22d40c/ArduPlane/mode_rtl.cpp#L92

For the last one in the log if you had been under your `Q_RTL_ALT` of 15 meters then it would have gone directly to QRTL without the one second in RTL because of this check:

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/18ced5a5f2c5033ae8e2734770c58c7cbf22d40c/ArduPlane/mode_rtl.cpp#L27-L36

So if your low with VTOL motors active it will already do what you want. In your use case you would be better to either set QRTL on your aux switch rather than RTL or use `Q_RTL_MODE` "QRTL Always".

author: sundar249
body:
I kindly request consideration of one of the following improvements:

Remove the 1-second delay for QuadPlane RTL transitions.

Immediately evaluate QRTL when:

Vehicle is QuadPlane

RTL is triggered

Aircraft is already within RTL_RADIUS

Add a parameter to optionally disable the 1-second delay for VTOL platforms.

Bypass delay during failsafe-triggered RTL events.

Why This Matters

Low-altitude aborts near home are common during:

Battery failsafe events

Emergency mission termination

In these cases, immediate VTOL authority significantly improves safety margins.

This is not a tuning issue but a mode sequencing safety concern for hybrid platforms.

author: jinmussj
title: Copter: Clarify FLIP “rise for 1 second then flip” docs vs SITL behavior
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

Flip Mode docs state: **“Vehicle will rise for 1 second and then rapidly flip.”**
(https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/flip-mode.html#flip-mode)

In Copter SITL, the flip appears to start much earlier than 1 second after entering FLIP mode. Based on DataFlash timestamps, roll exceeds 30° about **0.35s** after MODE: Flip.

I’d like maintainer confirmation: **is the doc wording outdated/simplified, or is the implementation missing an intended ~1s pre-ascend delay?**

**Steps to reproduce (SITL / MAVProxy)**

1. Start Copter SITL (Quad).
2. mode guided → arm throttle → takeoff 20
3. rc 3 1500 → mode alt_hold (stabilize)
4. mode flip
5. Review DataFlash .BIN in Mission Planner (Log Browser): MODE and ATT (Roll).

**Expected behavior (per docs)**
Vehicle rises for ~1 second after FLIP entry, then flips.

**Actual behavior (from log)**
Flip starts ~0.35s after FLIP entry (Roll > 30°).

title: Copter: LAND docs say “throttle has no effect”, but high throttle can cancel LAND when PILOT_THR_BHV enables it
body: ## Bug report **Issue details** Landing mode documentation states: “The throttle stick has no effect.” However, in SITL I can reproducibly cancel LAND using high throttle input when PILOT_THR_BHV enables “high throttle cancels landing”. The DataFlash log records EV: LAND_CANCELLED_BY_PILOT and the flight mode transitions from LAND back to ALT_HOLD immediately after throttle is raised. This report is primarily to confirm intended behavior and update documentation if needed. This appears to be a doc vs implementation mismatch (missing conditions / incomplete doc). I’m requesting maintainer confirmation: is LAND cancellation by high throttle an intended behavior under certain conditions (and the doc needs clarification), or is this unintended and should be changed? **Steps to reproduce (SITL / MAVProxy)** 1. Start Copter SITL (Quad). 2. Take off in GUIDED to ~20m. 3. Set throttle mid-stick and switch to ALT_HOLD: - rc 3 1500 - mode alt_hold 4. Enable “high throttle cancels landing”: - param set PILOT_THR_BHV 2 5. Induce bad position / no-GPS aiding (to enter the no-position landing behavior): - param set SIM_GPS1_ENABLE 0 - (EKF failsafe / bad position messages appear; vehicle may enter LAND due to failsafe) 6. Ensure the vehicle is in LAND mode (either failsafe-triggered or manual mode land). 7. Raise throttle high: - rc 3 2000 8. Observe that LAND is cancelled and mode returns to ALT_HOLD. **Expected behavior (per docs)** Throttle stick has no effect in LAND (no cancellation / no mode escape). **Actual behavior (observed)** High throttle cancels LAND and switches to ALT_HOLD. DataFlash confirms EV: LAND_CANCELLED_BY_PILOT, and MODE changes to ALT_HOLD at the same timestamp. **Evidence (DataFlash .BIN / Mission Planner Log Browser)** **MODE:** - 2026-02-08 17:45:30.108 — MODE: Land - 2026-02-08 17:45:40.848 — MODE: AltHold **RCIN:** - 2026-02-08 17:45:40.840 — RCIN: C3 (throttle) = 2000 **EV:** - 2026-02-08 17:45:40.848 — EV: LAND_CANCELLED_BY_PILOT Interpretation: while in LAND, throttle was raised to 2000 and within ~8ms the log recorded LAND_CANCELLED_BY_PILOT, and mode returned to ALT_HOLD (same timestamp as the event). This contradicts, or at least requires clarification to, the doc statement that throttle has no effect in LAND. **Questions for maintainers** 1. Is “high throttle cancels LAND” intended behavior when PILOT_THR_BHV enables it (and should the LAND mode doc be updated to mention this condition)? 2. Is this behavior intended only under certain landing paths (e.g., bad position / no GPS aiding), or should it be consistent across landing paths? 3. author: tpwrules
body:
Please supply more of the test harness so we can understand how the fuzzed data is being fed into the firmware. It should be a simple matter to compile with debug symbols and get a backtrace from QEMU as well. It would also be helpful to decode the payload so it is obvious what the field values are.

In general, ArduPilot is not designed to be robust to arbitrary MAVLink messages due to the resources required to validate every combination of payloads. It is also impossible to determine the safety of many payloads, as they depend on the particular vehicle and mission etc.

There are payloads for MsgID 75 in particular which [deliberately cause](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/c207edeacc6cb266ef58a7d4f05c29e13078e7e5/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp#L3511) an adverse effect as a debugging tool, so the fact that some other payloads also cause a problem is not very interesting.

The 16 bit CRC provides some protection against random data interpreted as, or corruption causing mutations into, a message with an adverse effect. For high-strength protection against corrupt or malicious messages, MAVLink signing needs to be used.

If your fuzzer can find a message with an incorrect CRC (or other malformation in the framing) that causes a problem, then this would be a serious issue. So would a message that causes a problem on a vehicle with signing enabled from a source that does not know the correct key (noting that the key is ignored over USB). But it doesn't seem clear from this description that your fuzzer is capable of finding issues like this.

## Bug report

**Issue details**

I was fuzzing the mavlink handler inside of `GCS_MAVLINK::update_receive` and was crafting packets like so:

```
    while (true) {
        read_count = fuzz_buffer_read(last_anchor_id, g_fuzzing_input, sizeof(g_fuzzing_input));
        if (read_count > 15 && read_count < 262) {
            break;
        }
        fuzz_finish(last_anchor_id);
    }
    // one byte length
    uint8_t length = g_fuzzing_input[0];
    // 24-bits to msgid
    uint32_t msgid =
        ((uint32_t)g_fuzzing_input[1] & 0xFF) << 16 |
        ((uint32_t)g_fuzzing_input[2] & 0xFF) << 8  |
        ((uint32_t)g_fuzzing_input[3] & 0xFF);
    // get crc extra from mavlink message entry
    const mavlink_msg_entry_t *mavlink_msg_entry = mavlink_get_msg_entry(msgid);
    if (mavlink_msg_entry == NULL) {
        // fprintf(stderr, "Unknown MAVLink message ID: %u\n", msgid);
        fuzz_finish(last_anchor_id);

    uint8_t crc_extra = mavlink_msg_entry->crc_extra;

    uint8_t sys_id = g_fuzzing_input[4];
    uint8_t comp_id = g_fuzzing_input[5];

    // payload is rest of data
    const uint8_t *payload = (const uint8_t *)&g_fuzzing_input[6];

author: tatsuy
title: AP_NavEKF2/3: EK2/EK3_GPS_CHECK mismatch between “255” docs and AP_Int8 (0–127)
body:
The EK2_GPS_CHECK and EK3_GPS_CHECK parameters are documented as 8-bit bitmasks (bits 0–7):

> "Set to 0 to bypass all checks. Set to 255 perform all checks. Set to 3 to check just the number of satellites and HDoP. Set to 31 for the most rigorous checks that will still allow checks to pass when the copter is moving, eg launch from a boat."

However, in the implementation both `EK2_GPS_CHECK` and `EK3_GPS_CHECK` are stored as `AP_Int8`:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_NavEKF3/AP_NavEKF3.h#L428

Because `AP_Int8` is a signed 8-bit type, the parameter value is clamped to the range `-128..127`. If a user sets EK2_GPS_CHECK or EK3_GPS_CHECK to **255** via a GCS, it is stored internally as **127 (0x7F)**.

Practically, the only way to get all 8 bits set is to use **-1**, which maps to `0xFF` at the bit level, but this is not documented anywhere in the parameter description.

This is confusing for users trying to follow the documentation and can result in the horizontal-speed preflight GPS check (bit 7) remaining disabled even when they think they have requested “all checks”.

Suggestions:

* the documentation should be updated to say “set to -1 to enable all checks”, or  
* `_gpsCheck` should be changed to AP_Int16.

author: ES-Alexander
title: Rover/Boat: add support for water barometers
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
1. It's difficult to tell how loaded a boat is, especially from telemetry
    - Multiple barometers at opposite ends of a boat (and/or in opposite hulls of a catamaran) could even potentially provide high-resolution pitch or roll estimates, to estimate load distribution (which impacts travel efficiency and controller tuning)
2. Boats have no feedback if they have water ingress or get overloaded
    - If a boat with a winch tries to pick up something heavy (or something lands on it) it could sink without warning
3. It's safety-critical for an underwater crawler to tell how deep it is, to prevent hull/component implosion
    - This isn't a boat, but is still Rover

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1. `BARO_TYPE_WATER` sensors should be supported in Rover (at minimum in the boat firmware)
    - I believe this would at least require [specific gravity parameter support](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/d4e9bf05b9995657b72eedd7d6a7e41c82284cdb/libraries/AP_Baro/AP_Baro.cpp#L143), for the water density
    - I'm unsure what else is required - the rest of the driver code might already be compiled in?
2. A pressure/altitude failsafe should be implemented
    - Should ideally share implementation with [the proposed Sub one](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/32090)
3. Ideally [barometer positions could be specified](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/30727), and used as an alternative roll/pitch source (or at least in a warning/failsafe/pre-arm-check capacity if the average difference gets/is too high)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
[A leak failsafe](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/19103) could at least warn about active water ingress, but that's somewhat independent functionality.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[X] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
ArduSub already supports water barometers, so could be used for inspiration.

author: Rama542
body:
This PR adds support for BARO_TYPE_WATER sensors to the Rover (Boat) firmware, enabling direct water pressure–based feedback for surface vessels and underwater-capable rovers.
The implementation reuses existing water barometer logic where possible and focuses on safe, incremental enablement rather than introducing new vehicle behavior by default.
Motivation:
Rover currently lacks direct sensing for water pressure or submersion depth. Supporting water barometers enables:
-Detection of unexpected submersion or water ingress
-Load/overloading awareness via pressure changes
-Safer operation for amphibious or underwater rover platforms
-Improved telemetry for monitoring hull safety and operating limits
Similar functionality already exists in ArduSub, making Rover a natural extension point.
Implementation Details:
-Enabled recognition and initialization of BARO_TYPE_WATER sensors in Rover
-Reused shared barometer infrastructure and ArduSub logic where applicable to avoid duplication
-Added water density / specific gravity handling consistent with existing water baro usage
-Introduced pressure-to-depth handling suitable for Rover safety monitoring
-Changes are gated so existing Rover configurations are unaffected unless a water barometer is configured
Safety & Failsafe Considerations:
-Pressure-based depth values are exposed for use in safety logic
-This PR does not enforce new failsafes by default, but provides the plumbing required for:
     -Depth limit warnings
     -Water ingress detection
      -Platform-specific safety policies
-Feedback welcome on preferred default behaviors for Rover vs Sub
Testing:
-Added autotest coverage to verify correct detection and reporting of BARO_TYPE_WATER sensors in Rover
-Manual SITL testing performed to validate pressure-to-depth behavior
-No regressions observed in existing Rover barometer handling
Scope & Limitations:
-This PR focuses on sensor support and data availability, not mission-level behaviors
-Multi-barometer orientation handling (for roll/pitch estimation) is intentionally left out of this change
-Follow-up PRs can extend this for imbalance detection if desired
Reviewer Notes / Questions:

author: ES-Alexander
title: Sub: add an external pressure failsafe
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
If a vehicle goes too deep (e.g. beyond its component depth ratings), it can implode / get destroyed under the pressure. We don't currently have a means of directly warning about this before it starts happening.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Make a dedicated external pressure failsafe, which monitors a baro specified as `BARO_TYPE_WATER`. That keeps setup, defaults, and user intuition simple, at the cost of some ambiguity around what to do if there is more than one water baro available (I vote just check the primary baro, and use it for the failsafe if it is a water baro).

Ideally it would be a multi-level failsafe, with low and critical depths specified (like with battery voltage). I believe the most logical supported actions are "Warn only", and "Surface", but "Depth hold" could potentially be an option in between 🤷‍♂️ .

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could alternatively expand the current _internal_ pressure failsafe to more generally provide failsafes for each available barometer (similar to the battery failsafes, which exist per battery). That's more complex to set up because you need to know how many internal baros there are, but it does provide more control if that happens to be desired.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[X] Submarine

**Additional context**
The existing leak failsafe and internal pressure failsafe can potentially provide some warning of an imminent implosion as the enclosure starts to flex and/or leak, but that's much less comforting than being preemptively warned when close to component ratings.

author: bhuvan-somisetty
body:
This PR introduces battery voltage compensation for helicopter throttle curves and the heli governor in Copter, addressing long-standing head-speed instability caused by battery voltage sag.

Motivation
Current heli throttle curves and governor logic assume a relatively constant supply voltage. In real-world heli setups, however, battery voltage varies significantly during flight, leading to:
- Underspeed conditions when throttle curves are tuned for a full battery
- Rotor overspeed and excessive vibration when curves are tuned for low-voltage states
- Increased mechanical stress and reduced flight safety.
This makes it difficult to maintain consistent head speed across the full discharge range without compromising safety.

What this PR does
- Adds battery voltage–aware scaling to heli throttle curve and governor output
- Maintains consistent rotor RPM across varying battery voltages
- Reduces the risk of underspeed, overspeed, and vibration-induced issues
- Designed to be safe by default, with conservative limits to prevent ESC over-commanding

Design notes
- Compensation is based on measured battery voltage relative to a configurable nominal voltage
- Integrates cleanly with existing heli governor logic
- Does not alter behavior for non-heli frames or when compensation is disabled
- Keeps computational overhead minimal

Why this matters
Helicopters are particularly sensitive to RPM variation. Providing native battery voltage compensation:
- Improves flight consistency
- Reduces tuning complexity
- Increases mechanical

author: amarburg
title: Sub: Sudden dive on transition from manual to alt hold
body:
## Bug report

See also [this thread at the BlueRobotics community forums](https://discuss.bluerobotics.com/t/sudden-dive-on-transition-from-manual-to-alt-hold/22286/3).

We are working to confirm this behavior with our other BlueROVs.

Testing on a BlueROV2 Heavy running BlueOS-1.4.2 with Ardupilot 4.5.7 (also tested with 4.5.5). 

Under a very specific set of circumstances:

1. Vehicle in the water, armed, running in alt hold
1. Disarm vehicle
1. Set to manual mode
1. Arm vehicle (now in manual mode)
1. Set to alt hold mode

The vehicle will descend suddenly by ~1m, then stabilize at a depth slightly below its original depth. The second and third steps are interchangeable (manual then disarm or disarm then manual).

# Expected behavior

On **all** transitions from manual mode to alt hold mode, the vehicle should hold the current vehicle depth.   

**Issue details**

If the sub is disarmed in manual mode, the output "throttle" (vertical control) is set to 0.0, corresponding to full downward thrust.  While this value is not used in manual control, it is used as an initial value on subsequent mode changes (e.g. to ALT_HOLD).  

Set to 0.5 (neutral, no vertical thrust) instead.

**Version**

BlueOS 1.4.2, Ardupilot 4.5.7 (also observed with 4.5.5)

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[ X] Submarine

**Airframe and hardware type**

BlueROV Heavy **with Pi5 and Navigator5 board**

**Logs**

Logfile attached, see interpretation in the BR Forum post linked above.

[00000039.BIN.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24970598/00000039.BIN.zip)

author: Suresh-Krishna-P
body:
Hello @amarburg ,

I’d like to work on this issue and have outlined a proposed implementation strategy below. I’d appreciate your feedback. 
 
- Root cause: when disarmed in Manual/Acro the code sets the internal attitude controller throttle output to 0.0 (full-down). That stale 0.0 value can be picked up later when switching into ALT_HOLD after arming, causing a sudden dive.

- Fix: set the internal throttle output to neutral (0.5) while disarmed in ArduSub Manual/Acro so ALT_HOLD never starts from a full-down command.

What I can change

- Make the disarmed branch in ArduSub modes set attitude_control->set_throttle_out(0.5f, ...) instead of set_throttle_out(0, ...).
- Files touched (minimal):

    - ArduSub/mode_manual.cpp
    - ArduSub/mode_acro.cpp
  
Why this is safe

- ModeAlthold already uses 0.5 for the disarmed path; this makes Manual/Acro consistent with that behavior for subs.
- This only changes the internal controller’s stored throttle output while disarmed; it does not alter RC mapping while the vehicle is armed.
- It prevents ALT_HOLD mode from initializing from a false full-down throttle command.

If you’re okay with this approach, I’m happy to open a PR.

title: AP_HAL_ESP32: GPIO bugs when using them as relays
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
I have encountered 2 bugs when i was trying to setup L298N motor driver in ardupilot on ESP32   
Bug 1: For some unknown for me reason [AP_Relay::get_pin_state method](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/046fb7d5d6400db23f269f53f8bd05d2ef922178/libraries/AP_Relay/AP_Relay.cpp#L505) changes the pin state via `hal.gpio->pinMode(pin, HAL_GPIO_OUTPUT)`. The problem is that serial console is getting flooded with logs from         `gpio_config(&io_conf);` because of current log level, as this method is called at LOOP_RATE frequency. 
The solution is to get/store current pin mode and check if it is already set to desired value. Unfortunately there is no [gpio_get_io_config function](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32/api-reference/peripherals/gpio.html#_CPPv418gpio_get_io_config10gpio_num_tP16gpio_io_config_t) in [esp idf v5.3](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/v5.3.4/esp32/api-reference/peripherals/gpio.html) that is currently used by AP_HAL_ESP32, so for now i have decided to store the current pin mode in static variable in pinMode method.

Bug 2: [GPIO::read method](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/f24951c015e6afa244ba71268fda97c13201e9af/libraries/AP_HAL_ESP32/GPIO.cpp#L54) calls [gpio_get_level function](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/v5.3.4/esp32/api-reference/peripherals/gpio.html#_CPPv414gpio_get_level10gpio_num_t) from esp idf gpio driver, which has following warning: _"If the pad is not configured for input (or input and output) the returned value is always 0."_ and the problem is that pinMode method uses GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT instead of GPIO_MODE_INPUT_OUTPUT and thus the relays set the pin to HIGH and can never set it to LOW because it checks current pin state before changing the output and always receives that pin is LOW.
The solution is to change GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT to GPIO_MODE_INPUT_OUTPUT in pinMode method

**How to reproduce**
Setup L298N motor driver according to the [documentation for brushed motors](https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-brushed-motors.html#l298n-note)

author: muramura
body:
I believe that RC_OVERRIDE should not be recommended as a generic vehicle control interface.
Instead, MANUAL_CONTROL should be the default approach.

The reasons are as follows:

RC_OVERRIDE is based on raw PWM values and therefore strongly depends on
RC vendors, protocols, and calibration differences.

This design pushes hardware-specific knowledge onto the GCS or companion computer side.

MANUAL_CONTROL uses normalized inputs in the range -1.0 to +1.0,
representing pilot intent rather than hardware-level values.

If PWM output is required, it should be derived inside ArduPilot using RC calibration,
and raw PWM values should not be required as an external API.

maybe the best of both worlds would be to support for MANUAL_CONTROL , and RC_OVERRIDE  or RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE as PWM-based override of any channels?
My main "issue" with MANUAL_CONTROL is that has support for very few channels.

author: peterbarker
body:
>     * Firmware tends to have support for things happening based on RC channel PWM values. Specifically gimbal stuff.

Certainly some gimbals are connected to the autopilot using (e.g.) three PWM wires which can be used to control the gimbal.  That's really rather rare, 'though, and isn't really a great setup.

>     * If the firmware had support for RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE then a GCS could do interesting things with joysticks which output RC stuff to make things happen. Move gimbals, press buttons to take actions, operate a servo to do some payload thing, ...

All of those operations are better done through specific messages rather than `RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE`.  gimbals are far better controlled by sending in one of the gimbal-position or gimbal-rate messages.  That allows the GCS to be agnostic about just what sort of gimbal it is talking to.  I've got servo gimbals, mavlink gimbals and proprietary-protocol gimbals floating around on my desk at the moment, but I use exactly the same commands to control them.  

Not really sure what "press buttons" means... but ArduPilot uses a huge list of auxiliary functions which can be triggered through a variety of sources.  You actually use that list when setting (e.g.) `RC5_OPTION` in QGC - the population of that dropdown box is the list of auxiliary functions.  These auxiliary functions can *also* be triggered via mission items using `MAV_CMD_DO_AUX_FUNCTION`, or via a direct mavlink message to the vehicle using that same `MAV_CMD`.  The same functions are also available to our Lua scripting.  You can *also* trigger those functions by pressing physical buttons on the vehicle!  It's a cheap and cheerful interface which is *really* useful :-)

MissionPlanner actually has a tab set aside for aux functions in its interface.  You already actually use `MAV_CMD_DO_AUX_FUNCTION` for toggling the interlock in QGC.  These AUX functions would probably work in really well with the "quick button" array thing you can have in the QGC interface (might have been replaced with Fly View Actions now?)

There's MAV_CMD_DO_SET_RELAY to handle relays (and the "repeat" equivalents).

>     * QGC already has joystick button support to make things happen all working from the GCS side. But I think this might open up even more possibilities.
> 
>     * It's not about flying the vehicle with RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE it's about everything else that might be possible

I'm afraid I don't see a compelling reason to couple anything to RC overrides.  Better for the vehicle to know what it is doing so it can deal with the device in other ways (e.g. stow camera for landing, use camera/gimbal in missions, ....)

I've seen things go pretty wrong with them, however.

Don't get me wrong, they're astonishingly useful in some circumstances, particularly when setting a vehicle up, or when you need to hack something together.  But where there are existing mechanisms to accomplish something we really should try to fit in with those mechanisms.

author: bhuvan-somisetty
body:
This PR implements a dedicated ground truth state publisher for SITL environments, enabling accurate ROS visualization and sensor fusion workflows where estimated state feedback would create circular dependencies or introduce unnecessary noise.

 Motivation
When integrating external sensors (cameras, LiDAR, etc.) for state estimation in ROS/ROS2 ecosystems, using the vehicle's estimated state creates a problematic feedback loop. Visualization and sensor fusion pipelines require access to the actual simulated state rather than filtered estimates. This is critical for:

- Vision-based navigation development: Comparing visual odometry against ground truth
- Sensor fusion validation: Testing EKF/UKF implementations with known truth data
- Algorithm benchmarking: Quantifying estimation accuracy in controlled scenarios
- Multi-sensor integration: Synchronizing external sensor data with true vehicle state

Implementation
New DDS Topic: `/ap/sim/groundtruth`

Publishing Rate: 50Hz (configurable)  
Scope: SITL only - zero overhead on flight hardware  
Message Type: Custom message providing comprehensive state information

Message Structure

std_msgs/Header header

Geographic position
float64 latitude    # degrees
float64 longitude   # degrees  
float64 altitude    # meters above mean sea level

Cartesian position in ENU frame relative to home position
geometry_msgs/Vector3 position

Orientation quaternion in ENU frame
geometry_msgs/Quaternion orientation

Linear velocity in ENU frame (m/s)
geometry_msgs/Vector3 linear_velocity

Angular velocity in body frame (rad/s)
geometry_msgs/Vector3 angular_velocity
```

Key Features
- High-frequency updates (50Hz) for smooth visualization and real-time sensor integration
- ENU frame consistency aligning with ROS conventions (REP-103)
- Comprehensive state including position, orientation, and velocities
- Geographic + Cartesian coordinates for flexible integration
- SITL-only compilation ensuring zero impact on production builds
- Timestamped messages for proper sensor synchronization

Testing
- Verified compilation with DDS enabled in SITL
- Confirmed 50Hz publishing rate in simulation
- Validated coordinate frame transformations (ENU)
- Tested with RViz visualization
- Verified zero impact on non-SITL builds
- Checked message synchronization with other DDS topics

Benefits
1. Eliminates estimation feedback loops** in external sensor development
2. Enables accurate benchmarking** of estimation algorithms
3. Facilitates ROS ecosystem integration** with standard conventions
4. Supports research and education** use cases
5. Maintains zero overhead** on actual flight hardware

Platforms Supported
- Copter
- Plane  
- Rover
- Sub
- AntennaTracker

Breaking Changes

None - this is a purely additive feature for SITL environments.

Documentation

- Added DDS topic documentation to SITL setup guide
- Updated message definitions reference
- Included usage examples for ROS/ROS2 integration

author: Khalid-Hersafril-Flowcopter
title: `LOG_FILE_DSRMROT`: allow to work with replay
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Our setup currently uses a CubeOrange+ flight controller paired with a separate system-controller MCU, each with independent logging systems. To troubleshoot recurring EKF issues (such as altitude discontinuities), we have enabled EKF_REPLAY with LOG_DISARMED set to always on, as recommended in the documentation for effective replay functionality.

However, LOG_DISARMED causes the flight controller to continuously log to a single .bin file across multiple flights until reboot is performed. We usually like to separate our system's log per flight. This makes it relatively troublesome to correlate flight controller logs with our system-controller logs on a per-flight basis, as each flight’s data is embedded within one large file rather than segmented by flight event.

At the moment, the workaround that we have done to correlate the flight controller logs and the system controller logs is that we have a separate lua script that captures the current bin file number and transmit it over CAN which is stored in the system controller log. This makes it relatively easier to find the correct flight logs, but the issue where the flight logs gets really big (~300MB or potentially even more) still stands.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
I was wondering if it would be possible that another feature be added where maybe, the log stops being recorded X seconds after the drone is disarmed, and then it creates a new log file afterwards. This would potentially allow us to have 1 log per flight, instead of having multiple flights being recorded (before a reboot is done) in a single bin file which can be quite annoying to analyse.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Up until now, to reduce the file size, we performed the following workaround:
- Reboot the flight controller prior to every flight test (not entirely practical once out in the field) to capture one flight per log
- Transmit the current .bin file number over CAN through the use of lua script to simplify the process of finding the corresponding BIN files to the system controller logs. We can then use the timestamps from our system controller logs and the flight controller logs to find the exact flight event.
- Disable INS logging unless necessary to reduce the file size

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[x] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Yes. In GPS-denied navigation (e.g. indoor flight), optical flow fusion can be intermittently rejected by EKF3, causing the filter to fall back to dead-reckoning without an obvious reason visible to the user or in logs.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
Expose the existing EKF3 optical flow fusion gating logic as an explicit trust state and DataFlash logging, derived directly from current checks (tilt, height validity, innovation tests, rate limits).

This would improve debuggability of GPS-denied navigation without
changing estimator behavior or tuning.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Relying solely on post-flight log analysis or indirect EKF status flags, which makes it difficult to identify why optical flow was rejected at a given time.


**Platform**

This proposal is intended as a small, non-invasive improvement focused on observability only. No fusion logic, thresholds, or estimator behavior would be modified.

author: rmackay9
title: Copter: Guided should resume horiz pos control when takeoff completes regardless of WP_NAVALT_MIN
body:
Guided mode's use of [WP_NAVALT_MIN](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/parameters.html#wp-navalt-min-waypoint-navigation-altitude-minimum) is different from Auto mode in that in Auto mode, once the vehicle completes the takeoff it resumes horizontal position control regardless of whether the vehicle is above WP_NAVALT_MIN or not.  In Guided mode however, the vehicle does not resume horizontal position control when takeoff completes meaning the vehicle may drift.

The issue can be reproduced in SITL.  First test in Guided mode:

1. param set SIM_WIND_SPD 10
2. param set SIM_WIND_DIR 90
3. param set WP_NAVALT_MIN 20
4. GUIDED
5. arm throttle
6. takeoff 10

The vehicle will drift with the wind until the mode is changed

Next test in Auto mode:

1. create a mission with only a single TAKEOFF command with alt of 10m
2. param set AUTO_OPTIONS 3
3. arm throttle

The vehicle will takeoff to 10m, drifting with the wind as it climbs but upon completion of the takeoff will stop its horizontal movement

This issue exists in both Copter-4.6 and latest/master

Thanks to @CraigElder, @Ryanf55 and @tpwrules for finding/investigating this issue

body:
For simulation purposes, you could try running sim_vehicle and the ROS workspace in separate containers. I've created a simple docker-compose file if you'd like to try it out. It sets up 3 containers: sim_vehicle, micro-ros-agent (DDS), and a ROS2 Jazzy workspace. I haven't done extensive testing yet—I only ran ros2 topic echo /ap/clock in the Jazzy container to verify that data was being transmitted successfully.

```yaml
services:
    micro-ros-agent:
        image: microros/micro-ros-agent:jazzy
        container_name: micro_ros_agent
        network_mode: host
        environment:
            - ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
            - RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_fastrtps_cpp
        command: udp4 --port 2019 -v6
        restart: unless-stopped

    ardupilot:
        image: ardupilot
        container_name: sim_vehicle
        volumes:
            - <path_to_ardupilot>:/ardupilot
        user: "${UID:-1000}:${GID:-100}"
        command: sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --enable-DDS
        network_mode: host
        stdin_open: true
        tty: true
        depends_on:
            - micro-ros-agent
    
    ros_workspace:
        image: osrf/ros:jazzy-desktop 
        container_name: ros
        network_mode: host
        command: bash
        stdin_open: true
        tty: true
        environment:
            - ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
        depends_on:
            - micro-ros-agent
```

author: ViharDuggi2005
title: Copter: support Native Ship / Moving Platform Landing Support
body:
Currently, ArduCopter does not provide a native, documented way to land on a moving platform (e.g. ship deck) comparable to the existing Plane / QuadPlane ship landing support.

While Plane has:

SIM_SHIP_ENABLE

Built-in ship simulation

Documented RTL-based landing logic

Official examples and Lua scripts

ArduCopter users must rely on:

External Rover “beacon” vehicles

Undocumented FOLLOW behavior

Custom Lua scripts

Trial-and-error configuration

This makes ship landing with Copter difficult, fragile, and inconsistent, especially in SITL and for research/testing use cases.

author: ViharDuggi2005
body: Could anyone help with the lua script required for landing ArduCopter on a moving platform like ship?

author: comsompom
body:
This script uses the `Follow` library (normally used for "Follow Me") to get the ship's position and velocity, but instead of hovering, it uses `GUIDED` mode to force a synchronized descent.

#### Prerequisite
The ship must be transmitting its position and velocity to the drone (via MAVLink `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT`). In a real setup, this is usually done via a telemetry radio pair where the ship (or the GCS on the ship) broadcasts to the drone.

#### The Lua Script (`ship_land.lua`)

```lua
-- ArduCopter Moving Platform/Ship Landing Script
-- Triggers a velocity-synchronized landing on a moving Mavlink target (Follow target)
--
-- HOW IT WORKS:
-- 1. Switch assigned to RCx_OPTION = 300 (Scripting1) is pulled HIGH.
-- 2. Script switches drone to GUIDED mode.
-- 3. Script reads the 'Follow' target (the ship) position and velocity.
-- 4. Script calculates a velocity vector: Ship_Velocity + Position_Correction.
-- 5. Drone flies to the ship, matches speed, and descends.

local PARAM_TABLE_KEY = 72
local LOOP_TIME_MS    = 50  -- 20Hz update rate

-- Configuration
local LANDING_SPEED   = 1.5 -- Descent speed in m/s
local APPROACH_HEIGHT = 5.0 -- Meters above target to switch to strict descent
local XY_P_GAIN       = 1.5 -- Position controller gain (higher = harder correction)
local DISARM_DELAY    = 2000 -- ms to wait on deck before disarming

-- State variables
local is_landing = false
local landed_start_time = 0

-- Mappings
local MODE_GUIDED = 4
local MODE_RTL    = 6

function update()
    -- 1. Check control switch (RC input channel assigned to Scripting1)
    -- You can hardcode a specific channel e.g., rc:get_pwm(6) if preferred
    local switch_pos = rc:find_channel_for_option(300) 
    
    -- If switch not assigned or low, reset and wait
    if not switch_pos or switch_pos:get_aux_switch_pos() ~= 2 then
        is_landing = false
        return update, LOOP_TIME_MS
    end

    -- 2. Check if we have a valid target (Ship)
    -- The 'follow' library grabs the lead vehicle info from MAVLink
    local target_loc, target_vel = follow:get_target_location_and_velocity(0)

    if not target_loc or not target_vel then
        gcs:send_text(6, "ShipLand: No target detected!")
        return update, 1000 -- Slow down updates if no target
    end

    -- 3. Initial Engagement
    if not is_landing then
        if vehicle:set_mode(MODE_GUIDED) then
            gcs:send_text(6, "ShipLand: Engaged! Matching Velocity.")
            is_landing = true
        else
            gcs:send_text(2, "ShipLand: Failed to enter GUIDED mode")
            return update, 1000
        end
    end

    -- 4. Calculate Relative Position (NED)
    local curr_loc = ahrs:get_position()
    if not curr_loc then return update, LOOP_TIME_MS end

    local dist = target_loc:get_distance_NED(curr_loc) -- Vector from Target to Drone
    -- Invert to get Vector from Drone to Target
    local pos_error_x = -dist:x()
    local pos_error_y = -dist:y()
    local pos_error_z = -dist:z() -- Positive means drone is ABOVE target (usually)

    -- 5. Control Logic: Velocity Feed Forward
    -- Target Velocity = Ship_Velocity + (Position_Error * Gain)
    
    local cmd_vel_x = target_vel:x() + (pos_error_x * XY_P_GAIN)
    local cmd_vel_y = target_vel:y() + (pos_error_y * XY_P_GAIN)
    
    -- Vertical Logic
    local cmd_vel_z = 0
    
    -- Current height relative to the target (approximate)
    local rel_alt = math.abs(pos_error_z)

    if rel_alt > APPROACH_HEIGHT then
        -- Phase 1: Approach (Descend slowly or hold alt until close in XY)
        local xy_dist = math.sqrt(pos_error_x^2 + pos_error_y^2)
        if xy_dist < 5.0 then
            cmd_vel_z = 1.0 -- Descend slowly to approach height
        else
            cmd_vel_z = 0.0 -- Stay high until we are closer horizontally
        end
    else
        -- Phase 2: Terminal Descent
        cmd_vel_z = LANDING_SPEED
    end

    -- 6. Safety: Convert "Down" velocity to NED standard
    -- In NED, Down is Positive. LANDING_SPEED is positive.
    
    -- Send command to flight controller
    -- usage: set_target_velocity_NED(vel_ned, accel_ned, yaw_rad, use_yaw, use_yaw_rate, relative_yaw)
    -- We ignore accel and yaw for now (letting standard yaw hold)
    vehicle:set_target_velocity_NED(
        Vector3f():new(cmd_vel_x, cmd_vel_y, cmd_vel_z),
        Vector3f():new(0,0,0)
    )

    -- 7. Landing Detection & Disarm
    if vehicle:get_likely_flying() then
        landed_start_time = 0
    else
        -- Drone thinks it has landed (throttle low, not moving vertically)
        if landed_start_time == 0 then
            landed_start_time = millis()
        elseif (millis() - landed_start_time) > DISARM_DELAY then
            gcs:send_text(6, "ShipLand: Touchdown. Disarming.")
            arming:disarm()
            is_landing = false
        end
    end

    return update, LOOP_TIME_MS
end

return update()
```

### Setup Instructions

#### 1. ArduCopter Configuration
Save the script above as `ship_land.lua` on your SD card in the `APM/scripts/` folder.
Set the following parameters in Mission Planner:

*   `SCR_ENABLE` = 1 (Enable Lua Scripting, requires reboot)
*   `FOLL_ENABLE` = 1 (Enable Follow mode logic)
*   `FOLL_SYSID` = [The Mavlink System ID of your ship/GCS]
*   `RCx_OPTION` = 300 (Scripting1) -> Assign this to a switch on your controller.

#### 2. The "Ship" (SITL or Real)
The drone needs to see a "Target".
*   **In Real Life:** The ship needs a GPS and a telemetry radio. It must broadcast its position. If using Mission Planner on the ship, connect the drone's telemetry to the laptop, and press Ctrl-F -> "Mavlink Mirror" or verify the GCS is sending location data. Alternatively, a second ArduPilot board on the ship (Rover firmware) is the most robust way.
*   **In SITL (Simulation):**
    1.  Start ArduCopter SITL.
    2.  Start a second instance (Rover) to act as the ship: `sim_vehicle.py -v Rover -f boat -I 1 --sysid 2`.
    3.  Connect the two instances via MAVLink. In the Copter params, set `FOLL_SYSID` = 2.

#### 3. Execution
1.  Take off with Copter.
2.  Drive the Ship (Rover) so it is moving.
3.  Flip the switch assigned to `RCx_OPTION 300`.
4.  The drone should switch to **GUIDED**, fly towards the ship, lock onto its X/Y velocity, and descend until it touches the deck and disarms.

### Important Adjustments for Real Ships
*   **Compass Interference:** Large steel ships play havoc with magnetometers. You generally need to disable the internal compass and rely on a high-mounted GPS-Heading (Moving Baseline) setup, or the drone will toilet-bowl upon getting close to the deck.
*   **Relative Altitude:** The script assumes standard barometric/GPS altitude. If the ship deck is higher than the launch point, or if pressure varies, you should add a Rangefinder (Lidar) to the drone.
*   **Lidar Update:** If you use a Lidar, change `local curr_loc = ahrs:get_position()` to read the rangefinder distance for the Z-axis logic.

author: ctrlsill
title: SIGFPE via incorrect type conversion on fence file upload
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
A **SIGFFPE** signal is raised in functions **_convert_MISSION_ITEM_INT_to_AC_PolyFenceI_item_int_** ([MissionItemProtocol_Fence.cpp](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/MissionItemProtocol_Fence.cpp)) and/or _**is_positive**_ ([AP_Math.h)](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Math/AP_Math.cpp)) during an attempted upload of a crafted fence files with invalid values of parameter **_param1_**. Floating point exception occurs due to unchecked type conversions, leading to immediate autopilot process termination and loss of GCS – vehicle communication. 


**Steps to reproduce**
Vulnerability can be triggered by uploading fence files with parameters set to invalid values:

1. **_fence-oor.txt_** – with **_param1_** set to “_**-1e+10**_” (minus 10 billion)
```
QGC WPL 110
0	0	0	5001	-1e+10		0	0	0	0	0	0	0
```
2. _**fence-nan.txt**_  - with **_param1_** set to “_NaN_” (Not-a-Number)
```
QGC WPL 110
0	0	0	5003	 NaN		0	0	0	0	0	0	0
```
To reproduce the vulnerability for ArduCopter in SITL environment, follow below steps:

1. Run SITL simulation for ArduCopter in debug mode
    `$ Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map -w -D -G -ubsan`

2. Wait for vehicle to initialize into PreArm state
   `pre-arm good`

3. Upload one of the fence files to the vehicle using MAVProxy GCS console
```
> fence load fence-oor.txt
> fence load fence-nan.txt
```

4. Observe GCS connection and vehicle process termination

```
Sent all 1 fence items
no link
link 1 down
```

Exception raised for **_fence-oor.txt_** 
```
Thread 1 "arducopter" received signal SIGFPE, Arithmetic exception.
MissionItemProtocol_Fence::convert_MISSION_ITEM_INT_to_AC_PolyFenceItem (mission_item_int=..., ret=...)
    at ../../libraries/GCS_MAVLink/MissionItemProtocol_Fence.cpp:117
117             ret.vertex_count = mission_item_int.param1;
(gdb) print ret.vertex_count
$5 = 0 '\000'
(gdb) print mission_item_int.param1
$6 = -1e+10

```

Exception raised for **_fence-nan.txt_**
```
Thread 1 "arducopter" received signal SIGFPE, Arithmetic exception.
0x00005555555cd03c in is_positive<float> (fVal1=nan(0x400000)) at ../../libraries/AP_Math/AP_Math.h:68
68          return (static_cast<float>(fVal1) >= FLT_EPSILON);
(gdb) print fVal1
$7 = nan(0x400000)
```

Backtrace shows that both input files had a similar effect upon upload, resulting in the FPE due to unchecked type conversions, but raised in different parts of the code:

1. **_fence-oor.txt_** - function **_convert_MISSION_ITEM_INT_to_AC_PolyFenceI_item_int_** responsible for converting MAVLink mission item into an **_AC_PolyFenceItem_** structure,
performs an unchecked assignment of **_param1_** value to **_vertex_count_** of type _uint_8_t_.
2. **_fence-nan.txt_** - function **_is_positive_**, which simply checks whether a float is greater than zero, makes a float-to-NaN comparison between **_fVal1_** (holding _**param1**_ value) and **_FLT_EPSILON_** (of type float), which raises floating-point operation exception. 

**Root cause**
The root cause of this vulnerability is the lack of sufficient validation of parameters carried by **_param1_**, allowing out-of-range or non-numerical values to trigger an unhandled exception. Existing sanitization routine performs none or minimal input validation by doing only upper bound check (>255) for selected parameters, making it highly insufficient. 
Also keep in mind that demonstrated examples exploit only single case for specific 
commands (5001 and 5003), but the same vulnerability is present in all fence-specific commands:

- _MAV_CMD_NAV_FENCE_POLYGON_VERTEX_INCLUSION_  (5001) for  **_vertex_count_** =<(_-1e+10_)
- _MAV_CMD_NAV_FENCE_POLYGON_VERTEX_EXCLUSION_  (5002) for **_vertex_count_** =<(_-1e+10_)
- _MAV_CMD_NAV_FENCE_CIRCLE_EXCLUSION_  (5003) for **_radius_** == _NaN_
- _MAV_CMD_NAV_FENCE_CIRCLE_EXCLUSION_  (5004) for **_radius_** == _NaN_


**Impact**
The impact of this vulnerability is severe, affecting both operational reliability and flight safety across all ArduPilot vehicles. When an attacker in the network or unintentional operator uploads improperly constructed fence file, the autopilot software immediately crashes due to unhandled exception. As a direct result, the connection between the GCS and the vehicle is abruptly lost, so any ongoing automated mission is terminated. For vehicle in the air, this loss of control may lead to dangerous situations including uncontrolled flight, failure to perform failsafe procedures, or even a crash.

**Recommendation**
Enforce strict input validation and bounds checking on all externally supplied fence parameters before they are stored or used in arithmetic operations.
