author: ctrlsill
title: SIGFPE via incorrect type conversion on mission file upload
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

A **SIGFFPE** signal is raised in the function **_mavlink_int_to_mission_cmd_** ([AP_Mission.cpp](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Mission/AP_Mission.cpp))  during an attempted upload of a crafted mission file with invalid values of parameter **_param1_**.
Floating point exception occurs due to unchecked float-to-integer type conversion, leading to immediate autopilot process termination and loss of Ground Control Station (GCS)   – vehicle communication.

**Steps to reproduce**

Vulnerability is triggered by uploading mission file with **_param1_** set to out-of-range value. 
That leads to failure during unchecked _**float**_ (32 bit) to **_uint_16_t_** (16 bit) conversion in _**mavlink_int_to_mission_cmd**_ ([AP_Mission.cpp](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Mission/AP_Mission.cpp))  function. Below demonstration uses a sample crafted mission file following plain-text format, with param1 set to **_1e+10_** (10 billion), that was uploaded to ArduCopter using MAVProxy _**wp load**_ method. 

```
QGC WPL 110
0	0	0	0	1e+10	0	0	0	0	0	0	0
```
To reproduce the vulnerability for ArduCopter in SITL environment, follow below steps:

1. Run SITL simulation for ArduCopter in debug mode
    `$ Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map -w -D -G `
2. Wait for vehicle to initialize into PreArm state
     `pre-arm good`
3. Upload mission file to the vehicle using MAVProxy GCS console
    `> wp load mission.txt`
4. Observe GCS connection and vehicle process termination
```
Sent all 1 waypoints
no link
link 1 down
```

```
Thread 1 "arducopter" received signal SIGFPE, Arithmetic exception.
AP_Mission::mavlink_int_to_mission_cmd (packet=..., cmd=...)
    at ../../libraries/AP_Mission/AP_Mission.cpp:1103
1103            cmd.p1 = packet.param1;
(gdb) print cmd.p1
$1 = 0
(gdb) print packet.param1
$2 = 1e+10
```


**Root cause**

Backtrace of the error shows that insecure type conversion occurs within the **_mavlink_int_to_mission_cmd_**   ([AP_Mission.cpp](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Mission/AP_Mission.cpp)) function, which converts MAVLink message into a **_Mission_Command_** object to be stored in EEPROM vehicle memory. SIGFPE signal is raised at line 1103 due to an arithmetic exception caused by an unsafe assignment between mismatched types with vastly different ranges.
- **_packet.param1_** is a 32-bit float
- **_cmd.p1_** is a 16-bit unsigned integer

The root cause of this vulnerability is the lack of sufficient bounds checking on **_param1_** prior to type conversion, allowing out-of-range values to trigger a hardware exception. Existing sanitization function **_sanity_check_params_** only performs minimal validation by rejecting infinite or selectively NaN values for parameters 1–4 and does not enforce any command-specific numeric ranges or limits, making this protection highly insufficient.


**Impact**
The impact of this vulnerability is severe, affecting both operational reliability and flight safety across all affected ArduPilot vehicles including ArduCopter, ArduRover and ArduSub. When an attacker in the network or unintentional operator uploads improperly constructed mission file, the autopilot software immediately crashes due to unhandled exception.  As a direct result, the connection between the GCS and the vehicle is abruptly lost, so any ongoing automated mission is terminated. For vehicle in the air, this loss of control may lead to dangerous situations including uncontrolled flight, failure to perform failsafe procedures, or even a crash.


**Recommendations**
Enforce strict input validation and bounds checking on all externally supplied mission parameters before they are stored or used in arithmetic operations.

title: Provide a method to get a binary log of all serial data
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I have a serial port, currently configured for a mavlink connection. The autopilot is not accessible when the vehicle is assembled. I want to have an easy way to decode traffic on the port. If it was, I'd use a Saleae logic analyzer, decode as async serial, and then run use pymavlink to decode the stream.

I cant use the mavlink inspector in mission planner because this is an internal connection in the vehicle, and some packets on this mavlink interface are not also repeated on the GCS link.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Provide an option to enable logging for the serial port, which will log all data to a binary file on the SD card.
I can then use mavftp to transfer this to my computer and interpret the contents.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Turning on LOG_REPLAY does not log serial port traffic.

author: peterbarker
body:
This is a bug in the documentation ( @Hwurzburg ).  We should just remove the statement. 

You're on the ground in a non-pilot-controlled mode which isn't trying to descend or in some other way land the vehicle.  Not disarming is probably correct.

Exactly the same things happen if you use `GUIDED` mode instead of `BRAKE` mode.

We could change the logic so that if you're not in a mode which obeys pilot input then we don't look at the pilot throttle level while working out whether to disarm.  That would be No Small Change in behaviour.

@Lqs66 did you want to work up a patch against the documentation?

author: muramura
title: New MAVLink message RADIO_RC_CHANNELS_MASKED for bandwidth optimization on low-baudrate links
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, RC channel transmission over MAVLink (using `RADIO_RC_CHANNELS`, ID: 420) is inefficient for low-bandwidth telemetry links (e.g., LoRa, Satellite). 

In the existing implementation, the value `0` represents the neutral/center position (1500µs). Because `0` is a valid data point, MAVLink V2's trailing-zero trimming cannot discard these values if they appear in the middle of the array. For example, if only CH10 is updated and CH1–CH9 are at neutral, the entire array up to CH10 must be transmitted as zeros, which prevents effective payload trimming.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to propose a new message: `RADIO_RC_CHANNELS_MASKED`. This message is designed to fully leverage MAVLink V2's trimming capabilities by redefining the array structure:

1. **32-bit Mask (`active_mask`):** A `uint32_t` bitmask indicating which channels are included in the packet (Bit 0 = CH1, ..., Bit 31 = CH32).
2. **Packed Array (`channels`):** Only the values flagged in the mask are packed at the beginning of the `int16_t[32]` array.
3. **Trailing-Zero Optimization:** All elements not included in the current update are set to `0`. Since these "null" values are packed at the end of the payload, MAVLink V2 physically trims them during transmission.
4. **Data Consistency:** Values use the same 13-bit centered-at-zero format as ID 420 to ensure precision and compatibility.
   - Conversion: $PWM = (\text{value} \times 5/32) + 1500$

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Standard `RADIO_RC_CHANNELS` (ID 420) or `RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE`. These messages cannot achieve sparse, event-driven updates because their fixed-index structures force the transmission of neutral "0" values, neutralizing the benefits of MAVLink V2 trimming.

**Platform**
[ X ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**

### Proposed XML Definition

```xml
<message id="510" name="RADIO_RC_CHANNELS_MASKED">
  <description>Bandwidth-efficient 32-channel RC message. Uses active_mask for channel presence and int16_t offsets (center 0) to maximize MAVLink V2 trailing-zero trimming efficiency.</description>
  <field type="uint8_t" name="target_system">System ID.</field>
  <field type="uint8_t" name="target_component">Component ID.</field>
  <field type="uint32_t" name="active_mask">Bitmap of included channels (bit 0 = CH1). 1: Valid, 0: Invalid/Unused.</field>
  <field type="uint16_t" name="status_flags">
    Bitmask for RC status. 
    Bit 0: FAILSAFE (1: Link lost, 0: OK). 
    Bit 1: FRAME_LOST (1: Packet loss detected, 0: OK). 
    Bit 2: ENCRYPTED (1: Link is encrypted, 0: Unencrypted). 
    Bit 3: HYPER_RESOLUTION (1: Values are 0.1us units, 0: 1us units).
  </field>
  <field type="uint8_t" name="rssi">Receive signal strength indicator (0-255). 255 for unknown.</field>
  <field type="int16_t[32]" name="channels">RC channel values as offsets from neutral (center 0). Raw SBUS 1024 -> 0. PWM 1500 -> 0. Elements at the end must be 0 for MAVLink V2 trimming.</field>
</message>
```

### Key Improvements in this Proposal:

* **32-Channel Support**: Future-proofing for complex vehicles, high-axis gimbals, and advanced payload controls.
* **Bandwidth Efficiency**: By using `int16_t` with a center value of 0, this message fully utilizes **MAVLink V2's trailing-zero trimming**. Channels not in use (or at neutral) at the end of the array are not transmitted, significantly reducing telemetry overhead.
* **Active Masking**: The `active_mask` allows the receiver to distinguish between a "valid neutral 0" and an "inactive/skipped channel," providing native support for non-contiguous channel assignments.
* **Robust Status Handling**: Added `status_flags` to provide parity with SBUS and other professional protocols, ensuring critical states like **Failsafe** and **Frame Lost** are communicated explicitly rather than being inferred from channel values.


### Efficiency & Optimization

* **Time on Wire:** For a typical 2-channel update, the transmission time is reduced by approximately 80% on serial links compared to the standard `RADIO_RC_CHANNELS` message.
* **CPU Overhead:** The decoding process on the Flight Controller can be optimized by terminating the bitmask loop as soon as it reaches the maximum channel count configured in ArduPilot parameters (e.g., `RC_CHAN_CNT`). This avoids redundant checks for unused higher-index bits, ensuring the workload is proportional to the actual hardware configuration.

author: Lqs66
title: Unexpected Disarm in ACRO mode when Throttle at zero during GCS/RC Failsafe while airborne
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

In ACRO mode, if the vehicle is airborne and the throttle is at the minimum position, triggering an GCS/RC Failsafe causes the copter to immediately disarm in mid-air.

While the "Disarm on low throttle" logic is expected on the ground, it should not be triggered when the flight controller detects the vehicle is still in flight (Airborne), especially during a failsafe event where a controlled RTL or Land is expected.

See line 472:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/cef6eb780255cc398657a97aa4ef13e438296490/ArduCopter/events.cpp#L463-L482

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Take off and switch to ACRO mode.
2. Lower the throttle stick to the minimum position.
3. param set FS_THR_VALUE -1 (trigger an RC Failsafe)/param set FS_GCS_TIMEOUT 0 (trigger a GCS Failsafe).
4. The copter disarms immediately and falls.
5. Expected Result: The copter should trigger the configured Failsafe action (e.g., RTL or Land) regardless of the throttle position, as long as it is airborne.

**Version**
Copter 4.4 -> main

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[x] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
sitl

**Logs**
RC Failsafe:
[log_0_2025-12-27-12-45-46.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24352570/log_0_2025-12-27-12-45-46.zip)

GCS Failsafe:
[log_0_2026-1-7-16-26-53.bin.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24468172/log_0_2026-1-7-16-26-53.bin.zip)

author: IamPete1
body: At zero throttle in acro the vehicle is already falling. So your already having a crash before the failsafe happens. Have you actually hit this in real life?

author: deepak61296
body:
I was able to reproduce this and found the issue. it's in the `should_disarm_on_failsafe()` function at line 472 in events.cpp.

**the problem:**

currently uses OR logic:
```cpp
return ap.throttle_zero || ap.land_complete;
```

disarms if throttle is zero OR vehicle landed. so when airborne with zero throttle, failsafe just disarms you mid-air.

**the fix:**

change `||` to `&&`:
```cpp
return ap.throttle_zero && ap.land_complete;
```

only disarms when throttle is zero AND actually landed.

**tested in SITL:**

took off to ~280m, zeroed throttle in ACRO, triggered failsafe.

before: immediately disarmed and fell
after: switched to RTL mode. still crashed because the copter was already falling hard in ACRO when RTL kicked in, but at least it tried to execute the failsafe action instead of just disarming.

triggering RTL is the right call - gives the copter a chance to recover. if caught earlier it should work fine.

opened PR #31806 for this. same fix applies to all failsafe types since they use this function.

---

title: [SITL + ardupilot_gazebo] Iris with 3-DOF gimbal: gimbal jumps to an unexpected pose during SITL startup initialization
body: ## Bug report **Issue details** **Steps to reproduce** (1)Start the Gazebo world and model (the gimbal is initially aligned with the vehicle heading in Gazebo): gz sim -v4 -r ~/ardupilot/ardupilot_gazebo/worlds/iris_runway.sdf (2)Start SITL and load the gimbal parameter file: ./Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -D -v ArduCopter -f JSON \ --add-param-file=$HOME/work/ardupilot/ardupilot_gazebo/config/gazebo-iris-gimbal.parm \ --console --map **Expected behavior** After starting SITL, the gimbal should not suddenly jump to an extreme pose during initialization. At minimum, it should remain aligned with the vehicle heading, or first stabilize to a predictable neutral/retract pose. If RC Targeting is the default mode, a more reasonable initial RC input is expected. **Actual behavior** After starting SITL, the gimbal in Gazebo quickly twists to a strange orientation, and the initial pose aligned with the vehicle heading is broken. Early RC inputs captured from RC_CHANNELS are: chan6_raw=1000 chan7_raw=1000 chan8_raw=1800 Meanwhile, the parameter file configures the calibration range for RC6/7/8 as RCx_MIN=1100, RCx_MAX=1900, so the raw values at startup are below the configured lower bound (at least CH6/7: 1000 < 1100). author: LupusTheCanine
title: ESC to RPM sensor processing
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

* AM32 ESCs sometimes report RPM values that are significantly out of range (50k+ RPM on a motor that spins at 4k RPM). Thist mostly happens during spool up causing heli governor using ESC RPM telemetry to fail to engage)
* BDShot RPM telemetry (on AM32 ESCs) is jittery ±10RPM jitter at 4k RPM which probably messes with the Ardupilot governor, causing throttle jitter.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Adding lowpass filter to RPM library and respecting RPMx_MAX when taking data from ESC telemetry would alleviate these issues. At the cost of slightly decreased governor tracking accuracy

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

* Checking that the governor is engaged prior to takeoff
* Kickstarting the motor with the interlock to avoid the issue
* Cycling the interlock to re-engage the governor 
* Using throttle curve (not feasible due to large voltage range and apparent lack of voltage compensation)


**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[ X ] Copter (heli)
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
Will add screenshots soon.

I think the ESC should handle such slip ups more gracefully, but it is what it is. Spool up event, this one wasn't caught by the RPM library 🤷‍♂️. The filter I want mostly to deal with the ESC telemetry being limited to the resolution of eRPM frames for with the LSB represents 8RPM at 4000 RPM, 16RPM above 4088RPM according to the documentation and progressively getting worse. I think smoothing it down a bit could improve governor jitter (which shakes the tail). Unfortunately, I do not have experience with tuning the ESC to make the spool up more reliable and the AM32 documentation doesn't really help either. author: ES-Alexander
title: TemperatureSensor: Add Rangefinder to the TEMPx_SRC sensor source options
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Rover (and [hopefully soon Sub](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/31622)) make use of a `WATER_DEPTH` MAVLink message, which includes temperature data from a downward-facing rangefinder. Rangefinders don't always include temperature sensors (or they may not be super accurate), so it could be nice to be able to sub that in from a dedicated temperature sensor.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a `Rangefinder` option to the temperature sensor [source options](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_TemperatureSensor/AP_TemperatureSensor_Params.h#L43), to allow the rangefinder driver temperature data to be overshadowed via the [`TEMPx_SRC`](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/parameters.html#temp1-src-sensor-source) parameters.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
1. The `WATER_DEPTH` message could automatically fall back to another temperature source if one is provided, but that either reliant on the rangefinder not providing temperature data, or makes it ambiguous as to what is being used
2. The source could be specified as "water temperature" instead of specifically rangefinder, which could make it more broadly useful in future, but also makes it less clear when and where it's likely to be used.
3. We could add dedicated MAVLink reporting for temperature sensors, and/or specifically for water temperature, which are both potentially good ideas, but then it's potentially unclear what source is being used for the temperature data in the `WATER_DEPTH` message

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[x] Rover
[x] Submarine

**Additional context**
#31616 may be a good reference for the temperature sensor library side of things.

author: Parshv-sudo
body:
Hi @ES-Alexander,

I’ve been going over the `AP_TemperatureSensor_Params` setup and wanted to confirm my understanding before I move ahead.
It looks like this could fit into the current temperature routing model without needing changes to MAVLink or rangefinder drivers.

Here’s my idea:
- Add a `Rangefinder` option to `AP_TemperatureSensor_Params::Source`, similar to the ESC and Servo sources in #31616.
- When `TEMPx_SRC = Rangefinder`, treat the temperature sensor as an explicit external override for the rangefinder frontend.
- Make the rangefinder frontend prefer this value over driver-reported temperatures for `WATER_DEPTH` while keeping MAVLink packing and backend code the same.

This keeps the feature optional, maintains defaults, and follows the same override pattern. I would appreciate your thoughts on whether this approach makes sense or if you’d recommend a different direction.

I’m happy to make changes before proceeding.

author: ES-Alexander
body:
Hi @Parshv-sudo,

I think the approach you've outlined generally makes sense, with a minor caveat:
  
> - When `TEMPx_SRC = Rangefinder`, treat the temperature sensor as an explicit external override for the rangefinder frontend.
> - Make the rangefinder frontend prefer this value over driver-reported temperatures for WATER_DEPTH while keeping MAVLink packing and backend code the same.

This combination doesn't completely make sense to me. If the temperature sensor is acting as an override in the rangefinder frontend (which does seem like the desired behaviour 👍 ), then the code for `WATER_DEPTH` MAVLink message creation (and anywhere else the rangefinder's temperature is being used) shouldn't need to know or care that that's happening - they just use whatever value the rangefinder frontend is reporting.

I agree that MAVLink packing and backend code should not be affected.

> This keeps the feature optional, maintains defaults, ...

Indeed - the feature will only be accepted if it is optional, and does not break any existing functionality or expectations.

author: Parshv-sudo
body:
Thanks for the feedback @ES-Alexander. That makes sense.

In other words, the override will be handled entirely in the rangefinder frontend. Any users downstream, including `WATER_DEPTH` MAVLink packing, won’t know if the temperature comes from the driver or an external sensor. They will just use whatever value the frontend provides.

With that clarification, I think I can proceed with the approach we discussed. The feature will be completely optional, and existing behavior will be kept by default.

author: ES-Alexander
title: Sub: 4.5 forward-port list
body:
This is a list of anything in an ArduSub release branch that needs equivalent behaviour implemented in master. Some PRs/commits may be able to be directly forward ported, while others will require additional considerations and discussion for their relevance and implementation with respect to the other ArduPilot firmware variants. If new missing items/commits are identified they will be added.

## Parameter migration / bad configuration detection
- [x] Automatic transition from old `BRD_PWM_COUNT` GPIO determination functionality, to new `GPIO (-1)` `SERVOx_FUNCTION` values and/or using the `SERVO_GPIO_MASK`
    - #31685
    - #31702
    - Without this the leak sensor may be silently broken, which is a critical warning system in Sub vehicles
    - It also affects relays, which could benefit from some user warnings if the autopilot can tell they're misconfigured
- [ ] Automatic transition from `RCIN9 (59)`/`RCIN10 (60)` channel passthrough piggy-backing to new dedicated `Lights1 (181)`/`Lights2 (182)` `SERVOx_FUNCTION` outputs
    - #31109
    - This parameter change also broke programmatic control of lights outputs, which has not yet been resolved
        - The illuminator protocol [is being considered](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/28814#issuecomment-3617607624) as a replacement for the old [`DO_SET_SERVO`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO) commands (which required knowing the channel number of the output), although it is a fair amount more complex
- [ ] Automatic transition from old `Disabled (0)` to new `Actuator1 (184)`/`Actuator2 (185)`/`Actuator3 (186)` `SERVOx_FUNCTION` outputs
    - #31109 
    - This parameter change also broke programmatic control of actuator outputs, which has not yet been resolved
        - [`DO_SET_ACTUATOR`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_ACTUATOR) MAVLink commands [are planned](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/28814) as a replacement for the old [`DO_SET_SERVO`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO) commands (which required knowing the channel number of the output)

## Release notes
- [ ] Update master to include [the release notes](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/Sub-4.5/ArduSub/ReleaseNotes.txt) from the various 4.5 versions that have been released
    - Some of these are related to the features that need forward-porting, so it likely doesn't make sense to bring them through until those features are also available in master (and there'll likely be one for 4.5.7 with the leak/relay details)

## Bug report

I've been analyzing the Mode::land_run_vertical_control function and noticed a conflict between the official documentation and the actual code logic regarding the descent rate below 10m.

The Discrepancy: As a result, a copter at 5m altitude (which is "below 10m") will likely descend much faster than LAND_SPEED because the controller sees sufficient braking distance to the 1m target. The "10m switch" described in the docs does not appear to exist in the code unless LAND_ALT_LOW is manually set to 1000.

Is this a case of documentation lag, or is the code behavior intended to be purely parameter-dependent regardless of the 10m rule mentioned in the wiki?

author: rmackay9
title: Copter: Dijkastras may get stuck if "Allow fast waypoints" options is enabled and WPNAV_RADIUS > 2 and
body: If users set the OA_OPTIONS bit "Allow fast waypoints" and set WPNAV_RADIUS > 2 the vehicle may get stuck as it flies a path provided by Dijkstras (e.g. a path around a fence) The core problem is that [OA_PathPlanner](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_Avoidance/AP_OAPathPlanner.h) is responsible for returning the next two waypoints that the vehicle should fly to but it doesn't know when AC_WPNav has actually completed these waypoints. [The code here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_Avoidance/AP_OADijkstra.cpp#L224) tries to figure this out using the vehicle's current location but it assumes the vehicle will come within 2m of the point which it may actually not if "allow fast waypoints" is enabled. The problematic [line is here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_Avoidance/AP_OADijkstra.cpp#L224) and copied below `const bool near_oa_wp = current_loc.get_distance(destination_new) <= 2.0f;` Here's an example mission and fence that exhibits the problem. When the vehicle RTLs at the end The proper solution is not as simple as just passing in the WPNAV_RADIUS to Dijkstras though because while this parameter sets an **upper limit** on how far the vehicle may fly from the waypoint, the vehicle normally flies closer than this. In fact a user could set the WPNAV_RADIUS = 100m and still the vehicle would fly quite close to the waypoints. In this case if Dijkstras used 100m it would consider intermediate points complete far too early and would likely cut corners which could lead to breaching the fence. I think the proper solution is to improve the interface between [AP_OAPathPlanner::mission_avoidance()](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_Avoidance/AP_OAPathPlanner.cpp#L196) and [AP_OADijkstra::update()](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_Avoidance/AP_OADijkstra.cpp#L50) (which is currently passing back and forth [avoidance_info stuctures](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_Avoidance/AP_OAPathPlanner.h#L98)) so that Dijkstras provides not just the next two intermediate points but instead the entire path around the obstacle. Then [AC_WPNav_OA](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_WPNav/AC_WPNav_OA.h) should hold onto this path and take responsibility for feeding the next two points into the [AC_WPNav base class](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_WPNav/AC_WPNav.h). AC_WPNav_OA can do this better than Dijkstras because it can keep track of where the vehicle is along the path by calling the base classes's [reached_wp_destination()](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_WPNav/AC_WPNav.h#L240C18-L240C40) method BTW, I've done some work in [this PR to restructure Dijkstras](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/28542). We should consider merging this restructure to master and converting AC_Avoidance to always use meters before trying to resolve this issue.

author: henry-sensoriis
title: AC_PrecLand LOCAL_FRD support yaw rotation sign error
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

It appears that there is a sign error on the recently introduced support for LOCAL_FRD MAV_FRAME in the AC_PrecLand module. From my perspective it seems that "_inertial_data_delayed->Tbn" describes the rotation quaternion from the Body Frame to the NED frame. To rotate BODY_FRD (the previous, well tested MAV_FRAME used in AC_PrecLand) we rotate the FRD unit vector by the _intertial_data_delayed->Tbn quaternion to get NED Frame.

When doing this for LOCAL_FRD (which is yaw only, gravity aligned so no roll/pitch) we extract the Euler rotations from the BODY->NED quaternion and rotate by the Yaw only. This is correct, except that we are using rotate_xy( **-** yaw) which I believe to be incorrect.

I have flight-tested and proved this issue by changing my precision landing sensor from BODY_FRD (working) to LOCAL_FRD. Changing to this MAV_FRAME within the LANDING_TARGET message causes divergent behaviour any time the Copter is not aligned with North. If I remove the negative sign from the line below, I get comparable behaviour with BODY_FRD which is expected, as these are both body-yaw aligned frames.

Line in question:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_PrecLand/AC_PrecLand.cpp#L674

The functionality for LOCAL_FRD support was added in this PR: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/30446

I believe there also must be an issue in the Simulation environment somewhere as this issue was clearly not picked up during the pull request completion.

**Version**
V4.7.0-dev | any version past the above linked PR.

## Bug report

**Issue details**

In summary, in ArduPlane, if you have the parameter ALT_OFFSET set (to say climb 300 meters), when you go to command the aircraft to a waypoint, TECS will somehow double the ALT_OFFSET leading to risk of an altitude excursion. Was able to replicate in SITL. I don't know if this is due to misuse of ALT_OFFSET, or if it's a bug with how it's interpretted

The prerequisites installation script (`install-prereqs-ubuntu.sh`) does not currently recognize the Linux Mint codename **“zara”**, which corresponds to Linux Mint 22.2. When running the script on Mint “zara”, it fails during release detection with:

```
Unable to map zara to an Ubuntu release.
```

Because the script cannot translate the Mint codename to the correct Ubuntu base, installation halts prematurely.

## **Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a translation entry for Linux Mint **“zara” → Ubuntu “noble” (24.04)** within the existing Mint-to-Ubuntu mapping block:

```
linuxmint)
    case ${RELEASE_CODENAME} in
        wilma | xia | zara)
            RELEASE_CODENAME='noble'
            ;;
```

This ensures the script correctly detects the system and proceeds with the expected package installation.

## **Describe alternatives you've considered**

* Editing the script locally (works, but not ideal for other Mint users).
* Allowing users to manually override the Ubuntu codename (would require additional script logic).
* Failing early with a more descriptive message (does not solve the underlying mapping problem).

Adding the proper Mint → Ubuntu mapping is consistent with existing behavior and previous merged PRs.

## **Platform**

[ x ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

## **Additional context**

Linux Mint “zara” (22.2) is based on Ubuntu 24.04 (“noble”), as documented on the Mint website:
[https://www.linuxmint.com/download_all.php](https://www.linuxmint.com/download_all.php)

I have tested the fix locally and confirmed that installation completes successfully after adding the mapping. A pull request with the change is ready to be submitted.

author: ES-Alexander
title: Sub: add support for `WATER_DEPTH` MAVLink reporting
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Many underwater vehicles have downward facing sonar sensors that are capable of measuring the distance to the water floor. Currently those are reported via [`DISTANCE_SENSOR`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#DISTANCE_SENSOR) and [`RANGEFINDER`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/ardupilotmega.html#RANGEFINDER) MAVLink messages, but both of those have limited export utility without contextual information that then needs to be cross-referenced with other messages (at risk of being incorrect from timing deltas).

Water temperature is also ambiguously reported in ArduSub via `SCALED_PRESSURE*` messages, which requires a receiver to know which and how many temperature sensors are connected to determine which one(s) refer to the water (e.g. outside the enclosure).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Rover [has support for](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/28875) a [`WATER_DEPTH`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/ardupilotmega.html#WATER_DEPTH) message for boats, which seems to include most of the relevant information to be directly usable in map creation / bathymetry situations, and for high level autopilot state reporting. It seems reasonable to expand that support to ArduSub firmware.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Do nothing, which keeps things difficult for control station software, and keeps them reliant on cycling/filtering through `DISTANCE_SENSOR` and `SCALED_PRESSURE` messages for water depth and temperature estimates.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[X] Submarine

**Additional context**
_Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here._

author: has1172
body:
Hello, @ES-Alexander, thanks for your guidance!

I see what you mean about the water barometer support. Since AP_Baro currently assumes air density for altitude calculations, using get_altitude() directly would return incorrect depth values underwater.

My plan:

First, I will focus on enabling the WATER_DEPTH message in Rover which is guarded by a check for either Rangefinder OR a valid pressure reading.

For the "Water Barometer" support, should I look into adding a water density parameter to AP_Baro, or should I handle the raw pressure-to-depth conversion locally in Rover for this PR?

author: ES-Alexander
body:
> enabling the WATER_DEPTH message in Rover which is guarded by a check for either Rangefinder OR a valid pressure reading.

This is too broad, and mixing cases. A boat should only support rangefinder-based WATER_DEPTH message generation. An underwater crawler (maybe detectable by a rover that is not a boat frame, but has water sensors enabled/available?) should likely only support water barometer based triggering.

> For the "Water Barometer" support, should I look into adding a water density parameter to AP_Baro, or should I handle the raw pressure-to-depth conversion locally in Rover for this PR?

Water depth driver support is already available for sensors like the MS5837 and KellerLD. That shouldn't be re-implemented in Rover, just conditionally enabled for boats and/or users who want it.

author: has1172
body:
Thank you @ES-Alexander for your feedback.

I understood regarding the separation of concerns.

1. Logic Split: I will refactor the logic to be strict:

Boats: Will only trigger WATER_DEPTH from Rangefinder data.

Crawlers (Non-Boats): Will only trigger from Water Barometer data (if water sensors are detected/enabled).

2. Implementation Details: Regarding the driver support—since drivers like MS5837 already exist, does AP_Baro::get_altitude() automatically return the correct water depth when these specific drivers are active (handling the density calculation internally)?

Or would you prefer I add a helper to AP_Baro (e.g., get_water_depth()) to expose this explicitly for the GCS?

author: Maarrk
title: Support RTL_ALTITUDE when using RTL_AUTOLAND
body:
## Feature request

We have a fixed-wing plane which has a complicated landing sequence, which forces us to always land in AUTO mode using `RTL_AUTOLAND` parameter. However, this means that `RTL_ALTITUDE` is ignored, since the vehicle always proceeds to the first waypoint after `MAV_CMD_DO_LAND_START`. I also need a way to support "return at current altitude", set when parameter is equal to -1.
The landing sequence contains `MAV_CMD_NAV_LOITER_TO_ALT` at 50m AGL which is required for final approach, but the plane glides to it in a straight descending line, potentially crashing into terrain.

*I would like the vehicle to complete the RTL route on altitude set in `RTL_ALTITUDE` parameter, also when landing in AUTO mode, and only descend when close to landing sequence.*

**Workaround**
By adding a `MAV_CMD_NAV_WAYPOINT` after `MAV_CMD_DO_LAND_START` and before `MAV_CMD_NAV_LOITER_TO_ALT`, I can adjust the return altitude on this mission item, and have the plane climb to it immediately by setting bit 14 of `FLIGHT_OPTIONS`. I am including the Lua function below.

The problem is, that **this script needs to reliably detect when RTL mode is triggered** to update the waypoint. When using `RTL_AUTOLAND` the vehicle switches to AUTO immediately, and I might miss it between the calls of the script. When changing the mode from GCS, I can listen to `MAV_CMD_DO_SET_MODE`, but can't detect RTL triggered by another script or RC transmitter. Finally, I can't simply look at the index of current waypoint, because I don't want to climb to RTL altitude when mission proceeds to landing sequence as planned.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[x ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
I'd be happy to contribute either a reliable way to detect RTL in Lua when using Automatic landing or some more involved behaviour for RTL, as preferred by the dev team.

I searched the issues for `RTL_AUTOLAND` and `RTL_ALTITUDE` but didn't find anything with both for my use case. There's a thread [Altitude behaviour on RTL using DO_LAND_START with RTL_AUTOLAND=2](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/altitude-behaviour-on-rtl-using-do-land-start-with-rtl-autoland-2/83922) which confirms that adding a waypoint is the way to do it.

```lua
-- Update first waypoint of landing sequence to recreate RTL_ALTITUDE behavior in AUTO
-- 
-- This must be called every time the vehicle enters RTL. Because the altitude target is specified
-- as a regular waypoint with large acceptance radius, the vehicle might not reach it if it's already close.
-- Note that if RTL is switched into AUTO and vehicle continues the mission it will fly to RTL altitude,
-- this can be reset to original value by reuploading the mission plan from GCS.
local function update_rtl_altitude()
    local doland_idx = find_do_land_start_index()
    if not doland_idx then
        return
    end

    local rtl_idx = doland_idx + 1
    local rtl_item = mission:get_item(rtl_idx)
    if (not rtl_item) or rtl_item:command() ~= MAV_CMD_NAV_WAYPOINT then
        return
    end

    local rtl_altitude = RTL_ALTITUDE:get()
    if not rtl_altitude then
        return
    end

    if rtl_altitude == -1 then
        local current_rel_alt = -ahrs:get_relative_position_D_home()
        rtl_item:z(current_rel_alt)
    else
        rtl_item:z(rtl_altitude)
    end

    -- Never write altitude smaller than 50 m
    if rtl_item:z() < 50 then
        rtl_item:z(50)
    end
    -- Ensure the altitude is relative to home like the parameter
    rtl_item:frame(MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT)

    mission:set_item(rtl_idx, rtl_item)
    gcs:send_text(MAV_SEVERITY.NOTICE, string.format("Doing RTL at %.0f m (REL)", rtl_item:z()))

    -- If already flying there, update the navigation target after mission was modified
    if mission:get_current_nav_index() == rtl_idx then
        mission:set_current_cmd(rtl_idx)
    end
end
```

*Contribution on behalf of @FlyfocusUAV*

author: LupusTheCanine
body:
You can use waypint with Lat=lon=0 to immediately set altitude to RTL_ALT value after entering RTL.
followed by waypoint with RTL_ALT at target coordinates.
Unfortunately acceptance radius seems to be limited to 256m so it can't really be used to skip these waypoints when close to home.
If your mission is offset you could use DO_LAND_START placed further out toward the mission direction and one over the landing area to select when those waypoints will happen.

Another option is to use RTL_AUTOLAND=1 as the plane will follow RTL_ALTITUDE when returning to home. Rally points are unfortunately limited to returning at rally waypoint altitude :-(

author: Maarrk
body:
It turns out that we're doing a lot of A to B flights, where we can't land where we release the plane, so RTL_AUTOLAND=1 is not an option for us.

For now, I gave up on detecting RTL and went with opposite approach. The plane always uses RTL_ALTITUDE when approaching landing, even during normal AUTO mission without using RTL at all.

---

A dream would be to have a new value for RTL_AUTOLAND, so the complete table is like this *additions in italic*:

Value | Meaning
-- | --
0 | Disable
1 | Fly HOME *at RTL_ALTITUDE* then land via DO_LAND_START mission item
2 | Go directly to landing sequence via DO_LAND_START mission item
3 | OnlyForGoAround
4 | Go directly to landing sequence via DO_RETURN_PATH_START mission item
*5* | *Fly to closest DO_LAND_START mission item at RTL_ALTITUDE and continue the landing sequence*

The value in 5 probably needs NAV_LOITER_TO_ALTITUDE so the glide path doesn't get affected when coming from different altitudes, but that can be done in stock QGC already. Since it's just mixing functionality from two already present behaviours, I don't expect it to be too complex to implement. We'll do our testing and report here or in a new PR if it's viable.

author: rmackay9
title: Copter: Ch6 tuning of WP Speed overshoots during the beginning of the first leg
body:
Copter supports transmitter based tuning ([see wiki here](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-transmitter-tuning.html)) including the ability to adjust the speed during auto missions.  Unfortunately it seems this doesn't take effect immediately when auto starts so the vehicle will overspeed in the first segment of the mission.

The issue can be reproduced in SITL with AP-4.7.0-dev (or higher) by doing the following:

1. param set RC6_OPTION 219 (Transmitter Tuning)
2. param set TUNE 10 (WP Speed)
3. param set TUNE_MIN 100 (1m/s)
4. param set TUNE_MAX 1000 (10m/s)
5. param set AUTO_OPTIONS 3 (allow arming and takeoff in Auto mode)
6. create an auto mission with long segments (e.g. a big square)
7. auto
8. arm throttle
9. rc 6 1000

The vehicle should fly at 1m/s but instead it will fly at up to 6m/s for the first segment before slowing to 1m/s

This issue was found as part of the investigation of [this user report](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/copter-4-6-3-released/140596/29).

author: IamPete1
body:
Some of these seem like trivial changes, is the goal just to find a small change in name just to make it harder for users to copy values across? If we already has a good name then in some cases this makes it worse, for example `RTL_SPEED` to `RTL_SPD`.

From a plane point of view we need to keep in mind the `Q_` prefix. For example currently `WPNAV` is to `Q_WP` on plane. Its either the same length or shorted. If we change to `WP` for copter it does mean that the plane and copter parameters are closer in name, which I think is a improvement. However, we will have to keep in mind that there still needs to be room for the extra `Q_`. We already hit this issue for the pilot yaw stuff, on plane we had to do `Q_PLT_Y_RATE_TC` where as copter its `PILOT_Y_RATE_TC` because `Q_PILOT_Y_RATE_TC` is too long.

So from a plane point of view I would be happy with shorter prefixes so long as we keep the full name on copter 14 chars or less so plane can add the two extra.

However, in the `WPNAV` -> `WP` example this means there will be no name change on plane, because its already `Q_WP`, so I think that means that it doesn't meet to goal of changing the name to prevent users from blindly copying?

> ANGLE_MAX
> -> PILOT_ANGLE_MAX

From a pure code structure point of view it would save some messing about to move the param down into the attitude controller. But then we have to use the `ATC` prefix for example: `ATC_PLT_ANG_MAX`

> (Future PR)
> ATC_CORR_ACCEL_P
> ATC_CORR_ACCEL_R
> ATC_CORR_ACCEL_Y

I know this won't be in the first PR but my preference where would be to have a overall maximum rather than split it like this. Not so important for rate accels but we should follow the same pattern else where. I would like to see absolute parameters for max speed, there are often export control requirements on capabilities speed, payload, endurance ect, max speed params would allow a manufacture to configure them as read only as a means of compliance. We would then have a arming check if the target params are set too close to the limits.

author: lthall
body:
> Some of these seem like trivial changes, is the goal just to find a small change in name just to make it harder for users to copy values across? If we already has a good name then in some cases this makes it worse, for example RTL_SPEED to RTL_SPD.

Yep, I completly agree. The problem space is:
-  is we need to change from cm to m,
- we can't use the same name to prevent loading old parameters in different units,
- we can't use the same memory location,
- we can't use more than 16 characters,
- we need to accommodate quad-plane,
- we need to do parameter conversion for seamless upgrade,
- we need names that make sense and self consistent if possible.

So we can change the prefix for all the parameters:
- ATC
- PILOT
- WPNAV
- PSC

We can change the naming, SPEED -> SPD

We can add suffex if we have space _M or _DEG ect.

> However, in the WPNAV -> WP example this means there will be no name change on plane, because its already Q_WP, so I think that means that it doesn't meet to goal of changing the name to prevent users from blindly copying?

I didn't consider that. That really sucks.

> ANGLE_MAX -> PILOT_ANGLE_MAX
> From a pure code structure point of view it would save some messing about to move the param down into the attitude controller. But then we have to use the ATC prefix for example: ATC_PLT_ANG_MAX

It could be ATC_ANGLE_MAX or similar. This is basically the manual mode angle max that we also use as the default angle max for the deeper modes if they are not set. To be clear on the motivation for that dependency isn't because ANGLE_MAX is more important or higher in the hierarchy, it is because it is set first during tuning and accommodate users who want to minimise setup time and complexity.

> I know this won't be in the first PR but my preference where would be to have a overall maximum rather than split it like this. Not so important for rate accels but we should follow the same pattern else where. I would like to see absolute parameters for max speed, there are often export control requirements on capabilities speed, payload, endurance ect, max speed params would allow a manufacture to configure them as read only as a means of compliance. We would then have a arming check if the target params are set too close to the limits.

This is an interesting idea and may also work well for a set of PSC parameters that act as maximum's for Loiter, Auto and Guided. It would also make sense the for ATC_ANGLE_MAX but then it could only be used as the default PILOT_ANGLE_MAX because it must always be bigger than PSC_ANGLE_MAX.

In any case it would be great to come up with a consistent set of rules we can apply and follow so we can move forward with a clean set of parameters. That may not be possible though.

author: julianoes
title: ArduPilot doesn't start on some boards with PX4 bootloader
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

ArduPilot doesn't start (immediately crashes) on STM32H7 boards where a PX4 bootloader is used. You can see the bootloader appear on USB and then disappear after a few seconds, and nothing happens after that.

Also see proposed (likely wrong) fix and discussion in https://github.com/ArduPilot/ChibiOS/pull/98.

FYI: @tpwrules, @andyp1per, @bugobliterator 

**To reproduce:**

1. Backup AP parameters in case you don't want to lose them!
2. Flash PX4 (e.g use QGroundControl and flash PX4 firmware. (It says stable 1.16 but in fact installs 1.17alpha1, which works to install the bootloader anyway)
3. In QGC, go to Analyze Tools -> MAVLink Console and run `bl_update /etc/extras/cubepilot_cubeorange_bootloader.bin` for CubeOrange or `bl_update /etc/extras/cubepilot_cubeorangeplus_bootloader.bin` for CubeOrange+.
(Alternatively, you can set param `SYS_BL_UPDATE` to `1` (Enabled) and reboot the board, however, this only works with 1.17/main but not 1.16 or 1.15 where it is broken.)
4. Flash ArduPilot

**Version**
ArduCopter 4.6.3 (and previous)

**Platform**
[ x] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
N/A

**Hardware type**
Likely all STM32H7, e.g. CubeOrange, CubeOrange+ 

**Logs**
N/A

author: tpwrules
body:
Thanks for the clear reproduction.

I discussed some of this with @tridge, and your problem would probably be fixed if you added `env USE_ALT_RAM_MAP 1` to the hwdef.dat file for the board and recompiled. That swaps around our memory map to not put the stack in RAM which the PX4 bootloader does not turn on, and is a thing we enable for H7 boards that come from the factory with the PX4 bootloader so that they work. The downside is that it fragments our memory map and results in running in (slightly) slower RAM, so it's not turned on for all boards. I will test later and confirm.

I think it's strange of us to rely on memory which is not turned on out of reset, I do think we should fix that. Now having diagnosed the root cause [here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ChibiOS/pull/98#issuecomment-3537435645), we should be able to turn the RAM on in the early startup code and get rid of the alternate map so all H7 boards work consistently.

I considered putting the stack in DTCM which is turned on out of reset, but the PX4 bootloader turns it off so we end up in the same situation. This is an unfortunate quirk of the PX4 bootloader but one we will have to accommodate.

author: tpwrules
body:
I checked with my Cube Orange and `env USE_ALT_RAM_MAP 1` is indeed the solution, it boots and seems to work fine with the PX4 bootloader.

However, that causes the SD card to fail to mount the first time and the board makes an unhappy startup noise. This is true even with the AP bootloader. I don't know if `fmuv6*` hardware behaves like this, I don't have any to test.

I also did have to wipe the params by setting `FORMAT_VERSION` to 0 to get all the sensors to come up but presumably AP is just misinterpreting however PX4 uses the FRAM.

author: julianoes
body: @bugobliterator this is still unsolved by the way. If there won't be a good fix, then we should at least note the problem and workaround in the ArduPilot and/or CubePilot docs. What do you think?

author: peterbarker
title: AP_Mount_Scripting location_is_valid method broken
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/23837 removed setting of `target_loc_valid` to anything other than true from the AP_Mount_Scripting backend.

The Lua binding is the only thing that makes use of this state.

We should also probably not have target_loc_valid at all - the location can be set to all-zeroes to flag it as invalid (dependent variables that don't exist can't get stale).  The same is true of `_roi_target_set` and `_target_sysid_location_set` (which we should probably use in place of target_loc_valid; i.e. switch on the current mount mode and return based on the presumably-set-correctly variables.

**Version**

[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

all

author: rbeall
title: No Parameter Length Validation at build
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

When you define a parameter with a name (including the full prefix chain) that's longer than 16 characters, everything compiles fine and the firmware uploads without any warnings. But then the autopilot just crashes silently during startup when it tries to initialize the parameters. There's no error message, no indication of what went wrong - it just fails back to boot loader.

The AP_MAX_NAME_SIZE limit of 16 chars makes sense, but the build system should catch this before you even get to the upload stage.

**Version**

Master branch (current as of 13NOV25)

**Platform**

[X] All

**Airframe type**

Affects all airframe types - this is a build/parameter system issue

**Hardware type**

Tested on various STM32 builds (ie Cube Orange, custom Periph Hardware etc)

**Logs**

No useful logs which was a part of the difficulty in finding this bug - Could pull GDB etc, but the issue is pretty clearly that the user defined Parameter name out of bounds is triggering watchdog loop back to boot loader.

author: RBirdie001
title: After upgrading to arduplane 4.6.x GPS bitrate 115k can't be enforced by option.
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

In Arduplane 4.6.x stopped working option GPS_DRV_OPTION=4 (bitmask xxxxx1xx) to enforce GPS bitrate 115200.
This can be because parameter GPS_TYPE was removed in 4.6.3
In versions 4.5 and lower it was necessary to set GPS_TYPE=2 (ublox) to make GPS_DRV_OPTION=4 work (even it's not logical, it didn't work with autodetection, only with fixed GPS type.)
I'm using a GPS beacon "sniffing" on the GPS data which can't  work with bitrate higher than 115k.

Long time ago discussed here: https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/is-it-possible-to-limit-maximal-negotiated-gps-serial-bitrate-tbeacon-stopped-working-after-upgrading-to-plane-4-2/88011
Then I found that GPS_TYPE=2 is needed so I set it like this and it worked ... until 4.6.

**Version**
Arduplane 4.6.3 bdshot

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[ X] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

body:
I found the problem was my misunderstanding that GPS_TYPE was newly replaced with GPS1_TYPE and this is why GPS_DRV_OPTION=4 didn't work.
After setting GPS1_TYPE=2 the option GPS_DRV_OPTION=4 works as previously.
Anyway this is an undocumented dependency so it would be great to be either corrected or documented but it's not a new bug.
Sorry for the confusion!

author: rbeall
title: DroneCAN Deadlock in dronecan_0 Thread on CubeRed Hardware
body: ## Bug report **Setup** [1] Mavproxy connecting to Cube Red via TCP connection and forwarding via out=udp:127.0.0.1:14550 onto my local machine [2] DroneCan GUI Tool connected via MavCAN connection [3] Cube Red configured as TCP server on LWIP stack **Issue details** Critical deadlock detected in the dronecan_0 thread (error code 83, 0x20000010) causing internal errors (0x8000) on CubeRed hardware. The deadlock appears to be related to a potential lock ordering issue in the DroneCAN pipeline. Issue is repeatable and occurs when using DroneCAN GUI Tool connected via MavCAN with MAVProxy forwarding TCP connections from a Cube Red configured as TCP server on LWIP stack. **Version** master **Platform** Discovered on Rover/Boat, but likely on All [?] All [ ] AntennaTracker [ ] Copter [ ] Plane [X] Rover [ ] Submarine **Airframe type** Boat **Hardware type** CubeRed **Logs** AP: CRITICAL Deadlock 83 dronecan_0 0x20000010 AP: Internal Errors 0x8000 Critical failure 0x8000 sysid=1 compid=1 AP: CRITICAL Deadlock 83 dronecan_0 0x20000010 Critical failure 0x8000 sysid=1 compid=1 AP: CRITICAL Deadlock 83 dronecan_0 0x20000010 Critical failure 0x8000 sysid=1 compid=1

author: rbeall
body:
The TCP-to-UDP forwarding topology likely triggered the deadlock because:
CAN_MCAST thread aggressively sends frames with IsMAVCAN flag
Callbacks invoked while holding callbacks.sem could call back into CAN methods
Multiple threads (dronecan_0, CAN_MCAST, main) created contention
Callback re-entrancy or cross-thread lock acquisition caused circular waits

**Likely Required Changes:**

[1] libraries/AP_HAL/CANIface.cpp - Prevent callback re-entrancy deadlock: Modify send() and receive() methods to snapshot callbacks before invocation, releasing the semaphore before calling them. This prevents callbacks from deadlocking when they call back into CAN methods. 

[2] libraries/AP_HAL_ChibiOS/CANFDIface.cpp - Fix lock ordering violation: Restructure the send() method to ensure parent class methods are called outside of critical sections, preventing AB-BA deadlock between hardware locks and callback semaphores.

author: Caped-Crussader
body:
# AP_DDS Servo Control Implementation Summary

## Feature Overview
Servo control functionality for ArduPilot's ROS 2 DDS integration, enabling remote servo command and telemetry access.

## Implementation Details

### Topics

**`/ap/servo_out` (Publisher)**
- Publishes current PWM values for all 32 servo output channels
- Update rate: 50ms (20 Hz) by default, configurable via `AP_DDS_DELAY_SERVO_OUT_TOPIC_MS`
- Message type: `ardupilot_msgs/msg/Servo`

**`/ap/servo_in` (Subscriber)**
- Receives servo PWM commands from ROS 2 nodes
- Accepts PWM values in 800–2200 microsecond range
- Zero value indicates "no command" for that channel
- Invalid or out-of-range commands are rejected with warning messages


### Configuration Options
All settings in `libraries/AP_DDS/AP_DDS_config.h`:

- **`AP_DDS_SERVO_OUT_PUB_ENABLED`**: Enable/disable servo output telemetry (default: 1)
- **`AP_DDS_SERVO_IN_SUB_ENABLED`**: Enable/disable servo input commands (default: 1)
- **`AP_DDS_DELAY_SERVO_OUT_TOPIC_MS`**: Servo output publish rate in milliseconds (default: 50ms)
- **`AP_DDS_SERVO_PROTECTED_CHANNELS`**: Number of initial channels to protect from external commands (default: 0)

### Safety Features
- **PWM Range Validation**: Only 800–2200 µs accepted; out-of-range values rejected
- **Zero-Value Semantics**: Zero = "no command" per channel, enabling partial multi-channel updates
- **Channel Protection**: Configurable via `AP_DDS_SERVO_PROTECTED_CHANNELS` to safeguard critical channels 
- **Integration with Existing Safety**: Respects `SERVOx_FUNCTION` assignments and ArduPilot failsafe logic

I have implemented the above features, Does this implementation meet the requirements? 
I have a pull request ready if you confirm.

author: rmackay9
title: FileSystem: allow crash_dump.bin files to be deleted via MAVFTP
body:
crash_dumps are quite rare but [according to our wiki](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-watchdog.html) once they occur, the user cannot arm the vehicle and the only way to delete the file is to re-upload the firmware.

I understand that we want the crash dump files but I think users should be able to simply delete the file via MAVFTP (hopefully after sending them to us).  Forcing them to update the firmware seems like an unnecessarily cumbersome step to put the users through

author: lthall
body: Having dealt with this I agree. This is painful for both manufacture and customer.

author: IamPete1
body: At the bottom of the wiki page it does mention `ARMING_CRSDP_IGN` which you can set to allow arming, but it is reset on every boot.

author: peterbarker
body:
[9:28 AM]Peter Barker: It's not possible to delete the file without a reflash of the firmware; the crash dump file is flashed into the board's actual flash after the ArduPilot firmware.  Due to the fact you erase a page a a time in flash you can't get rid of the crash dump without reflashing the firmware.

... and it's not just a matter of "we want the crash dump file".  The firmware has crashed hard - if it didn't take the vehicle out with it this time it might next time.

author: rmackay9
title: Rover: GPS glitch can cause EKF failsafe
body:
It seems that Rover will more easily enter an EKF failsafe compared with Copter.  This can be easily reproduced in SITL by doing the following:

1. start Rover using "Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py --map --console -f motorboat"
2. create a small auto mission (e.g. a square)
3. auto, arm throttle
4. param set SIM_GPS1_GLTCH_X 0.0001

When the lane switch occurs (which also happens with Copter) the vehicle will immediately switch to Hold mode

This was found during testing of this EKF reset PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/31357

This issue is present in 4.6 and master/latest

author: rmackay9
body:
There are two possible solutions to this:

1. set AHRS_OPTIONS = 3 to disable the fallback to DCM
2. change the EKF failsafe code in Rover so that it attempts to switch lanes before triggering.  This bit of code exists in the Copter EKF failsafe but not Rover

author: rmackay9
body: This is resolved in 4.7 by disabling DCM by default

author: rmackay9
title: Rover: Dijkastras should handle case where vehicle is started outside of fence
body:
Rover can end up outside the fence without the user doing anything particularly bad:

- create a polygon fence
- set LOIT_RADIUS to 10m
- place a waypoint with a 60s delay closer than 10m to the fence boundary

When the rover loiters at the waypoint it may stray outside the fence, RTL will trigger but the vehicle will not be able to return

To resolve this we should enhance Dijkstras so that it handles the case where the vehicle starts outside the fence

author: Yiaiyang
title: AP_Math：SIGFPE in AP_Math::is_equal<float,float> when setting extreme float at least twice via PARAM_SET (e.g., PILOT_THR_FILT = -FLT_MAX) from MAVLink
body: ## Bug report ### **Issue details** When a MAVLink `PARAM_SET` writes an extreme float (e.g., `±FLT_MAX`) into a float parameter such as `PILOT_THR_FILT`, ArduCopter SITL crashes with a **SIGFPE** inside `AP_Math::is_equal()`. The crash is reproducible when two consecutive `PARAM_SET` operations set the same parameter to `+FLT_MAX` and then to `-FLT_MAX`, making `handle_param_set()` compare `±FLT_MAX` in `is_equal()`. ### **Observed behavior** * Process aborts with `Floating point exception`. * Top of the stack shows `AP_Math::is_equal` called from `GCS_MAVLINK::handle_param_set`. * Local variables indicate `param_id="PILOT_THR_FILT"`, `param_type=MAV_PARAM_TYPE_REAL32 (9)`, with values close to `±3.40282347e+38`. ### **Source code references (permalinks)** - AP_Math `is_equal<>` (crash site): https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/d2a361afa744223354faa2cf989740458fe5b38c/libraries/AP_Math/AP_Math.cpp#L39 - GCS_MAVLink `handle_param_set` (PARAM_SET handling): https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/d2a361afa744223354faa2cf989740458fe5b38c/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Param.cpp#L315 - GCS_MAVLink `handle_common_param_message`: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/d2a361afa744223354faa2cf989740458fe5b38c/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Param.cpp#L531 - GCS_MAVLink `update_receive` (RX loop): https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/d2a361afa744223354faa2cf989740458fe5b38c/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp#L1966 - GCS_MAVLink `packetReceived`: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/d2a361afa744223354faa2cf989740458fe5b38c/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp#L1914 - GCS_MAVLink `handle_message` (dispatch): https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/d2a361afa744223354faa2cf989740458fe5b38c/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp#L4322 ### **Steps to reproduce** 1. Start ArduCopter SITL (e.g., Quad). 2. Send two `PARAM_SET` messages for `PILOT_THR_FILT`: * First set to `+3.4028235e+38` (`+FLT_MAX`), * Then set to `-3.4028235e+38` (`-FLT_MAX`). 3. SITL terminates with `SIGFPE`, stack showing: * `AP_Math::is_equal` (AP_Math.cpp), * called from `GCS_MAVLINK::handle_param_set` (GCS_Param.cpp), * `param_id="PILOT_THR_FILT"`, `param_type=REAL32`. ### **Severity / Impact** * **Severity:** Critical — deterministic crash of the flight-control process (SIGFPE) when handling `PARAM_SET`. * **User impact:** Immediate autopilot process termination; the ground station loses the MAVLink/telemetry link. * **Reproducibility:** 100% with the provided PoC (`+FLT_MAX` then `-FLT_MAX` to the same float parameter). ### **Minimal PoC (PyMAVLink)** ```python from pymavlink import mavutil, mavwp import time c = mavutil.mavlink_connection('udp:127.0.0.1:14550') c.wait_heartbeat() ts, tc = c.target_system, c.target_component REAL32 = getattr(mavutil.mavlink, 'MAV_PARAM_TYPE_REAL32', 9) name = b'PILOT_THR_FILT' c.mav.param_set_send(ts, tc, name, 3.4028235e+38, REAL32) # +FLT_MAX time.sleep(0.5) c.mav.param_set_send(ts, tc, name, -3.4028235e+38, REAL32) # -FLT_MAX ``` ### **Root cause (analysis)** * `GCS_MAVLINK::handle_param_set()` compares “new vs. old” values via `AP_Math::is_equal<>()`. * When the pair is `±FLT_MAX`, `is_equal()` performs difference/scaling that triggers a floating-point exception under SITL’s FPE trapping. * The issue is not specific to `PILOT_THR_FILT`: any `AP_PARAM_FLOAT` written with extreme values (including `NaN/Inf`) could travel the same path. ### **Repro stability** * Reproduces 100% in ArduCopter SITL with steps above. * First write to `+FLT_MAX` may succeed; second write to `-FLT_MAX` triggers the comparison of `±FLT_MAX` and consistently crashes. ### **Version** * ArduCopter SITL, master. ### **Platform** [ ] All [X] Copter [ ] Plane [ ] Rover [ ] Submarine [ ] AntennaTracker ### **Airframe type** Quad (SITL default) ### **Hardware type** SITL (software-in-the-loop) ### **Logs** Please see the attached/referenced files from the failing run (SITL): * exception19151.txt — includes the SIGFPE notice and backtrace showing AP_Math::is_equal(v_1=-3.40282347e+38, v_2=3.40282347e+38) called from GCS_MAVLINK::handle_param_set(...) with param_id="PILOT_THR_FILT". * bt-19151.txt — gdb backtrace of the crash. * dumpstack.sh_arducopter.19151.out in error_out.zip— stack-dump script output. * dumpcore.sh_arducopter.19151.out in error_out.zip— core-dump script output (“Saved corefile …”). * ap-19382-19151.core in error_out.zip— core file (if maintainers want to reproduce locally). * impact.png — the screenshot showing the impact when the ground station loses the MAVLink/telemetry link. * Attached: [bt-19151.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23190926/bt-19151.txt) [exception19151.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23190925/exception19151.txt) [error_out.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23191034/error_out.zip)

author: peterbarker
Yiaiyang
body: My initial aim was to explore whether differences between the commonly used range domains for physical parameters of drones in the SITL and the range domain information of data types defined in its static source code would impact drone program execution. During fuzz testing, I discovered this case caused the ArduCopter program to crash immediately. I wonder if boundary protection is necessary for this issue?

author: peterbarker
body:
> My initial aim was to explore whether differences between the commonly used range domains for physical parameters of drones in the SITL and the range domain information of data types defined in its static source code would impact drone program execution. During fuzz testing, I discovered this case caused the ArduCopter program to crash immediately. I wonder if boundary protection is necessary for this issue?

We can't afford the flash space on real vehicles.  We allow SITL to crash so people developing software to drive the vehicles remotely can pick up problems before they start commanding real vehicles with bad software.

author: Yiaiyang
body:
@peterbarker Thanks — I agree that crashing in SITL can be useful to expose undefined math.
Here the crash sits on the public MAVLink PARAM_SET path, not deep inside a control loop. With two legal floats (±FLT_MAX) the process aborts when handle_param_set() compares them via AP_Math::is_equal(). That means a GCS can trigger a deterministic process exit just by setting an extreme value and then its negation. For interface robustness we should reject/guard and report, not exit.

author: peterbarker
body:
> [@peterbarker](https://github.com/peterbarker) Thanks — I agree that crashing in SITL can be useful to expose undefined math. Here the crash sits on the public MAVLink PARAM_SET path, not deep inside a control loop. With two legal floats (±FLT_MAX) the process aborts when handle_param_set() compares them via AP_Math::is_equal(). That means a GCS can trigger a deterministic process exit just by setting an extreme value and then its negation. For interface robustness we should reject/guard and report, not exit.

The remedy here is "don't send in FLT_MAX or FLT_MIN".

We are not spending the flash on validating these inputs - we are working in a resource-constrained environment, we don't have the luxury of doing all the sanity checks we would like to do.

If you can find an attack on ArduPilot which works if you do not using the signing key while we are enforcing signing we really do care, however.  If you want to help find bugs, look there.

tl;dr - If you are allowed to send traffic to the autopilot - don't send in garbage.

author: tizianofiorenzani
title: DDS: Bad commanded velocity results in fly away
body:
It appears that a bad value (inf or NaN) sent through the `/ap/cmd_vel` topic causes the vehicle to just fly away. I suggest to screen the message before calling the external control.

Like:
```
    if (isnan(cmd_vel.twist.linear.x) || isnan(cmd_vel.twist.linear.y) || isnan(cmd_vel.twist.linear.z) || isnan(cmd_vel.twist.angular.z)
       || isinf(cmd_vel.twist.linear.x) || isinf(cmd_vel.twist.linear.y) || isinf(cmd_vel.twist.linear.z) || isinf(cmd_vel.twist.angular.z))
    {
        return false;
    }
```

body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

From an ArduPilot partner:

When we do a software reboot of ardupilot, only 1 GPS is configured.  A hardware reboot of the system is required to get both GPS's back

author: rmackay9
title: Rover/AP_Arming: silent arming failure if mission contains terrain alt
body:
If an mission containing terrain altitudes is added, Rover will fail to arm but annoyingly will not display the failure.  This leaves the users wondering why they cannot arm

The issues appears to be [here in AP_Arming](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Arming/AP_Arming.cpp#L1215) where it has an incorrect comment that the error should have already been reported by the system checks.

author: rmackay9
body: this is resolved with the above linked PR, txs!

author: rmackay9
title: Copter: invalid RC input may be consumed if FS_THR_ENABLE>0 and vehicle force armed
body: As mentioned in the title Copter-4.7 can consume invalid RC inputs if the RC failsafe (aka Throttle failsafe) is disabled and the vehicle is force armed. This can lead to various issues including: - the vehicle may rotate in yaw during Auto mode missions - the vehicle may move horizontally in RTL and Land modes (due to repositioning) The issue can be reproduced in SITL by doing the following: - param set SIM_RC_FAIL 1 - param set FS_THR_ENABLE 0 - param set AUTO_OPTIONS 3 (to make it easy to takeoff in Auto mode) - create a simple mission consisting of just a takeoff and RTL command - reboot the autopilot - auto - arm throttle This issue was discovered during the recent Japan Innovation Challenge and it was quite alarming. We resolved it by enabling the joystick/RC This issue does **not** exist in 4.6 (and earlier). I don't want to point fingers but I think this PR caused the issue https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/25822

author: slovak194
body:
Having the same issue.

>> We resolved it by enabling the joystick/RC

The proposed workaround works only for one vehicle connected. It does not help if multiple vehicles are controlled. So only the active vehicle is being fixed by connecting the controller.

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @slovak194,

Txs for the report.  we have a fix being reviewed here https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/31351

So you're flying 4.7?  This issue only affects 4.7.0-dev (aka "latest") and not 4.6.x (stable).  I just want to be sure that we're both seeing the same issue.

author: slovak194
body: > Hi [@slovak194](https://github.com/slovak194), > > Txs for the report. we have a fix being reviewed here [#31351](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/31351) > > So you're flying 4.7? This issue only affects 4.7.0-dev (aka "latest") and not 4.6.x (stable). I just want to be sure that we're both seeing the same issue. Hi, @rmackay9, I'm pretty sure it is the same issue, and I'm eager to test the possible fix in a multi-vehicle setup. Particularly in cases when RC is not present at all, or present but available to one vehicle at a time. I'm not on the recent master, but branched out after 4.6 was released. I first noticed it when I had to set FS_THR_ENABLE = 0. This led to a random spinning of drones in guided and follow modes. I did not want to change it back and instead went through all the "Ignore pilot yaw" options in guided, auto, RTL, and srtl modes. It almost helped, but not for the last stage of the landing, where drones were still spinning. I had to modify the code in rtl mode to prevent this by returning "false" from the use_pilot_yaw() method. This fixed the yaw spin, but the lateral move in landing/repositioning is still present. I've posted this on Discord, but I'd better do it here next time.

author: rmackay9
body:
@slovak194,

OK, what you're describing is exactly this issue.  The fix is in PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/31351 so if you're comfortable compiling yourself then it's just a one line change.  Alternatively tell me which autopilot you're using and I'll create a firmware tomorrow which you can test.

author: slovak194
body:
Hi, @rmackay9 ! I've just performed a limited flight test.

1. 3 drones flying, no RC connected.
2. Only fbc7bd381c9eb72b72e5376672546b955209699d was  cherry picked.
3. GUIDED, RTL, SRTL, and AUTO modes were still configured with "ignore pilot yaw" option.
4. The issue that I've observed with the final descent in RTL disappeared. Before I observed severe lateral deviations.

Further down, I'll gradually remove "ignore pilot yaw" from the aforementioned modes and test as well. But that will be next week.

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @slovak194,

Great!  thanks for the testing and feedback. I hope we can get the fix merged to master next Tuesday but we shall see

author: simopanzer89
title: Copter: height setpoint drift during LOITER_TURNS in AUTO mode
body: ## Bug report **Issue details** Hello, we incurred into an issue when flying in AUTO mode with our multicopter. We loaded a mission in which we require the drone to perform a series of circles using the LOITER_TURNS command. We set [Frame: Relative] in the mission plan items. We would expect the drone to follow a circular trajectory in the plane, while maintaining constant height. Instead, the height setpoint is varying during the circles, and looks like it is slowly drifting away as time goes on. The estimated height follows the setpoint. The behaviour looks non-deterministic and the issue occurs consistently every time the experiment is repeated. We tried to replicate the behaviour by simulating the same mission in SITL, but were not able to obtain the same behaviour, which is apparently occurring only in real flight experiments. Any clues? **Steps to replicate the issue** * Load the mission plan mission_loiter_turns.waypoints * Set AUTO mode * Run the mission. **Version** Copter-4.4.1 **Platform** [ ] All [ ] AntennaTracker [X] Copter [ ] Plane [ ] Rover [ ] Submarine **Airframe type** Octo quad x - X8 multirotor **Hardware type** Cube Orange **Other relevant information** * Terrain tracking: disabled * GPS setup: 2x F9P ublox onboard GPS modules + GPS RTK base station: Emlid Reach RS2+ **Mission file** mission_loiter_turns.waypoints https://drive.google.com/open?id=12OpJn7Jca3S8FCIT4m8af4emJKwh2AKp&usp=drive_fs **Logs** 2025-10-01 12-55-50.bin https://drive.google.com/open?id=1khzxwX_3krzGEs9Eaq3qC9h4RB2xjMG7&usp=drive_fs **Plots from log file**

author: lthall
body:
This appears to be associated with a GPS_PRIMARY_CHANGED event. It is changing the set point so it must be coming in via a EKF reset or something similar.

In circle mode we do control altitude by setting a zero climb rate during the circle so an EKF reset will result in persistent change in altitude because we reset the target with the estimated altitude to prevent a step change going through the controller.

Looking at the EKF altitude it does look like this is caused by the EKF reset.

author: simopanzer89
body: @lthall thanks for your feedback. I confirm we had several GPS_PRIMARY_CHANGED events, and that the discontinuities in the height setpoint are correlated with EKF resets (innovation dropping to zero) as visible from the plot below. Notice that the circles start from approx 500 s, and despite there are innovation resets even before that time instant, the height setpoint would not change; the drift occurs only during the circles. Though, the flag "GPS in use" is switching several times, but it does not look correlated with the discontinuities in height setpoint.

author: lthall
body: Yes, this is because circle commands zero climb rate during the circle, not a specific height. This means that when we have an EKF reset that moves our estimated altitude up or down we move both the set point and the estimate together. This means that the controller doesn't see the step and you don't get a jump in the aircraft thrust.

author: rmackay9
body:
For the Circle flight mode (where arguably the pilot is in control) it makes sense that we just ignore the change in altitude estimate but for auto missions where the user has specified an altitude it makes sense for the vehicle to maintain that.  Just like we don't shift the horizontal position (if there's an EKF reset) in Auto mode but we do in Loiter.

BTW I've added this to the 4.6 issues list although I suspect we won't resolve this until 4.7

author: simopanzer89
body: Thanks for your feedback and support. We realized that the EKF reset issue might be due to some issue in the GPS configuration. Indeed we observed that the two onboard GPS modules had been configured to run at 10 Hz, but looking at the logs they apparently were not able to keep a steady 10 Hz rate, rather it would oscillate between 5 and 10 Hz. We then relaxed the configuration of both the GPS modules to run at 5 Hz and now the rate looks much more stable and matches the desired one. We repeated the test, and this time we observed that (see the plot below): * there were no resets in the EKF innovation over more than 10 min of circles; * the height setpoint is now constant; * there are still a lot of GPS_PRIMARY_CHANGED events and the "GPS in use" flag keeps switching. In conclusion, we still have not found the root cause of the EKF switching, though we obtained the desired result (that is, keeping the height setpoint constant over time during the circles) and improved stability in operation of the GPS modules. We would be interested in testing the next stable release, if this is going to be fixed.

author: tridge
