author: rmackay9
title: Scripting/GCS_MAVLink: scripts may receive corrupted mavlink messages
body:
During preparations for this's years' Japan Innovation Challenge (JIC) we noticed that the [copter-slung-payload.lua](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Scripting/applets/copter-slung-payload.lua#L183) script (running on a CubeOrangePlus running AP-4.7.0-dev) could receive corrupted [GLOBAL_POSITION_INT](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#GLOBAL_POSITION_INT) messages with impossible lat, lon and alt values from a Here4 (running Copter-4.6).

The result was at best the script would fail with this error:

`Lua: /APM/scripts/copter-slung-payload.lua:185: bad argument #1 to 'alt' (out of range)`

.. but even worse, in some situations the values were within range but crazy leading to unexpected copter movements.

This issue only occurred when the telemetry connection was overloaded.  In this situations Mission Planner's mavlink connection would show the GLOBAL_POSITION_INT updates from the payload were slower than the configured 10hz rate which suggests to me that Mission Planner was rejecting the corrupt messages while the AP script was being fed the corrupted messages

author: IamPete1
body:
This is done explicitly here:

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/ae038a588651d3e55c0494bb2e28712bbdfcf5bc/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp#L1974-L1980

The goal was to allow unknown messages to be used in scripting. The intention was that the Lua MAVLink parser would check the CRC, but that has never been added.

author: IamPete1
body:
I looked at the blame, it was me. I actually did add support to checking the crc in lua. https://github.com/ArduPilot/pymavlink/pull/983

I think we just need to update the parser which is in tree to a freshly generated one.

Edit: in fact the parser is up to date, we just need to update the message definitions to provide the crc extra.

author: rmackay9
title: Scripting/GCS_MAVLink: set-message-interval doesn't appear to work for some Network ports
body:
In this year's Japan Innovation Challenge (JIC) our vehicle uses Ethernet to connect the autopilot, camera and companion computer ([setup as described here](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/companion-computer-blueos.html)).  With this setup the autopilot creates a mavlink connection using these params:

- NET_P2_TYPE = 2 (UDP Server)
- NET_P2_TYPE = 2 (MAVLink 2)
- NET_P2_IP0/1/2/3/Port: 0,0,0,0,14560

BlueOS running  on the RPI then connects to the autopilot as a UDP Client.  The GCS connects to BlueOS again as a UDP Client.

We've noticed that the [set-message-interval.lua example script](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Scripting/examples/message_interval.lua) does not seem to work no matter what value we set the ["serial_port"](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Scripting/examples/message_interval.lua#L32C7-L32C19) to.  The regular set-message-interval run from a GCS (e.g. Mission Planner) does work however.

I don't think the problem is within the script though, instead I think maybe there's an issue in either [GCS_MAVLink:: get_channel_from_port_number()](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp#L3248C9-L3248C60) or [AP_SerialManager::get_serial_by_id()](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_SerialManager/AP_SerialManager.cpp#L697C21-L697C67) function.

author: amilcarlucas
imperator-maximus
title: GPS_RTCM_DATA messages sent via DroneCAN MAVLink tunnel are not processed by GPS injection handler
body:
### **Issue Type:**
Bug

### **Affected Versions:**
- ArduPilot 4.6.2 (Rover)
- Likely affects all vehicle types (Copter, Plane, Rover, Sub)

### **Hardware:**
- Flight Controller: Orange Cube Plus
- GPS: Holybro H-RTK Unicore UM982
- Companion Computer: Raspberry Pi sending RTCM via DroneCAN

---

### **Description**

GPS_RTCM_DATA messages sent via DroneCAN MAVLink tunnel (`uavcan.tunnel.Targetted`) are not processed by ArduPilot's GPS injection handler, preventing RTK correction data from reaching GPS modules when sent from companion computers over CAN bus.

**Working scenarios:**
- Mission Planner → USB/Serial → ArduPilot → GPS ✅ RTK works
- also CAN connection between RaspberryPI and Orange Cube works (e.g. ESC commands)

**Broken scenario:**
- Raspberry Pi → DroneCAN tunnel → ArduPilot → GPS ❌ RTK does not work

---

### **Root Cause Analysis**

After extensive debugging with custom firmware builds, the issue was identified:

1. **DroneCAN tunnel receives data correctly** (`AP_DroneCAN_serial.cpp:136-140`)
   - `uavcan.tunnel.Targetted` messages are received
   - Data is written to `Port::readbuffer`

2. **Data is never read from the buffer**
   - DroneCAN Serial Ports are registered with `AP::serialmanager().register_port()` 
   - **BUT they are NOT registered as GCS MAVLink backends**

3. **No MAVLink message processing occurs**
   - `GCS::setup_uarts()` only creates MAVLink backends for ports found via `find_serial(SerialProtocol_MAVLink, i)`
   - DroneCAN Serial Ports are never added to the GCS channel list
   - Therefore `GCS_MAVLINK::update_receive()` never reads from these ports
   - GPS_RTCM_DATA messages never reach `AP::gps().handle_msg()`

**Code references:**

**Problem location 1:** `libraries/AP_DroneCAN/AP_DroneCAN_serial.cpp:47`
```cpp
AP::serialmanager().register_port(&p);  // Registered with SerialManager
// BUT NOT registered as GCS MAVLink backend!
```

**Problem location 2:** `libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp:2826-2835`
```cpp
void GCS::setup_uarts()
{
    for (uint8_t i = 1; i < MAVLINK_COMM_NUM_BUFFERS; i++) {
        AP_HAL::UARTDriver *uart = AP::serialmanager().find_serial(AP_SerialManager::SerialProtocol_MAVLink, i);
        if (uart == nullptr) {
            break;  // DroneCAN ports are never found here!
        }
        create_gcs_mavlink_backend(*uart);
    }
}
```

**Expected behavior:** DroneCAN Serial Ports configured with MAVLink protocol should be registered as GCS MAVLink backends to enable bidirectional MAVLink communication.

---

### **Steps to Reproduce**

1. **Hardware Setup:**
   - Connect Orange Cube Plus to Raspberry Pi via CAN bus
   - Connect RTK GPS (e.g., UM982) to flight controller

2. **Parameter Configuration:**
   ```
   CAN_D1_UC_OPTION = 1 (Enable DroneCAN)
   CAN_D1_UC_SER_EN = 1 (Enable DroneCAN Serial)
   CAN_D1_UC_S1_NOD = 125 (Raspberry Pi node ID)
   CAN_D1_UC_S1_IDX = 0 (Serial port index)
   
   GPS_INJECT_TO = 127 (Inject to all GPS instances)
   GPS_AUTO_CONFIG = 1
   ```

3. **Raspberry Pi Python Code:**
   - Implement NTRIP client
   - Package RTCM3 data into `GPS_RTCM_DATA` messages (following Mission Planner implementation)
   - Send via `uavcan.tunnel.Targetted` with `protocol = UAVCAN_TUNNEL_PROTOCOL_MAVLINK2`

4. **Observe:**
   - Mission Planner MAVLink Inspector shows NO `GPS_RTCM_DATA` messages
   - GPS remains at fix_type=3 (3D fix), never achieves RTK
   - Same RTCM data works perfectly when sent via Mission Planner over USB

---

### **Expected Behavior**

GPS_RTCM_DATA messages sent via DroneCAN tunnel should be processed identically to messages received via direct MAVLink connections (USB/Serial), enabling RTK correction injection from companion computers.

---

### **Actual Behavior**

GPS_RTCM_DATA messages sent via DroneCAN tunnel are silently ignored. Data reaches the DroneCAN serial port buffer but is never read or processed by MAVLink message handlers.

---

### **Proposed Solution**

**Option 1: Register DroneCAN Serial Ports as GCS backends**

Modify `AP_DroneCAN_Serial::init()` to register MAVLink-protocol ports with GCS:

```cpp
// In libraries/AP_DroneCAN/AP_DroneCAN_serial.cpp
void AP_DroneCAN_Serial::init(AP_DroneCAN *_dronecan)
{
    // ... existing code ...
    
    for (uint8_t i=0; i<ARRAY_SIZE(ports); i++) {
        auto &p = ports[i];
        p.state.idx = base_port + i;
        if (p.node > 0 && p.idx >= 0) {
            p.init();
            AP::serialmanager().register_port(&p);
            
            // NEW: Register MAVLink ports with GCS
            if (p.state.protocol == AP_SerialManager::SerialProtocol_MAVLink ||
                p.state.protocol == AP_SerialManager::SerialProtocol_MAVLink2) {
                gcs().create_gcs_mavlink_backend(p);
            }
            
            need_subscriber = true;
        }
    }
}
```

**Option 2: Add explicit DroneCAN port scanning in GCS::setup_uarts()**

Modify `GCS::setup_uarts()` to also check registered ports:

```cpp
// In libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp
void GCS::setup_uarts()
{
    // ... existing code for standard serial ports ...
    
    // NEW: Check registered ports (e.g., DroneCAN Serial)
    for (auto *p = AP::serialmanager().get_registered_ports(); p != nullptr; p = p->next) {
        if (p->state.protocol == AP_SerialManager::SerialProtocol_MAVLink ||
            p->state.protocol == AP_SerialManager::SerialProtocol_MAVLink2) {
            create_gcs_mavlink_backend(*p);
        }
    }
}
```

---

---

### **Additional Context**

- Forum discussion: https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/um982-moving-baseline-rtk-ntrip-connected-but-stuck-at-fix-type-3/138165
- This bug affects any use case requiring MAVLink communication via DroneCAN tunnel (not just GPS injection)
- The issue was identified after adding extensive debug logging to track data flow through the system
- Time spent debugging: Multiple weeks

---

### **Testing Evidence**

Custom firmware with debug output confirmed:
1. ✅ DroneCAN tunnel receives data: `DCAN_TUN: node=125 proto=1 len=X written=X`
2. ✅ Data written to readbuffer successfully
3. ❌ No `GPS: RX GPS_RTCM_DATA` messages (handler never called)
4. ❌ No `GPS: inject_data` messages (injection never occurs)

---

### **Impact**

**High Priority** - This prevents:
- RTK correction injection from companion computers via CAN
- Any bidirectional MAVLink communication via DroneCAN tunnel
- Modern distributed autopilot architectures using CAN-based companion computers

I tested the upgrade behavior on KakuteH7Mini-Nand:
1. Flash stable 4.6.2 copter, erase params and dataflash

author: Georacer
body:
@rmackay9 you mean we leave the old parameters in the new firmware, because MP always uses the new params XML regardless of the AP version connected?

Kind of makes sense:

title: Possiblity of AHRS not reporting the correct Accel index
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
It is possible for the EKF to be using gyro and accelerometer readings from different IMUs. This happens when the accel is marked unhealthy within the Inertial Sensor library while the gyro is still healthy. The EKF core would continue to use the gyro but switch over to the next healthy accel. 
 
The problem is that the AHRS assumes that EKF is using the same accel instance as gyro. This can cause very weird symptoms, like the landing detector never triggering (log linked below from a real vehicle where this actually happened), because the vehicle would end up using the bad accel. This is one of many problems that could happen due to this issue. 

I have added an autotest here that shows how to reproduce this problem and is obviously failing right now: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/31087

author: ES-Alexander
title: AP_Gripper: support HOLD command option
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Explicit gripper control is currently limited to active releasing and grabbing, which leaves out stopped/neutral operation. The EPM gripper driver seemingly has an option to automatically return to neutral some fixed time after a grab or release, but that is privately scoped and has no direct control action.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1. MAVLink [now supports a HOLD command for grippers](https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink/pull/2393), which I think should be used to trigger stopped / neutral functionality of the gripper.
2. With drivers that expose that functionality, it could also be integrated into AUX functions / joystick button function support, as the return point when a grab or release button stops being held.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could just not implement this, but it's a missing functionality that seems useful for certain gripper types and applications.

**Platform**
[x] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
The lack of this functionality is what has thus far stopped ArduSub from regularly using ArduPilot's gripper functionality (opting to instead use momentary servo commands via joystick buttons), so this would reduce ArduSub's reliance on joystick button functions, while also making gripper configuration more intuitive.

author: neo-0007
body:
Hello, I would like to take on this feature request.

I see that the necessary MAVLink change (GRIPPER_ACTION_STOP) has already been merged in [mavlink/mavlink PR #2342](https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink/pull/2342).

Looking at the code in `libraries/AP_Gripper/`, I found that a `STATE_NEUTRAL` already exists in the `gripper_state` enum but lacks command interface:
```cpp
    typedef enum {
        STATE_NEUTRAL,
        STATE_GRABBING,
        STATE_RELEASING,
        STATE_GRABBED,
        STATE_RELEASED,
    }  gripper_state;
```
Current Implementation Details:
- In Servo backend it is used once during initialization to set the servo's starting position. After that, it only moves between the grab and release positions.
- In EPM gripper there is a private `neutral()` method  . After a `grab()` or `release()` command, a timer starts, and the `update_gripper()` function automatically calls `neutral()` to de-energize the magnet
```cpp
// neutral - return the epm pwm output to the neutral position
void AP_Gripper_EPM::neutral()
{
    if (!should_use_uavcan()) {
        // move the servo to the off position
        SRV_Channels::set_output_pwm(SRV_Channel::k_gripper, config.neutral_pwm);
    }
}
```
The missing functionality is the ability to explicitly command the gripper to this neutral state via MAVLink.

Proposed Implementation Plan:

MAVLink Command Handling
- Update command processors in `GCS_Common.cpp` and vehicle-specific MAVLink handlers
- Add `GRIPPER_ACTION_STOP` recognition to existing `MAV_CMD_DO_GRIPPER` handling

AP_Gripper Core Changes
- Add public `set_neutral()` method to main gripper class
- Ensure state machine properly handles neutral transitions
- Update status reporting for neutral state

Driver Backend Updates
- Make EPM `neutral()` method accessible via base class
- Ensure servo gripper can return to neutral position during operation
- Verify all backends implement neutral behavior consistently

AUX Function Integration
- Extend RC_Channel options to include gripper neutral command
- Enable momentary button control where button release triggers neutral
- Update documentation for new RC function

Does this approach seem correct? If so, please feel free to assign this issue to me. I'm looking forward to contributing!

author: ES-Alexander
body:
Hi @neo-0007, thanks for the interest :-)

Your points seem to generally match what I found when looking into it, and your contribution would be appreciated.

> Add `GRIPPER_ACTION_STOP` recognition to existing `MAV_CMD_DO_GRIPPER` handling

You'll want to make sure this includes the handling in AP_Mission :-)

> - Ensure servo gripper can return to neutral position during operation

I don't remember what's currently done for PWM values, but it seems to make sense to me that the neutral point for a servo driver would be to return the gripper to the trim value of whichever output channel has its `SERVOn_FUNCTION` set to the Gripper function.

> - Enable momentary button control where button release triggers neutral

As a potential extension (which could happen in a separate PR to the initial support of this feature), ArduSub would likely benefit from adding gripper open and close joystick button functions, which return to neutral on release ([in `ArduSub/joystick.cpp`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/ArduSub/joystick.cpp#L85-L88)).

author: neo-0007
body:
[This](https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink/pull/2342) PR by @ES-Alexander  in mavlink/mavlink changed the existing message definitions of gripper commands and added a GRIPPER_ACTION_STOP command .

New command definitions in upstream MAVLink:
[mavlink/mavlink common.xml lines 594–606](https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink/blob/b401fe0238b9647f8ea18d58d9e968b79b347916/message_definitions/v1.0/common.xml#L594C1-L606C12)

```xml
    <!-- gripper action enum -->
    <enum name="GRIPPER_ACTIONS">
      <description>Gripper actions.</description>
      <entry value="0" name="GRIPPER_ACTION_OPEN">
        <description>Gripper commence open. Often used to release cargo.</description>
      </entry>
      <entry value="1" name="GRIPPER_ACTION_CLOSE">
        <description>Gripper commence close. Often used to grab onto cargo.</description>
      </entry>
      <entry value="2" name="GRIPPER_ACTION_STOP">
        <description>Gripper stop (maintain current grip position).</description>
      </entry>
    </enum>
```

Since ArduPilot maintains its own fork, should I:

- update the existing gripper commands in ArduPilot/mavlink to match the upstream MAVLink definitions, or
- keep the current definitions and just add GRIPPER_ACTION_STOP (along with the regenerated headers)?

Current ArduPilot MAVLink definitions:
[ArduPilot/mavlink common.xml lines 582–591](https://github.com/ArduPilot/mavlink/blob/4924617b8ddd9871506a01e16675a41464fdba49/message_definitions/v1.0/common.xml#L582C1-L591C12)
```xml
    <!-- gripper action enum -->
    <enum name="GRIPPER_ACTIONS">
      <description>Gripper actions.</description>
      <entry value="0" name="GRIPPER_ACTION_RELEASE">
        <description>Gripper release cargo.</description>
      </entry>
      <entry value="1" name="GRIPPER_ACTION_GRAB">
        <description>Gripper grab onto cargo.</description>
      </entry>
    </enum>
```

Also, I don’t have much experience working with submodules — from what I’ve read in the [Arduwiki](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/git-submodules.html), I need to : 
- Push the updated common.xml and generated headers to ArduPilot/mavlink.
- Update the MAVLink submodule pointer in ArduPilot/ardupilot to point to the new commit.

I just wanted to confirm that this is the correct approach before proceeding.

I had interpreted the requirement in a wrong way in the past and implemented some other thing
i have pushed it to a branch in my fork [here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/commit/8e54adde7287613990589bbfdd2255cc1fced8bd) (sorry for the single commit ) and this was done with the previous naming changes in mavlink which is now being reverted , if @ES-Alexander you are not working on this , can i give it a try again ?

@peterbarker  I also noticed that the mavlink submodule in Ardupilot is pointing towards a old commit , is it updated periodically or after a new release ? , I am a little confused with these.

author: ES-Alexander
body:
> if you are not working on this , can i give it a try again ?

You're more than welcome to do so - I was planning to ask if you were still interested in it once I confirmed the MAVLink PR had been merged in :-)

>  I also noticed that the mavlink submodule in Ardupilot is pointing towards a old commit , is it updated periodically or after a new release ? , I am a little confused with these.

I don't believe there is a standard process for this. From [the history](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/commits/master/modules/mavlink) it looks to normally just be updated to the latest state as part of pull requests that need to reference a recent change - I expect it should be fine to just update the mavlink submodule as part of your PR.

I'd personally be inclined to add [a regularly scheduled workflow that does it weekly](https://github.com/bluerobotics/BlueOS/pull/3174/changes) or something, but that is better handled in its own PR, and likely requires a dev-call discussion because it involves automatic changes of code.

author: bringert
title: AP_Mount_Gremsy sends AUTOPILOT_STATE_FOR_GIMBAL_DEVICE too often
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

The [Gremsy driver](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/f04add8b1b0ef6ff8051d2e58e6e10cd4652964d/libraries/AP_Mount/AP_Mount_Gremsy.cpp#L260) wants to send [AUTOPILOT_STATE_FOR_GIMBAL_DEVICE](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#AUTOPILOT_STATE_FOR_GIMBAL_DEVICE) at 50 Hz:

```
#define AP_MOUNT_GREMSY_ATTITUDE_INTERVAL_US    20000  // send ATTITUDE and AUTOPILOT_STATE_FOR_GIMBAL_DEVICE at 50hz
...
const MAV_RESULT res = _link->set_message_interval(MAVLINK_MSG_ID_AUTOPILOT_STATE_FOR_GIMBAL_DEVICE, AP_MOUNT_GREMSY_ATTITUDE_INTERVAL_US);
```

With the default `SCHED_LOOP_RATE` this causes the autopilot to spew `"Requested rate for message ID 286 too fast. Increase SCHED_LOOP_RATE"`.

This message comes from [set_message_interval](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/f04add8b1b0ef6ff8051d2e58e6e10cd4652964d/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp#L3221) which disallows message frequencies above 0.8 * SCHED_LOOP_RATE.

Setting SCHED_LOOP_RATE to 75 gets rid of the error.

It would be nice if the Gremsy driver worked out of the box with the default parameters, or at least if there was a way for the user to change the frequency for the AUTOPILOT_STATE_FOR_GIMBAL_DEVICE message.

body: ## Bug report **Issue details** I'm reposting my previous forum [post](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/ekf-in-flight-reset-and-bad-initialization-during-compass-less-operation/138886), since i didn't get any answers and I believe this may point to a software bug. Description of the problem: Today we experienced a strange event that caused the drone to tilt dangerously beyond 60º (even though ANGLE_MAX was set to 30º) while flying in Stabilize mode. title: SBUS failsafe not triggered when Receiver stuck in Packet Loss
body:
I have had a configuration with multiple Futaba receivers connected to splitters that did not trigger a failsafe because the SBUS flag bit remained stuck at 1 (loss of frames) rather then becoming 2 (loss of link).

I refer to this particular line of code: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_RCProtocol/AP_RCProtocol_SBUS.cpp#L142

I get that my configuration was quite unique, but I think that we could overcome this corner case by adding a simple counter that increases every time we have a bad frame and set `sbus_failsafe = true` when we pass a threshold.

```
if (++ctr_lost_frames > SBUS_FRAME_LOST_THR) {
    sbus_failsafe = true;
}
```

Looking forward to your comments.

author: ES-Alexander
title: Rover: add automatic motor reversal and enumeration detection
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Hardware and wiring can be messy, and it is possible for users to incorrectly wire up their motors, which then requires troubleshooting and subsequent fixing or software compensation. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
ArduSub supports a motor reversal detection mode which runs one motor at a time, and uses the vehicle's resulting motion to determine output configuration issues relative to the frame's expected motor motion contribution factors, and reports errors and/or sets the `SERVOn_REVERSED` parameters as relevant. As rover vehicles are constrained to a surface, it should be readily possible to achieve the same effect, and also detect and correct for issues in the motor ordering/enumeration (assuming the motors are at least connected to the configured _set_ of pins).

This would be useful where motor wiring is difficult to adjust, and also specifying which motor connections should be swapped (or are not working as expected) for users who would prefer to fix things at the hardware level.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The current approach is to investigate manually and set relevant parameters / correct wiring by hand, which _works_, it's just not very friendly, and could be made easier.

title: Add the New QWIKER TUNING option to Copter
body:
## Feature request

The QUIKTUNE Lua has been great for fine-tuning in Copter due to its speed.  We have used this as a starting point.  But it is limited to H7 and more powerful FCs with SD card support.  It is also not completely safe and can be dangerous when used with some setups. It also overtunes the drone, which is also bad.  The fact that QUIKTUNE uses LOITER flight mode and does not drift during tuning is a positive.

It would be great if we could create a new tuning option for Copter that has the speed and loiter capability of QUIKTUNE and the reliability of AUTOTUNE.  

Ideal timing would be under 10 mins.  So this can be done in a single flight.

author: amilcarlucas
body: Use Autotune, it works on F4 processors, it's very mature and safe and gives more deterministic and consistent results than quicktune.

author: FlyingRobotZA
body: Autotune does work. But the speed of QWIKTUNE is much better to get the drone flyable in less than a 2min flight. Plus it works in Loiter so there is zero drift while tuning.  Autotune can be used later to refine on each axis.

author: lthall
body:
QWIKTUNE does not stimulate the aircraft during the process and instead relies on noise or external disturbances to excite the oscillation. This means that a low noise aircraft being tuned on a calm day can result in a tune that dangerously oscillates. As such we do not consider this algorithm reliable enough to include in the C code base.

We are considering ways that we can produce a similar capability but this is an ongoing effort.

author: FlyingRobotZA
body: @lthall As discussed yesterday.  I agree, QWIK tune is not safe for all aircraft.  Maybe we could change this Feature request to be a better solution.  Combining the best of Autotune and speed of QUIKTUNE.  Ideally, the goal would be the best Tune possible in under a 10 minute flight.

author: SuperLei917
title: BUG:The operator function for quaternion division in the quaternion library seems to be incorrect
body: I am currently studying EKF3 and have discovered a function in the magnetometer fusion section controlMagYawReset() [https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/aabbe500aa4b682305b3062116edebc3fd0528c6/libraries/AP_NavEKF3/AP_NavEKF3_MagFusion.cpp#L42](url) Assuming two quaternions are defined as follows: The product of the two is calculated as follows: This is consistent with the multiplication operator function in the code, and there is no problem with it. But the subsequent division operator function seems incorrect. Before dividing quaternions, the code has already specified the normalization of quaternions. Combined with the inverse calculation of quaternions, the following can be obtained: In fact, it is the conjugate of y. So x/y is actually using the conjugate of y (y ^ -1) to replace y in the product result, and the calculation result is as follows: But this calculation result is not consistent with the operator function: [https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/aabbe500aa4b682305b3062116edebc3fd0528c6/libraries/AP_Math/quaternion.cpp#L776C1-L799C2](url) ```cpp ret.q1 = (rquat0*quat0 + rquat1*quat1 + rquat2*quat2 + rquat3*quat3); ret.q2 = (rquat0*quat1 - rquat1*quat0 - rquat2*quat3 + rquat3*quat2); ret.q3 = (rquat0*quat2 + rquat1*quat3 - rquat2*quat0 - rquat3*quat1); ret.q4 = (rquat0*quat3 - rquat1*quat2 + rquat2*quat1 - `rquat3*quat0); ``` The quantities of rquat1... rquat3 in ret.q2, ret.q3, and ret.q4 do not seem to be correctly multiplied by a negative sign.

author: tpwrules
body:
It appears this result is consistent with MATLAB which is where a lot of this EKF code came from: https://stackoverflow.com/a/68712650

MATLAB for whatever bizarre reason calculates division as $y^{-1}x$ instead of your $xy^{-1}$.

Searching for the symbol name `_ZNK11QuaternionTIdEdvERKS0_` in a CubeOrange binary, the only other uses are
* https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/aabbe500aa4b682305b3062116edebc3fd0528c6/libraries/AP_NavEKF3/AP_NavEKF3_MagFusion.cpp#L83
* https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/aabbe500aa4b682305b3062116edebc3fd0528c6/libraries/AP_NavEKF3/AP_NavEKF3_MagFusion.cpp#L1658
* https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/126fbfb99f1900ad950613340f030d629ae87c73/libraries/AP_NavEKF3/AP_NavEKF3_core.cpp#L917

author: custeve
title: Plane: SITL: sitl_airsped.cpp is passed EAS but expects TAS
body:
Two recommendations: to resolve issues with SITL at high altitudes. At issue is that the the SITL has the correct EAS airspeed, but the AHRS and dynamics, do not. (1/eas2tas is applied twice).  

1) In libraries/sitl/AP_HAL_SITL/sitl_airspeed, the _update_airspeed(float) function expects a TAS to be passed in, and it is then converted to EAS. This is fed from sitl->state.airspeed. TAS is not needed for this function, recommend passing in EAS airspeed and removing the conversion. 

2) The calling function in libraries/sitl/SIM_Aircraft.cpp updates airspeed in update_eas_airspeed() using 'airspeed = velocity_air_ef.length() / eas2tas;', suggest changing this to velocity_air_bf.length() for contextual accuracy (though the vector length is the same, just rotated). 


ping @tridge

title: Rover: may get stuck if Dijkstras and Simple avoidance enabled
body:
If rover has both Dijkastras and Simple avoidance enabled they both use the same margin distance meaning the vehicle may get stuck as it passes each "safe point".  Rover's don't "slide" like Copters do, they stop.

One solution might be to separate the margins used by the two and then enforce the simple mode margin is smaller than the other

This was found by @tridge

author: SuWeipeng
title: How many users have a requirement for processing large(>1GB) bin log files?
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

* With the increase in device endurance, log file are becoming progressively larger. The ability to quickly and accurately parse these log file profoundly impacts our experience in exploring, learning and debbuging ArduPilot software and hardware. I've developed an open-source tool to improve the reading and parsing .bin log files, and I'm intrested in understanding how many people share this same need.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

* Selective loading for focused analysis
    * In many cases, a specific analysis does not require reading the entire log file. For instance, if an analysis only needs to examine ATT (attitude) and BARO (barometer) data, filtering for these messages during the reading and parsing process can result in significant memory savings.

* Time based log slicing
    * For long flight or mission, you might be only interested in data from a  specific time period. Slicing the log by a desired time range on demand not only saves a substantial amount of memory but can also improve processing speed to some extent.

* One-click custom visualizations
    * For specific research, it's often necessary to reference several data sets simultaneously. Plotting each data series one by one in Mission Planner can be a tedious process. The ability to load a custom script with a single click to generate the desired plots after reading the data offers a much cleaner and more efficient workflow.

* Seamless export for advanced tools
    * For more advaced analysis, it is often necessary to use external tools like Python or Matlab. The capbility to export data into formats such as CSV and SQLite database facilities easier cross-platform processing and integration with these powerful environments.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Mission Planner can read and parse bin logs, but it's not enough for me, so I have developed another tool using Qt 6.8.3, the same developing environment as QGroundControl.

[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
[ArduPilotLog](https://github.com/SuWeipeng/ArduPilotLog)

author: JWaik
body: I found that the problem has been fixed in the latest dev version with [this commit](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/commit/6338d10b5fc817b26a61c9959aa7c6ec0389db0a#diff-85564705aaabd4078d2bdcbd56ca87fc94a95e3ff47b626b062fa80da0889423). However, the fix depends on using a board with external flash storage.

author: peterbarker
body:
So the story here is that unfortunately AP_TEMPERATURE_SENSOR_ENABLED is lying about whether the feature is built in.

What's being detected there is a set of "dummy methods" we use to have the temperature sensor code compiled in by default on Sub but not on any other vehicle.

So it's actually not a matter of "TEMP*" parameters missing - it really isn't compiled into the code, regardless of what features.txt says.

You can use the custom build server to actually compile it in.

As @JWaik found, we *do* compile it in on boards with  more than 2MB of flash.

author: LupusTheCanine
body:
> You can use the custom build server to actually compile it in.

I did that, it would be nice if it wasn't lying.

author: rob-clarke
body:
Have been exploring this myself. For boards between 1MB and 2MB flash (and not Sub), if `AP_TEMPERATURE_SENSOR_ENABLED` is not explicitly set in the hwdef, the current setup results in a strange situation where the standard builds don't have any real temp sensor support, but building on the custom build server with only the feature defaults set does include the support. My expectation was that building with the feature defaults would get the same result as the non-custom build.

A potential fix (though brittle) for the lying feature detection would be to use an `ExtractFeatures.FindString` in `extract_features.py` to look for 'AP_TemperatureSensor must be singleton' to detect if the real or dummy implementation has been used.

A nicer approach might be to use the symbol size (that's captured but not used as far as I can see) but I'm not sure if that is more prone to breaking. Is there a reliable correlation between code and symbol size?

author: IdoBuchman
title: Support Differential Thrust for VTOL Position Control Modes
body: ## Feature request I have a VTOL QuadPlane with two cruise motors (not tilt-rotors) with a physical layout that limits yaw authority, especially in Q-modes however where flaps are left ineffective. To handle wind, my QuadPlane will certainly use its cruise motors, throttle left and right, for position control but not attitude control for yaw stability using differential thrust. This has been talked about in the forums - https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/help-with-differential-thrust-for-a-vtol/56029. As can be seen in the attached screenshot, in simulation, a yaw imbalance is observed, which the hover motors attempt to correct (as indicated by their differing PWM outputs). However, the forward cruise motors (CH9 and CH10) consistently produce identical PWM values, confirming they are not utilizing differential thrust to contribute to yaw correction. **Describe the solution you'd like** Differential thrust for yaw authority is well established as I see in master: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/ArduPlane/servos.cpp#L766-L791 . I propose this same function to be available for position holding modes like QLoiter by parameter configuration. Using Q_FWD_THR_USE to add option “Differential thrust for yaw authority” seems like a good implementation. I would implement the change in the same snippit - https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/ArduPlane/servos.cpp#L766-L791 , which already handles differential thrust, extending that function for “is_vtol_mode” to be true seems appropriate. **Describe alternatives you've considered** I considered implementing differential thrust in position-control modes via a Lua script, but that approach felt less elegant as it bypasses the main control system. It would also be less scalable and harder to maintain compared to integrating the functionality directly in the codebase. **Platform** [ ] All [ ] AntennaTracker [ ] Copter [X] Plane [ ] Rover [ ] Submarine

author: rmackay9
title: Copter: Log_Write_Guided_Position_Target re-used to log Location (lat, lon, alt)
body:
Copter's Guided mode logs the target it has received via MAVLink using the Log_Write_Guided_Position_Target method.  This is fine except that sometimes we receive a target as an offset from the EKF origin and sometimes as a Location (e.g. lat, lon, alt).  Trying to log the Location with this same function leads to a loss of accuracy and it's also very confusing for the user trying to graph the message.

This issue is raised based on discussion between @lthall, @peterbarker and @rmackay9 re PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/30756

author: Shashwatt-git
body:
Hi @rmackay9,

I’ve been looking into this issue while exploring Guided mode logging and as you suggested the main problem comes from mixing two different coordinate representations in the same log message.

Currently Log_Write_Guided_Position_Target() is used for both:
• NED offset targets (relative to EKF origin), and
• absolute Location targets (lat/lon/alt).

My proposed approach is:

1. Keep Log_Write_Guided_Position_Target() for NED-offset targets only
2. Introduce a separate log message (e.g. GUIDLOC) for Location-based targets
3. Add a dedicated logging helper for Locatin inputs
4. Update set_destination() to use the new logging path
5. Maintain backward compatibility with existing logs

I’m currently preparing for a GSoC application focused on AI-assisted log analysis, so understanding and improving logging semantics is directly relevant for me.

Before starting implementation, I wanted to confirm that this direction aligns with the intended solution discussed around PR #30756.

Thanks!

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @Shashwatt-git,

That approach sounds ok to me, thanks

author: ES-Alexander
title: Sub: Depth sensor error with nominal values
body: ## Bug report **Issue details** We have [had](https://discuss.bluerobotics.com/t/rov-depth-sensor-issues-30-bar-incorrect-readings-1000m-sensor-error-message/20914) [some](https://discuss.bluerobotics.com/t/depth-sensor-error-with-bar100/12400) [reports](https://discuss.bluerobotics.com/t/bar-100-depth-sensor-error/16335) of difficult to explain depth sensor errors, and recently determined that one cause is from the water-based sensor readings being consistent enough that they will occasionally pass the 2 second [`BARO_DATA_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_MS`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/Sub-4.5/libraries/AP_Baro/AP_Baro.h#L23) value while the sensor is still working fine. Given water and a submarine vehicle can potentially be expected to experience higher data consistency, while also not having the risk of falling out of the sky, it seems worth increasing that timeout for water-based depth sensors to at least 5s, or possibly 10-30. Rovers have similar (or higher) stability compared to Sub vehicles, and [may have water-based barometers in future](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/20721), so it seems worth factoring that into the change. **Version** 4.5 / 4.1 **Platform** [ ] All [ ] AntennaTracker [ ] Copter [ ] Plane [X] Rover [X] Submarine **Hardware type** Pixhawk, Navigator Depth sensors are MS5837-30BA (Bar30) and (more commonly for the error, seemingly) Keller PA-7LD (Bar100). **Logs** Screenshot from a meeting with @Williangalvani:

author: mareschn
title: Sagetech MXS ADSB Broken
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

It appears that we can't use the Sagetech MXS ADSB with Ardupilot due to impossible altitude data provided by the autopilot; the altitude data fields are all zeros. One of those zero bits is telling the ADSB that the autopilot is unable to provide altitude, and another tells the ADSB that it must not use the unit's internal pressure sensor; therefore, it breaks without any source of altitude available.

**Version**
V4.6.2

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[X] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
Quadplane

**Hardware type**
Cube Orange

**Logs**
In capturing some serial data from the autopilot to the MXS ADSB, I see operating messages that look like this:
AA 03 02 0C 02 80 02 00 **00 00** FF F9 EB D1 80 01 74

AA=Start Byte
03=Operating Message
02=Incrementing Sequence ID
0C=Payload Length (12 Bytes)
02=Payload Byte 0
80=Payload Byte 1
02=Payload Byte 2
00=Payload Byte 3
**00=Payload Byte 4
00=Payload Byte 5**
ETC.

I'm not sure if there are other problems, but payload bytes 4 and 5 (Altitude) are what I noticed cause trouble: 
Bits 0-13 are Altitude data starting at -1200 ft with either 25 or 100ft scaling (so it is indicating -1200ft in either scaling case)
Bit 14 is the Host [Ardupilot] Altitude Available bit (0=unavailable, 1=available)
Bit 15 is the Internal [ADSB] Altitude Enable bit (0=do not use internal sensor altitude, 1=use internal sensor altitude)

It should be somewhat easy to provide altitude to the ADSB, but if not, bits 14 and 15 should not both be zero.

If the autopilot can't provide altitude, then it should set bit 15 to allow the use of the internal altimeter (0x8000). It is not possible to use the MXS with ArduPilot in its current state because there is no way of getting any altitude data.

author: robustini
title: Plane: ARSPD_AUTOCAL should respect ARSPD_USE=2 and only calibrate at zero throttle
body:
There is a conflict in behavior between ARSPD_AUTOCAL and ARSPD_USE = 2 that can lead to a corrupted airspeed ratio.
The current behavior is as follows:

    ARSPD_USE = 2 (UseWhenZeroThrottle) correctly prevents the flight controller (TECS) from using airspeed data when the throttle is active. This is perfect for configurations like front-motor gliders where the pitot tube is in the prop wash.

    ARSPD_AUTOCAL = 1 enables the background calibration of the ARSPD_RATIO.

The issue is that the ARSPD_AUTOCAL function does not check for throttle status or the ARSPD_USE setting. It continues to gather data and update the ARSPD_RATIO even when the motor is running. In a prop-wash scenario, this means the calibration algorithm is fed with artificially high airspeed readings, leading to a consistently incorrect and corrupted ARSPD_RATIO.
While the plane flies safely because TECS ignores the bad data, the underlying calibration becomes progressively worse over a flight.

author: adnanyusuf85
title: Watchdog Reset and In-Flight Crash Caused by Logging Thread Stall and Log Buffer Overrun on Pixhawk 4 (ArduCopter v4.5.5)
body:
## Issue Summary

A Pixhawk 4-based drone running ArduCopter v4.5.5 experienced a mid-air reset and subsequent crash. Post-flight log analysis indicates that the issue was triggered by logging thread congestion, which resulted in flight loop delays, a watchdog-triggered reset, and failure to recover after reboot due to a repeated log buffer overflow. The issue appears systemic, as the logging configuration (`LOG_BITMASK`) was verified to be consistent with other functioning drones in the fleet.

---

## System Details

- **Firmware Version**: ArduCopter v4.5.5  
- **Flight Controller**: Pixhawk 4
- **Autopilot Type**: ArduCopter  
- **Flight Mode at Time of Failure**: LOITER
- **SD Card**: SanDisk Ultra 32GB UHS-I, Class 10, FAT32  
- **Was this Reproducible?**: Occurred once; other drones using same config have not shown this behavior yet  
- **Custom Firmware or Parameters?**: No; standard ArduPilot build with standard logging settings  
- **Ground Control Software Used**: Mission Planner 1.3.81  
- **Environment**: Outdoor mission, GPS lock maintained, no reported vibration or EMI issues  
- **Power Status**: No brownouts recorded; stable power throughout until reset  
- **Log File**: Not recovered due to drone crash and burn

---

## Failure Timeline (Based on Log Analysis)

1. **Logging thread stalls**  
   - Possibly caused by SD card latency or high-frequency log writes.  
   - `LOG_BITMASK` was verified to be standard and consistent with other aircraft.

2. **Flight loop delays grow**  
   - Performance Monitor (`PM.Nlon`) shows loop overruns up to 200μs.

3. **Watchdog timer triggers**  
   - Flight controller reboots mid-air due to unresponsive behavior.

4. **Post-reboot recovery fails**  
   - Logging resumes but encounters `0x800` buffer overflow error, indicating logging backend failure.

5. **Secondary failure occurs**  
   - FC shuts down again due to overload, resulting in unrecoverable crash.

---

## Observed Behavior

- Logging thread may have monopolized resources or introduced blocking behavior.
- Watchdog reset did not fully clear the underlying condition; reappearance of logging failure post-reboot led to final loss of control.
- No graceful degradation path or prioritization prevented this critical system function (flight stabilization) from being compromised.

---

## Expected Behavior

- Logging failures should not trigger a cascade that compromises flight control.
- The flight controller should maintain stabilization loops even under SD latency or logging overload.
- Post-reboot behavior should preserve minimal functionality for a safe landing or recovery.

---

## Suggested Areas to Investigate

- Logging thread scheduling behavior under SD write latency or fragmentation.
- Log buffer size limits, flushing logic, and overflow handling (particularly 0x800 condition).
- Interactions between watchdog logic and logging subsystem (should watchdog treat logging thread stalls as reboot-worthy?).
- Possible starvation of critical threads by log write backlog.
- Recommendations for safe logging limits and SD card class/spec enforcement at preflight.

---

## Impact

- **Severity**: High  
- **Risk**: Full loss of vehicle in mid-air due to internal software fault cascade  
- **Affected Users**: Pixhawk 4 users with high `LOG_BITMASK` settings and/or slow SD cards

author: ES-Alexander
title: Add support for barometer position compensation
body: ## Feature request **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** We have [sensor position offset compensation](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/common-sensor-offset-compensation.html) available for adjusting the perceived center of control, but the feature doesn't exist for the barometer. That means altitudes are always focused around the barometer position, which may not be possible to have near the IMU or center of mass (e.g. in Sub vehicles the barometer must be external to the electronics enclosure), so either forces the center of control to be configured to where the barometer is, or reduces control and telemetry coherence by failing to account for the separation. **Describe the solution you'd like** A set of offset parameters for the connected barometers, to allow compensating for their position offsets. **Describe alternatives you've considered** It is possible to use the barometer position as the reference point everything else is considered offset relative to, but that's arbitrarily decided by hardware constraints, and may result in unintuitive control. **Platform** [x] All [ ] AntennaTracker [ ] Copter [ ] Plane [ ] Rover [x] Submarine **Additional context** This is a common setup for Sub (and could be similar for planes) - barometer offsets are relevant for surface and bottom awareness/avoidance, as well as where the vehicle actually sits when maintaining an altitude/depth, especially while pitched (e.g. if [conducting a survey with a forward scanning/imaging sonar](https://bluerobotics.com/learn/understanding-and-using-scanning-sonars/#bottom-visibility)): The center of control is generally desired to be at the center of mass (or potentially the point of vision), and it's important to data accuracy to have a well-defined reference point that collected data is relative to.

author: JasonMDavey
title: Infinite loop in AP_HAL/utility/ftoa_engine when formatting floats with very small exponents
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
Invoking ftoa_engine (low-level function responsible for formatting floating point numbers, used by GCS::send_text) enters an infinite loop when invoked as below:

```
char *buf = (char*)malloc(255);
ftoa_engine(1e-44f, buf, 7, 7);
```

This appears to happen with other very small numbers (around e-44 exponent), and results in an infinite loop here, as `prod` and `decimal` are both zero:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/ae48665948b5c26ee21caca0f3cf23536614f698/libraries/AP_HAL/utility/ftoa_engine.cpp#L149

Adding the following to the start of the function seems to be a workable fix, although it may break the formatting of very small (denormalized) floats:

```
if (fabsf(val) < FLT_MIN) val = 0.0f;
```

**Version**
Plane Stable 4.6.2

**Platform**
[x] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
n/a

**Hardware type**
n/a

**Logs**
n/a

author: tpwrules
body:
Fun discovery, thanks. I can replicate in Lua too (though then it only freezes the Lua thread).

Your solution seems good as an initial fix. I don't see a situation where denormals not being formatted would make or break a flight. But longer term we could switch to a better formatting engine. There are relatively [recent developments](https://github.com/ulfjack/ryu) in the field. (I was looking into this recently cause I also want a better string -> float routine.)

I think we do also keep denormals enabled on hardware. I don't know if that has a performance penalty on Cortex cores, but if it has a severe one it may be safer to turn on flush-to-zero; it's supported by the Cortex FPUs. But I would have to do some serious thought on how it might mangle e.g. the EKF state or [screw up comparisons](https://randomascii.wordpress.com/2012/05/20/thats-not-normalthe-performance-of-odd-floats/).

title: simplyify the esp32 build system (aligned further with ChibiOS HAL)
body:
## Feature request 

@davidbuzz tagged specifically as the primary maintainer, trying to help not infuriate.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Adding boards to the esp32 configuration is hard to grok, and each board can have wildly different peripherals onboard and offboard which is currently directly configured into libraries/AP_HAL_ESP32/boards/MyCustomBoard.h and not in general hwdef.dat options applied to a board. 

I think we can move to a more-ChibiOS-aligned path (AIUI) where the hwdef.dat options on a board can generate the MyCustomBoard.h header programmatically. This should make it easier to maintain all the boards (or break them all at once, yes).

I did see a comment under issues/21843 that `esptool.py` knows the connected board type, but I think that ignores the need to know beforehand to properly configure the capabilities and build the appropriate modules. I think the hwdef.dat should have the esp32 type in it as if you're targetting a specific board you can expect an out-of-the-box ~working config that you can reconfigure as required in software, outside of which pins map to things.

Additionally it's quite hard for an outsider to navigate the path from board-specific flag, through `waf configure` to `waf build` and the interaction with CMake and the esp idf. I think it's possible to make this simpler, and document how to add options so they in fact do land in esp32 land, and I'd like to prove it.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Implementing board specific `hwdef.dat` fully, `esp32.py` above that with imbued knowledge of the different esp32's (or at least two to start with), and board-specific defaults.parm on the far side. Without breaking anything. Simples.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Getting a new esp32 board to build and behave can take a lot of changes, and then you're left with a mega-PR and reviewing that is hard, ensuring it's correct impossible.  I would rather avoid this, and send lovely small packets of provably working changes as small steps along this path, and then adding boards will be a doddle. 

Where possible, at least. I'll be pulling from a working (compiling, running on one board) branch but using my little AI-friend to slice off a working morsel, ensure it too works, and send that. No AI slop though, in the PR code or the documentation, is the promise.

Alternatively I could rebase off the pending ESP32 mega-PR but I'm not sure if that's progressing or has fallen afoul of the problem described above.

**Platform**
[X] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**

Once this is done I want to send further PRs for supporting other modules on the esp32, making things like wifi optional and having dynamic support for the PSRAM, and of course other boards. 

I figured I should (a) ask if you want to embark on this journey, since you have to review it and (b) if the approach is somewhat reasonable or if you want to go down a different path. The ChibiOS-like HAL approach seems reasonable/more understandable to me, but hey I'm new here.

Hi @mrlitr,

Setup instructions are [here on the wiki](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-caddx-gimbal.html).  I'm sure you've read them but for others who see this issue it could be good. author: Sametus
title: Plane: Allow dynamic, real-time airspeed change via MAVLink (DO_CHANGE_SPEED / GUIDED_CHANGE_SPEED) during AUTO/GUIDED
body:
In current ArduPlane firmware, there is no way to reliably increase or decrease the airspeed in real time via MAVLink while in flight—neither via DO_CHANGE_SPEED nor GUIDED_CHANGE_SPEED commands, regardless of mode (AUTO or GUIDED).

Mission-based DO_CHANGE_SPEED only works as a scheduled mission item, not as an immediate command.

For dynamic following/tracking missions, or real-time guidance scenarios, there should be a way to send a MAVLink command to immediately change the current airspeed target (e.g., to catch up with a moving leader, respond to sensor input, or change profile during flight).

Expected:

MAV_CMD_DO_CHANGE_SPEED or MAV_CMD_GUIDED_CHANGE_SPEED should be processable as real-time, in-flight commands in both AUTO and GUIDED modes.

The airspeed target should update immediately (with given acceleration), not only at mission item boundaries.

Use case:

Real-time following/tracking, dynamic autonomy, responsive flight.

Tested on:

ArduPlane 4.7.0-dev

pymavlink (direct MAVLink)

Result:

Command is accepted but does not affect current speed in-flight.

Request:

Please implement or activate dynamic speed change support for ArduPlane, similar to how Copter supports velocity/altitude commands via MAVLink.

author: IamPete1
body: Half way through the flight the EKF switched for IMU 2. This means that IMU 0 is no longer the primary, so the notches are not run. You can change this behavior with `INS_HNTCH_OPTS`/`INS_HNTC2_OPTS` "EnableOnAllIMUs" If you crop into the first part of the flight in the filter tool you can see the notches are working as expected You can also see the change in the post filter spectogram: When looking at the whole flight there is more time without the notches running than with, so the effect it reduced in the averaged FFT plot. The low pass filter is always running, so you still see its attenuation.

## Feature request

Bit of a niche application, but I've found any external AHRS output must match the AHRS_ORIENTATION, regardless of their mounting, at least when the external INS is being used as a sensor input to EKF3. In a couple of aircraft I've been flying, the autopilot has some unconventional rotations, the external INS is mounted in a fairly typical orientation. This results in having to setup the external INS with an output that aligns with the autopilot board, rather than vehicle axes. While this works fine, it adds an extra level of coordinate rotations to think about and some fairly unclear setup procedures. It would be handy to have either a custom rotation just for the external INS, or to automatically derotate the INS data back to the 'normal' aircraft coordinate system.

author: rmackay9
title: Copter: altitude estimate from pos change if no GPS
body:
As suspected during the review of PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/30037, Copter's position controller is falling back to use AHRS's get_relative_position_D_origin_float() for the vertical altitude estimate whenever the GPS (or some other external position estimate) is unavailable.  The problematic code is in [AC_PosControl::update_estimates()](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_AttitudeControl/AC_PosControl.cpp#L1334)

AHRS's get_relative_position_D_origin_float() was only intended to be used during the vibration failsafe and may produce a slightly worse estimate than the more regularly used inertial + baro estimate.

This issue was confirmed by performing the follow tests:

1. modified [AC_PosControl::update_estimates](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_AttitudeControl/AC_PosControl.cpp#L1334) to output debug when it's altitude was from AP_AHRS::get_relative_position_NED_origin vs AP_AHRS::.get_relative_position_D_origin_float
2. started SITL and set/unset SIM_GPS1_ENABLE

The detailed results are:

1. if GPS is enabled, relative position used from startup until EKF calculates a 3D position estimate after which time the regular estimate is used
2. if GPS is lost, EKF "stops aiding" and relative position is used
3. if GPS is regained, regular estimate is used

author: rmackay9
body:
Sorry, there is no problem.

The question was not to do with the position estimate but rather the vertical velocity estimate and whether we were incorrectly using [AHRS::get_vert_pos_rate_D()](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_AHRS/AP_AHRS.h#L308).  It seems that regardless of whether a horizontal position or velocity source is available or not, AHRS::get_velocity_NED() returns a vector meaning we do get the expected vertical velocity.

author: ddatsko
title: Wrong VTX power value displayed on OSD
body:
## Bug report

Hello everyone
I am using copter firmware (4.6.1) with MAMBA 5.8G 2.5W VTX that is configured via "IRC Tramp" protocol, with only TX being connected to it. I would like to have the ability to change the VTX power dynamically during the flight using `RCX_OPTION` parameter set to 94 (VTX Power).
This seems to be working, however I then noticed that the parameter "VTX_POWER" is not the same as the VTX power displayed on the OSD.

I think I have found the source of the bug, but I would like someone to verify that too. From what I can see now is that:
- When the RC channel is changed, the `AP::vtx().change_power(position);` function is called
- The `AP_VideoTX::change_power` function calls the `AP_VideoTX::set_configured_power_mw(power)`, that updates the `VTX_POWER` parameter. However, it doesn't touch the `_current_power` property of `AP_VideoTX`. As a result when the `AP_VideoTX::get_power_mw()` is called, it returns the wrong value.
- In the end, the power value is set properly to the VTX, as `AP_Tramp` simply calls the `AP_VideoTX::get_configured_power_mw()` and sends it to the VTX, but the OSD displays a wrong value.
- NOTE: considering that the VTX is connected only using the "TX" pin, `AP_Tramp::receive_response()` likely does nothing, thus `AP_VideoTX::set_power_mw()` is not called in a feedback manner


**Version**
4.6.1

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[ * ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: andyp1per
body: Thanks for the report. Unfortunately your analysis is not correct - setting the configured power is merely a request to the underlying VTX provider to change the power. The actual current power is represented by _current_power and this only gets updated when the vtx provider says that it is updated. The IRC protocol is half-duplex so can receive responses as well as send requests. So the behaviour you see indicates that the power is not getting updated correctly by the VTX.

author: ddatsko
body: Got it, thank you! Yes, I completely missed the fact that we can receive information from the VTX in half-duplex mode

title: Battery current limit can cause flyaway in Loiter
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
At least some of the time, the battery current limit can prevent the drone from braking or changing its attitude when flying in Loiter mode (and maybe other position modes?) if the current limit is constantly exceeded.

I attached a log which demonstrates this. Here the salient screenshot and the sequence of events:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/126e6b4a-957a-48e5-9206-2ab33449226b)
In this test, my battery current sensor was misbehaving and reporting 50+ amps while the configured limit was 50 amps, so the limit was always being exceeded.

2. I release the stick. The drone's attitude does not change. The position target continues to run away (I guess because the kinematic path is being drawn farther due to the drone still accelerating)

## Bug report

**Issue details**
Altitude demand seems to get corrupted in flight (hovering around 0 instead of the correct values for the mission) after exiting the landing state (e.g., after aborting a landing, or relaunching the vehicle without restarting the flight controller). This results in the aircraft sinking to the ground while still following the mission path. The problem only seems to affect waypoint navigation: altitude demand still works correctly in loiter navigation, takeoff, etc.

In our configuration, the TECS rate limits slow down the descent enough to react and switch to FBW-B.

We've also had this problem occur when launching the vehicle again right after landing (it was disarmed, mision reset, and then re-armed and launched in Auto).

author: robertlong13
title: Weird execution order for DO commands immediately after jump
body:
## Bug report

DO commands placed after a finite-loop DO_JUMP get executed at the start of the last loop. Here is a screenshot of what I mean:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be1068ed-49ce-48e8-8272-affc4bed1547)

This is the order of execution:
```
2025-06-17 1:00:48 PM : Mission: 1 VTOLTakeoff
2025-06-17 1:01:21 PM : Mission: 2 WP
2025-06-17 1:01:43 PM : Mission: 3 WP
2025-06-17 1:01:54 PM : Mission: 4 AuxFunction
2025-06-17 1:01:54 PM : Mission: 5 Jump 1/2
2025-06-17 1:01:54 PM : Mission: 2 WP
2025-06-17 1:02:12 PM : Mission: 3 WP
2025-06-17 1:02:27 PM : Mission: 4 AuxFunction
2025-06-17 1:02:27 PM : Mission: 5 Jump 2/2
2025-06-17 1:02:27 PM : Mission: 2 WP
2025-06-17 1:02:27 PM : Mission: 6 AuxFunction    !!!
2025-06-17 1:02:43 PM : Mission: 3 WP
2025-06-17 1:02:58 PM : Mission: 4 AuxFunction
2025-06-17 1:02:58 PM : Mission: 7 LoitTurns
2025-06-17 1:03:31 PM : Mission: 8 LoitAltitude
2025-06-17 1:04:20 PM : Mission: 9 LoitTurns
2025-06-17 1:04:36 PM : Mission: 10 VTOLLand
```

Where I'd expect to see this
```
2025-06-17 1:00:48 PM : Mission: 1 VTOLTakeoff
2025-06-17 1:01:21 PM : Mission: 2 WP
2025-06-17 1:01:43 PM : Mission: 3 WP
2025-06-17 1:01:54 PM : Mission: 4 AuxFunction
2025-06-17 1:01:54 PM : Mission: 5 Jump 1/2
2025-06-17 1:01:54 PM : Mission: 2 WP
2025-06-17 1:02:12 PM : Mission: 3 WP
2025-06-17 1:02:27 PM : Mission: 4 AuxFunction
2025-06-17 1:02:27 PM : Mission: 5 Jump 2/2
2025-06-17 1:02:27 PM : Mission: 2 WP
2025-06-17 1:02:43 PM : Mission: 3 WP
2025-06-17 1:02:58 PM : Mission: 4 AuxFunction
2025-06-17 1:02:27 PM : Mission: 6 AuxFunction    <- here instead
2025-06-17 1:02:58 PM : Mission: 7 LoitTurns
2025-06-17 1:03:31 PM : Mission: 8 LoitAltitude
2025-06-17 1:04:20 PM : Mission: 9 LoitTurns
2025-06-17 1:04:36 PM : Mission: 10 VTOLLand
```

[DoJumpWeirdOrder.waypoints.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20768437/DoJumpWeirdOrder.waypoints.txt)

I spent most of the day trying to wrap my head around this and fix it, and I learned a bit about the cause, but I'm at a loss as for how to fix it. I'm half-leaning toward documenting it and thus upgrading it to "feature".

### Cause
We doesn't immediately execute the DO commands we come across while advancing the mission. We store it in `_do_cmd` and move on. Each call to `update()` we execute the `_do_cmd` and load up the next one. This repeats until a nav command is hit (or the end of the mission, whatever). When the last jump executes, and the NAV command is sent back for the last time, the DO_JUMP is marked as complete, and when `update()` goes to advance to the next DO, it runs past it. This is why they all run at the beginning of the last loop.

**Version**
Discovered on master, but willing to bet this is long-standing behavior

[  ] AntennaTracker
[ x ] Copter
[ x ] Plane
[ x ] Rover
[ x ] Submarine

author: rishabsingh3003
title: Instantiate DroneCAN sensor backends unconditionally to avoid boot-time initialization issues
body:
Currently, for DroneCAN-based sensor backends (e.g. RangeFinder, GPS, Airspeed, etc.), the backend instantiation is deferred until a valid and relevant message is received from the CAN bus. While this may work in normal operation, it creates several problems during boot:

As an example, SYS_STATUS sensor flags may incorrectly show the DroneCAN device as disabled or missing at boot if no message has yet been received. Downstream code may expect the backend to exist once enabled by parameters, but it's not present yet due to no message being received.

A hack for DroneCAN rangefinder was done here because of this issue:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/30364

Proposed solution:

Instantiate the DroneCAN sensor backends unconditionally at boot based on parameter configuration.

author: wyunc
title: Overflow Issues in MAV Commands
body:
## Bug report

Hi : )
I previously reported some of these on discuss.ap to Lucas(amilcarlucas). For easier tracking, I’d like to summarize here a few MAV commands that have been found to cause overflow issues.

The following commands can trigger arithmetic overflow or floating-point overflow when given certain special values. In most cases, the cause is that the x, y, or z values are not properly handled or constrained.

1.The following are present in both copter,plane, and rover:
mavcmd MAV_CMD_DO_SET_HOME [1, 180, 84, 180, 399, 300, 699]
mavcmd MAV_CMD_DO_SET_ROI [1, 37, 479, 0, 706, 608, 441]
mavcmd MAV_CMD_DO_SET_ROI_LOCATION [426, 0, 0, 0, -1381736522, -585139360, 135]
mavcmd MAV_CMD_CAN_FORWARD [498, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
mavcmd MAV_CMD_EXTERNAL_POSITION_ESTIMATE [25, 23, 434, 0, 834, 25, 916]

2.The following command only works with copter:
mavcmd MAV_CMD_NAV_LOITER_TO_ALT [1, 650, 0, 0, 458, 291, 615]

**Version**
4.7.0

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[X] Copter
[X] Plane
[X] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: peterbarker
body:
We are quite aware that we're not bounds-checking stuff coming in over mavlink.  For extra fun try passing in NaN values in the parameters.

We are very flash-contrained on our embedded targets.  Sanity checking every parameter is *costly* in terms of flash.

If you find bug where we're not simply doing bad things in terms of types (eg. buffer overflows), we will definitely care.

... and we will add sanity checks - this PR of mine, for example: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/28866/files

author: wyunc
body:
Hi @peterbarker ,thanks for your response and the clarification.

Apologies for the delayed reply — I’ve been swamped with a deadline recently...

I fully understand the flash constraints on embedded targets, and I agree that checking every incoming parameter is not always feasible. That said, the inputs I reported are not just about unbounded values or random edge cases — they consistently trigger arithmetic(floating-point) overflow during execution. 

I also noticed that the issues I encountered are very similar to those described in #28790, especially in how unexpected MAVLink input leads to unsafe or undefined behavior. So while I’m not suggesting widespread input validation, I do think these particular cases represent valid bugs, as they result in observable runtime errors in normal test scenarios.

Could you help confirm whether these overflow issues should be tracked as bugs (or enhancements), and whether the team would consider adding minimal bounds checks or clamping for these specific commands?

body:
## Bug report

Non consequential errors reported by a Septentrio GPS, such as a
congestion on an unrelated port (error 0x40) or a full sd card (error 0x200 [ref](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/sbf-error-changed/90756))
cause the GPS to be counted as unhealthy, which may inhibit arming.

author: RickReeser
title: AP_ESC_TELEM: Handle negative RPM
body:
Some DroneCAN ESCs report negative RPM to differentiate clockwise vs. counter-clockwise. The ESC telem MAVLink message sends these values as 0: [github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/ArduPilot-4.6/libraries/AP_ESC_Telem/AP_ESC_Telem.cpp#L467](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/ArduPilot-4.6/libraries/AP_ESC_Telem/AP_ESC_Telem.cpp#L467)

The MAVLink message [definition ](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/ardupilotmega.html#ESC_TELEMETRY_1_TO_4)requires the value to be uint, so maybe all we can do is abs() it and lose the differentiation of direction, but I think that is preferable to just sending 0.

title: Plane: Automatic hand-launch from moving vehicle
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Recently, attempting to perform an automatic takeoff (hand-launched) from a moving vehicle, I saw the aircraft pitch down back to the ground after being launched. Further investigation concluded that the TAKEOFF mode logic assumed the aircraft was already flying, and simply commanded a climb to the takeoff altitude using regular TECS. See: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/0bf65c3a8719ba97b3ac684bdc6b3d630930ecd8/ArduPlane/mode_takeoff.cpp#L91
 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be nice to support automatic takeoff from moving vehicles (ie. pick-up truck). One alternative could simply be to add an option for moving vehicle takeoff, which would bypass the logic checking if the vehicle is already flying.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatively, the logic checking if the vehicle is already flying could additionally check if the vehicle is above the wings level altitude for an automatic takeoff.

[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[X] Plane

author: peterbarker
body: So you're driving along holding the vehicle and now you want it to throttle-up and go.  What actually makes the vehicle decide to do that?  For handl-laucnhes we have mechanisms like the accel-threshold-detection stuff - but you're presumably just releasing the vehicle and hoping it will go - but the vehicle (unless you're doing fancy things outside the standard code) can't tell you've let it go!

For those users who are transferring from DJI (or flying both DJI and AP vehicles) it is convenient if they can continue to use the same arm/disarm stick gestures as DJI.  We probably only need this on Copters although it would do no harm on other vehicles.

The code implementing this is [here in motors.cpp](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/ArduCopter/motors.cpp#L29)

This was received at the Japan Drone Expo 2025

author: peterbarker
body:
Could we *please* not do anything more vehicle-specific stuff than we need to?  Common user experience on something like arming between Copter and Plane is *important*!

Once https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/16091 goes in all vehicles can have the same gesture.

author: muramura
body: I implemented DJI-style arming ($\diagdown \diagup$) and disarming ($\diagup \diagdown$) via a Lua script. Since this method involves all four channels, it's also useful for detecting channel anomalies.However, if the sticks are returned to neutral too slowly after arming, the flight controller might interpret it as an attitude command. To prevent this, I’m planning to add a process that ignores all inputs until the sticks return to the neutral position right after arming.

author: rmackay9
title: GCS_SEND_TEXT messages should support different languages
body:
AP sends many important messages to the ground station and we should support displaying these in different languages.  It's not only convenient but especially for important warnings it can be a safety issue

This request was received at the 2025 Japan Drone Expo

author: peterbarker
body:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/17244 is relevant.

You can't really "translate" `GCS_SEND_TEXT` messages as different languages want different substitution strings in different orders - so your string ("Your %s %d is > %u") may need to be `XYZZY %d YY >%u %s` in a different language.

The mavlink events interface is supposed to allow for this sort of thing.

author: fsaulo
title: DroneCAN GPS: Satellite count (num_sats) zeroed when no fix received
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

`satellites_visible` in `GPS2_RAW` is always zero for DroneCAN GPS2.

When using a DroneCAN device for GPS2, the `satellites_visible` field in the `GPS2_RAW` MAVLink topic consistently reports zero, even when a non-zero satellite count is provided in the simulated `gnss.Fix2` message.

**Version**
ArduCopter 4.5.7 (it is also present upstream)


**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Configure the secondary GPS as a DroneCAN device in SITL.
2. Simulate a `gnss.Fix2` message with a non-zero `sats_used` value.
3. Send the simulated `gnss.Fix2` message through a virtual CAN device to the DroneCAN GPS2.
4. Observe the `satellites_visible` field of the `GPS2_RAW` MAVLink topic.

**Expected Behavior:**

The `satellites_visible` field in `GPS2_RAW` should reflect the `sats_used` value from the received `gnss.Fix2` message, even if a full fix is not yet available.

**Observed Behavior:**
The `satellites_visible` field in `GPS2_RAW` remains zero.

**Root Cause Analysis:**
A preliminary analysis of `AP_GPS/AP_GPS_DroneCAN.cpp` ([line 336](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/9eed018bd77efc34cc48bb6c320170174ab88223/libraries/AP_GPS/AP_GPS_DroneCAN.cpp#L336)) indicates that `gnss.Fix2` messages are not processed unless a valid fix is present. This results in the `num_sats` variable being zeroed out.

**Impact:**
This behavior specifically affects the DroneCAN GPS driver and does not apply to other GPS input methods, which correctly report satellite counts even without a full fix. This can hinder debugging and accurate satellite visibility monitoring when using DroneCAN GPS.

author: peterbarker
body:
@fsaulo just to be sure here - you are aware that Fix2 is used by *all* GPSs, not just the second one, right?  It's not "fix for second GPS", it's "second generation of DroneCAN message to convey GPS data because we completely screwed up the first generation message".

ie. however this is working for the second GPS should apply just the same for the first GPS.

author: fsaulo
body:
Hi @peterbarker, thanks for taking a look at this, I really appreciate it.

> [...] you are aware that Fix2 is used by all GPSs, not just the second one, right? It's not "fix for second GPS", it's "second generation of DroneCAN message to convey GPS data because we completely screwed up the first generation message".

Yes, I'm aware. I realize now that I mentioned `GPS2_RAW` so emphatically, but to clarify, I was just referring to this particular experiment (minimal reproducible example).

For this point:
>Your waypoints are defining a vertical altitude profile your aircraft is supposed to be following - the vehicle is just making up for what it couldn't physically accomplish.

author: LzREngineering
title: Plane: Q>FW transition does not remove Q_TRIM_PITCH offset in some modes
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
I use the Q_TRIM_PITCH param to set an upward pitch on my VTOL plane in Q-modes, which helps get some 'free' lift in the wind and also gives more control authority for the vectored yaw. In FW modes this offset needs to be removed for level flight; PTCH_TRIM_DEG should be used in those modes to provide an equivalent function if needed (I have this set to 0). However, during certain transitions this does not happen:

- QLOITER>FBWA or FBWB = the Q_TRIM_PITCH offset is removed and the horizon uses PITCH_TRIM_DEG as an offset.

- QHOVER, QSTABILIZE>FBWA or FBWB = the Q_TRIM_PITCH offset does **not** change when the fixed wing mode is selected, generally resulting in a crash.

I would like to be able to build up speed in QSTABILIZE then switch to FBWA for a more 'manual' transition, however this currently won't work if the pitch offset does not change as it should.

Note, this also seemed to exist in beta versions of 4.6.0 but seems to still be present in the official release.

**Version**
4.6.0 official

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[ / ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
Tilt-rotor VTOL (4 tilting motors)

**Hardware type**
Matek h743 v3

**Logs**
[https://w-si.link/YtLaZAKPaa7Zipc28](https://w-si.link/YtLaZAKPaa7Zipc28)

author: IamPete1
body: Can you upload a dataflash log of your failed test please.

author: LzREngineering
body:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d45b69a-23fd-4769-b784-4de0b7d6787f)

The symptoms are actually slightly different when the flight mode is changed via RC: QHOVER>FBWA does work correctly in this case (previously I was changing flight modes in Mission Planner). The QSTABILIZE>FBWA change consistently does not work correctly.

log: [https://w-si.link/YtLaZAKPaa7Zipc28](https://w-si.link/YtLaZAKPaa7Zipc28)

author: IamPete1
body:
This is due to the controller that is used for the first stage of the transition.

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/baab8528d60baaeabd25c3ff2eaceb7c04a11ca2/ArduPlane/quadplane.cpp#L4271-L4279


There is no fundamental difference between modes, or the source of the mode change. It is due to being in throttle wait here:

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/baab8528d60baaeabd25c3ff2eaceb7c04a11ca2/ArduPlane/quadplane.cpp#L1673-L1681

If throttle wait is active transition is skipped so the FW controller is used. If throttle wait is not active (like when your really flying) then the transition goes into the airspeed wait phase. Since you never reach airspeed this never completes.

So, the code does seem to be working as it should. The goal of using the VTOL controllers for the first stage is to prevent any vector miss-alignments from causing large yaw changes. The FW controller has no vectored yaw control to prevent this.

I can see why the large pitch offset might cause issues in this case, we could look into ways to mitigate. It will clear once the transition is completed.
