author: rmackay9
title: AP_Camera/AP_Mount: add support for external camera gimbal manager
body:
ArduPilot already supports the [MAVLink Gimbalv2 protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/gimbal_v2.html#gimbal-manager-messages) but it is always essentially the "gimbal manager" (as opposed to the "gimbal device").

Some of the mavlink commands that AP accepts (as gimbal manager) are described on our development wiki

- [mount commands](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/mavlink-gimbal-mount.html)
- [camera commands](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/mavlink-camera.html)

We should also add support for ArduPilot to communicate with another gimbal manager.  This would most likely be a program running on a companion computer accepting the same sorts of mavlink messages as ArduPilot does (see above).

Implementing this would likely require writing a new driver (e.g. MNT1_TYPE = GimbalManager).  In many cases ArduPilot would just pass through mavlink commands received from the GCS to the gimbal manager but in cases where ArduPilot is the one providing targets it would need to create and send new mavlink messages.  This later case includes when the Pilot is attempting to control the camera gimbal using RC or when a mission is being executed that contains camera or gimbal commands.

author: Lqs66
title: Copter: Unchecked range of parameter PILOT_SPEED_UP may cause drone crash
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

I noticed that the range of parameter PILOT_SPEED_UP is checked in PreArm check, but after takeoff, some flight modes (e.g., loiter, alt_hold, poshold, and zigzag, etc.) are not checked with this parameter, which could lead to the drone not having enough lift and crashing.

See
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/865cffa5f2a850f892ab43def2d4ad21b8a9adca/ArduCopter/mode_loiter.cpp#L109
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/865cffa5f2a850f892ab43def2d4ad21b8a9adca/ArduCopter/mode_poshold.cpp#L90
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/865cffa5f2a850f892ab43def2d4ad21b8a9adca/ArduCopter/mode_sport.cpp#L69
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/865cffa5f2a850f892ab43def2d4ad21b8a9adca/ArduCopter/mode_zigzag.cpp#L311
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/865cffa5f2a850f892ab43def2d4ad21b8a9adca/ArduCopter/mode_althold.cpp#L43
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/865cffa5f2a850f892ab43def2d4ad21b8a9adca/ArduCopter/mode_flowhold.cpp#L246

**Replay**

Run SITL and enter the following command in the mavproxy terminal:
1. `mode stabilize`;
2. `arm throttle`;
3. `rc 3 1500`;
4. `mode poshold` or another of the above modes;
5. `param set PILOT_SPEED_UP -1000`.
Then drone crashes to the ground.

**Version**

I have only verified this on Copter-4.4, but the latest 4.6 version also has the above problem.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[X] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
SITL

**Hardware type**
N/A

**Logs**
None

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @Lqs66,

Thanks for the investigation and report.

We could add protection but there are a lot of parameters that, when set to invalid values, could cause the vehicle to crash.  There will be a lot of extra code added to AP if we check every single one.  We could argue that this is a misconfiguration and it is possible to lock down parameters to stop users from changing them to invalid values.  I feel this might be a better solution than adding protection everywhere.  Also what is invalid depends upon the vehicle.  For example, it's possible to make a vehicle crash by setting some of the PID parameters to low values, but these PID values are perfectly valid for another vehicle.

Here is the Lua script for 4.7 that helps locking down parameters.  I have not actually tested it myself yet

- [script](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Scripting/applets/param-set.lua)
- [description](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Scripting/applets/param-set.md)

> 
> We could add protection but there are a lot of parameters that, when set to invalid values, could cause the vehicle to crash. There will be a lot of extra code added to AP if we check every single one. We could argue that this is a misconfiguration and it is possible to lock down parameters to stop users from changing them to invalid values. I feel this might be a better solution than adding protection everywhere. Also what is invalid depends upon the vehicle. For example, it's possible to make a vehicle crash by setting some of the PID parameters to low values, but these PID values are perfectly valid for another vehicle.
> 
> Here is the Lua script for 4.7 that helps locking down parameters. I have not actually tested it myself yet
> 
> * [script](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Scripting/applets/param-set.lua)
> * [description](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Scripting/applets/param-set.md)

Hi,

I understand the concern about adding extensive parameter checks increasing code complexity in the AP system. However, I'm inclined to propose integrating parameter range protection directly within the AP_ParamT-related classes.

My idea is to load both the default values and their valid ranges for parameters directly from the configuration file into the flight controller. This way, if a user attempts to modify a parameter with an invalid value, the system can automatically reset it to its default value based on the predefined range.

The benefits of this approach are:

Centralized Management: This tightly couples parameter validity checks with the parameter's own data structure, avoiding dispersed and independent check code for each parameter.
User-Friendly: When a user inputs an invalid value, the system can provide immediate feedback and automatic correction, preventing potential system instability or crashes.
Prevent Runtime Issues: Even "misconfigurations" can be prevented at the earliest possible stage, significantly reducing the flight risks associated with invalid parameters.
While this approach would add some logic to the AP_ParamT classes, I believe this centralized, automated protection mechanism offers a more robust and immediate safety guarantee compared to relying solely on external lockdown scripts.

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @Lqs66,

OK, we've talked about this kind of thing before but we've always instead relied on the GCSs to implement the protection.  Mission Planner for example has a "Password Protect Config" checkbox on the Config / Planner page ([see here](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/prevent-access-to-parameters-and-configuration-from-fc/109545/9))

The min/max values can also be different for each vehicle and putting the table of min/max values into C++ will certainly consume a significant amount of flash space which will almost certainly mean that other features will need to be sacrificed in order for the protection to fit.

Anyway, if you want to try and implement it, the dev team will certainly review it

BTW, I think a modified version of the lua script linked above would actually have a better chance of being accepted.

author: LupusTheCanine
body: @rmackay9 IIRC we have about 1.2k parameters, a lot of them would benefit from simple checks like >=0 or <=0, we could simply reject arming if any parameter is out of range (unless appropriate flag is set). With 1 byte per parameter to store reference to limits and two or three arrays for limits (one per variable size 8,16,32 bits) we probably could get away with about 3kB of memory footprint, less if we can keep the tables not in RAM.

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @LupusTheCanine,

Thanks for that feedback.  I agree that a 3kb memory cost would probably be worth it.  So far we've seen 98 bytes of flash for a single check which would add up to >100k of flash which is quite a lot.  If someone can implement it efficiently so it's more efficient in terms of flash cost then I think the idea has a chance.

author: MichelleRos
body:
> Methodic Configurator recommending 800Hz

That definitely does not sound like a good idea. Especially if that's as part of the initial setup. A lot of flight controllers can't handle 800 Hz, and even though you do have an H7, you might want to use the extra CPU for other things - there are very few vehicles where this fast loop rate makes enough of a difference to be worth it (mostly small FPV quads). 

I'd definitely recommend leaving it at the default 400 Hz and just getting it hovering stably first before experimenting with different loop rates. One of the reasons is issues like this which only turn up at higher loop rates. Even with an FPV quad, I'd recommend getting a stable hover at 400 Hz (and finishing the setup) before raising the loop rate. I have yet to come across a copter that won't at least hover stably at 400 Hz (and I fly a 50g whoop on ArduPilot as one of my vehicles).

As for the error, your third IMU without fast sample is now running at only 1000 Hz, which is less than 1.8 times the loop rate of 800: 1.8*800=1440. AP has a pre-arm check to make sure the IMU rate is at least 1.8 times your loop rate. That is the error you're seeing. So if you want to keep such a fast loop rate, you either need to turn fast sampling back on, or turn that 3rd IMU off completely - which may not be a good idea, because, at least in the Cube Orange, it is the only non-isolated IMU, and there are some failure modes that can affect only the isolated IMUs - that's why that third one is there.

author: Ryanf55
title: ArduPlane - Allow terrain lookahead to work for lawnmower AGL missions
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Use case: Fixed AGL mapping (lawmower) in steep terrain with TERRAIN_FOLLOW=1

When a plane receives a mission, if there is a hill in the middle of a lawnmower that is steep, then lookahead does not register the hill until after the vehicle is too close to the hill. This results in an undershoot of the mission plan, and a crash into terrain.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Change `float Plane::lookahead_adjustment(void)` to consider the projected nominal mission path. If lookahead is needed, the plane should start climbing earlier, so we don't have to resort to "Can't make that climb" to save the vehicle. The plane should bias being above the mission points, or have some option bit to configure that because being to low can mean a crash.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Post-process the AGL flight plan, use a companion computer or Lua, and feed the autopilot intermediate waypoints in absolute frame.

**Platform**

[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[x] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
Here is a discontinuity in desired height as soon as the current lookahead detects a hill in the flight path. This is from a partner vehicle on a real survey mission.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d88a1cf8-d388-45c4-bcd7-dcda4d4d1c2c)

**Steps to reproduce**

./Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v Plane --console --map --custom-location "39.9948854, -105.2789980, 1786, 0"
param set TERRAIN_FOLLOW 1

Other trace from the discussion thread:

```
validate_structures:526: Validating structures
Loaded defaults from Documents/GitHub/ardupilot/Tools/autotest/default_params/gazebo-zephyr.parm
warning: arduplane was compiled with optimization - stepping may behave oddly; variables may not be available.
Process 11439 stopped
* thread #1, queue = 'com.apple.main-thread', stop reason = EXC_BAD_INSTRUCTION (code=1, subcode=0x1e201863)
    frame #0: 0x0000000100003f84 arduplane`Plane::calc_speed_scaler(this=0x00000001002eecb8) at Attitude.cpp:19:13 [opt]
   16  	        const float airspeed_min = MAX(aparm.airspeed_min, MIN_AIRSPEED_MIN);
   17  	        const float scale_min = MIN(0.5, g.scaling_speed / (2.0 * aparm.airspeed_max));

After some trouble shooting, I'm 90% sure this is the issue: 
https://developer.arm.com/documentation/dui0773/l/Coding-Considerations/Floating-point-division-by-zero-errors-in-C-and-C---code

author: clydemcqueen
title: Sub: disarm + arm while in surftrak (range hold) mode will cause sub to dive
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

If you disarm + arm a sub while running surftrak with a rangefinder target set, the sub will dive until it hits the seafloor.

Steps to reproduce in SITL with the standard parameters:
* arm throttle
* rc 3 1200
* descend below -1m
* rc 3 1500
* mode 21
* disarm
* arm
* the sub will dive until it hits the seafloor

What appears to be happening:

In normal surftrak operation the position controller z offset is the current terrain altitude estimate (altitude - rangefinder).

When you disarm, alt_hold.run_pre() calls position_control->relax_U_controller(), which sets the z offset to 0.

When you re-arm, the z offset is still 0 but surftrak expects it to be the seafloor altitude (around -5000 cm in SITL). The sub will dive trying to achieve an offset value of -5000, and will hit the seafloor.

A workaround is to switch to any other mode, then back to surftrak.

AFAICT this has been there since the original surftrak PR. It affects all versions of sub 4.5 and later. I'm surprised that nobody has reported this, but I suppose disarm + arm while running surftrak isn't all that common.

Fix + autotest to follow.

Sub 4.5, master.

author: eufrizz
title: Fixing ExternalNav + GPS
body:
## Bug report
(previously discussed on Discord under the partner-theseus channel)
**Issue details**
Ardupilot is fusing external nav and GPS data when only external nav is selected as the input source.
From my understanding, only one of the two sources should be used for position at a time, as defined by EK3_SRC_POSXY and EK3_SRC_VELXY. However, if external nav is selected and GPS data is available, the filter incorrectly fuses this data too. This prevents flying on external nav with the ability to switch to GPS as a backup.
It manifests as an unstable position with high variances and resetting behaviour, if the two position estimates diverge - which will be the case with sources like VIO.
The difference can be demonstrated running a replay log with and without GPS data:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/081b7e71-1f6e-4498-878f-d1f117d8246d)
(notice the jagged position and very high innovations with resets)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8eff5b9-3618-4594-8405-340dce3be129)
(notice the smooth position and much lower innovations - though still a bit high)

Upon inspecting AP_NavEKF3_PosVelFusion.cpp, it seems the if statements in FuseVelPosNED are just not correctly written to separate external nav from GPS. What happens is that FuseVelPosNED is called with `extNavVelToFuse == gpsDataToFuse == fuseVelData == fusePosData == 0`, but with `fuseHgtData == 1` (presumably due to only having baro data). Thus when an if statement like the following is encountered:
```
if (extNavVelToFuse) {
                obs_data_chk = sq(constrain_ftype(extNavVelDelayed.err, 0.05f, 5.0f)) + sq(frontend->extNavVelVarAccScale * accNavMag);
            } else
#endif
            {
                obs_data_chk = sq(constrain_ftype(frontend->_gpsHorizVelNoise, 0.05f, 5.0f)) + sq(frontend->gpsNEVelVarAccScale * accNavMag);
            }
```

The else statement is triggered, incorrectly, incorporating GPS data when in fact external nav is selected. There needs to be an extra check for gpsDataToFuse or something like that.

~~Have fixed it in a branch, will add a pull request tomorrow, I published this issue prematurely by accident lol.~~
PR here: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/30080

author: rmackay9
title: Flash ECC handling problem on boards where params are stored in flash
body:
During AP-4.6 beta testing we discovered that we have at least one issue with our flash ECC handling on boards where the parameters are stored in flash (e.g. the same place where the firmware is stored).

This issue was discovered on some TBS boards where the user found that occasionally the board's firmware would be cleared forcing the user to reload the firmware.

The bug in our ECC handling is that we check for errors in the parameter area (which as mentioned is also in flash) but then clear the firmware and leave the parameter area untouched.  This means that theoretically the ECC check should trigger again after the firmware is reloaded.  Strangely this is not the case though, the ECC check is not triggering again

Related PR:

- PR fix for 4.6: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/30031

author: rmackay9
title: Hardfault on arming if CAN_SLCAN_CPORT set non-zero and have SERIAL6_PROTOCOL set to 22
body:
@robertlong13 found a hardfault bug in 4.5, but I think it's still present in master. Fortunately, this one can't happen in flight, just on the transition from disarmed to armed if you have SLCAN set up.

If you accidentally leave CAN_SLCAN_CPORT set non-zero and have SERIAL6_PROTOCOL set to 22 (as is currently default on Cubes still; we actually usually have it set to 2, but we have to use SLCAN temporarily to flash/configure our Currawong ESCs), there's a chance of a hardfault every time you arm. I hit this while doing some motor tests today.

update_slcan_port gets called from the main thread (see attached stack trace image) when writing servos/escs, and sets CANIface::_port to nullptr when armed. Meanwhile, the DroneCAN thread might be in the middle of a function that has to dereference CANIface::_port (see my crash dump analysis screenshot).

This is an easy thing for me to mitigate. We already don't usually use SLCAN, so we just have to make sure to use the temporary setup method using CAN_SLCAN_SERNUM (which I wasn't aware of until digging in to this) instead of setting SERIAL6_PROTOCOL to 22.

But, we probably should fix this bug anyway. I'm thinking, instead of clearing _port, we could introduce a flag and replace all the _port == nullptr early returns to use that flag instead. Would that work? Or do I just huck a semaphore in there instead?

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db09d658-268f-4a54-a978-3254b1e96b2a)

author: rishabsingh3003
title: AP_NavEKF3: Position reset should not use GPS when using ExtNav
body:
Currently, when a position reset is triggered within EKF3 (due to prolonged rejection of the position estimate), the filter resets to a "default" position source:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_NavEKF3/AP_NavEKF3_PosVelFusion.cpp#L835

If GPS is available, it is automatically chosen as the reset source. This behaviour is problematic when flying with External Navigation (e.g., VISO), because the external navigation solution may have significantly drifted from the absolute GPS position. When the reset occurs to the GPS location, any subsequent ExtNav observations are likely to be rejected due to large innovation values.

This results in the EKF continuously resetting its position, preventing proper fusion of external navigation observations and leading to unstable or unusable state estimation.

author: patrickelectric
title: Add Zenoh integration
body:
## Feature request

[Zenoh](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh) is a mature framework (5 years old) maintained by [Eclipse foundation](https://www.eclipse.org/) and [ZettaScale](https://www.zettascale.tech/), it outperforms MQTT, Kafka, and DDS. From a [performance study](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.09419), it can achieve “up to 67 Gbps on single-machine tests and 51 Gbps on multiple-machine tests with a 100 GbE network when the peer mode was used. For the largest performance gaps in bitrates, Zenoh even shows one to two orders of magnitude improvement on MQTT and Kafka (more than 50x and 100x in both scenarios) and could double the throughput of Cyclone DDS. For the closest numbers, Zenoh can still be several times the performance compared to the others. For latency, Zenoh has lower numbers than MQTT and Kafka. Although DDS obtains shorter latency than Zenoh does for the single-machine scenario due to its use of the UDP multicast transport mechanism, we can see that the microcontroller implementation of Zenoh, i.e. Zenoh-pico, which has already realized the UDP multicast transport, can perform better than DDS in all cases. This capability will be supported by all Zenoh implementations in the future (2023).”

[ROS2 study for a RWM alternative](https://discourse.ros.org/uploads/short-url/o9ihvSjCwB8LkzRklpKdeesRTDi.pdf), Zenoh was chosen to be the DDS alternative after being compared to [Cyphal](https://opencyphal.org/), DDS, [eCal](https://github.com/eclipse-ecal/ecal), [Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/intro), [LCM](http://lcm-proj.github.io/lcm/), MQTT, [NNG](https://github.com/nanomsg/nng), OPC-UA, [TCPROS](http://wiki.ros.org/ROS/TCPROS) and [ZeroMQ](https://zguide.zeromq.org/docs/chapter1/).

Zenoh already supports officially [Rust](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh), [C++](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-cpp), C ([embedded](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-pico) or [not](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-c)), [Python](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-python), REST, [Java](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-java), [Kotlin](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-kotlin), [TypeScript](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-ts) (now stable), [C#](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-csharp) and [Go](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-go) (both in hold), with bridges for [ROS](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-plugin-ros2dds)1/2, [DDS](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-plugin-dds), [MQTT](https://mqtt.org/) and support for multiple storage plugins such as [influxdb](https://www.influxdata.com/), [s3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3), [rocksdb](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb) and [filesystem](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-backend-filesystem). It also provides a Wireshark [plugin](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-dissector) for network development / debug.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
No.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Zenoh integration in ArduPilot.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
AP_DDS is a possible alternative.

**Platform**
[x] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**

- Just released 1.0, a stable API that will be maintained and supported, also designed with extensions points in the protocol to be backward compatible if necessary.
- Has QoS[1](https://speakerdeck.com/kydos/qos-dds-vs-zenoh),[2](https://docs.rs/zenoh/latest/zenoh/qos/index.html)
- Was projected to be very efficient on the wire, very low overhead, close to 10s bytes, close to bluetooth that uses 8. Topic names are mapped to integers.
Any message is used as a keep alive message, if nothing happens a keep alive is used every 10s.
- There are applications running in Time Sensitive Networking (TSN) [time sliced]

Note: I believe that @khancyr and @Ryanf55 would be interested on that 
Ref: #23424

title: Vector3p output of position from _inav.get_position_ned_m();
body:
## Feature request

The one area of our code that doesn't support long range resolution is our measurement of position. We use Vector3f for all other positions other than our reference.

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/8ad6e96bf75e04203ff6a67b887cf8ce77c57b49/libraries/AC_AttitudeControl/AC_PosControl.cpp#L669

author: timtuxworth
body:
This is a known bug, specifically the Terrain lookahead function doesn't correctly detect high terrain between the current location and next WP. This will also happen in an AUTO mission.

In my "Terrain Avoid" Lua script, I re-implemented the terrain lookahead to detect this and then to react by:
1. Attempting to pitch up over the "hump"
2. If that doesn't work, attempting to "loiter up" to gain altitude to get over the hump. This looks left/right to pick the best way to go to avoid hitting other high terrain.
3. Worst case, engaging the VTOL motors to quickly gain altitude

This only works with a quadplane, but except for #3, this would also apply to a regular fixed wing.

My PR for this is pending real world testing. I've tested it extensively in SITL.
#28625

author: VermennikovMV
body:
ArduPilot (4.3+) publishes two BATTERY_STATUS messages over MAVLink - id = 0 and id = 1 - each containing an array of 6 (or up to 12) cell voltages.
The second battery data is ‘lost’ to Mission Planner if at least one of the conditions is met:
   1. Identical BATT_SERIAL_NUM (i.e. equal to the same number): the firmware decides that the monitors belong to the same battery 
   and writes both cell portions to the same pack.
   2. Old MP build (< 1.3.82): before patch [#3105](https://github.com/ArduPilot/MissionPlanner/blob/master/ChangeLog.txt?utm_source=chatgpt.com) the HUD interface had only one Battery widget and ignored the id field, so the 
   second batch would overwrite the first (there was just a bug that Batt1 was sending packets with the same id as Batt2).
   3. New MP, but the widget is not enabled: after the edit, the ‘Battery 2’ widget needs to be ticked on the HUD (see screenshot).
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a790d4fe-88e8-46df-b5bc-7cc414bc4ebd)

For example, these are the parameters I have set:
BATT_MONITOR = 7
BATT2_MONITOR = 7
BATT_SERIAL_NUM = 1
BATT2_SERIAL_NUM = 2 

Additionally MP does not have fields for cycle count yet, so even the latest version does not draw them, although the firmware passes them. If you want such functionality to be added, I can make a commit to the MissionPlanner repository with a proposal for new functionality.

body:
Hi VermennikovMV
I think I have not conveyed the issue in the right manner.
Please see the screenshot.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/801218c6-181c-45fb-a2a6-a7eb5ed2e811)

I have connected two 6s Battery monitors to the FC. And all the parameters are being shown correctly in the HUD as well as in the Status Tab.
The issue that we are facing is, we are able to see cell voltages of the first monitor BAT1 only in the status tab. The cell voltages of BAT2 are not being shown anywhere. What we are expecting is, the cell voltages from the second monitor should start from Cell 7-Cell 12.
Is it possible to initiate this change in MP or should I change some configuration in MP? 

Also it would be great if can make a commit to the MissionPlanner to add Cycle Count field.

author: wyunc
title: Vehicle incorrectly reports waypoint reached after flying continuously away from it
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

I loaded a square mission identical to issue  #26519. When I set the parameter MOT_PWM_MIN to 2000, the copter continuously moves forward, getting progressively farther away from the waypoint, which is expected behavior. However, after traveling some distance in this direction, ArduPilot suddenly and incorrectly declares that the waypoint has been reached and switches to the next one. After continuing for some time, it again mistakenly marks this next waypoint as reached.

I suspect this issue is similar to the "fast waypoint" bug described in issue #26519. I've confirmed that the previously buggy code from #26520 has been patched in the version of ArduCopter I'm currently testing, yet the problem persists.

Additionally, setting the parameter MOT_SPIN_MIN to 1 also triggers the same bug.

Perhaps there is some undiscovered default value accumulating when calculating the distance from the vehicle to the waypoint reference point?

**Version**
4.7.0-dev

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[X] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @wyunc,

Thanks for the report.  It's funny that we merged PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/26520 but didn't close issue https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/26519.  I suspect that was just an administrative oversight.

This report does definitely seem like a duplicate of https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/26519 but your testing indicates that we may not have fixed the bug completely

Similarly, after a certain amount of time, ArduPilot incorrectly reported WP2 as reached, then switched navigation to the next waypoint (WP3). However, the rover continued circling at the same distant location and, again after some time, incorrectly reported WP3 as reached—even though it never approached WP3.

body:
So I've been trying to reproduce this without luck.

@wyunc when you say, "getting further from the waypoint", is this moving directly away from the waypoint?

ArduCopter can consider a waypoint complete *even if you are getting further away from the waypoint* if you cross the "finish line".  Here's an example of a mission which progresses once the vehicle passes the finish line, even 'though the vehicle is getting further from the current waypoint: 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e406c41-206b-4a78-a77a-065c858dd5f4)

(this is not a bug, it's a feature ;-) )

When travelling 3->4 there's a finish line perpendicular to the edge between 3 and 4 (in this case)

I've created https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/29945 which you can use to reproduce the above image.

I'm unable to reproduce your problem given your instructions, *apart* from this finish-line mechanism.

@wyunc could you provide more details about this "completes waypoint even 'though it's getting fruther away" problem, please?  It would be nice if you could modify the autotest I've created in that PR to reproduce the problem you're seeing - so when we fix it it stays fixed!

author: lthall
body:
Ok, the first thing is we are looking at an aircraft that is unable to control it's position, so the only thing we are looking at here is that the fact that fast waypoints don't currenlty check the instantainous distance to the waypoint to declare we have reached the waypoint.

Fast waypoints are treated as just one point on a kinimatic path. As such the WP_Nav libary manages the position along the kinimatic path, through fast waypoints, to ensure the target position doesn't move further along the path than the aircraft is currently positioned. This is done correctly here.

This is confusing because while the aircraft position is not under control, it is drifting in the general direction of the specified path. As such the instantainouos target along that path is moved only slightly in front of the minimum cross track distance. 

This will continue until the direction of the path, and therefore the target location, moves away from the current aircraft location. At this point the speed along the track will decay exponentially towards zero. As this is an exponential decay it won't ever reach zero so we will still move towards the next waypoint, but at an ever slower rate. This is the change made in #26520, previously it could only slow down to 10%.

I wouldn't call this a bug as the code is working exactly as we intend. Instead I would ask some questions:
- Do we want to slow down the progression along the path if the cross track error becomes large compared to the waypoint radius. 
- Should we change the slowing along the path to a liniar rather than exponential decay so we do come to a complete stop.
- Should we abort a mission and call some sort of failsafe if we can't control position past some threashold. (especially as this is required to demonstrate this behaviour)

I would suggest we close this issue as it is more realisticly shown in #26519.

author: rmackay9
body:
OK, I'll go ahead and close this issue.

Thanks @wyunc for the report and this does confirm that we still have an issue.

author: Ryanf55
title: AP_DDS: Support throttle suppress in GUIDED mode for plane
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I can't use GUIDED mode to turn off the throttle on a motor glider using either mavlink or DDS.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Guided should respect overrides so you can suppress throttle.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Adding offboard mode

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**

I want to ensure the motor is off, commanding target speed does not do that. 
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/4337
This previous issue says that disabling overrides in guided was by design, but this is limiting guided to a subset of the control that other modes have.

See `SoaringController::suppress_throttle` which requires a reference to the TECS controller. Maybe guided can get a reference to TECS too? The tecs controller is private to the Plane object.

**Future enhancement**

Give DDS full throttle control in GUIDED

author: peterbarker
body:
The referenced issue https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/4337 doesn't have anything to do with servo outputs.  Overriding your throttle to be zero won't make an inch of difference.

I'm not sure this is something that should go into "guided".  Perhaps into that new "offboard" mode I've been hearing about?

author: Ryanf55
body:
Approach discussed today: set_gliding_state ROS -> AP_DDS-> AP_ExternalControl -> AP_ExternalControl_Plane -> plane.TECS_controller.set_gliding_requested_flag

See https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/14643 and https://github.com/Jaeyoung-Lim/mav-soaring/tree/master for how [POSITION_TARGET_LOCAL_NED](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#POSITION_TARGET_LOCAL_NED) was used to suppress throttle.

Also mentioned - we should remove the gliding requested flag on mode exit so you don't get stuck without motor if the plane failsafes.

author: Ryanf55
title: Warn if using BLHeli 32.9 or lower
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

BLHeli 32.10 has fixed a major issue with unintentional motor spoolups.

I've seen multiple instances of spoolups, or disarming and the motors not stopping because they detect the wrong protocol.

This is a major safety issue for anyone using BLHeli 32.9 or less. Multiple users have posted to BLHeli complaining of injuries with unintentional spoolups too.


**Describe the solution you'd like**

On bootup, ArduPilot can try to communicate with DSHOT to retrieve the blheli version. If the version is not 32.10, a warning can be issued. ArduPilot could request the version and warn users that if they fly 32.9 or less, they could consider to throw their ESC's away and replace them with something safer (like AM32), or advanced users can reflash them.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Not warning users their ESC's are dangerous. Vendors could recall ESC's, but they won't. 
We could also warn in the wiki, but most people won't connect the configurator or know their version.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**

https://github.com/bitdump/BLHeli/issues/743

https://github.com/bitdump/BLHeli/releases/tag/Rev32.10

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4cfe2e09-8d5d-4b20-b01b-b5f8f318269f)

author: LzREngineering
title: Plane: TILT angle only logged for FL and FR
body:
## Feature request

Request based on 4.6.0 beta 5.

In the logs of a Tilt Rotor VTOL plane, three values are currently recorded for TILT servos: .Tilt (overall) .FR and .FL

Whilst this is sufficient for tri-tilt rotors, in cases where there are more than two tilt servos there may be some benefit in recording the demanded tilt angle from every tilt servo (as defined by Q_TILT_MASK?). Would it be possible to have angular values recorded for all tilt servos eg TILT.RL and TILT.RR (possibly more?)

I know it's also possible to derive the angle from the RCOU log message using the servo max/min pwm parameters - as an alternative, could a new preset be added to UAV Log viewer to enable this?

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[ /] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: IamPete1
body: The front and rear are the same in all VTOL modes, the only difference is if you have forward flight vectoring enabled.

author: LzREngineering
body:
> The front and rear are the same in all VTOL modes, the only difference is if you have forward flight vectoring enabled.

I thought that may be the case. So to confirm, TILT.FL=TILT.RL and TILT.FR=TILT.RR? Or to put it another way, all tilting motors on one side of the plane will tilt by the same amount. Under what circumstances would forward flight vectoring created a difference front to rear? looking at my logs, all servos seem to be tilting forwards by 'roughly' the same amount during forward flight. If it can be confirmed that this is alway the case, then I agree this request is not necessary. 
However, could the description for these log meassages in the documentation be updated to reflect the fact that it's the angle of all left side/all right side tilt motors?

author: IamPete1
body:
> Under what circumstances would forward flight vectoring created a difference front to rear?

`Q_TILT_FIX_GAIN` none zero. Then the front and rear tilts will differentially vector in forward flight for pitch control.

author: LzREngineering
body:
> > Under what circumstances would forward flight vectoring created a difference front to rear?
> 
> `Q_TILT_FIX_GAIN` none zero. Then the front and rear tilts will differentially vector in forward flight for pitch control.

In that situation, would the rear tilts remain locked at zero (fully forward)? - if not, there may still be a benefit in recording TILT.RL and TILT.RR meassages.

author: IamPete1
body:
> In that situation, would the rear tilts remain locked at zero (fully forward)? - if not, there may still be a benefit in recording TILT.RL and TILT.RR meassages.

No, to pitch up for example the fronts would tilt up and the rears tilt down.

body:

IMO as there are situations where tilt can vary front-to-rear as well as left-to-right I still think it would be useful to have TILT logged for each tilting motor. However I woudn't see it as a high priority as this information can be derived in post-analysis.

One thing I was looking to do was display the TILT on the OSD - not sure if that is currently possible?

body:
If it's working the way I think it is, the code is just dropping a WP for the follow vehicle to fly to, it keeps dropping new "pins" ahead as the target moves, so it never catches up, but if the target stops moving the pin will stop moving and standard "loiter at WP" logic kicks in, which is a circle around the point.

On Plane, I found this behavior so annoying that I stopped using it altogether and I'm now directing the follow vehicle using heading, not WP.

author: rubenp02
title: Plane: Pitch stick mixing doesn't conserve energy
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
Stick mixing operates by changing the attitude demand, which is fine for roll but can have really bad consequences for pitch, as the system is decoupled from the TECS. If a stick nudge is held long enough, an overspeed or a stall WILL occur. This could be worked around by weighting the mix with the flight energy, but ideally the pitch mixing logic should live in the TECS itself and operate by nudging the altitude rate instead of the pitch directly.

Since there's a removed "DIRECT" stick mixing mode that falls back to the FBW logic, this could become the way to use the current stick mixing logic with FBWA-style pitch control, and a new "FBWBMixing" mode that uses the TECS-based pitch mixing could replace the "FBWMixing" mode, and be the new default. The "DIRECT" mode would be renamed to "FBWAMixing".

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[X] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: Georacer
body:
Hi Ruben!

In general, we consider it important that each flight mode flies as expected.
For example, MANUAL mode is expected to provide direct control to the servos.
FBWA is expected to map directly to roll/pitch angles.
And FBWB is expected to govern roll angle and climb rate.

It's not clear to me to which mode this style of mixing that you describe would/should apply?

author: rubenp02
body:
It would apply to all modes that provide stick mixing support, such as Auto, Guided, Loiter, etc...

The only difference between it and the current "FBWMixing" default stick mixing mode would be that the pitch stick would nudge the TECS rate instead of the pitch demand like it currently does.

author: Georacer
body:
Ah, I got confused with servo mixers, my apologies.

I must admit I haven't used stick mixing much. But indeed currently I would expect them to act upon angle, not climb rate.
This is simpler, because the attitude controller doesn't hold a lot of state. Whereas it would be harder to reset TECS back onto the original trajectory.

I agree that an 'FBWBMixer" would be the safer option.

author: rubenp02
body:
I've taken a shot at a safe, FBW-B style pitch stick nudge, and it turns out it is not trivial like I thought. The idea was to implement it as a rate nudge (a given pitch stick position commands a rate that is added or subtracted to the current rate), but since the setpoint of the system is an altitude and the rate is its derivative, that's not really possible.

Here's a diagram of the possible behaviours of this approach:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cc3cc72-daac-4b33-a642-c16d855dedd8)

In this example, a 3 m/s rate nudge is added and held, which of course means the aircraft should climb at 3 m/s. But the problems arise when the nudge is changed (in the example, increased to 5 m/s):

- Pink option: Discontinuities in the altitude demand occur when the nudge changes. The altitude reference point must be reset on stick release, which introduces even more discontinuities. The longer the nudge is held, the worse this behavior gets.
- Blue option: Starts a new rate path on nudge change. Among other issues, this causes an initial move in the opposite direction when the nudge is increased. If the previous nudge was held for a long time, this deviation can be very large and highly undesirable.
- Green option: It's the only one that doesn't introduce discontinuities, but effectively makes the nudge persistent, defeating its purpose. If it's reset to zero when the stick is released, going from a minimal nudge to zero would cause a large correction with no way to immediately undo.

Furthermore, in practice, the stick inputs would be continuous and noisy, which makes pink and blue even less viable. 

So the only somewhat viable option is nudging the altitude instead of the rate, which would of course have limits and probably feel quite unintuitive to control. Because the existing pitch stick mixing is very likely to cause stalls/overspeeds if overused (and a stall in an autonomous mode is very bad news, as the attitude control tends to make the aircraft spin), maybe a way to disable pitch stick mixing would be a good idea? By the way, the current pitch mixing has a bug in it: it doubles the stick input on max deflection in an attempt to ensure full override of any pitch setpoint, but since pitch limits are typically asymmetric, this can result in cases where the override is not fully achievable.

Edit: At least some sort of warning text in the documentation and/or STICK_MIXING param. description should be added IMO.

author: LupusTheCanine
body:
1. We probably need TECS rework to support more "edge of envelope" though automatically finding max flight path angle velocity will likely be quite hard without a characterization flight and there would be need to update it if weight/performance changes.
2. I would do a combination ±0.9 is either linear or exponential altitude offset and edges of the range are maximum vertical speed climb/descent. If we exceed offset range switch to half range vertical speed control (unrestricted climb/descent) where midpoint means return to setpoint at maximum rate, ±0.5 maintains altitude and ±1 moves away from setpoint at maximum rate. Switchback to offset mode would occur when demanded offset would be greater than current offset (minding the sign of correction).    
I would provide option to allow or inhibit unrestricted climb/descent though I am not sure which would be better.

PS modern RC systems aren't that noisy.

author: rubenp02
body: I agree with point 1 but I a simpler and more immediate solution should probably be implemented in the meantime, no? As for point 2, I like the idea in general (although maybe it's a bit too complex to be immediately intuitive? Not sure), but there's currently no non-hacky way to command a specific climb/sink rate, and the hacky ones can't be cleanly integrated with the standard altitude control without introducing height demand discontinuities which I think introduce too much potential for bugs/unpredictable behavior. As for the noisy input, I was mostly referring to the jitter in user input, not to RC noise.

author: peterbarker
body:
The current "damn the controllers, full speed [up]" approach is there quite on purpose.

We don't involve the controllers as if auto or loiter or whatnot isn't doing what you expect and you need to control the vehicle - you *really* shouldn't be involving the controllers in responding to those inputs.  This is how we get ridiculous i-term buildups and whatnot when doing stick-mixing.  It's known and expected :-)

We in fact balance things so that the operator can always override the controllers.

Do you think that reasoning is sound?  It's not neat, it's very messy, but it is *also* extremely reliable.

author: rubenp02
body: I completely agree that the current FBWMixing mode is useful for what you say, i.e., emergency situations where there's an immediate obstacle, the aircraft has lost control, etc. In those situations, the energy control is of course a secondary issue. I also agree that its very reliable because its behaviour (aside from the stick mapping bug) is simple and predictable, whereas a safer version probably wouldn't. My main issue is that, as it is right now, you'd want to disable it for well tuned, production aircraft, because its an inherently unsafe feature. Since the roll part is fully safe and also nice to have for reasons other than emergency situations/obstacle avoidance, IMO at least that should be possible to keep enabled.

author: tridge
title: IOMCU - surfaces not moving
body:
We have had a report of control surfaces not moving on IOMCU connected servos in a pre-flight check.
@peterbarker and I have also seen this once on an aircraft in Canberra, although we did not capture a log (we had assumed it was a hardware issue and were very surprised to find a reboot fixed it).
My current guess is that one of the configuration registers in the IOMCU is not being transferred correctly. For example, if PAGE_REG_SETUP_CHANNEL_MASK was transferred incorrectly then it would cause exactly these symptoms, as it would disable some channels. These type of config registers are only sent when they change, and the transport CRC is quite weak (just 8 bit). It is possible that a bad transfer could cause this issue.
In the log from the affected user SERVO_GPIO_MASK is set to 15360, which is Servo 11|Servo 12|Servo 13|Servo 14. A single bit corruption in this value would cause the symptoms of one aileron not moving.
I think we need some way of confirming the correct configuration:
Maybe a 32 bit CRC of all expected config registers and re-send if not correct? Maybe only do this when disarmed?
We could store a mirror of the expected config values in the FMU, and have a 1Hz fetch of the current CRC on the IOMCU, triggering a resend if needed.
Alternatively we could just have a list of registers we confirm in a cyclic fashion while disarmed?

author: rmackay9

author: tridge

it would have to be a 2 bit error. With line noise this is unlikely I think, but what about clocking error?

body:
A clocking error should cause UART framing errors too. Do we have any way of recording errors on the IOMCU link so that we can see if affected boards are seeing caught errors?

I recognize this particular message is sent once, but lots of messages are sent to fly the aircraft and uncaught corruption in any of them could be bad. But they should also occasionally get errors too if there is a problem with the link.

author: kcx1207
title: Yaw rate control issue: large attitude error combined with high yaw rate leads to increasing spin rate (possible control logic flaw)
body:
**Issue details**

When flying a traditional helicopter in ALTHOLD mode, if the aircraft experiences a large attitude error (for example, large roll and pitch deviations) and is already spinning at a high yaw rate, the current control logic sets the desired yaw angular velocity (_ang_vel_body.z) equal to the current gyro reading (_ahrs.get_gyro().z).
While this design might be intended to prevent over-control during large attitude errors, in the case of a helicopter already spinning, this behavior leads to the following critical issue:
    1.The controller continuously commands the same high yaw rate as the current gyro reading.
    2.This causes the yaw rate to increase uncontrollably.
    3.Eventually, this leads to complete loss of control and a crash.

I have confirmed:
    1.My helicopter’s tail rotor system is mechanically sound.
    2.Yaw control works normally under normal conditions.
    3.However, when attitude errors become large (e.g., due to disturbances or aggressive maneuvers) and the helicopter enters a spin, this control logic unintentionally sustains or even worsens the spin.

It seems the current control design assumes large attitude error but no existing spin, and tries to maintain current yaw rate to prevent overcorrection.
However, for helicopters, if a spin has already developed, continuing to command the same yaw rate can amplify the spin drastically.

I believe this is a genuine bug in the control logic specific to traditional helicopters.

Additionally, I would like to ask:
 1.Could this issue also occur in other flight modes (e.g., Loiter, Stabilize, etc.)? 
 2.Does the current logic apply universally to all frame types, or is it specific to helicopters?

**Version**
Copter 4.4. 0

**Platform**
Copter

**Hardware type**
Pixhawk

Steps to reproduce
    1.Fly a traditional helicopter in ALTHOLD mode.
    2.The helicopter begins to spin (high yaw rate).
    3.Induce a large attitude error in flight (e.g., forceful pitch or roll angle disturbances).
    4.In logs, it can be observed that the expected yaw rate is almost equal to gyro.z.

**Code reference**

The problematic code is located in:
```
libraries/AC_AttitudeControl/AC_AttitudeControl.cpp
Function: AC_AttitudeControl::thrust_heading_rotation_rate(...)
```
Relevant snippet:
```
if (_thrust_error_angle > AC_ATTITUDE_THRUST_ERROR_ANGLE * 2.0f) {
    _ang_vel_body.z = _ahrs.get_gyro().z;
} else if (_thrust_error_angle > AC_ATTITUDE_THRUST_ERROR_ANGLE) {
    _feedforward_scalar = (1.0f - (_thrust_error_angle - AC_ATTITUDE_THRUST_ERROR_ANGLE) / AC_ATTITUDE_THRUST_ERROR_ANGLE);
    _ang_vel_body.x += ang_vel_body_feedforward.x * _feedforward_scalar;
    _ang_vel_body.y += ang_vel_body_feedforward.y * _feedforward_scalar;
    _ang_vel_body.z = _ahrs.get_gyro().z * (1.0 - _feedforward_scalar) + _ang_vel_body.z * _feedforward_scalar;
} else {
    _ang_vel_body += ang_vel_body_feedforward;
}
```

author: bnsgeyer
lthall
body:
Hi @kcx1207,

You are mostly correct with your interpration. I do think the following part isn't completly accurate:

> 1.The controller continuously commands the same high yaw rate as the current gyro reading.
> 2.This causes the yaw rate to increase uncontrollably.
> 3.Eventually, this leads to complete loss of control and a crash.

The purpose of setting  the desired yaw angular velocity (_ang_vel_body.z) equal to the current gyro reading (_ahrs.get_gyro().z) is to relax the yaw controller, zeroing the P and D terms. So there is nothing left to cause a further increase in spin rate, much less uncontrolled increase. In fact, the only residual output should be the I term and that should be still opposed to any initial yaw rate.

>> However, when attitude errors become large (e.g., due to disturbances or aggressive maneuvers)

Disturbances yes but aggressive manuvers should not cause a large atitutde error on a properly setup aircraft.


>> It seems the current control design assumes large attitude error but no existing spin, and tries to maintain current yaw rate to prevent overcorrection.

This isn't completly correct. When I wrote this the intention was to minimise control output to yaw and instead focus all control power to roll and pitch to bring the atitutde error back under control. Heli is actually one of the airframes that have a seperate yaw actuator and this doesn't have a significant impact on the ability of the aircraft to actuate roll and pitch.


So this isn't a bug but the question remains, does this code have some unintended behaviour in some corner of the flight envelope that we may be able to improve for heli?

There is a lot of information missing from your discription of the problem. It would be helpfull for me to see your log. I assume you are using a simulator of some sort and can reproduce the problem. Could you make sure fast logging is turned on to maximise the data in the log.

Thanks.

author: IamPete1
body: There are some other vehicles where yaw is not coupled to the roll and pitch. Tricopters (technically it is, but only a minor coupling) and other vectoring vehicles, coax copters. We could add a method on motors that could return if the relax should be done.

author: lthall
body:
> There are some other vehicles where yaw is not coupled to the roll and pitch. Tricopters (technically it is, but only a minor coupling) and other vectoring vehicles, coax copters. We could add a method on motors that could return if the relax should be done.

While I dissagree with your assessment of tricopters and coax copters (tricopters coupling isn't minor in my opinion and yaw can half the thrust of coax copters and with it half the athority of roll and pitch), I do agree that this is something we could make a option that a frame can turn on or off. However, before I did that I would like to understand what is happening here as the discription of this problem doesn't seem to match what I expect from the physics. I really need to see a log.

author: erbornemeier
title: AP_Periph+CubeNode DroneCAN Multiframe Message Drops
body:
## Bug report


**Issue details**

I am running AP_Periph on the head of master on a CubeNode, which is setup to communicate GPS Fix messages over DroneCAN at 1Mb/s on CAN1. Additionally, I have SLCAN enabled on the OTG interface allowing me to connect via the DroneCAN GUI over serial.

The issue I am seeing is that, while I see all messages intending to be sent properly on the SLCAN interface, messages are not actually appearing on the actual CAN bus in full when viewed from a separate socketcan interface tied into the bus directly.

After some detailed investigation, it appears that the STM32H757xx has a configured hw tx buffer size of 7 frames, and the CubeNode is only able to send 7 frames of data out at once when several messages (of the same or different multiframe type) are queued in quick succession.

Here is an image of the gnss messages that are intending to be sent at 5Hz on the bus. The left side is the SocketCAN bus monitor, and the right side is the SLCAN bus monitor on the CubeNode. This is not isolated to gnss messages either, I see similar behavior on the GetNodeInfo message types.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b72d389-2006-4e45-8de5-85b2ef67cb76)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b98db0a-414f-4d07-a81e-8c58017e6a00)

Enabling the CAN stats also shows zero cause for concern, and after reading the code, it seems like drops this severe should be incrementing either the tx errors field. There are also no error frames on the bus when viewed over socketcan. A different SLCAN interface on a CubeOrange on the same bus shows exactly what the socketcan interface does as well. The bus itself also looks healthy on an oscillocope and is properly terminated / topology is in order.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca04ff26-e87e-41e2-aec3-77bd26156e2e)

I am suspecting at this point that there is a bug within the AP Periph firmware as I am struggling to find any reason otherwise, but given where the implementation is at today it appears like this has been shown to work by others.

Any ideas / help / confirmation on any of the above would be much apperciated as I feel I’ve exhausted my custom firmware tweaks at this point to try and get this working.

**Version**
Head of master plus some additions to hwdef.dat for CubeNode to enable GPS, moving baseline, SLCAN, serial remaps.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine
[X] AP_Periph

**Hardware type**
CubeNode soldered to simple breakout board

author: erbornemeier
body:
A conversation around this is happening in the ap_periph discord channel - but as an update to connect things here:

I've seemingly found a workaround today. If I alter the `processTx()` function to only send one message (`break;` on successful send), and then alter the `HAL_PERIPH_LOOP_DELAY_US` to `1024` (default is `64` for the STM32H7) in the `hwdef.dat`, I'm seeing all the messages come out on the bus. I suspect this is less of a fix and more of a workaround since I'm effectively just throttling the sends to every 1ms or so which presumably gives the transceiver time to get messages out of the hw queue. Hoping that is good enough for now while hopefully a better fix is found.

author: Ashishbsharma
body: A potential enhancement would be to add a check in processTx() function to see if the TX FIFO is full before sending the next frame, perhaps using HAL_CAN_TxReady() or something similar. This could help prevent dropped multi-frame messages instead of relying only on loop delay throttling.  Happy to test if needed.

author: tejashah88
title: Feature request: Better handling of default behaviour when installing dependencies for Ubuntu/Debian-variants
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I was trying to install ArduPilot on Linux Mint "xia", which is the equivalent of Ubuntu "noble", but in the `Tools/environment_install/install-prereqs-ubuntu.sh` file, the translation for that codename was missing and the script assumed the release codename to be "bullseye". This led into a rabbit hole of trying to figure out why the script failed to `apt install python-argparse`, and thus the submission of #29704. 

My main issue is that there was no warning regarding the default selection of "bullseye", and it was not obvious as to why the script was trying to install a package that doesn't existing in the apt repositories. For context, Debian "bullseye" was first released in 2021 and while it's still maintained, there are clearly some incompatibilities with any modern Ubuntu-based Linux flavors, as seen in the script.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would prefer a mechanism in the script to warn the user of this default and/or the option to specify your own release codename if it  wasn't recognized from `lsb_release -c -s`. I wouldn't want to change the default behaviour in case people still rely on it but I personally prefer explict warnings over silent defaults in these situations.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

title: Mission Rewind on Resume failing with edge cases
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
As per @MattKear's  attempt to put together a list of edge cases that break the mission rewind on resume feature, I've found two situations. 
Both of these require a simple mission with the first mission item being the DO_SET_RESUME_REPEAT_DIST with the first param set to 10, followed by several waypoints.

1. During the mission, if the operator goes direct to a waypoint with the 'set waypoint' command, the resume repeat feature fails to work for the remainder of the mission. 
2. If the user starts the mission but goes into GUIDED mode before the first waypoint is reached, and then resumes auto, the resume repeat feature fails to work for the remainder of the mission. 


**Version**
Plane 4.5.7

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[X] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
traditional fixed wing 

**Hardware type**
Cube Orange+, sitl
**Logs**

author: MattKear
body:
Thanks @Bill-B i will take a look.

Point 1 was done by design.  The thinking was that by setting a way point via a command, you are doing the mission "out of order" and it is essentially impossible for us to tell if a user will want the mission rewound to include the "out of order" part of the mission or not.  Can you tell me more about your use case? What do you want to see happen in this case? Perhaps I have miss understood what you want are trying to achieve.

Point 2 sounds like a bug, I will try and replicate the issue.

author: Bill-B
body:
Hi Matt. 
Point 1, I see what you mean about not knowing what the user wants to rewind. Our use case is as follows: Fly a waypoint mission with large distances between waypoints. Often, we go to GUIDED mode to loiter, and when we return to AUTO we need to pick up where we left off the large mission. Sometimes, we may need to 'skip' part of the planned mission, and go direct to a later waypoint where we then need the resume repeat feature to start working again. For our case we need the "rewind" feature 'always on' when travelling between waypoints, with a very small repeat distance. So it is OK to delete the history and start recording the history when we arrive at the new waypoint. Of course, by going direct to a waypoint, the operator may have skipped over another DO_SET_RESUME_REPEAT_DIST command and so that one would not take effect. 

Point 2, thanks.

author: peterbarker
title: Internal error from multi-heap allocation
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

An ArduPilot partner running a custom frame configured via scripting is getting internal errors and failure-to-allocate errors.

```
2025-03-18 12:29:53 PM : PreArm: Internal errors 0x100000 l:58 flow_of_ctrl
```

That's from this:
```
    if (heapp->current_heap_usage != 0) {
        // lua should guarantee that there is no memory still
        // allocated when we destroy the heap. Throw an error in SITL
        // if this proves not to be true
        INTERNAL_ERROR(AP_InternalError::error_t::flow_of_control);
    }
```

**Version**
stable, "latest" and 4.6.0-beta4

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[x] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
scripted

**Hardware type**
SITL

**Logs**
Ask partner

author: tpwrules
body:
We weren't sure if there was a perhaps-error-case where the "guarantee" won't hold. I don't think it matters on a real vehicle but it will cause a memory leak in SITL. It might also cause a problem with reallocation which would indeed be bad.

Can the script be shared so I can reproduce locally? Why is scripting restarting before they arm?

author: tpwrules
body:
I am able to replicate this using mission planner SITL on real Windows by restarting scripting enough times (sometimes zero times). In my case the internal error is always paired with this error: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/d5098c6b0c3d4697f1d95fc829d1ed4089bd75f2/libraries/AP_Scripting/lua_scripts.cpp#L493-L497 which AFAICT only happens if Lua can't allocate memory to start.

This suggests the heap is not being initialized properly (`current_heap_usage` doesn't start at zero) which also explains why it's failing to be consistent on shutdown. We sort of assume it's initialized based on our various hacks to make malloc/new zero memory blocks on allocation, but that keeps [breaking on various platforms](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/29005) and [in various ways](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/27473) and I think it has again here. I do not personally plan to fix it again.

author: axoaxel
title: Handling of sensor reconfiguration in ArduPilot
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

Our recent research has identified an implicit trust in sensors connected to the flight controller. Upon sensor reconfiguration, Ardupilot fails to detect the incorrect configuration of the peripherals. Sensor reconfiguration can destabilize UAVs, leading to crashes or significant deviations from planned trajectories, without triggering the failsafe. 

##### Steps to Reproduce:

A message is injected into the UAV's local sensor bus to reconfigure sensors (e.g., I2C, SPI), such as suspending their operation or changing the sensor operating frequency. The sensor will start behaving differently from expected. The data coming from the reconfigured sensor is processed by the UAV's flight controller, leading to incorrect state estimations. The UAV executes erroneous control actions based on these faulty estimations, resulting in destabilization or crashes.

As a POC, we provide an example for the BMI270, BMI055 sensor by changing the firmware to operate with a suspended sensor or at a lower frequency (by relying on the information provided in the sensor's datasheet). In our research, we identify that this can be done without changing the firmware.

For BMI270, 
Inside read_fifo() https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/9fb1e2b9f7b746716397aa1d298943c201d9dd8a/libraries/AP_InertialSensor/AP_InertialSensor_BMI270.cpp#L374

    // Add the following for a frequency change
    write_register(BMI270_REG_ACC_CONF, 1U<<7 | 0x06); // set Accelerometer frequencyto 25Hz
    write_register(BMI270_REG_ACC_RANGE, 0x03);
    write_register(BMI270_REG_GYRO_CONF, 1U<<7 | 1<<6 | 2<<4 | 0x06); //set Gyro frequency to 25Hz
    write_register(BMI270_REG_GYRO_RANGE, 0x08);

    // Add the following for sensor suspend
    write_register(BMI270_REG_PWR_CONF, 0x01); //Advanced power mode enabled.
    hal.scheduler->delay(1);
    write_register(BMI270_REG_PWR_CTRL, 0x00); //Disable the Gyro and Accelerometer


For the BMI055, inside the read_fifo_accel() https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/9fb1e2b9f7b746716397aa1d298943c201d9dd8a/libraries/AP_InertialSensor/AP_InertialSensor_BMI055.cpp#L239

    // Add the following for a frequency change
    dev_accel->write_register(REGA_PMU_BW, 0x09, true); //set frequency to 15.63 Hz

    // Add the following sensor suspend 
    dev_accel->write_register(REGA_PMU_LPW, 0x80, true); //set accelerometer suspend

inside the read_fifo_gyro() https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/9fb1e2b9f7b746716397aa1d298943c201d9dd8a/libraries/AP_InertialSensor/AP_InertialSensor_BMI055.cpp#L299

    // Add the following for a frequency change
    dev_gyro->write_register(REGG_BW, 0x87, true); //set ODR 100Hz with filter bandwidth 32Hz

    // Add the following sensor suspend 
    dev_gyro->write_register(REGG_LPM1, 0x80, true); // set gyro sensor suspend

##### Expected Behavior:

The UAV should detect the sensor configuration change, trigger the failsafe, or reissue the correct configuration.

##### Actual Behavior:

The UAV fails to detect the sensor reconfiguration, processes incorrect sensor data, and performs destabilizing control actions, leading to potential crashes or significant deviations from its intended path.

Specifically, we identify three cases.

- **Armed State with Sensor Frequency Change**: No alarms are raised when a sensor's frequency is modified during flight (i.e., when the drone is armed). The drone continues to operate with the altered sensor update rate, leading to flight destabilization or crashes due to inadequate sensor data processing. From our experiments with SITL, we found that this behavior will not trigger the failsafe or the 'main loop slow' error.

- **Sensor Suspend**: Disabling a sensor during operation results in varied behaviors within the control system, depending on the sensor behavior during suspend. Specifically, we identify three possible behaviors for the sensor suspend: Default Data (the sensor, when queried, responds to the microcontroller with a constant value), Absent Data (No response to the data read), and Stale Data (the last sensed value is repeatedly reported to the controller). Those three sensor behaviors will result in two consequences at the flight controller: 
    1. **Control Loop Halting**: The control loop stalls, leading to a loss of control and potential crashes. This behavior will not trigger the failsafe.
    2. **Erroneous State Estimation**: The system might resort to using default or stale data, which can cause incorrect control responses and instability. This behavior will trigger the failsafe, but from our experiments in SITL, there is a high time to detect for such manipulations.

- **Unarmed State with Sensor Frequency Change**: Additionally we observed in SITL that altering a sensor's update frequency while the drone is unarmed triggers a 'main loop slow' error.

##### Impact:

Sensor reconfiguration can result in UAV crashes or significant deviations from planned trajectories (over 30 meters), posing safety risks and potential mission failures.

##### Recommendations:
Since current chip designs cannot prevent sensor reconfiguration, a viable solution is to periodically attest the sensor configuration. While this approach does not eliminate the underlying issue, it helps mitigate the implicit trust assumption associated with sensors.
- **Sensor Configuration Attestation**: Implement mechanisms to verify the integrity and authenticity of sensor configurations and data to detect unauthorized modifications (attestation).

**Version**
version 4.4.0-DEV pulled on January 2023, applicable to newer verisons.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[ x ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
N.A.

**Hardware type**
Various hardware setups. Tested the reconfiguration of the following flight controllers i) Kakute H7 Mini (BMI270 IMU); ii) Pixhawk 6C with a dual-IMU (BMI055 IMU and ICM-42688-P IMU); iii) Omnibus F4 (MPU6000 IMU). 

**Logs**
In the logs we show the behavior observed for the BMI270 under sensor reconfiguration.

Suspend, flight controller on a table --> default data behavior, producing erroneous state estimation.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca60a929-3594-4ff2-9c59-fd8aa531b136)

Frequency reconfiguration, flight controller on a table --> 
As long as the sensor sampling frequency is higher than 400Hz, the reconfiguration does not show any consequence on the controller. When the sensor frequency is reduced below 400Hz, we can observe that the Kalman Filter estimation gets slowed down. Moreover, we observed scheduled tasks in the ROTS being slowed down (e.g., barometer sensor will be sampled less frequently).
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10649805-2eed-4641-98ba-57960ff8cb7c)

author: IamPete1
body:
I certainly agree that if this were to happen it would be bad, but how would this happen in the wild?

Obliviously we can't protect against someone changing the firmware to introduce such changes. I guess someone could use another device on the bus to change the configuration, but if they are going to that effort then there are lots of other things they could do too.

author: axoaxel
body:
Hi, thanks for the quick reaction to the issue.

While the concept of sensor reconfiguration is general, in our research we envision two possibilities for this reconfiguration to occur:
- Through the use of another device on the bus (as it was correctly pointed out in the previous comment).
- Through the use of intentional electromagnetic emissions (IEMI).

Abstracting from how the reconfiguration is achieved, ArduPilot is not reacting to those changes at the moment causing the described impact on the control loop (slowing down or halting the control routines or inducing wrong state estimation).

author: peterbarker
body:
> Since current chip designs cannot prevent sensor reconfiguration, a viable solution is to periodically attest the sensor configuration. While this approach does not eliminate the underlying issue, it helps mitigate the implicit trust assumption associated with sensors.

Indeed, that is a viable solution... which is why we have "checked register" support in ArduPilot, and have since 2016.

```
  using checked registers allows a device check that a set of critical
  register values don't change at runtime. This is useful on key
  sensors (such as IMUs) which may experience brownouts or other
  issues in flight
```

We don't use this code everywhere, just where we have encountered problems with dodgy sensors.  flash is a limited resource, so we can't add (at least into default builds!) checks for things that don't happen in practice.

If you believe we could really do with more checked-registers on some devices because problems *are* happening on actual devices in the real world, please do raise PRs!

Given we do "handle sensor reconfiguration in ArduPilot" (as deemed necessary...), I think we can close this one?

author: LupusTheCanine
axoaxel
peterbarker
body:
OK, it would be nice to keep these issues as actionable and closable (we have an unmanageable 1500 issues open ATM!)

This is by no means the worst issue in our repository, but, "do things really, really well" doesn't make for a good issue (more of a Wiki page, or a discussion forum topic :-) .

To that end, could we keep this tight by re-titling this issue to "Pro-actively check_registers instead of on data receipt" to make this something that can actually be ticked of as done?

Along those lines.  We don't currently check a huge number of registers.  We can't afford flash space for all of them.  It might be feasible to add more as a compile-time option for those that feel they need it.  But please note I can't see anyone on the Dev Team getting really enthusiastic about the work, so we'd be relying on contributions from outside.

author: peterbarker
body:
@rmackay9 this comes about because the hwdef is saying, "there is a sensor of this type on this bus at this address".  So when we create the hwdef.h for the board we add lines saying, "probe using this sensor driver backend at this bus and address".

We do not check that that sensor driver backend is actually compiled into the code - we just attempt to call the method.

We could relatively easily wrap the call to the probe method in `#ifdef`s.  We have not done that to date because it is considered unlikely that the user would *not* want to compile in support for the compasses which are physcially soldered to their autopilot's main board.  So instead we throw ugly compiler errors at them.  We have special carve-outs in various sanity-checking tools because we don't have these #ifdefs (https://github.com/ardupilot/ardupilot/blob/master/Tools/autotest/test_build_options.py#L79)

I would be perfectly happy with the `#ifdef`s to avoid the compilation failures.  A user could have a legitimate reason for not wanting support on their boards.

author: wyunc
title: The description of MAV_CMD_NAV_LOITER_UNLIM does not match reality
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

I posted the same thing in [discuss.ardupilot](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/the-description-of-mav-cmd-nav-loiter-unlim-does-not-match-reality/131214)

When executing a flight mission, I wanted the drone(ArduCopter) to pause midway. I added the ​[MAV_CMD_NAV_LOITER_UNLIM](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-mavlink-mission-command-messages-mav_cmd.html#mav-cmd-nav-loiter-unlim)​ command, whose description states: "Loiter at the specified location for an unlimited amount of time." However, in practice, this caused the drone to abruptly enter loiter mode. Since the throttle wasn't pre-configured and I failed to promptly use rc 3 to adjust throttle power (as I wasn't continuously monitoring the drone's flight status), the drone crashed directly to the ground.

I'm uncertain whether there's a design flaw in this command. It simply transitions the drone into loiter mode without any warning to immediately increase throttle output via RC.
Could this command be enhanced?​ For example, by providing a default throttle PWM value when the user hasn't explicitly set one, to prevent unintended descents or crashes?

**Version**
4.7.0

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[X] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

body:
Hi @wyunc,

Thanks for the report, I've replied on the discussion you've linked above.

I'm going to go ahead and close this because I don't think it's really a bug, it's more a misunderstanding and lack of documentation that is the real issue.  We can re-open if necessary

author: k-o-s-m-o
body:
Hi.

I have the same issue, both on iA6B and iA10B with Plane 4.6.3 running on SpeedyBee405Wing Mini.
I spend some time debugging, and here are my findings:

- The problem is not related to number of sensors (appears on 4 sensors enabled as well as on 16).
- The problem is not related to number of stop bits (original sensors have short gap between bytes, however arduplane sends next byte right after stop bit of previous one).
- Original FlySky sensors respond in within 1ms from request, while arduplane responds in around 1.2-1.7ms (with jitter)
   I was not able to reduce the respond time enough to match with original FlySky sensors.
   (any suggestions in this area?)

author: mhornsby
title: Rover: FS_CRASH_CHECK Pitch and Roll
body: Wondering if [FS_CRASH_CHECK](https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/parameters.html#fs-crash-check) can be expanded to include an option for pitch and roll. My Rover is running on mild terrian so if say Pitch or Roll is more than +/- 45 then its likely the rover is in trouble e.g. run a wheel up fence or tree

author: Zandriy
body:
Looking from the code of Rover::crash_check() I see  the roll and pitch angles are covered already by [FS_CRASH_CHECK](https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/parameters.html#fs-crash-check), but you should set another parameter for point the allowed roll and pitch angles [CRASH_ANGLE](https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/parameters.html#crash-angle).
So I think to solve the problem in the described case two parameters should be set:
FS_CRASH_CHECK = FS_CRASH_HOLD_AND_DISARM
CRASH_ANGLE = 45

Let me know if I misunderstood the problem.

author: rmackay9
body: Yes @Zandriy is correct!  This apparently went in as part of our [balance bot support](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/8701) but we never documented it on the wiki!  I've created an issue for the wiki here https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot_wiki/issues/6880
