author: wyunc
title: Setting TERRAIN_SPACING Too Small Causes Instant Crash Instead of Running Out of Storage
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
Hi~
When the parameter TERRAIN_SPACING is set to a value less than 1, the system crashes, causing the GCS to lose connection.
For example, param set TERRAIN_SPACING 0 or param set TERRAIN_SPACING 0.5
(But there are no errors when TERRAIN_SPACING =1 or 1.5)

According to the parameter [description](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/parameters.html#terrain-spacing-terrain-grid-spacing):
"Grid spacings lower than 100 meters waste SD card space if the GCS cannot provide that resolution."

If the value is set below 100, it should only result in wasted storage space (eventually leading to an SD card running out of space), but it should not cause an instant crash. Therefore, I think this is a bug.

The error message from debugging is as follows:
Thread 1 "arducopter" received signal SIGFPE, Arithmetic exception.
0x00005555556979a4 in AP_Terrain::calculate_grid_info(Location const&, AP_Terrain::grid_info&) const ()

**Version**
SITL, copter, 4.7.0-dev

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[*] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: peterbarker
body:
This is an integer parameter.  It's being truncated to zero, leading to division-by-zero.

You *really* want sub-metre accuracy?

author: rmackay9
body: Maybe we should protect against unrealistically small values especially if they can cause problems on a real vehicle

author: wyunc
body:
Thank you @peterbarker  and @rmackay9 ,
In my opinion, if you want to fly indoors (within a 50-square-meter area), setting the grid resolution to sub-meter might be a reasonable approach. I tend to agree with what @rmackay9  suggested — it would be best to prevent this situation from happening.

I think the simplest solution would be to add a constraint in the code, so that when the grid resolution is set to less than 1, it defaults to 1. Alternatively, we could add a note in the documentation stating: "Do not set TERRAIN_SPACING to less than 1."

Another option could be to enhance support for sub-meter resolution, though I'm not entirely sure if that's necessary.

author: tridge
title: EKF3 velocity divergence pre-arm
body:
We had a divergence of EKF3 velocity pre-arming on the ground which caused a roll over on takeoff of a quadplane.
GPS velocity looks fine, EKF3 velocity is very bad. Normalised innovations were low.
Replay log here:
http://uav.tridgell.net/tmp/00000082.BIN
replays nicely, no log packet loss
firmware is 4.6.0-beta4, but master replay shows the same issue.

old versions tested:
 - 4.5.7 gives same replay result
 - 4.4.4 gives the same replay result
 - 4.3.8 gives almost the same result (same general VE divergence)
 - 4.2.3 reproduces the issue
 - the 4.1.x replay doesn't work with the log

you can use replay with EKF2 on this log with this PR:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/29405
and --force-ekf2
Using EKF2 the velocity does not diverge, so this looks to be an EKF3 only issue, and one that has been in EKF3 for a very long time

Apart from the divergence, the other worrying part of this log is that the scaled innovations presented to the EKF failsafe code and to the user over MAVLink do not show any health issues with the EKF. Same goes for the lane switching error scores. So no fail-safes, no GCS warnings, no arming check failures.

Other notes:
 - delaying the start of GPS fusion in EKF3 to be after 90s of stability in NavEKF3_core::calcGpsGoodToAlign() instead of 10s "fixes" the issue

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3c9cfaa-f5d1-4805-ad76-77bf9883c417)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82d19bf0-38aa-49a9-8d45-576162bef959)


update:
 - two more examples of a copter here: https://uav.tridgell.net/tmp/Lift/

author: robustini
title: V4.6.0 Beta 4 - Obvious problems with Passthrough and AM32 ESC
body:
Before opening this issue, I consulted with Alka, the AM32 developer, and we cross-tested different FCs and ESCs.
From my tests, I ascertained that @andyp1per solved the problem of incorrect requests with PR #29056 but unfortunately the flash of the ESC firmware does not work, it randomly stops, often around 50% of the process with the AM32 online configurator, and with offline you are able to flash infrequently.
In the same hardware I have installed INAV V8 and have repeatedly reflashed the firmware without the slightest hesitation, always successful the first time.
So I think the passthrough on this thing continues to have unresolved problems.

title: Build Server: create .abin for all boards with SD cards
body:
We support [updating the firmware via SD card](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-install-sdcard.html) but we only produce the necessary .abin files for a very small number of boards (perhaps just the CubeOrangePlus?).

We should ideally produce the .abin file automatically for all boards that have an SD card

This is apparently the line that needs to be added to the .hwdef
```
# build ABIN for flash-from-bootloader support:
env BUILD_ABIN True
```

author: peterbarker
body:
I'm going to close this one now.  ArduPilot *does* support the message, it can be requested and streamed.

Considering we've recently had reports (and I've experienced) overflowing telemetry on 57.6kB links, we can't afford to start streaming more messages by default (we'll break people's existing setups).

Hopefully @DonLakeFlyer can move forward to requesting more messages from the autopilot.  There are actually several that are very useful that aren't streamed by default.  MissionPlanner gets the vehicle to start streaming generator-related messages when its generator control panel is opened, for example.  We'll really want this sort of support for `GNSS` (which should replace `GPS_RAW_INT` and `GPS2_RAW` - we really want to be using the new message but streaming `GNSS` by default will whomp people's links and we can't stop streaming the existing ones for quite some time!

title: SITL: WP Panic in Guided mode wo EKF Origin
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

While on ground, disarmed and in Guided mode, setting global destination point (FlyTo in MavProxy) before setting EKF Origin triggers a Panic freeze in SITL, though command is rejected.
The problem happens when trying to send `POSITION_TARGET_GLOBAL_INT` message:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/f8d13d34d9b0c5019c65a94c6ec0efe1aa8f555d/ArduCopter/GCS_Mavlink.cpp#L119-L129
which tries to change altitude frame for (0,0,0) location
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/f8d13d34d9b0c5019c65a94c6ec0efe1aa8f555d/libraries/AP_Common/Location.cpp#L109-L115
And `get_wp` in Guided with positional control (`GUID_OPTIONS` bit-6 = 0) returns True even for (0,0,0) Location.
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/f8d13d34d9b0c5019c65a94c6ec0efe1aa8f555d/ArduCopter/mode_guided.cpp#L403-L411

**Version**
Copter-4.4/4.5.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[ X ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
_What type of airframe (flying wing, glider, hex, Y6, octa etc)_

**Hardware type**
SITL

**Logs**
_Please provide a link to any relevant logs that show the issue_

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @pavloblindnology,

Could you test with master?  It would be good to know if we've already resolved this in the master branch before we consider going back to older releases

author: pavloblindnology
body:
Hi @rmackay9 
You're right, in master it's fixed with this commit fcebd0c8c2f13fd6cb1aa397fea7d94245851277.
What is not fixed, is that if Guided uses waypoint navigation (`GUID_OPTIONS` bit-6 = 1) then submode still changes before trying to set target. Though this doesn't lead to Panic freeze, as WP nav checks for EKF origin.
Similar reordering in WP part won't work as `wp_control_start` will overwrite destination with stopping point. So, probably just check for EKF Origin before `wp_control_start` will do.

author: pavloblindnology
body:
@rmackay9 
Also please note, that arming in Guided, or switching to Guided in flight is possible wo EKF Origin set if in relative aiding (OptFlow, `ARMING_CHECK.GPS lock=0`).
Then, flying to local target (0,0,0) leads to Panic, though the taget is totally valid.
In `Copter-4.5` additionally, flying to global target leads to flying down (to (0,0,0) destination).
So, seems like additional check for EKF origin is needed in `ModeGuided::get_wp` for positional control.

Or even switch to/arming in Guided should be forbidden without EKF Origin set.

author: rubenp02
title: Plane: Auto-trim misaligns ailerons with asymmetric deflection
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

When using ailerons connected to different channels and that are configured to have a different range in the up vs. down position (say, 25º up vs just 15º down, which is useful in some designs to reduce adverse yaw when rolling), the auto-trim functionality may incorrectly adjust both ailerons in the same direction toward the center of the PWM range. This leads to an unintended pitch trim instead of a proper roll trim.

**Version**
4.5.7

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[X] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
Flying wing

author: IamPete1
body:
> This leads to an unintended pitch trim

That should be corrected by the pitch autotrim. 

What you may be seeing is that the autotrim will only trim to in +-10% from the average of min and max. So if one output is against that limit on the the other will be trimmed so you get asymmetric results.

This sort of thing is very hard to do, we have to try and work out the intent of the person who configured the aircraft. We can't tell from parameters alone.

author: rubenp02
body: The problem is the assumption that the average of min and max is the neutral position for the control surface, which doesn't hold for control surfaces that are set up to be asymmetric. I understand that the current parameters and the way auto-trim is done don't allow for a simple fix to this, but I think it's a pretty big issue for a feature that the wiki recommends turning on. Even the parameter description just says "the automatic trim won't go more than 20% away from a centered trim", which may be interpreted as a physically centered control surface instead of the PWM midpoint.

author: IamPete1
body:
The limits are called out on the wiki with a example (https://ardupilot.org/plane/docs/auto-trim.html). 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b17e1ecb-cfb8-42d1-83d8-65f01f5eebc2)

If you have a better wording we could update it.

author: LupusTheCanine
body: The issue is that auto-trim adjusts servo centerpoints instead of adjusting command centerpoint. The autotrim is inherently incompatible with differential ailerons if the differential action is implemented through different PWM ranges for up and down deflection. Over subsequent trimming actions any differential deflection will be replaced with negative aileron chamber.

author: rubenp02
body:
Yes, so maybe the trim should be a different parameter? Or even better (and I know this is a large change for a relatively minor issue), change the *_TRIM param. suffix to something more accurate, like *_NEUTRAL, and then have a *_TRIM parameter for each attitude control axis, which should be the only ones the auto-trim system touches.

The current *_TRIM suffix is a bit of a misnomer IMO so that could be a point in favor of such a change.

author: Hwurzburg
title: Terrain following/RTL verify command
body:
While working on terrain following for AUTOLAND I discovered a few curious things. I think we need a code modification.

1. In AUTO, if the destination altitude is marked as ABOVE_TERRAIN, navigation from the previous waypoint **_will_** use TERRAIN following independent of the TERRAIN_FOLLOW bitmask.This is explained in the wiki. Therefore, there is no need for the AUTO enum in TERRAIN_FOLLOW since it has no effect on AUTO mode terrain following and can be removed. There are no mission items that I can find without an alt/frame param (ie non-navigation) that would need this enum to terrain follow, and do_change_alt ignores frame and is only relative alt, nav_return_to-launch switches out of AUTO to RTL, which brings up the next item.
2. I find no code path that actually uses the verify_RTL code. NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH mission item changes out of AUTO mode to pure RTL mode and therefore never calls verify_RTL. I think it can be removed.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[ X] Plane
[  ] Rover

`ModeAutoLand::_enter` looks at whether the current mode *allows* terrain following via the parameter.

author: Ryanf55
title: AP_GPS Undulation is opposite common convention causing incorrect ellipsoid height
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

ArduPilot's idea of undulation is not following common convention. It's been this way since it was [first implemented](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/21075#pullrequestreview-1065920977), and we have seen [PR's come through to correct device drivers undulation](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/23942), when in fact, ArduPilot was using the wrong definition. 

See here for a report:

[Ardupilot GPS Issue - PUBLIC3.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18610916/Ardupilot.GPS.Issue.-.PUBLIC3.pdf)

If you use ellipsoid height for an algorithm, you may run into large offsets on some GPS's.

**Version**
Every version of ardupilot that publishes GPS_RAW_INT and dataflash logs to report UND, including `master`.

**Platform**
[x] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
All

**Hardware type**
A few GPS's have been tested

**Logs**
N/A

author: tpwrules
body:
After some experimentation and private discussion with Ryan it appears that (fortunately!) this issue does not affect the common use case of DroneCAN, UBX, or NMEA GPSes. When using these GPSes, whether through AP_Periph or a flight controller, the ellipsoid height is correct over MAVLink `GPS_RAW_INT` and/or DroneCAN's `uavcan.equipment.gnss.Fix2` message. So the issue in these cases is only visible in dataflash `GPA.Und`.

This makes a fix a lot more palatable for me personally and I do think it is important for users of other GPSes.

author: rmackay9
title: AP_OpticalFlow: mavlink driver should consume OPTICAL_FLOW message's flow_rate_x, flow_rate_y
body:
The OpticalFlow_MAV driver consumes the [OPTICAL_FLOW](https://github.com/ArduPilot/mavlink/blob/master/message_definitions/v1.0/common.xml#L5056) message's "flow_x" and "flow_y" fields which are int16_t.  Instead we should consume the "flow_rate_x" and "flow_rate_y" extension fields which are floats and will thus give better accuracy.

We should also consume the "ground_distance" field

We should also consume the [OPTICAL_FLOW_RAD](https://github.com/ArduPilot/mavlink/blob/master/message_definitions/v1.0/common.xml#L5138).  I'm not sure why both messages exist but perhaps this one was created specifically for flow sensors to send their readings to the autopilot while OPTICAL_FLOW was meant for autopilots to send their flow data to the GCS?  I'm not sure why we'd need to separate the uses though

body:
This issue has been mostly completed.  PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/30663 adds support for consuming the floating point fields.  To complete this issue we still need:

2. consume the OPTICAL_FLOW_RAD message

author: collinhundley
body: @rmackay9 what's the status of this? Without consuming `ground_distance` we're unable to use an optical flow sensor as a rangefinder.

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @collinhundley,

No progress on consuming the OPTICAL_FLOW messages's ground_distance I'm afraid but I'm not sure that even if we do that it will resolve your issue.  Consuming the ground_distance will simply mean that an optical flow sensor that ends data using MAVLink will also be able to send in the distance from its built-in rangefinder.  Normally an optical flow sensor is not used "as a rangefinder".  Optical flow sensors can be used to estimate the distance to the ground (if paired with a GPS) and ArduPilot's EKF does support this but that distance is not exposed to the user as a rangefinder nor can it be used for terrain following.  Could you explain in more detail what you're trying to do?

author: Gromitvt10
title: Lidar/Rangefinder used ONLY for VTOL takeoff and VTOL landing in Quadplane
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
_When flying my quadplane with Lidar installed i enable rangefinder for automatic landing. The rangefinder will be used both on the landing approach and for final flare.  But, if the lidar, for any reason shows a low reading, it will trigger the alt_assist even when not on approach or landing. This in turn initiates the VTOL motors to start and creates a lot of drag. 
The problem is this aircraft can fly for 8 hours, what if it was flying miles away and the lidar randomly starting doing this, false low readings.  It will constantly be turning the VTOL motors on and off and would eventually drain its battery.  We can fix or replace this particular lidar unit, but that doesn't mean the new one won't eventually do the same thing. This issue surfaced only after many flights on the aircraft, who's to say it won't happen again with a new lidar unit after many flights.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
_We currently set the Alt_assist to zero, but that turns it off completely. I would like a way to use the lidar only for VTOL takeoff (transition height-use until transition is complete) and landing measurements (over landing spot all the way until touch down). I would like to use Baro for Alt-assist. I don't need the lidar when i'm flying at 1000ft, especially when it can only read up 300ft.  A setting or flag that lets you chose to "use lidar only for takeoff and landing" would be great.  If not checked then it uses lidar for everything, when checked it uses Baro for Alt_assist.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
_I have considered not using lidar at all, but then why even have it. Discussed changing the unit or changing unit parameters, this may fix this particular instance but won't fix the overall issue of Ardupilot engaging Alt assist for false readings._

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[ X ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
_This issue has been brought up and discussed in my partner chat_

In the example above the IMU is supposed to have a FRD (x-axis pointing forward, y-axis pointing right and z-axis pointing down) orientation. In this case the expected measured acceleration in the line above should be `9.81` rather than `-9.81`. Is this correct or did I understand this incorrectly?

author: Tuxliri
body: Okay I have figured this out. When the drone is on a surface the accelerometer of the imu senses the counteracting force of the flat surface pushing up against gravity, thus an upward acceleration of `9.81 m/s^2`. In the FRD body reference frame (*z-axis pointing down*) this is an acceleration of `-9.81 m/s^2`.

author: Tuxliri
body: Added a clarification in the code.

author: tridge
title: possible regression in quadplane attitude controller?
body:
I've had some strange and quite severe oscillations with a GriffinPro tilt quadplane recently when running master. The oscillations are bad enough that I am at risk of losing the aircraft. The odd thing is that running the same parameters on 4.5.7 I have not been able to reproduce the issue.
There are some complicating factors, so it isn't absolutely certain this is a regression, but I think it is worth looking into.
This is what happens on master:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/048d587f-6f3c-42a6-b686-97e7f430d879)
notice the increasing amplitude of oscillation in QLOITER. Changing to QHOVER did allow it to slowly recover, but still huge overshoots. 
This is the same parameters on 4.5.7:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5c6799f-3592-4e20-a366-b65b38ea91d1)
there is still some overshoot, but not dangerous.
the complicating factors are:
 - the tune is pretty bad. I don't know quite how I ended up with this tune, it is clearly a manual tune as it has round numbers for the gains. My past logs showed I changed to these gains sometime last year, but I can't remember why. Maybe some experiments I was doing at the time? The rate PID gains are clearly too low for the angle P gain of 10. I could retune it easily and make it fly a lot better, but my concern isn't getting a good tune, it is explaining why master seems much worse than 4.5.7 in case this impacts other users
 - I recently increased the payload a bit, adding a RPi4 and a 4G radio, which I suspect is why it is worse now than it has been on previous flights, but as a percentage of total weight the extra payload is small (maybe 250g out of 10kg or so?)
 - the ESCs are blheli32/dshot, but are going via a L431 DroneCAN adapter, so changes in the CAN code need to be considered as well as high level quadplane and attitude controller

Some things I've looked at:
 - given the number of filtering changes in master compared to 4.5.7 I looked at the unfiltered vs filtered gyro data and I don't see any filter induced lag in the logs
 - I'm intrigued by the flat bottom on the RATE.RDes graph above for master. That is probably the 75 deg/s limit from Q_A_RATE_R_MAX, but I don't see an equivalent flat bottom on the tests with 4.5.7. Some change in the rate limiting? Or just the different way of triggering the oscillation (I had to use the sticks to start the movement in 4.5.7 whereas with master it spontaneously oscillates when descending).
 - i looked at the RPM feedback from the ESCs versus the demand in RCOU and I don't see any higher lag in master than in 4.5.7. 

I haven't tested the 4.6.0 beta. To do that safely I think I'll need to retune first to get a safe set of gains, then use a script to switch to these gains to see if 4.6.0 is affected.

Logs are here:
http://uav.tridgell.net/tmp/GriffinProOscillation/

author: bnsgeyer
body:
@tridge @rmackay9 @lthall 
I have been doing some investigation into this behavior.  Initially Tridge and I worked to take the quadplane SITL model and give it some lightly damped characteristics (bad tune) that showed a roll oscillation around 1 hz.  Tridge tried to excite the dynamics using the AHRS_TRIM param and see if he could get the same behavior as what he saw with his real aircraft.  He reported that he didn't have much luck.  

I saw that a user had posted something similar (or at least sounded similar) to what Tridge experienced with the quadplane but with a multirotor.  So I decided to explore this in Copter using a state space model that I developed for the 3DR X8-M multirotor.  I looked at two tune configurations, one with good tune and one with a poor tune that had very obvious oscillatory behavior around 1 hz.   

I performed frequency sweeps of the attitude controller for both configurations in both 4.5.7 and 4.6-beta3.  The frequency responses of the aircraft with a good tune looked nearly identical.  There may have been a slight bit of phase loss in the 4.6 response but I would consider it negligible (equated to about 2 milliseconds of time delay).  For the comparison of the poorly tuned aircraft, there was a noticeable difference in particular with the peak of the lightly damped mode.

Here is a comparison of the frequency responses for the poorly tuned aircraft.  On the left is 4.6-beta3 and the right is 4.5.7.  You can see the higher peak (indicating a lightly damped oscillation) with the 4.6-beta3 firmware with the difference being about 1.5 dB between the two firmware.  There is also more phase loss in the 4.6-beta3 firmware.  I don't know if this is enough to say 4.6 would crash an aircraft. I mean this just takes an aircraft that already badly oscillates about the roll axis in 4.5 and just makes it a little worse in 4.6.  Certainly not a night and day difference.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33582f5e-2fdb-4d45-96b8-c97a6e44d531)

I then flew the poorly tuned aircraft in loiter.  The 4.6 firmware definitely exhibited the characteristics that Tridge saw with the quadplane.  The oscillations grew pretty quickly and switching into stabilize resulted in the oscillations slowly dying out.  You can even see the 75 deg/s clipping once in stabilize.  I had my sticks centered so just the error correction was working and limiting the target rate to 75 deg/s

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37e00257-7707-4d1b-8eed-0f837e0faba3)

I flew the poorly tuned aircraft in loiter with 4.5.7.  It was better behaved and the oscillations didn't grow.   I had to increase the throttle quite a bit to get it to go unstable in loiter.  Here is the plot for that

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6543f343-1aa2-4923-85a4-bb64221fa48a)

Overall, I think that the attitude controller changed slightly where poorly tuned aircraft my encounter oscillatory behavior especially if the position controller was not tuned for the poorly tuned attitude controller.  which means that if they are using the default values of the position controller where the attitude controller can barely keep up with requests in 4.5 and then switch to 4.6, it is possible that they could see oscillations in position controller modes.  

Here is a link to the log files I used to develop the plots above.  I included a few extra and hopefully the file names are descriptive enough
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/10LSl4x9tDfLGBrBKewM_XHD_I6d4i5aQ?usp=sharing

title: [Cube Orange +] SERIAL1 and SERIAL2 perform much worse than SERIAL0 for Mavlink bin log streaming
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

Dear ardupilot community, I'm trying to use the LOG_BACKEND_TYPE=3 to have data flash logs both written to the SD card and streamed to the companion computer.
The quick prototype has shown that it works fine, as we do not have many logs enabled. This works with USB connection over UART0 even with a baud rate = 115200 showing no issues (no CRC errors, no missing log points, etc.).
However, when using UART1 or UART2, the situation is drastically different even if the baud rate is raised to 1500000. Logs on SD are still fine, but logs on the companion have multiple and large gaps.
Here is how the remote log stats look like for 3 different uarts all set up with 115200 baud rate:

UART0 (Over USB cable)
No resends and a number of retries stays almost constant over time.
Sent max shows a burst of sent blocks (up to 70) and then drops to ~7max and 1 average block.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21c15d37-37ee-4117-a773-99d4812655ee)

UART1
Sent max never exceeds 7. Sent average stays at ~5 all the time.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/285335fb-900c-423e-9c3e-eae766246f45)

UART2
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e28d3d7d-9ecf-479e-9431-3e429e05d4f1)

UART1(baud rate 1500000)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9fb07432-8b78-414d-9b46-d412828aacbf)

In the case of using UART1 or UART2, the number of resends and drops have grown over time, and pending/free shows that there is a bottleneck in sending blocks. Bin logs for those 3 cases are attached.

While searching for a possible solution I found this issue, which may be related: (Flow control serial port interaction) https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/16587
Even so, it seems solved way before today here is some additional info that may be relevant:

* The above tests were done with BRD_SER1_RTSCTS and BRD_SER2_RTSCTS  set to 0 (disabled) to reject the possibility of the mentioned issue here.
* As far as I understand UART0 has flow control enabled by default and there is no possibility to disable it. Does it mean that it will perform much better in any case because of that?
* Our target configuration will be BRD_SER1_RTSCTS = 0 and BRD_SER2_RTSCTS = 1.

Looking forward to and grateful in advance for any help/guidance with that issue.

Best regards,
Alex

**Version**
4.5.1

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[* ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
Quadcopter

**Hardware type**
Cube orange +

**Logs**
[uart_debug_logs.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18394422/uart_debug_logs.zip)

author: slovak194
body:
In case someone comes up with a similar question.

The "baud rate" that you set when connecting to a USB CDC ACM virtual serial port is just a number that gets sent to the device, and the device can ignore it or interpret it however it wants to. The baud rate does not affect the rate of data transfer over USB.

So in my case, SERIAL0 was always transmitting at a significantly higher baud rate than "real" SERIAL1 and 2 regardless of the baud rate you set in ardupilot and on companion.

author: robustini
title: Plane: separate mixing gain value for elevons and vtails
body:
In case of servox_function assigned to elevons or vtails a mixing is applied obviously to handle roll and pitch in the former case and yaw and pitch in the latter case.
The amount of mixing is defined by the MIXING_GAIN parameter.
The problem is that in Ardupilot in case both elevons and vtails are present the mixing goes to affect both.
Instead, it would be quite appropriate for the mixing to be separate but still parameterizable, e.g. “ELEV_MGAIN” and “VTAIL_MGAIN,” or perhaps keep “MIXING_GAIN” but in case of both elevons and vtails act only on the former.
I am trying to implement this with a LUA script but have not succeeded.
Since the functionality is interesting anyway it would be more appropriate in my opinion to have it built into the code.
In my case in this 3d printed fpv plane I would like to use the vtail more as a rudder and with very little pitch intervention, so as to possibly compensate for the amount of pitch authority of the elevons.

![immagine](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64928e5e-eb97-47bf-8419-da1f6ac23360)

author: IamPete1
body:
We added a script for this in the end: 
```

-- Setup param block, reserving 2 param beginning with VTAIL_
local PARAM_TABLE_KEY = 75
local PARAM_TABLE_PREFIX = 'VTAIL_'
assert(param:add_table(PARAM_TABLE_KEY, "VTAIL_", 2), 'could not add param table')

-- Add a parameter and bind it to a variable
local function bind_add_param(name, idx, default_value)
    assert(param:add_param(PARAM_TABLE_KEY, idx, name, default_value), string.format('could not add param %s', name))
    return Parameter(PARAM_TABLE_PREFIX .. name)
end

-- Duplicate mixing gain and offset params
local VTAIL_MGAIN = bind_add_param('MGAIN', 1, 0.5)
local VTAIL_MOFF = bind_add_param('MOFF', 2, 0.0)

-- Input servo function numbers
local k_rudder = 21
local k_elevator = 19

-- Use scripting servo function for output
local k_vtail_right = 94 -- k_scripting1
local k_vtail_left = 95 -- k_scripting2

-- Copy the mixing code from AP
-- https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/609551212afc02f0c0b30fda165f90211eed23df/ArduPlane/servos.cpp#L170-L196
local function update()

    -- the order is setup so that non-reversed servos go "up", and
    -- func1 is the "left" channel. Users can adjust with channel
    -- reversal as needed
    local in1 = SRV_Channels:get_output_scaled(k_rudder)
    local in2 = SRV_Channels:get_output_scaled(k_elevator)

    -- apply MIXING_OFFSET to input channels
    local offset = VTAIL_MOFF:get()
    if offset < 0 then
        in2 = in2 * ((100 - offset) * 0.01)
    elseif offset > 0 then
        in1 = in1 * ((100 + offset) * 0.01)
    end

    local gain = VTAIL_MGAIN:get()
    local out1 = (in2 - in1) * gain
    local out2 = (in2 + in1) * gain
    SRV_Channels:set_output_scaled(k_vtail_right, out1)
    SRV_Channels:set_output_scaled(k_vtail_left, out2)

    return update, 10
end

return update()
```

author: Ryanf55
title: Network: Add PTP clock synchronization protocol
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The [MAVLink TIMESYNC  Protocol V2](https://mavlink.io/en/services/timesync.html) is not precise enough for some applications, and it's bespoke. It also doesn't guarantee sync with the GPS, which is instead estimated using Jitter Correction. I'd like ArduPilot to support a clock synchronization protocol that is standardized and supported by nice GNSS units such as the Trimble PX-1. This allows the GNSS System, ArduPilot, and the companion computer, and even some cameras/sensors to all use the same clock.

I propose [PTP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precision_Time_Protocol) per [RFC-8173](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8173) and [IEEE 1588-2008](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1588/4355/). This should achieve 10uS precision.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

* Use the LWIP network support to add PTP support to ardupilot being a PTP slave. Assume the GPS is the PTP master.
* Use the LWIP network stack to have Ardupilot be the PTP master when you don't have GPS

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

* MAVLINK timesync
* PPS
* NTP

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**

https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/mavlink-time-synchronization/128496/4

author: vvazrod
body:
Hi! In our research group we specialize in time synchronization protocols and have come across this issue when looking at a shortcoming our colleagues found for their research. They are quite limited by MAVLink's 50 Hz maximum frequency for communications. Is this related to ArduPilot's millisecond resolution when performing time synchronization? If the timing resolution was increased to the wanted 10 us, could this frequency be increased further?

If this is the case, we would be quite interested in working on PTP support for ArduPilot over Ethernet.

author: Ryanf55
body:
You can boost mavlink higher past 50Hz, but it involves changing thread priorities that are not well tested and reduce safety of flight critical operations. Are you sure increasing rate is necessary to reduce clock error? Over 1/50 of a second, does CPU drift enough to warrant requiring increasing the data rate?

I think part of the issue is ArduPilot's serial IO is serviced at a lower thread priority, and we don't necessarily expose precise time information for each bit in the stream. Maybe DMA could help, but that's well out of my depth.

ArduPilot's AP_RTC class already support microsecond resolution. My comment on millisecond resolution is more related to how accurate the serial-based jitter correction supposedly can reach, however I don't have hard data to back this up.


I think it would be possible to set up some sort of some experiments to test time sync.
If you need professional help, I am happy to connect your research group direct with Trimble who are experts in time sync.

author: vvazrod
body:
Seems like I was quite off with my assumptions about MAVLink (don't really know a lot about the protocol, really).

Anyways, PTP over Ethernet would be the way to go for better accuracy, which I guess would be a great improvement for on-board robotics and sensor fusion. What other applications do you think are limited by the current synchronization accuracy?

We aren't really looking at professional help, but rather interested in working on this topic and probably contributing back to the project in any way we can.

As discussed on PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/28750 there are cases where the EKF source sets are configured so that the EKF is not using the GPS (for position, velocity, altitude or yaw) but the EKF may actually still use it.

author: tridge
title: Plane: quadplane tilt rate issues
body:
There are some issues with the quadplane tilt down rate for tilt-enabled quadplanes.
- the quadplane.assisted_flight flag oscillates during the TRANSITION_TIMER phase of the fwd transition
- if Q_TRANSITION_MS is smaller than the time it takes to go from Q_TILT_MAX to full tilt with the configured Q_TILT_RATE parameters then the last part will happen at 90 deg/s
- when we complete the transition there can be a sudden throttle change on the tilted motors, much faster than the THR_SLEWRATE should allow

### assisted_flight oscillation

The assisted flight flag oscillates as SLT_Transition::update() will set it to false once airspeed is reached due to should_assist() returning false. It then gets set back to true in the TRANSITION_TIMER further down in the same function. The impact is not significant, but it is confusing.

### too fast slew

If Q_TRANSITION_MS is smaller than the time it takes to go from Q_TILT_MAX to full tilt then the last part of the tilt will happen at 90 deg/s due to the fast_tilt logic and TRANSITION_TIMER no longer being true. Possibly we should stay in TRANSITION_TIMER until the full tilt is reached?

### instant throttle change

when the transition has completed and the VTOL motors are turned off the tilted motors move from VTOL tilt control to fwd throttle control. When this happens the throttle changes instantly and the sudden throttle change can disturb the aircraft pitch as the pitch PID does not have time to compensate.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ece78687-e630-4fd7-aa93-4f2e0aea59b0)

author: Ryanf55
title: Plane Offboard Support - Replace GUIDED mode
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

* Guided mode on plane is behind copter functionality
* GUIDED plane mixes the "FlyTo" GCS functionality with other lower level control commands which are hard such as [yaw rate control over DDS](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/26143)
* Guided mode on plane doesn't give a clear API for sending kinematically feasible dubins paths in 3D
* If you need to send multiple lower level guided commands (say, heading and turn rate), the [timeouts interfere](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/28526#issuecomment-2456573675) - they assume only a single control methodology at once
* The interface is inconsistent across DDS, Scripting, and MAVLink
* There is a lot of complexity in QuadPlane on what the intent is for certain commands (ie - should you fly in copter mode or in plane mode to accomplish the desired velocity)

**Describe the solution you'd like**

* Make GUIDED mode only for GCS FlyTo
* Create a new mode (name proposed is OFFBOARD) to handle more of these control methodologies using the reserved mode from [here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/28939)
* Allow a user to be able to achieve at least the same capabilities that missions have with position lookahead/s-curves by allowing fly-through positional control
* Allow velocity and acceleration control
* Give offboard/scripting better control for quadplane if it wants
* Allow Lua/DDS/Mavlink to register custom modes that build on "offboard" but call it something different - like "ACRO" or "SMART RTL"

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

* Continue to augment features in GUIDED which is already very convoluted

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[x] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**

* Let's gather some high level requirements on what this offboard mode should accomplish before diving into design/implementation
* Relates to https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/28930 as discussed in https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/dev-call-dec-23-2024/127890/2#p-507105-utc-0106-httpsgithubcomardupilotardupilotpull28930pullrequestreview-2521275286-15

**Requirements (WIP)**

* Be able to achieve FlyTo behavior of clicking a waypoint on a map, but levaraging more advanced Lua/DDS path plan validation as needed [here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/28562)
* Be able to control climb rate and turn rate at the same time
* Support position/velocity/acceleration control in body AND earth frame
* Allow a user-defined fallback if the low-level offboard controller fails (like current timeout behavior)
* Continue support of [MAVLink Standard Modes](https://mavlink.io/en/services/standard_modes.html)

author: rmackay9
title: Copter/Rover: maintain speed even when waypoints are placed close together
body:
Copter/Rover SCurves has a limitation where it only looks forward two waypoints (e.g. the current waypoint and the next one) and for safety reasons it plans the maximum speed so that the vehicle can stop in time for the 2nd waypoint.  This can lead to the vehicle unnecessarily slowing if the user places the waypoints close together.  How "close" depends upon the WPNAV_ACCEL and WPNAV_JERK parameters.

We could reduce the user experienced slowdowns by enhancing SCurves to look further ahead.

body:

- Quantify performance impact with specific waypoint spacing scenarios
- Current SCurves implementation limitations in path planning

author: xianglunkai
body:
@rmackay9 
Hello! Long time no see! I have three suggestions and questions:
1. Can Rover support both L1 and scurve algorithms, which is convenient for users to choose and compare?
2. At present, Scurve does not support obstacle avoidance and regression reference lines for simple path planning.
3. For the trajectory tracking of the boat, is there any consideration based on the angular velocity instead of the speed course, and the current mainstream is based on the course speed control

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @xianglunkai, nice to hear from you.

1. No, L1 is gone I'm afraid and there are no plans to bring it back in future versions.  It's too much development and support effort for our small team to support both L1 and SCurves.  Instead we've chosen to put our limited resources towards supporting and enhancing SCurves only
2. Rover's autonomous modes (including Auto, RTL, etc) do support both simple avoidance and path planning.  I think maybe you're referring to [this issue](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/20406) where Rover does not return to the original line?  It would be nice to fix that for sure
3. I don't fully understand the question but SCurves plans the path based on the user configured maximum speed, acceleration and jerk.  It does not consider the vehicle's maximum turn rate.  Turn rate can be calculated from speed and lateral acceleration but the frame's mechanical method of steering the vehicle (e.g. servo, vectored thrust, etc) can mean that you may or may not be able to adequate specify a maximum acceleration that closely matches how the vehicle can actually behave

Hope this helps, sorry if I've misunderstood something

author: Ryanf55
title: Support external path interface (scripting/ROS/offboard)
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I have a global path planner that runs offboard. It generates a vector of safe waypoints to achieve a high level navigation goal, such as crossing a mountain range in minimum distance. The path is kinetically feasible. I can't command the plane to follow this path today without using AUTO (or it's not clear how).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
An ability to feed these waypoints to the plane/copter/rover and have it do look-ahead to not stop at each waypoint.
**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Setting waypoint radius to zero or using auto, which won't work if the trajectory is created on the fly. 

**Expectation**

If I have a plane or a copter, and I take a large circular path (say, quadruple plan's loiter diameter), discretize it to 100 points offboard, I should be able to feed these
position targets into the vehicle (with lookahead), and it should follow a smooth circle path. Same for copter and plane and rover.

If the points are collinear, both copter and plane and rover should navigate at their cruising speeds and not slow down/circle at each point if desired.

**Platform**
[x] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**

If you try doing guided waypoints today on plane, it always tries to orbit. 
There is currently no way to supply a list of 10 waypoints in GUIDED mode that are all collinear and have the plane fly straight through all them. Copter slows down at each waypoint until you feed it the next one. This requires a companion computer to feed the points at the right moment, which cuts corners and relies on bespoke/precise undocumented timing and distances for each vehicle's navigation controller. This is NOT scalable for generic offboard autonomy.

* https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/22539
* https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/26143

author: snktshrma
body:
Hi @Ryanf55 ! In guided mode, have you tried to give a pursuit target instead of the waypoint directly? I mean instead of supplying next setpoint, give it a setpoint a few distance apart by interpolating the path in between. I have been doing that for long to allow copter to follow a set of setpoints that are close to each other and I get a very smooth motion.

It's a bit like L1 controller though it's actually not. What it does is it actually looks a bit ahead each time, either next waypoint if it's close enough or interpolate between next two waypoint upto a certain distance to limit any adverse situation, it tries to reach a waypoint. This way we get a smooth motion as target is updated each moment vehicle is in motion. Though I have added it directly in my offboard scripts but if we accommodate in main codebase, I think that might solve the issue.

author: ntamas
title: AC_Fence: misleading results from get_breaches() during manual recovery period
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

The bitmask of active fence breaches returned from `AC_Fence::get_breaches()` is not updated when the vehicle is in a manual recovery period (triggered by a mode switch when at least one fence is actively breached). This has multiple consequences:

* The onboard log is spammed with "fence breach cleared" `ERR` log records on Copter (subsystem = 9, error code = 0). This is due to `AC_Fence::check()` always returning zero (no new fence breaches) -- the logic in `Copter::fence_check()` hits the branch where `orig_breaches != 0` and `new_breaches == 0`, triggering a log entry every 40 msecs.
* Any third-party code that relies on the assumption that `AC_Fence::get_breaches()` always returns the _currently_ active breaches is broken because the breaches are not updated in the recovery period. If the behaviour is intentional, the comment of `AC_Fence::get_breaches()` should be updated to emphasize the existence of the manual recovery period and that it freezes the breach flags.

A preferred fix would probably make sure that `AC_Fence::get_breaches()` is always kept up-to-date and would only defer fence-related failsafe _actions_ until the end of the recovery period, but I cannot judge whether this would have any unintended consequences elsewhere.

**Version**
ArduCopter 4.5.7

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[X] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
Quad, but probably not relevant to the issue.

**Hardware type**
Custom, but probably not relevant to the issue.

**Logs**
I am not allowed to disclose the log where we found the issue, but I can provide it upon request to the developers. I can be reached on the ArduPilot and Skybrush Discord servers.

- `is_connected`: bool
- `receiver_rssi`: value in [0, 100]

I think there are two possible issues:

1. on reboot the last PWM signal can be shortened
2. on powerup the PWM pins may momentarily go high and then low again and some servos and ESCs may misinterpret this as a PWM signal and move.  Normally in the AP dev team we blame the servo or ESC for not having enough checks built in

Perhaps @joshanne is referring to the 1st issue while @thespova is experiencing the 2nd?  I'm not sure of course.

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @thespova,

To setup a pull down, normally a very high value resistor (like 1000 ohm) is connected to both the signal line and the ground pin.  The high resistor value results in just a small amount of power leaking from the signal line.  If there's no actual signal being provided this results in it becoming equal to ground.  If there is a signal provided it will easily overpower the "leak".

author: rmackay9
title: Autopilot firmware updates over Ethernet
body:
With AP's improved Ethernet support we have more flight controllers connected via Ethernet to companion computers.  It would be very convenient for users (and potentially companies with fleets of AP vehicles) if we could support over-the-air (OTA) updates by allowing the flight controller's firmware to be updated over ethernet.

I discussed this with @tridge and he said that this is already possible for AP_Periph devices so much of the code is already there.  We need to be careful though because this will involve updating the bootloader and we need to ensure we don't run out of space

## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Heli should not allow users to configure throttle-based dynamic notch.  "Throttle" is not related to motor RPM in anyway in Heli. author: rmackay9
title: RangeFinder: enhance mavlink driver to use RNGFNDx_ADDR field
body:
The AP_RangeFinder_MAVLink backend uses the [DISTANCE_SENSOR message](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#DISTANCE_SENSOR)'s orientation field to map to the RNGFNDx_ORIENT parameter ([see code here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_RangeFinder/AP_RangeFinder_MAVLink.cpp#L31))

We should consider enhancing this condition so that if the user has set the RNGFNDx_ADDR field (defaults to -1) then this is compared against the DISTANCE_SENSOR.id field.  This would allow more than one distance sensor in each direction to be used.

This request comes from [this wiki discussion](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot_wiki/issues/6436)

**Issue details**

Passing a param file to `sim_vehicle.py` with `--count` > 1 causes ArduPlane SITL to fail to start.

Reproduce by running the following in the same directory as a valid parameter file `my_plane.parm`:
`sim_vehicle.py -v plane --add-param-file=my_plane.parm --count 2`

Running ArduPlane on its own (executed verbatim from the sim_vehicle.py logs, see below), and connecting with MAVProxy from another terminal, I get:
`<ardupilot directory>/build/sitl/bin/arduplane -S --model plane --speedup 1 --slave 0 --defaults ../../../ardupilot/Tools/autotest/models/plane.parm,my_plane.parm --sim-address=127.0.0.1 -I0`

Failed

author: eschutz
body:
With some more investigation, I have found the issue to be that sim_vehicle.py doesn't account for relative param file paths. When you run sim_vehicle.py with --count > 1, subdirectories 0/, 1/ etc. are created from which each ardupilot instance is run, hence adding '..' to the param file path in line 798. However, this only occurs for the built-in param file and not user-supplied ones.

I will soon submit a PR with a fix. Until then, a workaround is therefore to **use absolute param file paths**.

author: timtuxworth
title: DDS should use the same networking configuration as other IP networking
body:
As per the discussion on this PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/28815, DDS is using a different architecture for IP networking support than the rest of AP. It should be consistent.

This is going to be one of the first things that I and others will want to do when using ROS2/DDS will be to connect the AP to an ethernet switch, either using the PPP interface or ethernet. ArduPilot will need to communicate with one or more gimbal/cameras, AI module and ROS2/DDS and other services running on a companion computer, using the same physical port on the AP.

This is a lot easier to do if the devices can use their "out of the box" configured 192.168.144.* IP addresses, with the only interface needing to be configured being the ethernet port on the companion computer.

This is why I previously suggested that DDS should not be doing it's own networking - it should use the IP addresses configured in the NET* parameters and should be able to run as a NET_Pn_PROTOCOL, so all these devices can be connected over a single physical port to the AP.

There is a suggestion that there might be performance concerns with this change. I don't see any justification for that, but I'd be surprised if it doesn't save some flash.

title: Sub should move away from using firmware-side button press handling
body:
Sub has a lot of functions that are triggered from buttons handled on the firmware side. That is not how most of the vehicles work, and it makes it harder to control it via MAVLink for autonomous functionality, and also requires specific handling on the GCS.
I'm opening this issue to document what can easily be changed and what needs further work.

Here's an idea of how to map things:

author: ES-Alexander
body:
- `k_shift` could be handled by the GCS, instead of discarding the option for button combinations
- `k_camera_source_toggle` seems like not the autopilot's jurisdiction - most likely it should also be a GCS level function?
- lights-related features could _maybe_ be handled by the [illuminator protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/illuminator.html)
- servo functions have now been switched to actuator outputs, but we still need support for DO_SET_ACTUATOR, and we should likely also [finish adding gripper support](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/31107)
- If the [`DO_AUX_FUNCTION`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/ardupilotmega.html#MAV_CMD_DO_AUX_FUNCTION) command definition could be expanded to allow servo-style inputs, scripting inputs could also make use of it
    - Alternatively this could (somewhat awkwardly) be handled via RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE messages, since [RC channels can already be assigned to scripting](https://ardupilot.org/sub/docs/parameters.html#rc1-option-rc-input-option)
- Toggle handling requires state knowledge
    - That exists already for servo outputs via `SERVO_OUTPUT_RAW` (relevant for actuator functions), but I'm unsure whether it's consistently available for the relay values (I know it works on Navigator, but unsure about other flight controller boards)

title: Missing/ empty/ extra ESC telemetry log data
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
I have a Quadplane with 5 esc’s connected. Since updating from 4.4.4, extra empty ESC’s (up to 8 in total) have been appearing in logs and the cruise ESC data is often empty.

On occasion data for 5 esc's has been observed in mission planner but only data for 4 has been logged.


Just verified to be a firmware issue as follows;

Flashed back to 4.4.4 - 5 esc’s correct data
Flashed 4.6.0 - 8 esc’s 4 with data 4 without
Flashed to 4.4.4 - 5 esc’s correct again.
I haven’t tried all the firmware releases in-between but 4.5.4 and 4.5.0 have also been shown to not work.

(https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/esc-telemetry-phantom-escs/127106)

Post 4.4.4

[  ] Copter
[ X ] Plane

[  ] Submarine

author: mbuzdalov
title: Copter: AutoTune produces ridiculously small ACCEL_MAX values
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

In my 2" whoop-sized quad, running AutoTune produces nice enough rate and angle PIDs, but too small maximum accelerations.

Example: `ATC_ANG_RLL_P` of 25+, but `ATC_ACCEL_R_MAX` of around 1000, written as 4000 because it was clamped from below.

These values are not safe to fly.

**Version**

GitHub master, commit 3ed6ada2e316c52ee9ebae4202c99c681e891693.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[X ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**

Quadcopter.

**Hardware type**

FlywooF405S-AIO

**Logs**

Two logs are attached, for roll and yaw. They are filtered to 5Hz because the flash chip is very small, but should likely be enough for analysis.

author: tridge
title: check that INS_HNTCn_REF is non-zero for ESC,RPM or FFT notches
body:
it is quite common when users setup notch filters with ESC or FFT notches to forget to set INS_HNTCn_REF to a non-zero value. When set to zero it becomes a single fixed notch which is almost certainly not what they want.
We either need an arming check, or we need to make the is_zero(ref) check in AP_Vehicle::update_dynamic_notch() only apply to the throttle based notch
The ref is only used for:
 - throttle based notch
 - RPM notch (as scale factor)
 - fallback to throttle notch for ESC notch (edge case)

author: menschel
title: Plane 4.6 beta - Takeoff throttle behavior for planes without airspeed sensor changed from 4.5.7
body:
## Bug report

In my application forced max throttle regardless of climb angle results in
- Over-speeding of the plane if climb angle is low
- Over-stressing the battery if there are constraints on the discharge curve.

**Issue details**
There have been design changes with Plane 4.6 that change takeoff throttle behavior for planes without an airspeed sensor.
Throttle is forced to max throttle while it was TECS controlled based on climb angle in Plane 4.5.7.

With the ZOHD Drift that I fly for recreational purposes and development, this breaks at least 2 constraints of the Plane.

- It has a recommended max speed of 50km/h or about 15m/s. This is well exceeded to 60km/h or 17m/s. There is also the suspicion that this over-speeds the wing profile, causing it to loose lift.

- It has a custom Li-Ion battery based on 18350 cells that are rated for 3A (5A burst for 10s).
With Plane 4.5.7, it was possible to adjust the current during takeoff by adjusting the takeoff pitch, i.e. 12° lead to 3A.
This is void with Plane 4.6 because it draws 5.5A for more then 30 seconds, thus violates the discharge profile.

**Version**
4.6beta

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[x] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
ZOHD Drift, i.e. Plane, sub 250g 

**Hardware type**
SpeedyBee F405 Wing Mini

**Logs**
![TkOff_Thr_Max_Overspeed_Overcurrent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0a27c8c-626c-4efe-8009-d21f31ad4482)

[24-11-18_12-43-12.bin](https://github.com/menschel/ardupilot/blob/stash/build/bin/Arduplane/24-11-18_12-43-12.bin)

author: Georacer
body:
We intentionally changed the throttle profile in airspeedless takeoff here: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/27174/files#diff-499a0c85162572f911764247ca98ae60042d4b6e52ba693b7fdcf9173532810b

And will document it here: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot_wiki/pull/6149/files#

We were discussing this in a thread which ends here: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/27174#issuecomment-2245498008. Although it can be a bit confusing as `TKOFF_LVL_ALT` is also mentioned there.

I think this is a good change, because in 4.5 TECS wouldn't actually control airspeed during airspeedless TAKEOFF anyways. It would:
1 Climb at full throttle up until `TKOFF_LVL_ALT` (5m by default).
2 Then it would switch to normal TECS flying, during its climb to `TKOFF_ALT`. During that stage, it would:
  1 operate under speedweight=0
  2 control throttle according to airspeedless laws (pitch-based)
  3 still risk stalling, depending on your aircraft. Primarily because you can't guarantee that you have accumulated enough airspeed past `TKOFF_LVL_ALT`.

author: rmackay9
body:
Based on @Georacer's comment I'm going to go ahead and close this.

@menschel, are you OK with this?  Thanks again for helping out with the beta testing

author: menschel
body:
Hello @rmackay9,

I'm no longer active on github due to the recent change of github's 
policy. They decided to purge users, that fit certain criteria but don't 
consent to their new rules, obviously on Microsoft's behalf.

Concerning the issue, I consider it a degradation of functionality that 
will eventually cause problems down the road.
I disagree with @Georacer's analysis on a technical basis. We've been 
though this discussion multiple times now.
By observation TECS does control throttle in 4.5.7 and throttle results 
roughly in ((ATT.Pitch / TECS_PITCH_MAX) * THR_MAX). Whatever the math 
is behind this, it is the outcome of the regular TECS tuning process.
If we disagree on that, I can't help it.

The workaround to cope with this degradation in 4.6 is to set takeoff 
altitude extremely low (10m) and set a regular waypoint to the intended 
takeoff destination with the intended altitude that results in the pitch 
value, that would normally be provided in the takeoff mission item. This 
also counters crosswind perfectly.

BR

[log_19_2024-11-19-16-31-18.bin.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17947568/log_19_2024-11-19-16-31-18.bin.zip)


I believe this issue is being caused by the GUIDED mode SubMode not being set to take-off, as the automatic take-off was being performed by an external controller. Should this be allowed, or should users use the ArduCopter automatic take-off feature instead? In our use case, we are able to activate our external controller in mid-air anyway, which would remove the need for this, but I suppose some use cases might want to experiment with external controllers for take-off.

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @afonsoVale,

The internal error is coming from [this line in the landing detector](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/Copter-4.5/ArduCopter/land_detector.cpp#L57) and I think we've probably fixed the issue in Copter-4.6 with [this PR](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/28129).

I wonder if you'd be happy to re-test with 4.6.0-beta1?  It's an early beta so there is a chance that it has issues but developers have been flying it so my guess is that it is safe.  Another option is to back-port the fix to 4.5.  It's probably quite straight forward if you're happy to re-compile AP.  If you're not then I could create a binary for you.

You could also get around the issue by changing how the companion computer attempts to control the vehicle.  Currently GUID_OPTIONS = 8 so the external computer's SET_ATTITUDE_TARGET message's Thrust field are interpreted as actual thrust instead of climb rates.  That matches the MAVLink spec but most people find it easier to control using climb rates

author: afonsoVale
body:
Hi @rmackay9,

Thank you for the response. I will have a try with the 4.6.0-beta1 and I'll get back to you.  I'm happy to compile AP as well, so I can integrate the PR in the current stable version as well, thank you for the help! From looking at the PR, I am unsure if it will fix it though, as I would imagine in our scenario set_angle() is never called with use_thrust = False, but I will for sure have a try.

About changing how the companion computer control the vehicle, I agree. Unfortunately in this application we have some MSc and PhD students who are working with MRS (https://ctu-mrs.github.io) for their higher level applications, and unfortunately this MRS framework relies on using thrust commands only rather than climb rate, although in my opinion using climb rate would be preferable as it would probably be safer and more stable too. (Note that MRS doesn't claim to be compatible with ArduPilot, but we have made the effort to do some slight modifications to it in order to support ArduPilot, as in the end it is using mavros anyway)

author: peterbarker
body:
> Warning: Duplicate APJ board ID 1062 for different boards: MatekL431-Periph and MatekL431

As @tpwrules mentions - this isn't a problem with those sharing the same board ID.  You can flash *all sorts* of different firmwares to that board :-)

To some extent this is a problem where our hwdefs aren't just defining hardware but features to build into the firmware we run on the hardware.  Our entire include system is a bit of a kludge to get around the lack of separation around the concepts.
Pro-tip: hardware doesn't change between hwdef.dat and hwdef-bl.dat :-)

author: peterbarker

> These warnings look strange to me:

> HAL_MONITOR_THREAD_ENABLED already in defines with same value
> HAL_MONITOR_THREAD_ENABLED already in defines with same value

Yeah, that's a bit of linting that could be done; it means that a board which is including X is setting a define to the same value that the thing it is including has already set it to - so you can remove the define in the board doing the including.

author: IdoBuchman
title: Add support for signing configuration for separate MAVLink channels
body:
## Feature request

I want to activate signing on my MAVlink communication channel between the FCU and the Mission Planner. When I activate signing, all the mavlink ports get activated, including the mavlink port that communicates with my companion computer. Usually, there's no need to protect a wired Point to Point serial communication, and it requires ongoing support to keep the companion computer signing-key updated (If we want to change it from time to time).

### Solution Proposal
I suggest adding a new bitmask parameter that states which of the mavlink serial ports should work with signing. For keeping backward compatibility, we will make sure the default is 11111 (All ports activated).

Specifically, I found this code snippet under `libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Signing.cpp` lines 93-100, in updated master (commit 4b040eef93e):
```c
    // activate it immediately on all links:
    for (uint8_t i=0; i<MAVLINK_COMM_NUM_BUFFERS; i++) {
        GCS_MAVLINK *backend = gcs().chan(i);
        if (backend == nullptr) {
            return;
        }
        backend->load_signing_key();
    }
```
I assume that adding here a simple condition can do the job :smile: .

### Alternatives
* Using another existing parameter with a similar meaning to this I want to add, and use it instead of introducing a new one.
  * I searched through all the parameters in the copter documentation and did not find a good enough candidate.
* Adding a way to easily update my secret key on my companion computer
  * I found that it makes the operations and ongoing support inconvenient, and would be happy to have a better option.

**Platform**
[X] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: ohitstarik
title: Plane: Pullup passes wait_airspeed stage without ever meeting airspeed criteria
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

The new bugfix of pullup (https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/commit/1c194878ee6d527ba30cc35c44d4780f79dbc1cc ) changes the behavior of stage wait_airspeed such that the stage passes if the desired airspeed is reached or pitch is above pitch_min. This is meant to cover a scenario where pitch trim is bad enough that the airframe pulls up before the desired airspeed is reached, most likely leading to stalls, or the wait_airspeed stage never passing. 

However, more concerningly, this introduces situations where if the aircraft is in a freefall and:
- gets caught in a line
- is released from anywhere but the tail
- tumbles due to wind (lower altitude testing)
- or is in any other situation where it meets the criteria for pitch_min, 

wait_airspeed is passed, and the vehicle begins pulling up before it is allowed to gain enough airspeed to do so, or have a stable enough attitude to do so, both of which are critical to a successful pullup maneuver at high altitudes.

I believe this bugfix needs to be reworked, or rolled back. I don't see a situation where a team would send a vehicle up to altitude with bad pitch trim, or without having tested the vehicle and its pitch trim numerous times on the ground. Meanwhile, an in-flight error is spontaneous and could happen at any time, allowing pitch_min to be reached and causing errors during the pullup maneuver. 

**Version**
4.6.0 beta

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[ x ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: DjMixMasterDragon
body: Can confirm this issue - we just got bit by this bug in real flight past week. Glider did not release from balloon initially and pitch sensor triggered the WAIT_AIRSPEED - I am glad you brought this up. We have reverted since.

title: MAV_CMD_SET_HAGL not used by TECS to flare
body:
## Bug report

### Summary

TECS does not use the external HAGL set by the `AP_MAVLINK_MAV_CMD_SET_HAGL_ENABLED` subsystem.
Instead, it uses `Plane::height_above_target()`, which is not made aware of this information.

### Issue details

This aircraft uses a Lua script to read a lidar and feed the distance to ground via the `MAV_CMD_SET_HAGL` message.

There are two logs attached, with automated landings with flares:
One where the landing was good and the plane flared in time: [log_good](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xYY7FpCI-dDoRJzQOL8uId1odeByASra/view?usp=drive_link)

The good log has ~2.5m/s.

G: The good log triggers at 25m via `LAND_PF_ALT`.

body:
The problem with game controllers is that they generally can't output minimum throttle and maximum yaw at the same time due to the circular aperture. I'm not sure this is Copter's fault, though the thresholds are fixed.

The software reading the controller and converting it into commands can calibrate or map differently to resolve this, though I don't know if any software supports that.

author: rmackay9
body:
OK, if @tpwrules is right then the controller is probably internally converting the stick's square movements into a circle.  AP also does this conversion and it's important because when you put the sticks in the corners you don't want the vehicle's lean angle to be ANGLE_MAX in both roll and pitch because that would result in a total lean angle of more than ANGLE_MAX

A solution could be to add an RC_OPTION to disable AP's conversion from square to circle

author: tpwrules
body:
The sticks can't move in a square, they can only move in a circle. I don't think they are converting anything, unless you refer to the plastic of the controller housing.

I also think this conversion would happen after the check for arming. The [arming check](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/2feee53a375513ad74d0df1e9da668bbcab8b84e/ArduCopter/motors.cpp#L39) is simply min throttle and yaw channel > 88%.

author: rmackay9
title: Rover: replace arming-required with auto-arm-when-ready feature
body:
Rover has an arming-required parameter which can be set to false allowing the vehicle to be in an armed state even though it hasn't passed the arming checks.  I'm not a fan of this because it forces us to implement checks in other places to confirm the vehicle doesn't behave badly when it's in an unsafe state (e.g. Auto mode needs to double check that it has a position estimate).  Implementing these checks here and there is error prone.

A better solution could be to remove the arming-required parameter and instead add an auto-arm feature which automatically arms the vehicle once it has passes arming checks.

This issue comes from [this discussion](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/sailboats-over-the-world/125973/21)

author: UAVcihang
title: There is a fatal bug in task scheduling
body:
![1731309927894](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5995c81-c231-41c3-ba70-54c5a433087d)


As long as one task list times out, the order of other tasks cannot be guaranteed. This is a false design and should be designed so that each task is independent. It is recommended to cancel this task list and replace it with a timer task

author: UAVcihang
body:
![1731310204181](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/531bd433-68d1-4b9b-a8a5-29729f265bd7)
For example, adding printing or adding logs randomly will cause this task to time out, and other tasks will not have a chance to be executed. Only when the rc-loop execution ends, the tasks in the task list will be executed, and quick tasks will also have a chance.Hope to refactor the task scheduling of APM

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @UAVcihang,

Thanks for the investigation and report

I don't think this is a problem in practice.  The scheduler does not guarantee that all tasks will complete in a single loop.  Instead if a single task consumes all the time allowed for the loop (e.g. 2.5ms) then on the next loop the remaining tasks will be run.  The scheduler also does not guarantee the order that the tasks will be run in.

Of course, if you add very slow tasks into the scheduler then the vehicle will perform badly but the we also have higher level checks to warn the user if the main loop is not running at the desired rate.

I think I will close this but I'll see replies as will other developers.

Also if you can show that the scheduler is not performing as designed we can re-open the issue

author: Ryanf55
title: Plane will breach fence in GUIDED "Fly To" command when it could reject the command for convex inclusion fence
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

1. Set FENCE_ENABLE to 1
2. Set FENCE_ACTION to 1 (we care about breaching the fence, it's not just level 0)
3. Configure this fence 
[fence-items.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17685179/fence-items.txt)

4.  `mode takeoff`
5. `mode guided` once at altitude
6. Submit a "Fly To" waypoint INSIDE the inclusion fence, but where part of the inclusion fence obstructs the line connecting the plane and the point.
7. Observe the plane ACCEPT the command, then fly right into the fence.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/853b5b1a-f8de-4b8d-9e79-dc8293770767)


**Expected Behavior**
If the plane knows that it cannot reach a guided Fly  To waypoint without breaching the fence, reject the command. In the future, invoke a planner and fly around the fence. This is wasting battery right now, and knowingly doing unsafe commands. 
Shouldn't ardupilot do everything it can to avoid situations it breaches fence or wastes battery?

**Actual Behavior**
The `DO_POSITION` command is accepted, the plane flies towards the goal, hits the fence, then recognizes that, switches to RTL, and flies home. 

**Version**
master, hash `963095978b57e976223e58b922e1c415d8bc2090`, ~4.6
Using `MAVProxy Version: 1.8.71`

**Platform**

[  ] Submarine

**Note**

I'd like to improve behavior, let me know the desired behavior. We can improve both the GCS and the vehicle. It might be nice to see if QGC or mission planner handle this.

author: Hwurzburg
body: Missions act the same.....they will breach and take breach action....would it be better to avoid in Guided fly to's...yes...but also we should make prearm fails for missions that fly thru fences....both are generally bad things....copters are slow enough to avoid something more difficult in planes so having improved safeguard to prevent flights or fly-tos into fences would be a good option...the question is how difficult and how much flash?

author: IamPete1
body:
Because we don't cross track on guided commands you can't assume that we just fly in a straight line, so its not as easy as it might seem. You would have to build a path that takes into account the initial turn. 

The other option of course is not to breach the fence in the first place. Bendy ruler and Dijkstra's will come to plane eventually.

author: LupusTheCanine
body:
1. ArduPlane not being proactive about fences is a well documented state of things.
2. We shouldn't provide unreliable checks to the user and given effects of wind, turn radius and possible user inputs using stick mixing such early check will be fairly unreliable.
3. We should account for wind effects in proactive fence avoidance as it can have significant effect on effective "turning radius"
4. IMHO Bendy ruler should work but Dijkstra's isn't ready for turn radius considerations of plane.

author: peterbarker
body:
So the consensus seems to be that we can't tell ahead of time that we will or won't breach a fence.

When we get path-finding (and the user enables it) we could potentially reject targets if the path-finder can't find a path, but in the meantime I think we should close this one - it's well-known behaviour.

author: Ryanf55
body: For me, I think the docs on fence could make a clear disclaimer that * There are many situations to breach the fence, in most modes * users should ensure that fences are sufficiently far from any obstacles because fences cannot currently be used for safety applications. * Fence is completely disregarded in other modes, such as takeoff and RTL * Test extensively in SITL before attempting to rely on fences to keep the vehicle safe Here's another example of GUIDED flying straight until it hits the fence. AP could decide to turn before it hits the fence and never breach it. ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a13b9e77-c36d-4182-bdd0-f51924c28013) And another, accepting an auto mode where a path segment goes through an exclusion fence. It might be well known behavior for devs, but I don't think that's a good reason to not make this abundantly obvious to users that the fence implementation is not yet capable of keeping the vehicle where the user configured it to fly.

author: Hwurzburg
body:
the statement "Fence is completely disregarded in other modes, such as takeoff and RTL" is not true.....fences are active and work in those modes, fence actions are limited, however....RTLing as an action in RTL mode is pretty feeble, but it does work,just doesn't do much....RTL in takeoff works on breach...

" fences cannot currently be used for safety applications." is a misstatement..
fences can indeed be used for safety purposes if constructed correctly.....Copter AVOIDs fence breaches in many cases....Plane primarily takes action to mitigate fence breaches....the only Plane fences that attempt avoidance are altitude limits

so I think a bit more accurate wording could be added, and I will attempt it when I get a chance
