author: SeptentrioGNSS
title: Request to remove or alter auto config for Septentrio GNSS receiver
body:
## Feature request
In the current and latest stable version of the ArduPilot code for the implementation of Septentrio receivers (SBF), there is an auto config for a logged stream to the internal disk of the receiver. The mention of this stream is in the file: **AP_GPS_SBF.h**. Is there a possibility to make it more configurable for any user to specify if they want this stream logged and what content needs to be logged. 

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
_A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...]_
Currently a setSBFOutput command is sent to the receiver. It overwrites configurations made on the receiver side or it might not be needed by the user to have this log and there is no way of removing this from the auto config. As there is no parameters to change the contents of the command this is very limiting as the overwrite happens on every boot of the autopilot. After boot the connected receiver needs to be reprogrammed in order to have the right configurations for a flight.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
_A clear and concise description of what you want to happen._
More customisation could be accomplished by adding 4 variables in MissionPlanner:
- Logging interval (OFF, sec1, msec100, msec50, OnChange) 
- Logged messages (Postprocess, PP+Support, PP+Support+BBSamples, PP+Event+Comment+ReceiverStatus)
- Logging overwrite (On, OFF)
- Advanced option (having an open field where commands in Septentrio format can be sent to the receiver)

With these variables the content of the message sent to the Septentrio receiver can be customised from MissionPlanner itself. The OFF variable assignment would mean no message regarding logging is sent. The variables define the fields needed in the Septentrio command line interface (CLI) command where the interval, the kind of messages logged and an overwrite can be set by the user. The advanced option would allow for an open text field that anny Septentrio command can be sent to the receiver. 

Regarding the other fields in the command (e.g. Stream# or Dsk1) it is fine to keep them fixed as I would suggest only making a note which states the usage of the fixed fields in the command so the user is aware of this on the README of the GPSdriver or the .h or .cpp of the SBF code. 


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
_A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered._
Removing the command so that the receiver logging configuration is not touched by MissionPlanner and all the necessary configurations can be made from Septentrio software tools but this adds a level of extra work as not everything can be done from MissionPlanner itself. The preferred solution is the one above as this incorporates a mostly all-in-one solution for integrations of ArduPilot and Septentrio GNSS receivers. 

**Platform**
[ X ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[ X ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
_Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here._
![ArduPilot_Code](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/151617650/989b381f-817a-4268-ad57-cde73084e5ff)
code in question is at line 87

author: peterbarker
body: Ping @WickedShell , who is responsible for the current logging settings and might have a vested interest in the current settings

author: WickedShell
body:
There are a couple of things we can do here, listed in ease of things that already exist:

- You can add custom configuration lines to the hwdef and do a custom build, which would allow specifying a different logging stream to be specified. This will technically send the hard coded line first, then follow it up with the custom one, which isn't great, but would work. The other downside is that this requires you to have a custom build which is less commonly available.
- You can send gps data injections from the GCS, there's exsisting MAVLink handling for this, but I don't think there is a convenient interface in MP for it. I've used this in a custom GCS to inject 1 way configuration messages to the GPS driver. This is annoying to do every boot though, and obviously is pretty custom again.
- Now we are at the spot of new changes. The easiest change is to make it so that if GPS_RAW_DATA was set to 0 to not emit the logging message at all from the configuration. Adding more meanings to this is a bit harder, as we've already made 2 have a special case for Septentrio GPS units (unmount the SD card when disarmed).
- Do something more complicated, as proposed above, but which is a bit harder to generalize for all units, although we could lean against the per driver specific parameters.

Regarding the comments made, I'd really prefer the ArduPilot implementation of logging continue to request `Comment+ReceiverStatus` as from a support perspective I've found both of these to be extremely useful, and pretty light weight. And if you are logging `PostProcess` having `Event` seems much more useful, and again if it's not connected it should be pretty low impact. Are you seeing problems with this?

My builds have been adding the `Support` block as I've found it to be valuable and nice. (I can be convinced it should be in the default logging set). If we add that in, that would only leave us needing to add a flag for `BBSamples` and rates I guess.

author: flyingthingsintothings
body:
I would like to work on this issue. I discussed the implementation with @SeptentrioGNSS and we had the following idea for a more flexible logging implementation.

There could be three new parameters added in the `GPS` module. The first would allow the user to choose a logging frequency from a set of discrete values (Off (0Hz), 0.1Hz, 0.5Hz, 1Hz... 20Hz). This frequency would then be used on a best-effort basis by every driver that wants to support custom logging frequency. Users could choose Off (0Hz) to disable logging completely which would prevent any logging setup from being performed on the receiver. The second parameter would represent a logging level that is then translated by each driver into actual data that makes sense for that level (e.g. `Lite` logs only contain `Comment+ReceiverStatus` on Septentrio GNSS receivers, `Basic` contains `Lite` + `PostProcess+Support`...). The levels could be called `Lite`, `Basic`, `Default` and `Full`. The specific data at each level for Septentrio GNSS receivers isn't decided yet, but would be properly documented so users know which level logs what. The third parameter would be used to indicate whether logging should be added to any existing logging that is already on the receiver, or would overwrite it.

Suggested names for the parameters would be `GPS_LOG_HZ` for the logging frequency, `GPS_LOG_LEVEL` for the logging level and `GPS_LOG_FORCE` for log overwriting.

The advantage of this approach is that the parameters are detailed enough for users to configure logging how they want, while being generic enough to support different drivers/receivers without adding driver-specific parameters. Any driver-specific things could be documented so users are aware whether their receiver will support the chosen parameter values.

I would love any input on this approach.

author: peterbarker

I don't know how checking after every write helps at all.

Your bootloader is hosed after a single bad write - whether we detect that straight-away or by doing the checksum isn't important.

Given you also need to erase entire sectors to fix the bad write, even working out that a particular page write failed isn't helpful.

Perhaps I'm misunderstanding the problem you're outlining.

author: Ryanf55
title: ArduPilot's use of submodules and recommended workflow hose the git tree when rebasing on top of master
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

When using git submodules, when they are moved around, it causes major issues when switching branches.

**Version**

* Start with HEAD at 5c1ed968b18ea196b8376cdd6cc7aeae9b3085c4 then try rebase on f67d8956778de0ed1e5ddebf159ecd1ca0f6f3d7

* git version: 2.34.1

* OS of Ubuntu 22.04.3

**Platform**
[x ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start with an empty directory
1. Clone my repo as origin ryanf55/ardupilot with --recurse-submodules at hash 5c1ed968b18ea196b8376cdd6cc7aeae9b3085c4
1. Change directory into ardupilot
1. Add an "upstream" remote of ardupilot/ardupilot
1. Fetch upstream
1. Rebase origin on upstream
1. Congrats, the work tree is hosed

**Attempted recovery**

* git submodule deinit --all --force
* git clean -dxf
* git reset --hard origin/master
* ./Tools/gittools/submodule-sync.sh
* git reset --hard upstream/master
* $ git reset --hard upstream/master
```
fatal: not a git repository: ../../.git/modules/modules/lwip
error: Submodule 'modules/lwip' could not be updated.
error: Submodule 'modules/lwip' cannot checkout new HEAD.
fatal: Could not reset index file to revision 'upstream/master'.
```


**Logs**

Full logs to reproduce this are attached.
[log.txt](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/files/13999273/log.txt)

The exact error occurs here:
```
ryan@B650-970:~/Dev/tmp_ws/ardupilot$ git rebase upstream/master
fatal: not a git repository: ../../.git/modules/modules/lwip
fatal: could not reset submodule index
error: could not detach HEAD
```

**Recommendations**

1. Add documentation to the [wiki on how to switch branches and rebase without error](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/git-rebase.html)
OR
1. Switch to a different version control tool for dependencies such as Conan, CPM, VCS, Google Repo

**References**

* https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Tools-Submodules#Issues-with-Submodules
* https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45215094/git-giving-warning-unable-to-rmdir/64724218#64724218

author: Craig-1965
body:
Hi all.

I have had the same problem with the PH6C Mini 

First issue was in a field test, I unfortunately had the internal compass temporarily disabled. The drone had been flying perfectly and was well tuned.  All of a sudden it turned 90 degrees and flew off at a speed in excess of 120km/h, never to be seen again.

The next drone I had to disarm and violently crash a flyaway mid flight due to the External compass disappearing an the Satellite connection degrading drastically (simultaneously) it dropped 60% of Connected satellites.

Product support from Holybro was poor and they attempted to place the blame cack on my setup.  To add context we have over 250 units in flight using the PH4 Mini and Pix32 from Holybro and no other such issues.

I have tested the setup ad nauseum using the HolyBro M8N, M9N and newest M10N and had intermittent faults on all.  Just powering the drone up and letting it stand for an hour,, powered up and along the way the External Compass Disappears and connected satellites will drop fom 18-21 down to 9-11.

Holybro**

author: David-OConnor
title: Request: QSPI flash storage
body:
I am requesting support for QuadSPI (QSPI) flash support on ArduPilot for use with Flash storage, as an alternative to SPI flash and SD Cards. QSPI is a protocol explicitly designed for use with flash memory.

Reasons:
- QSPI is a faster alternative to SPI flash, and can use memory mapping
- QSPI has no downsides compared to SPI other than requiring more pins
- All STM32 MCUs supported by AP have a QSPI peripheral
- Most (all?) memory chips supported by AP are capable of QSPI.

As an engineer, I would, choose QSPI over SPI for flash storage for any project that uses an MCU with QSPI support. So, it was surprising that AP supports traditional SPI for flash, but not QSPI.


[STM32H743 Reference manual](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/dm00314099-stm32h742-stm32h743-753-and-stm32h750-value-line-advanced-arm-based-32-bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) See Chapter 23: QUAD-SPI Interface

author: magicrub
body: Why do you think it's not supported? Have you checked? I count 7 hwdef targets in master that use it. Search for a hwdef that contains `QUADSPI_CLK`.

author: David-OConnor
body:
Could you please confirm that it is supported for data storage? My understanding is this is not the case, and it is only supported for program storage. You'll note that the targets you list are for ones with the <2Mb flash AP requires. (STM32H750 etc)

I don't think this should be marked `closed as completed`.

author: magicrub
body:
Well, you're half right. None of them use them as a dedicated non-volatile memory for params and missions. We've gone to an even faster model: use the internal program flash of the STM. A nice example of this is CubeRed where it uses 2x 128kB flash pages in the H757 for storage but then also has [QSPI for another lots-of-megabyte storage](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_HAL_ChibiOS/hwdef/CubeRedPrimary/hwdef.dat#L191C31-L191C31) for program memory.

There's actually no advantage of using QSPI for the small amount of flash we use for params and missions. For logs, that will never be enough, you'd need eMMC or an SD card for multi-gigabyte storage.. so QSPI eeprom ends up just being a waste of pins.

What did you have in mind? [Join us on our weekly developer call](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/ardupilot-discord-server.html#weekly-dev-calls) on Discord to talk about it!

author: IamPete1
title: Plane: Altitude wait: Servo wiggle does not work for left elevon.
body:
Plane "wiggles" servos in altitude wait. However because the same value is output to aileron elevator and rudder simultaneously the wiggles cancel out for left elevon (also V tail right I think). 

The fix would be to stagger the wiggles, so we wiggle aileron then elevator then rudder. This would mean both elevons do a "double wiggle" of half amplitude. 

This is the function that would need updating:

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/6fb99d6b1ebc5bf3bbd8edef199fd0bc8b34100f/ArduPlane/servos.cpp#L350-L383

title: Powerflag 0x16 on pixhawk 6c constantly upped
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

Hello! Powerflag 0x16 *MAV_POWER_STATUS_PERIPH_HIPOWER_OVERCURRENT=16, /* hi-power peripheral supply is in over-current state | */* is always upped, even fc is connected via USB to PC

**Version**
ArduCopter V4.3.2 (fcef79e7)
ChibiOS: 66e5de0d

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[ *] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
Hexacopter

**Hardware type**
Pixhawk 6C
**Logs**
As we can see [here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_HAL_ChibiOS/hwdef/Pixhawk6C/hwdef.dat) analog inputs are defined
```
# power sensing
PE3 VDD_5V_PERIPH_nOC INPUT PULLUP
PF13 VDD_5V_HIPOWER_nOC INPUT PULLUP
```
But STM32H743 (TFBGA100) doesnt have PF13)) Actually fault signal from ic bq24315DSG goes to pin B8 (PC11)

![photo_2023-08-18_13-45-07](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/142419832/bcff684a-b9fe-470a-b788-5522f37642fd)

PE2 (A3) - nVDD_5V_PERIPH_EN  OUTPUT HIGH
PE3 (B3) - VDD_5V_PERIPH_nOC INPUT PULLUP
PC10 (B9) - nVDD_5V_HIPOWER_EN OUTPUT HIGH
PC11 (B8) - VDD_5V_HIPOWER_nOC INPUT PULLUP

**Also!!**
Fault pin of bq24315DSG  is pulled up by 47K resistor. In same time STM input is pulled up logicaly.
Thats why STM will never detect low level on its pins))
![Screenshot_20230818_133849](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/142419832/e7f2a4ad-e3f5-4fc4-813f-544171420993)

author: stephendade
title: Rover: Circle mode instabilities
body:
Whilst attempting to tune my rover, I experienced some serious instabilities and "wandering off" in circle mode:

5m circle at 2m/s speed:
![xmaxx-2ms](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/1731976/75b908e8-f6a7-4d9a-a58f-9d1c64e4c18b)

A 5m circle at 1m/s speed was fine.

My current theory is that the default steering PID values are too low for this particular vehicle. I've confirmed in manual mode that the vehicle can definitely turn at the rates needed for a 5m circle at 2m/s (23deg/sec).

I could replicate it in SITL via restricting the ``ATC_STR_ACC_MAX`` and ``ATC_STR_RAT_MAX`` parameters to below the minimum degrees/sec required for the circle. So:
```
param set CIRC_RADIUS 5
param set CIRC_SPEED 4
param set ATC_STR_ACC_MAX 90
param set ATC_STR_RAT_MAX 30
```
SITL result:
![sitl](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/1731976/9ace43ee-a505-4bb2-a86c-00f379f4ab4f)


I usually wouldn't be concerned about an untuned vehicle performing badly in these higher level flight modes, but given the Quiktune feature requires running in circle mode, it should be expected that untuned vehicles will be running in this mode.

For a fix, I'd suggest that circle mode needs to stop the vehicle if it gets more than X metres outside the circle (where X is +20% on radius?) and suggest to the user that they either a) Increase the radius b) decrease the speed c) increase the Steering PID FF(?).

Alternatively, maybe the way circle mode calculates it's trajectory needs to be improved? I feel that it does wander more than necessary ... it's like it gives up after a while!

author: rmackay9
body: yes, I've seen these problems as well actually but haven't found a way to protect against the problem.  I think the issue occurs because we pass a target position, velocity and acceleration to the position controller but even a large position error does not overpower the velocity and acceleration inputs.  So maybe the solution should be that the desired velocity and acceleration only get to use whatever control bandwidth is left after the velocity and acceleration required to shrink the position error has been calculated.

author: stephendade
body:
As an update to anyone with a similar problem: Increasing ``ATC_STR_RAT_FF`` can "fix" the issue until a quiktune can be run.

>So maybe the solution should be that the desired velocity and acceleration only get to use whatever control bandwidth is left after the velocity and acceleration required to shrink the position error has been calculated.

So, emphasising having the correct position over having the correct forward velocity? It'd be sensible that the vehicle would slow down its velocity if it can't make the turn in time - much like AUTO mode's slowing-down-in-corners.

author: Ryanf55
title: EAHRS is performing duplicate temperature compenstation
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

Certain devices exposed through EAHRS, like the MicroStrain7, supply data that is already temperature compenstated.

https://s3.amazonaws.com/files.microstrain.com/GQ7+User+Manual/external_content/dcp/Data/sensor_data/data/mip_field_sensor_scaled_mag.htm
https://s3.amazonaws.com/files.microstrain.com/GQ7+User+Manual/external_content/dcp/Data/sensor_data/data/mip_field_sensor_scaled_accel.htm

When the External AHRS driver posts data to sensor libraries, they perform temperature compenstation on it again, as long as `HAL_INS_TEMPERATURE_CAL_ENABLE` is defined, which is based on board size.  

_Please describe the problem_

This causes double temperature compensation, leading to incorrect values.

**Proposed Solution**
Add `bool is_temperature_compensated;` to `AP_ExternalARHS::ins_data_message_t`, and then add the necessary hooks in `AP_InertialSensor::handle_external(const AP_ExternalAHRS::ins_data_message_t &pkt)` to stop doing temperature compensation if the supplied value is already temp-compensated.

See `ryanf55:eahrs-precompensated-sensors` for a prototype fix (WIP)

**Version**
master `1e644d56a51806b63dcd68d5e6566ec0f10248fc`

**Platform**
[ x] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: Ryanf55
body:
instead of a bool, use a 3-value enum

```
IsTempCalibrated
IsNotTempCalibrated
DoesntProvideTemp
```

Airspeed already handles this well, can copy the logic. 


This could be bad for the board - if EAHRS hard codes 25C, but board wants to be at 30C, and it uses the EAHRS temperature, than the board heater will stay on.

author: Ryanf55
title: AP_DDS: Gracefully handle runtime home location change
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

If the user uses their GCS to change the home location, the published local pose data in DDS will jump. Additionally, applications like terrain planners commanding position in global coordinates with an altitude frame relative to home will have the altitude wrong now. This could cause a crash if the new home location is significantly below the previous one because the plane will fly into the ground. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a notification in AP_Notify for a home change event, and then use that event to propogate the new home location via the static transform tree. This tree is currently populated in `AP_DDS_Client::populate_static_transforms`, but does not include the home position.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Prevent the user from changing home when DDS is enabled

**Additional context**

See https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/25722, which is vulnerable to a runtime home location change

author: robustini
title: Plane (tailsitter): starts the descent on the home only after it reaches it
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The most critical phase of a non-vectored tailsitter flight is landing.
After the transition in the case of (Q)RTL, the taisitter when switch into VTOL mode immediately begins the descent and repositioning to the home point.
These two simultaneous maneuvers often cause instability, especially in windy conditions.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Instead, it would be very helpful if the tailsitter in the case of RTL behaved in this way:

1) Once the transition from plane to vtol is made, the code should store the height reached immediately after the transition angle
2) Waits a couple of seconds for it to stabilize perfectly vertically, only then reposition to the home point while maintaining the stored height
3) Start the descent for the land only after reaching the home after a few seconds so as to stabilize

Basically the behavior would be as if after a transition from Cruise to QLoiter the pilot waits a few seconds with the sticks centered, then gives a pitch and roll command by repositioning the tailsitter at the desired point while keeping the throttle in the center of the stick, once the point is reached he puts the throttle at idle to make the descent.
When doing this with tx the tailsitter is absolutely stable, during RTL it is not.
I have performed transitions from Cruise to QLoiter with repositioning hundreds of times without any problems, but RTL remains critical instead because precisely to repositioning it adds descent.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[ x ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

Hi @nishant-sg, I tested the latest fix and always make a video to show its behavior, and I insert in the second RTL some wind to increase the difficulty.
As soon as the transition to VTOL is done it does not stop 5 seconds (I dropped from 7) as I had requested but proceeds towards immediately to home, it would be needed instead what I had requested.
Very good behavior instead when it gets to home, stops 5 seconds and performs LAND.
And you can see very well that now it doesn't go out of the flight envelope, it was as I thought, great!
So once the pause is inserted even immediately after the transition the change is perfect, it was as I predicted, well done!
The 5-second pauses should be two, one immediately after the transition into VTOL and the other (which works now) when it gets to home before doing the QLAND.
This first pause is useful to further stabilize the tailsitter at the end of the transition and in the case of weathervaning to allow it to perform the automatic yaw rotation before beginning XY repositioning at constant Z, i.e. to translate to the home sideways.
The second first immediately of the QLAND, i.e. the one that now works prevents starting the descent without first the tailsitter being stable with the nose up after repositioning in XY at constant Z.

body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Edgetx has telemetry mirror and it could out crsf telemetry data received from the drone, and GPS coordinates is included. There is no point of using a dedicated telemetry radio to get gps coordinates from drones if we can just use the telemetry from or radio controller. By doing so we could save both weight and money when building an aat

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Support for reading and decoding crsf raw telemetry data to get gps coordinates from drones.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Considered an Arduino to do the translation, from crsf to mavlink but it’s just more money and complexity.

author: timtuxworth
body:
Some thoughts to be included in a good definition of fences are included in this PR #25875  that @andyp1per and @Hwurzburg  have been working on regarding the current implementation.

The current implementation is not a good model, so it would be great if we can come up with something much better. Ideally for example, it should be possible to define behavior such as "return inside the fence" on breach - following a path that minimizes the amount of time spent outside the fence, and auto-reactivating the fence after the vehicle has returned inside the fence. (the fence is deactivated on breach ATM), as well as ideally avoiding the fence in the first place, which currently works for Copter (and Rover I think) but definitely doesn't work for Plane.

author: robustini
title: Copter: Waypoint "STOP & TURN" function
body:
It would be very useful to implement a stop & turn function where the drone stops on the WP, turns in the direction of the next WP, and then continues in the direction of the next WP and so on.
This function is very useful for missions with magnetometer or LiDAR scanners where the drone is already facing the next waypoint at the beginning of the line, as is already possible in DJI drone mission planners.
This function is necessary to avoid losing data during scanning, as the drone now rotates as it travels to the next WP.
I remember many years ago this function was implemented, originally the Copter did this, and I was the one who asked to not stop over the wp to correct by yaw but to do it while moving.
Unfortunately, I now realize that this behavior could have been useful as well.
The video describes the functionality, achieved with the help of the condition yaw and delay events, which is quite tricky.


https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/3864712/596c7c31-0e7d-4ed9-92be-4aa31d58f110

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[ x ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: PUNEET-KOUNDAL
body:
Hey sir,

I'm looking to enhance waypoint navigation for a drone by implementing a stop-and-turn functionality. This would involve the drone pausing at a waypoint, turning to face the next one, and then resuming its mission. I've seen a video using "condition yaw" and "delay events" for this purpose.

Before I start the implementation, I have a few queries:

1. **Preferred Technologies:** Any recommendations on the technologies or libraries that work well for waypoint navigation and turning in a drone? I want to make sure the solution aligns with the existing tech stack.

2. **Precautions:** What precautions should I consider when implementing a stop-and-turn function? Are there potential issues, such as drift or calibration challenges, that I should be mindful of?

3. **Community Contributions:** Has anyone in the community worked on a similar feature? I'd like to leverage existing knowledge and possibly contribute to an ongoing effort.

4. **Alternative Approaches:** I'm leaning towards a stop-and-turn approach, but I'm open to other ideas. What's your opinion on using fan RPM for smoother turns? I'm concerned about the potential impact on balance.

I'd really appreciate your insights and any guidance you can provide!

author: peterbarker
body:
Sooo... this one can be done on a normal waypoint by setting param1 to a non-zero value.  It does mean a 1 second pause, but given the dynamics desired I don't think that's a big issue...

Closing this one - but please feel free to re-open if the 1-second thing is insufficient....

author: rmackay9
body:
Hi @peterbarker,

Thanks for all the efforts to clear up old issues. I think we should actually leave this one open because the request is that the vehicle proactively turn on the waypoint before proceeding.  At the moment, the vehicle will start turning **after** it starts towards the next waypoint.

body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Similar to the GSOF support for configuring the driver and testing the configuration ability in SITL, the same thing is desired in MicroStrain. Currenly, users must use Sensor Connect to set up all the parameters. It's not documented how to do this. Rather than force users to perform all data rate setup in sensor connect, which is error prone and the driver cannot handle if you miss a single sub-packet, let's have ArduPilot configure the data rates it needs for all the channels.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

* Use GPS_RATE_JHZ to control GPS rate
* Add EAHRS params for desired IMU rate and desired filter rate
* Use the disable/enable packets support to put 3DM QG7 in standby while doing configuration, then resume once configuration is complete
* Tie this into `initialised()` front end such that the backend does not report initialization success until all configuration is set up and ACK'd

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Rely on users doing everything perfect in SensorConnect, which is windows only.

author: tkoivuro
title: Diagnostics/status meassages from FC to GCS are easy to miss
body:
Background: 

We are utilizing Arduplane and several different vendor FC hardware to fly BVLOS mapping missions with both traditional fixed wing planes and VTOLs. CGS is running MissionPlanner. 

What i would like to improve:

Telemetry connection between FC and CGS is not always perfect, as well as person who is sitting in front of the computer is not perfect. If telemetry connection is unstable as it sometimes happens, things like EKF lane switches, Airspeed sensore failures or GPS primary changes may go completely unnoticed by the person who is monitoring the flight at the CGS computer. Also our typical missions are 100s of waypoints long (1-2 hour flight time) even with perfect telemetry these messages tend to get lost between all waypoint reached messages. 

If the sensor configuration (Actice EKF lane, Primary GPS, Primary air speed source etc) changes during the AUTO mission the FC should constantly send some sort of warning message to GCS that could not be missed even if there is only very little telemetry connectivity.  Also there is no way to tell if Q assist has been activated in VTOL plane during the flight which annoying. Q assist is great helper but flight team *needs* to know if it has been activated. It is set in a way it sould never activate if things are going well.   

Currently we are utilizing companion computer on board that picks up these messages from mavlink data stream before it gets sent to the telemetry radio but this is pretty complicated and heavy solution for something that should run inside of the FC.

**Platform**
[ x ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

I have done many tests with that rx and this F405 FC and unfortunately I found that the problem is systematic.
After less than a minute the receiver stops communicating with the FC and obviously the fiaisafe enters.

I then contacted Fr-Sky asking whether the FPort protocol was different between ACCESS and ACCST firmware but rightly so if it works with Betaflight it is not a problem with the rx ACCESS firmware.

Sorry, for more context, that was notes from today's dev call.

 One reason I couldn't get DDS working over serial was because `SERIAL1_PROTOCOL` on most boards is not the 2nd USB interface. 
See here for CubeOrange: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/69bfe9b8375feb94e657cf99ba3f2809dbfd9f8e/libraries/AP_HAL_ChibiOS/hwdef/CubeOrange/hwdef.inc#L30-L31

author: maripuusiim
body:
It is possible that this issue might not appear with GNSS modules that have a slower hot fix time. I’m open to performing further tests on my system if anyone has better suggestions than delay.


We have been using DDS over serial PPP network on a KakuteH7-Wing with Mosaic-H GNSS module, running the exact same firmware for several months. Initially, both GNSS antenna cables were 2.5 m long to achieve better moving base yaw performance. The DDS initialization issue appeared only after shortening the antenna cables to 0.5 m. Mosaic-H has a hot fix of ~20 s (factory specs).

Before adding an additional delay before main loop in `AP_DDS_Client.cpp`, we performed repeated tests in indoor-outdoor scenarios, as well as quick sequential startups in a van (without GNSS signal) versus under open sky conditions. In all cases, DDS initialization consistently succeeded only without GNSS signal. After adding 5s delay the initialization issue has not reappeared over several days and approximately 10 flights.

author: clydemcqueen
title: Add signal_quality to RangeFinder_State
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Background: several rangefinder backends support signal quality (BLPing, LightWareSerial, MAVLink). For these backends the distance and signal quality are stored separately: distance is copied from the backend to the frontend by `update()` but signal quality remains in the backend and is accessed by `get_signal_quality_pct(...)`.

The problem: the backend API doesn't support a way to get the (distance, signal quality) tuple. Callers can get the distance from the frontend and the signal quality from the backend, but they might be out of sync. This is OK for most use cases, but it is hard to reason about and it makes testing tricky.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a field `signal_quality` to `RangeFinder_State`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Add a method `AP_RangeFinder_Backend::get_measurement(uint16_t &distance_cm, int8_t &quality_pct)`.

**Platform**
[ x ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover

title: AP_Servo/RC_Channel: RCIn3Scaled incorrect on Copter at least
body:
As [reported here in the 4.4 forums](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/release-rover-4-4-as-stable-ok/106080/6), when a Servo output is set to RCIN3Scaled on Copter the output is always in the range 1500 to 2000 when it should be between 1000 and 2000.

The issue is probably that the line in SRV_Channel_aux.cpp responsible for calculating the output PWM is using [RC_Channel::norm_input_dz()](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/RC_Channel/RC_Channel.cpp#L419) which returns a value of -1 to +1 when the input has ControlType::Angle but returns 0 to +1 when ControlType:Range.

`radio_in = pwm_from_angle(c->norm_input_dz() * 4500);`

See actual code line [here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/SRV_Channel/SRV_Channel_aux.cpp#L63).

author: Ryanf55
title: AP_GPS_GSOF: Support GPS_RAW_DATA for external logging
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Right now, there is no way to enable the internal logging on the PX1 GNSS  because the API is only available over the ethernet web UI. Internal logging is used for tech support to analyze system performance. Since PX1 has little flight hours on small fixed wing drones, this is particularly useful to have the ArduPilot community be able to supply logs.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

* Consume [GPS_RAW_DATA](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/parameters.html#gps-raw-data-raw-data-logging) in AP_GPS_GSOF
* Handle disabling logging on disarm, and log continuation on arm
* Send enable logging/disable logging commands as appropriate
* Stretch: Handle runtime param updates
* Update wiki entry for PX1: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot_wiki/pull/5540/files
* Create follow up issue for dealing with log data filling up and whether old logs are overwritten, the user is notified that logs are full, or something else

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Connect laptop temporarily.

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine


## Further details

The following binary data commands are what need to be sent for logging. There is no TransNumber, so just hard code these in the implementation file. If there is an ACK, parse the ACK.
```
Start Logging: 02 00 4C 09 08 44 45 46 41 55 4C 54 00 62 03 
Stop Logging: 02 00 4C 09 09 44 45 46 41 55 4C 54 00 63 03
```

## Dependencies

The configuration ack/nack pattern from `gsof-49-50` branch needs to be merged in before there is ability to do configuration responses. This ticket could be done without acks, however it will need to be changed.

author: Ryanf55
body:
The wiki is very brief: 
https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/apmcopter-programming-libraries.html

The main interface for GPS is here: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_GPS/AP_GPS.h

This library follows the frontend-backend split. 
https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/code-overview-sensor-drivers.html#frontend-backend-split

Implementation that all GPS's follow is here:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_GPS/AP_GPS.cpp

GSOF header file: 
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_GPS/AP_GPS_GSOF.h

GSOF implementation: 
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_GPS/AP_GPS_GSOF.cpp

For retrieving a parameter from the param server, you can do it like so:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/2e5af08a102d10b8b7d54414c7aa4f12f4a80ab9/libraries/AP_GPS/AP_GPS_GSOF.cpp#L63

Then, you need to write a validation function to ensure the user has not put a bogus value for the param, since param limits are not enforced:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/2e5af08a102d10b8b7d54414c7aa4f12f4a80ab9/libraries/AP_GPS/AP_GPS_GSOF.cpp#L363
For example, if a user sets `GPS_RAW_DATA` to a value of `99`, the validation helper should return false.

Next, write the implementation of the logger configuration message, similar to `requestBaud`:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/2e5af08a102d10b8b7d54414c7aa4f12f4a80ab9/libraries/AP_GPS/AP_GPS_GSOF.cpp#L164

The packet buffer structure was detailed on the initial issue description; seems like you can just hard code it as a `constexpr` buffer.

Make sure to calculate the checksum AFTER populating the transaction number `buffer[4]`.

> @Ryanf55 The second last hexadecimal is supposed to be checksum right? The checksum is a uint8_t. We rely on natural overflow of the uint8_t for it to work. 0x264 larger than the max value of uint8_t. Also, the first 0x02 is also excluded.

title: H743 I2C bug
body:
I have been upgrading a boat from a Omnibusf4pro to a Matek H743 Wlite. but I have ran into an issue with the i2c bus where setting an address of 0x70 on my sr04 sonar adapter (default for maxbotix i2c sonar) causing the i2c bus to lock up and stop detecting devices. 


the sonar was working on the omnibusf4pro before I changed over the controller so I thought I might have damaged something.
 I originally thought it was a wiring issue, so tested the adapter on a different H743 and it had the same result
 I thought the atmega168 might have got damaged somehow, so I swapped it for another 168 and same result.
 I thought it could be an issue with the 168, so I changed it for a 328 and same result 
so just to rule out some kind of software problem, I connected yuris i2c sensor adapter that runs on a 168 with address 9 and it worked fine. 

so i went and got the original 168 and tested it again with the original omnibusf4pro and it works, so now I know it's definitely not a sensor or adapter software or Arduino issue.

 I tried changing the sonar adapter to the same 0x09 9 address as the sensor adapter and it shows up on the i2c scanner and i can get it to work using the lightware i2c driver set to i2c 9 so its not a hardware issue.

If I change the sonar address back to its default 0x70 112 without doing anything else it will show up for a few seconds, then the i2c bus stops until I unplug it.

The compass is connected as i2c device 13, you can see it going offline after i change the sonar adapter i2c address.

author: Ryanf55
body:
I propose that a [MAV_CMD_DO_REPOSITION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_REPOSITION) with param3 set to `NaN` or `0.0`, that plane will interpret it as a fly through. 
If it is not fed another waypoint by the time is passes through the configured `WP_LOITER_RAD`, then it will circle the point.

This allows you to dynamically feed waypoints using Guided mode, and you only have to send the next point if the vehicle is within the destination by `WP_LOITER_RAD` to achieve a decent looking path that's close to auto's behavior.

author: timtuxworth
body:
In my plane follow script I achieve this by setting the waypoint radius p3 = 2.0 (i.e. 2 meters), this means it flies to within 2m of the location. By the time it gets that close to the WP, I've already dropped a new waypoint further ahead, so it never gets anywhere near the point. 

I agree - this is a problem that needs a solution.

author: timtuxworth
body:
> I propose that a [MAV_CMD_DO_REPOSITION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_REPOSITION) with param3 set to `NaN` or `0.0`, that plane will interpret it as a fly through. If it is not fed another waypoint by the time is passes through the configured `WP_LOITER_RAD`, then it will circle the point.

0 (zero), actually coded as <= 1, is already a special case - it means "use WP_LOITER_RAD". Maybe use the value 2 as the special case? Maybe NaN might work.

author: Ryanf55
title: Implement MAVLINK RFC0016 Support for Custom Modes for Companion/Lua to show custom mode on GCS
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When ROS wants to control a vehicle, the mode it's operating in is always reported as GUIDED, regardless of what kind of operation the companion computer is in. The user on the GCS sees Guided in ArduPilot. 

Reviewing the mavlink spec, [RFC0016](https://github.com/mavlink/rfcs/blob/master/text/0016-standard-modes.md) has recommendations. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A companion computer running ROS 2should be able to 
* Register a new flight mode at runtime (Terrain Navigation, Frontier Explore, Survey)
* Set AduPilot to the new the flight mode to its custom mode
* Unregister a flight mode

Note that LUA scripts should also be able to do the same thing, such as Tridge's acrobatic scripts should register a new "Acrobatic" mode. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Implement custom comms between ROS and the GCS without the autopilot.

author: AndKe
title: Quadplane: Transition fails if blowing with the wind during VTOL climb
body:
## Bug report

When starting in a significant headwind, it may be tempting to drift off backward, in order to do the transition closer to oneself. / or to save energy, rather han holding position during VTOL climb (pitching nose down towards headwind)

To reproduce: 
1 Climb in Qloiter or Qstabilize, keep nose into the wind, let the UAV drift "backward"
2 when at altitude - switch to (for example) Cruise
3 observe that the transition fails.

To me, it seems that the wind estimate goes bad when drifting/flying backward during VTOL climb.
![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/1468842/62b5fe54-35a5-4c26-b8cd-fa26edb4aa5d)


**Version**
AP4.4.0  (and newer)

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[ x] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
Quadplane

Cube orange

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1LPinfPQbLsfKwo_GzhEuuNPsuV78kXQ3/view?usp=sharing

author: IamPete1
body:
In this case you have a airspeed sensor so the wind estimate is not being used. 

It should not update when the VTOL motors are active. However we do get one change when you first switch into cruise:

![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/33176108/16811a8b-2b22-4c62-b8f6-04ef34172cc4)

@tridge  I think this is a race between `in_vtol_mode` going false and `in_assisted_flight` going true in `update_fly_forward`. The delay in changing from false to true we were talking about should fix this too.

In this case it looks like cruise locked in the flying backwards ground course, so it tried to do a 180 deg turn,  this is what I get in the sim:

![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/33176108/fe933f16-8d77-4d2c-b427-ba8362ac384e)

So the fix is just that we are flying forward over the ground before letting cruise lock in heading.

author: AndKe
title: Quadplane: Target speed logic error in VTOL transition to cruise.
body:
## Bug report

To reproduce: 

1 manual Take-off in Q-hover/loiter,  
2 keep RC throttle high, in order to climb.
3 at desired transition altitude, switch to Cruise
At this point, it is not intuitive to instantly lower throttle input, and keep throttle high as we wish to climb.
4 observe that during, and after the completed transition, the plane will do uncommanded descend. 

To me, this looks like the high throttle causes a very high demand for speed, which is met by sacrificing the altitude.
This can even be performed as the RC pilot inputs full throttle, and full up elevator( limited by fly-by-wire)

So the feeling is: a pilot takes off, and as terrain/obstacle approaches, it may be logical to input full throttle, and (given FBW) full up-elevator: and the result is a descent, at high speed.


![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/1468842/acbdf7b0-e542-4c96-9094-bcfb94735bac)

author: IamPete1
body:
The TECS height demands are in the TECS log msg.

![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/33176108/453295ae-94fa-495d-9a5a-d10ad8c972b3)

The input height from the pilot is in blue, the TECS target is in green. The problem is that the vehicle gains 7 or 8 meters in its transition, this puts is above its target height so it descends. Very soon after the pilot height demand increases the vehicle starts climbing again. It is only ever 1m under the altitude at which the transition finished.

author: IamPete1
body:
I also notice you have quite a large thrust to pitch coupling, this means that at high throttle the vehicle was quite out of trim when it first transitioned, this could be the cause of that climb.

![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/33176108/d8db3273-7211-4178-8786-62ce66e760ac)

The pitch I term follows the throttle level quite closely. You could try to minimize this with `KFF_THR2PTCH` or double check the physical thrust line on the vehicle.

title: Reports of drones breaching the geofence
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

_Please describe the problem_

**Version**
_What version was the issue encountered with_

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[√] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**


**Hardware type**
We verified the bug both in SITL simulation and on pixhawk

**Logs**
Two ways:
the first way:
Attack Steps:
- The operator intentionally controls the UAV to touch the edge of the electronic geo-fence to trigger a response to enter RTL mode
- When the drone enters RTL mode, it will fly to a preset return point.
- By setting the return point in a no-fly zone such as an airport, the aircraft will fly in the no-fly zone.
![$LU1E`$ C0$KQ_JYZ2UE4K8](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/42442851/dd314393-b1ce-4ebb-a0c8-1a5d6704cc9c)


the second way:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/c65675a64d453e28336230ac3bccad902b1133f3/libraries/AC_Fence/AC_Fence.cpp#L476
Because of this part of the code, when the values of both the was_breached and breached variables are true, the check for breaking the geofence will consistently return false, even if the drone is in a no-fly zone at the moment to perform its mission.
When a drone is in the air, paint the drone into a no-fly zone and the aircraft can still perform its mission.

Further exploitation of the second bug：
While the second option may seem less threatening, as it is the user breaking out of the no-fly zone they have drawn for themselves, further exploitation exists based on this vulnerability.
When the operator is malicious:
- Ardupilot supports importing no-fly zone files, and some diy aircraft manufacturers using this open source flight control choose to import airport no-fly zone information for their aircraft ahead of time.
- A malicious user could draw a new no-fly zone right next to the edge of an existing no-fly zone and close it.
- The new no-fly zone is turned on while the drone is flying in the new no-fly zone.
- There would be no additional status check at the junction of the two no-fly zones, which would allow a malicious operator to enter the existing airport no-fly zone.
![11](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/42442851/3b491015-50e4-478c-8fd7-1be0aefef23a)

author: czbxzm
body:
> By the way, in general AP does not attempt to protect against "malicious operators". The operator is assumed to have the best knowledge of what the vehicle should do and AP does not try to second guess that.

Thank you for your response, sir.I agree with you, don't assume users are malicious. It is possible for a benign user to breach a no-fly zone without any warning. This could result in them accidentally flying into an airport breaking the law, or having the plane fly into the woods and crash.  

When the drone is flying normally in the flyable zone, it will not enter the no-fly zone anyway, which makes the user feel that the geo-fence is reliable and logical. But when the drone touches the fence and enters rtl mode, or activates the fence in the middle of a mission, it quietly fails.

In addition, the failure of a single new geofence may further affect more existing geofences, as I have already mentioned in "Further exploitation" above.

I think this problem arises because the logic of prioritising no-fly zones is a bit confusing.We should fix the highest priority for geofencing, and even if a user wants to take over a no-fly zone they should first explicitly operate to cancel it.

After I reported the similar issue to PX4, they added a new check today to verify the relationship between home points and no-fly zones, which fixed the RTL mode breaching geofence issue.And they have now forbidden the uploading of geofences while the aircraft is armming, effectively fixed “the second way” mentioned above.

body:
Ok, I think I understand why you are confused.

I think you are expecting the desired speed to be zero any time you have the sticks in the middle. This is not correct.

Loiter is a drag based kinematic model. So the aircraft slows down proportional to it's speed (linear not squared relationship). Lets say the speed halves every second, it never gets to zero but it keeps getting smaller. So when you zero the sticks you are not commanding zero velocity, you are commanding zero acceleration and letting drag change the speed.

The reason we use is_zero, is_negative, and is_positive is because they check that the number is zero to within the a couple times the float's minimum size. So is_zero(0.000000000000000000000000000000001) or some small number will be true.

> Also, when the expected speed is equal to 0, it should be cleared to zero, as indicated below：

No, this is not true and is one of the basic principles of the command model. I suspect there are a few aspects of how loiter works that you have not fully understood. The _predicted_accel is not equal to the _desired_accel to account for the slower response time of the attitude controller. The desired velocity is not zero when you zero the sticks because you are commanding zero acceleration and waiting for the drag model to slow the aircraft.

author: SwiftGust
title: EKF3: improve support multiple navigation sources fusion
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Current EKF3 seems only use single source and support switching sources via [Lua script](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_Scripting/examples/ahrs-source.lua) as decribed in [docs](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-non-gps-to-gps.html), hard to say its fusion
**I'd like to raise request for support multiple sources fusion, most prominently External Navigation & GNSS with IMU with EKF3** rather than switching over sources which may cause discrete state, thus to the vehicle control

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- **Major problem is sources have different frames of reference** 
   - GNSS is earth's north aligned while most of External Navigation systems have yaw aligned to the forward where it initialized which is arbitrary
   - Finding yaw offset & with rotate xy alone with yaw offset relative to primary source - GNSS, Compass or External Nav will enable fusion of both without explicit switching for horizontal position, velocity & yaw estimate
 
-  **Another problem is how to fuse well with current EKF3 states**
   - automatically switch & use best sources (i.e minimum covariance)
   - weighted fusion with covariance reported by message or set by parameter
   - or other ways to fuse better, naturally

- **Also require support body velocity fusion for EKF3**
   - current ArduPilot only support velocity described in global frame via [Vision Speed Estimate](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#VISION_SPEED_ESTIMATE) or 
[forced to rotate body velocity into local velocity at the time of decoding](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/51cbaed9d949559ba37a2b7f42da98a4252af6ea/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp#L3602-L3605)
while body velocity - describes vehicle velocity in body-frame regardless of attitude relative to its origin
x: forward, y: right, z: down
thus which may hold correct state information while orientation may be wrong
to support this, will require to store velocity frame & support BODY_FRD or LOCAL_NED at least
if BODY_FRD then rotate velocity at the time of fusion with EKF3's estimated yaw

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
proper, complete implementation of existing align_position_to_ahrs() may be able to handle to some extent

**Platform**
[V] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
With proper implementation of the feature, then we may not require Lua script at all to support multiple sources fusion then will allow easier access, continuous operation environment regardless of indoor & outdoor

**Related Issues**
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/15859
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/18380
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/23485
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/23616

At the moment users need to assign a knob on CH6 for [Transmitter Based Tuning](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-transmitter-tuning.html).

author: rmackay9
title: AP_Camera/AP_Mount: status fov should only start when requested, stop when not requested
body:
PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/24657 adds support for sending the [CAMERA_FOV_STATUS](https://github.com/ArduPilot/mavlink/blob/master/message_definitions/v1.0/common.xml#L5902) message which uses the vehicle's location, gimbal's attitude and the terrain database to calculate the Location what the camera gimbal is looking at.

Also this feature probably doesn't use much CPU, we shouldn't waste CPU unnecessarily.  In particular we should only start the calculation of what the gimbal is looking at when the GCS (or someone) requests the CAMERA_FOV_STATUS be sent.  We should also stop the calculation perhaps 10 seconds after the GCS stops requesting to message.

author: rmackay9
title: AP_Camera: image-start-capture with all zeros leads to infinite pics at zero interval
body:
PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/24772 added support for the [IMAGE_START_CAPTURE](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_IMAGE_START_CAPTURE) command's (time) Interval and Total Images fields.

While it interprets the command correctly, if all fields are left as zero the result is:

CameraId:0 = all cameras
Interval=0 (as quick as possible)
TotalImages=0 (capture forever)

So the camera library will take tons of images very quickly and also send tons of notifications to the GCS.

While it may not be exactly according to the mavlink spec I think we should interpret an all zero command as wanting to take just a single picture on all cameras immediately.

author: AndKe
title: Plane failed(did not try) to climb in any autothrottle mode.
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**
Why flying in guided mode, we went to about FL80 when we discovered that we were unable to command a further climb (we went to FL100 several times before)

No altitude command that required climb, resulted in a climb, we could command a lower altitude, but not a higher (the plane would not try to climb -just cruising level).

We tried to issue the same command from another GCS.
We uploaded a mission , but AUTO would not climb.
Descended and switched into Cruise : unable to climb
then FBWA  - seems to climb
then  FBWB - unable to climb
then stabilize, which of course could climb...
Qassist started in a turn, switched momentarily to QLoiter and Cruise - and then, suddenly, the plane would climb.
From now on, it could climb in Guided mode again!

This seems to be some (potentially dangerous) bug in the altitude-controlled flight modes.
For a far/distant flight where one need to climb to return home, it could be catastrophic.


**Version**
4.4.0 

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[x ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
Quadplane

**Hardware type**
CubeOrange

**Logs**
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1iF0CmcsuafuWiayj3e61wqbcxVL72bDz?usp=sharing

author: magicrub
body: Thanks for reporting and including a log. We'll take a look.

author: IamPete1
body:
Not found a clear cause, but have got some steps on the way I think. 

First of all, the height demand was getting into TECS, so this is not a problem in the plane code. We see `TECS.hin` at the requested altitude, but `TECS.hdem` stops increasing. 

![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/33176108/e1c28301-2be4-464d-bae2-1d5a4e722de4)

Also note in `TEC2.KI` is 0 for the whole flight. KI is calculated here:

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/4a15d9cc1bedb9b95e8540216340759bf7453ec3/libraries/AP_TECS/AP_TECS.cpp#L1010-L1021

For it to be zero `inhibit_integrator` must be true. This can happen if `_pitch_dem_unc > _PITCHmaxf`. We see that same condition here:

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/4a15d9cc1bedb9b95e8540216340759bf7453ec3/libraries/AP_TECS/AP_TECS.cpp#L1187

So `max_climb_condition` would also be true. This causes the height demean to never increase. 

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/4a15d9cc1bedb9b95e8540216340759bf7453ec3/libraries/AP_TECS/AP_TECS.cpp#L1190-L1191

So, I think that we were hitting that `max_climb_condition` case. I'm not sure why that is. I'm not sure why `inhibit_integrator` is true for the whole flight but the vehicle can climb initially and then again at the end.

author: priseborough
body: This plane was operating with ARSPD_USE =0 which TECS handles as a special case in the pitch calculation  by setting _SKE_weighting to 0. This is why the kinetic energy error integrator remains 0. I have a log from another userflying a VTOL  tailsitter with ARSPED_USE = 0 where the TECS internal height demand wouldn't increase after transition into forward flight in AUTO mode. I'll investigate further.

author: AndKe
body: @priseborough Good catch. We disabled the ARSPD_USE during the previous flight when we suspected icing to be affecting the pitot tube.  (we had trace icing and light icing at some altitudes - observed by the leading-edge camera. )

author: vgade-invn
body:
The problem is caused due to the default setting of the sensors configuration. 

The default setting used in the the sensor is to to fine-tune the device for lower noise density at lower measurement ranges, while still providing the full sensor range. At around 100 dps, you can observe the sensor switching from low-range (low noise) to high-range (higher noise) mode, causing the gyro data to be sticky for a short duration of the time. When you change the setting to disable the switching automatically, the device will always be in high-range mode, with a slight detoriation in noise density at FSR < 100 dps.

The resolution to the issue is to set bit [7:6] = 01 at the address of 77 at bank 0 register. The default bit [7:6] = 10.

Thanks,
Vishal Gade,

@vgade-invn many thanks!

Thanks,
Vishal.

author: rsaxvc
title: direct modification of GPIO data and direction registers are vulnerable to read-modify-write data races
body:
@auturgy asked me to create this ticket: https://discord.com/channels/674039678562861068/854213651250020372/1152720064395616286

## Bug report

**Issue details**

Direct GPIO hardware register accesses on TI and Broadcom(RPi) boards have data races between ArduPilot threads as well as other userspace and kernel threads, resulting in GPIO register corruption causing dropped output changes or mode toggles. How often this may occur will vary widely with selected board as well as other software accessing GPIOs.

**Version**
master / d9818ae1abfef10caf2 , nearly all releases supporting BBB and RPI.

**Platform**
[ X ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Airframe type**
Basic peripheral driver issue unrelated to airframe.

**Hardware type**
On each GPIO write(): PXF, ErleBoard, BBBMini, Blue, Pocket
On each GPIO pinMode(): RPI-based boards

**Logs**

I pulled the following primitives out into godbolt(ARM GCC 11.2.1 -O3 -mcpu=cortex-a9 -ffunction-sections) so it may not exactly match instruction for instruction in released firmware, but the data races are present in both RPI and BBB builds.
```
Linux::GPIO_BBB::pinMode(unsigned char, unsigned char):
        tst     r1, #128
        bxne    lr
        lsr     r3, r1, #5
        cmp     r2, #0
        and     r1, r1, #31
        add     r0, r0, r3, lsl #4
        mov     ip, #1
        ldr     r2, [r0, #4]
        ldr     r3, [r2] //Data race begin
        orreq   r3, r3, ip, lsl r1
        bicne   r3, r3, ip, lsl r1
        str     r3, [r2]//Data race end
        bx      lr

Linux::GPIO_BBB::write(unsigned char, unsigned char):
        tst     r1, #128
        bxne    lr
        lsr     r3, r1, #5
        cmp     r2, #0
        and     r1, r1, #31
        add     r0, r0, r3, lsl #4
        mov     ip, #1
        ldr     r2, [r0, #12]
        ldr     r3, [r2]//data race begin
        biceq   r3, r3, ip, lsl r1
        orrne   r3, r3, ip, lsl r1
        str     r3, [r2]//data race end
        bx      lr
```

Compared to the Raspberry Pi implementation, whose implementation supports atomic write-one-to-set and write-one-to-clear registers, but only for the data registers(not the mode register):

```
Linux::GPIO_RPI::pinMode(unsigned char, unsigned char):
        cmp     r2, #0
        bne     .L11
        movw    r3, #52429
        ldr     ip, [r0]
        movt    r3, 52428
        umull   r2, r3, r3, r1
        lsr     r3, r3, #3
        add     r2, r3, r3, lsl #2
        ldr     r0, [ip, r3, lsl #2]//begin data race
        sub     r2, r1, r2, lsl #1
        mov     r1, #7
        add     r2, r2, r2, lsl #1
        uxtb    r2, r2
        bic     r2, r0, r1, lsl r2
        str     r2, [ip, r3, lsl #2]//end data race
        bx      lr
.L11:
        movw    r2, #52429
        ldr     ip, [r0]
        movt    r2, 52428
        mov     r3, #7
        umull   r0, r2, r2, r1
        lsr     r2, r2, #3
        add     r0, r2, r2, lsl #2
        sub     r1, r1, r0, lsl #1
        ldr     r0, [ip, r2, lsl #2]
        add     r1, r1, r1, lsl #1
        uxtb    r1, r1
        mvn     r3, r3, lsl r1
        and     r0, r0, r3
        str     r0, [ip, r2, lsl #2]
        ldr     r0, [ip, r2, lsl #2]//begin data race
        and     r3, r3, r0
        mov     r0, #1
        orr     r3, r3, r0, lsl r1
        str     r3, [ip, r2, lsl #2] //end data race
        bx      lr

//no data race. Constant is constructed in r3 with bits corresponding to GPIO pins to be cleared, then atomically written to gpclr0 or gpset0.
Linux::GPIO_RPI::write(unsigned char, unsigned char):
        cmp     r2, #0
        mov     r3, #1
        ldr     r2, [r0]
        lsl     r3, r3, r1
        strne   r3, [r2, #28]
        streq   r3, [r2, #40]
        bx      lr
```

**Problem Analysis**
If each thread conducts LDR, OR/BIC/AND, STR, it's likely that rare cases where the following operation order may occur(interruptions and context switches not shown): Thread1LDR, Thread2LDR, Thread2OR/BIC/AND, Thread2STR, Thread1OR/BIC/AND, Thread1STR. This could occur on parallel threads in an SMP device, or occur due to a context switch during the instructions I've annotated as 'data race' on even a single core device. Note that these register accesses aren't limited to ardupilot - other userspace thread using mmap() or sysfs()/GPIO or libgpiod or kernel threads touching the kernel GPIO interfaces at the same time could also trigger this. This is likely to be quite rare in practice, but I've seen it fail on other ARM systems.

**Some Potential Solutions**

1. Could move BBB and RPI based boards to sysfs like the other boards, which will go through the kernel GPIO interfaces, whose backends are usually protected through a spinlock. There will be some overhead to do so.
2. Could move BBB and RPI operations that cannot be synchronized to sysfs, while keeping others directly. For BBB, this would mean pinMode() and write() go through sysfs, and read() would remain as register-mapped. For RPI, only pinMode() would go through sysfs, and write() and read() would remain as register-mapped.
3. Could hope it doesn't happen often enough to justify preventing.

**Notes**

- I've mentioned sysfs quite a bit, whose GPIO interface is deprecated. Changing to libgpiod is considered separate from this, and could be substituted anywhere I mentioned sysfs/GPIO.
- Currently neither BBB nor RPI use a memory barrier instruction to ensure accesses to the GPIO registers are not reordered with accesses to other peripherals. This should probably be considered separately, at least for boards with multiple GPIO banks if there are peripherals wired across banks, or if relying on access ordering with other peripherals, like SPI or I2C.
- TI AM335x CPUs used in some beagle boards do support w1s and w1c registers called GPIO_CLEARDATAOUT and GPIO_SETDATAOUT, but this would need confirmed across all boards using that driver.

author: rsaxvc
body:
Bug confirmed on Raspberry Pi with the following tests(See https://github.com/rsaxvc/ardupilot/pull/new/linux_gpio_racer ):

- New ArduPilot unit test that toggles pin 12 from input to output, verifying afterward that the change worked.
- Bash loop hammering raspi-gpio set 13 ip;raspi-gpio set 13 op

Pins need to be two otherwise unrelated pins in the same config reg(3 bits per pin, 10 pins per register on RPI) that won't be reconfigured live.

ArduPilot test tends to die pretty quickly once both programs are running. But sometimes it runs a long time. And sometimes it dies immediately. My board only configures GPIO direction once during startup, so once I'm up, I'm up.

author: rsaxvc
body: FYI: @lucasdemarchi , @Williangalvani . Could we add Linux tag?

author: lucasdemarchi
body:
It's an expected race when accessing the HW directly bypassing the kernel. There's no possible synchronization in user space if you account for other programs.

For ardupilot's threads it would be a bug indeed.

I once had a GitHub issue to convert all the boards (that can be converted) to sysfs. However note that that interface is much slower.  If we are moving to the proper kernel abstraction, then we should go directly to the gpiod interface through the ioctl.

author: rsaxvc
body:
If I understand it right, as long as AP never shares individual pins with other programs/kernel:

Pin configuration through direct access: almost never safe.

GPIO read through direct register read: always safe.

GPIO write through direct register write: requires GPIO SET/CLEAR registers(not hooked up on AP BBB yet).



So I think we could do a hybrid implement. Pin configuration always through sysfs or gpiod, and low-overhead GPIO read & writes using direct hardware registers when it is safe to do so, otherwise falling back to gpiod/sysfs.

> How to rotate and calculate the stop point is crucial, and speed loop control is crucial. This affects the braking posture, otherwise there will be signs of nodding back and forth to brake

This is correct. If you have a poor tune, either the attitude controller or position controller then  you may see nodding. 

However, Loiter does not calculate a "stop point" so that part is wrong. Loiter simply slows down the velocity until it reaches zero, it doesn't care where it stops.

>> At the beginning, the braking force increases. When the braking force reaches the maximum braking force, maintain the continuous maximum braking force. When the expected speed is less than a certain value, start calculating the stop point, and then perform position control attitude

This is a very poor way of doing this.

Loiter is intended to resemble Alt_Hold when there is no wing with the additional ability to add some extra breaking when you let go of the sticks. I do intend to add a new control mode that is more robotic in feel that may be closer to what you want.

This issue doesn't describe a problem or articulate any enhancement request. I think this is more of a tuning and setup problem that should be discussed on the forums. I will close this and open it again if needed.

author: IamPete1
body:
@Refick79 Feel free to use whatever language your most comfortable with. There may not be a developer that can understand directly, but we will do our best with translation tools.

You can use scripting with `set_output_pwm_chan_timeout` override to ensure the outputs are 0 throttle PWM when they first connect. You can then wait some short time before removing the override and letting them function as normal. The core of your lua script might look something like this:

```
-- should fold motors if not using them currently
local motors_shutdown = motors:get_spool_state() == 0
local fold_motors = motors_shutdown and not quadplane:in_assisted_flight() and not quadplane:in_vtol_mode()

if fold_motors then
    -- Make sure the servo output channels 1, 2, 3,  and 4 stay at 1000 PWM for the next 2 seconds
    SRV_Channels:set_output_pwm_chan_timeout(0, 1000, 2000)
    SRV_Channels:set_output_pwm_chan_timeout(1, 1000, 2000)
    SRV_Channels:set_output_pwm_chan_timeout(2, 1000, 2000)
    SRV_Channels:set_output_pwm_chan_timeout(3, 1000, 2000)

end

```

You will need quite a bit more logic around that so it can run continuously and do the right thing when disarmed for example.

Its still not ideal because the vehicle is not aware that is can't use the motors, so it will still try even though there not outputting. So you will still have issues with I term wind up. Fixing that is quite complex, in the mean time a script should get you 90% of what you need.

author: nexton-winjeel
title: AP_Camera, AP_Mount: Camera Protocol messages don't have component IDs
body:
The `AP_Camera` and `AP_Mount` libraries have support for some of the messages in the [MAVLink Camera Protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/camera.html).

However, the handlers for some of these messages (e.g. `CAMERA_SETTINGS` and `CAMERA_INFORMATION`) are problematic if there are multiple camera backends:
* these messages do not have IDs (MAVLink intent is to use `compid` to distinguish components);
* the handlers send these messages from each backend with the `MAV_COMP_ID_AUTOPILOT1` `compid`, so they all appear to come from the same component. This will confuse a GCS.

_Originally posted by @nexton-winjeel in https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/24953#discussion_r1322303167_

author: sahilsihag
title: ArduCopter: `main_loop` keeps waiting for other thread to release semaphore
body:
## Bug report
**Issue summary**  
`io_thread` can be forced to obtain a semaphore and not release it for long time. Meanwhile `main_loop` thread might also require the same semaphore, in this case ChibiOS puts `main_loop` into sleeping state ([`chSchGoSleepS(CH_STATE_WTMTX)`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ChibiOS/blob/1ec9f168b2e64a043470a87225b405e79d187354/os/rt/src/chmtx.c#L216)) while waiting for `io_thread` to release semaphore.

**Issue details**  
```
MAVLink packet: fd0400003effe68700002186678f448a

Information:
Payload: TERRAIN_CHECK (135)
    lat (int32_t): -1889040863
    lon (int32_t): 0
```
leads to `case DiskIoWaitRead` ([libraries/AP_Terrain/TerrainIO.cpp](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/502702df62572519b56971fe9fed5b2883640879/libraries/AP_Terrain/TerrainIO.cpp#L370)). 

```cpp
    case DiskIoWaitRead:
        // need to read in the block
        open_file();
        if (fd == -1) {
            return;
        }
        read_block();
                                         // inside `read_block()`
                                         // `AP::FS().lseek(fd, file_offset, SEEK_SET)` <-- tries to lseek to file_offset (calculated from latitude, longitude)
                                             // this calls `AP_Filesystem_FATFS::lseek` and it obtains semaphore sem `WITH_SEMAPHORE(sem);
```
After obtaining the semaphore [`sem`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/502702df62572519b56971fe9fed5b2883640879/libraries/AP_Filesystem/AP_Filesystem_FATFS.cpp#L526), it calls `f_lseek` ([ardupilot/modules/ChibiOS/ext/fatfs/source/ff.c](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ChibiOS/blob/1ec9f168b2e64a043470a87225b405e79d187354/ext/fatfs/source/ff.c#L4423)) where the offset (`ofs`) value is 280303616 and cluster size (`bcs`) is 4096. Because of the high offset value, large amount of time is consumed before exiting out of the while loop in [this function](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ChibiOS/blob/1ec9f168b2e64a043470a87225b405e79d187354/ext/fatfs/source/ff.c#L4529).
```cpp
				while (ofs > bcs) {						/* Cluster following loop */
					ofs -= bcs; fp->fptr += bcs;
#if !FF_FS_READONLY
					if (fp->flag & FA_WRITE) {			/* Check if in write mode or not */
						if (FF_FS_EXFAT && fp->fptr > fp->obj.objsize) {	/* No FAT chain object needs correct objsize to generate FAT value */
							fp->obj.objsize = fp->fptr;
							fp->flag |= FA_MODIFIED;
						}
						clst = create_chain(&fp->obj, clst);	/* Follow chain with forceed stretch */
						if (clst == 0) {				/* Clip file size in case of disk full */
							ofs = 0; break;
						}
					} else
#endif
					{
						clst = get_fat(&fp->obj, clst);	/* Follow cluster chain if not in write mode */
					}
					if (clst == 0xFFFFFFFF) ABORT(fs, FR_DISK_ERR);
					if (clst <= 1 || clst >= fs->n_fatent) ABORT(fs, FR_INT_ERR);
					fp->clust = clst;
				}
```
Therefore, we have an `io_thread` which obtains semaphore `sem` and does not leave it for a long time. In the mean time, we can request log list with the help of another packet:
```
MAVLink packet: fd0500003fffe67500000000ffff01ce67

Information:
Payload: LOG_REQUEST_LIST (117)
    target_system (uint8_t): 1
    target_component (uint8_t): 0
    start (uint16_t): 0
    end (uint16_t): 65535
```
This forces `main_loop` to obtain semaphore [`sem`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/502702df62572519b56971fe9fed5b2883640879/libraries/AP_Filesystem/AP_Filesystem_FATFS.cpp#L695) for calculating number of available logs. Since the semaphore is already owned by another thread, we trigger [priority inheritance protocol of ChibiOS](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ChibiOS/blob/1ec9f168b2e64a043470a87225b405e79d187354/os/rt/src/chmtx.c#L158) and put `main_loop` into sleeping state (`chSchGoSleepS(CH_STATE_WTMTX)`) for the mean time.

**Additional Comments**  
1. Card speed: The time spent in while loop is dependent on microSD card speed. Speed class 4 takes a while and newer microSD cards take less time. But offset value can also be increased to a bigger number to incorporate new cards.  
2. Requesting log list is only possible when the drone is not armed. I have not exhaustively searched for operations in `main_loop` which try to obtain same semaphore while in flight.
    - In general, what is the behavior when a thread does not release a semaphore that is required by `main_loop`?
3. Additional threads such as FTP that require same semaphore also stop responding.
4. OmnibusF4 restarts when such situation occurs. I am not sure if the response is same on all boards.

author: sahilsihag
body:
@tridge I agree that the current situation is only possible when the drone is not armed (See Additional Comments: point 2). But I will still like to have discussion about the underlying problem: the interplay between main thread and another thread for shared resources.

When terrain check does not find things inside in-memory cache, it is possible to lead it to `DiskIoWaitRead`. In this case separate IO thread takes care of reading files from disk. In the issue described above:
1. IO thread can take long time to read from disk
2. Meanwhile when log list is requested, main thread keeps waiting for IO thread to finish its work (see priority inheritance protocol of ChibiOS). Therefore, we can starve main thread when the drone is not armed and cause firmware restarts repeatedly on ground.

While this one example is dependent on file system operation (and not a problem while device is armed), this situation can also arise in other cases due to priority inheritance protocol. My main question is: What saves the main thread from becoming a victim in other similar situations?
