author: sahilsihag
title: ArduCopter: Terrain Check request leads to reappearance of deleted FATFS contents
body:
## Bug report
**Issue summary**  
A TERRAIN_CHECK (135) request for a random latitude, longitude leads to appearance of a file. This file contains data that has been earlier deleted but not overwritten from the microSD card (FATFS). The size of file can be influenced by changing values of latitude, longitude.

**Issue details**  
```
MAVLink packet: fd030000a7ffe6870000244aca85cb

Information:
Payload: TERRAIN_CHECK (135)
    lat (int32_t): 13257252
    lon (int32_t): 0
```
leads to `case DiskIoWaitRead` ([libraries/AP_Terrain/TerrainIO.cpp](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/502702df62572519b56971fe9fed5b2883640879/libraries/AP_Terrain/TerrainIO.cpp#L370)). 

```cpp
    case DiskIoWaitRead:
        // need to read in the block
        open_file();
                                         // inside open_file()
                                         // AP::FS().open(file_path, O_RDWR|O_CREAT); <-- tries opening "/APM/TERRAIN/N01E000.DAT"
                                         // Open is successful
        if (fd == -1) {
            return;
        }
        read_block();
                                         // inside read_block()
                                         // AP::FS().lseek(fd, file_offset, SEEK_SET) <-- tries to lseek to file_offset (calculated from latitude, longitude)
                                         // lseek is successful

                                         // AP::FS().read(fd, &disk_block, sizeof(disk_block)) <-- tries to read after reaching offset
                                         // but now `ret != sizeof(disk_block)` is True 
                                         // read is unsuccessful. Enabling `TERRAIN_DEBUG` leads to "read empty block ..."
        break;
```
If we now query filesystem via mavproxy, we see:
```
ftp list /APM/TERRAIN                        
STABILIZE> Listing /APM/TERRAIN                
   N01E000.DAT  0                            
Total size 0.00 kByte  
```
`fd` is not closed yet in the expectation of being reused. So, we send a different packet:
```
MAVLink packet: fd0400000678e687000084ada60f7e9c

Information:
Payload: TERRAIN_CHECK (135)
    lat (int32_t): 262581636
    lon (int32_t): 0
```
this again leads to `case DiskIoWaitRead` ([libraries/AP_Terrain/TerrainIO.cpp](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/502702df62572519b56971fe9fed5b2883640879/libraries/AP_Terrain/TerrainIO.cpp#L370)). 

```cpp
    case DiskIoWaitRead:
        // need to read in the block
        open_file();
                                         // But now there is different story
                                         // inside open_file()
                                         // AP::FS().close(fd); <-- closes old fd
                                         // rest does not matter for this bug
```
If we now query file system again via mavproxy, we see:
```
ftp list /APM/TERRAIN    
STABILIZE> Listing /APM/TERRAIN
   N01E000.DAT  1290240  
   N26E000.DAT  0  
Total size 1260.00 kByte  
```
The size of `N01E000.DAT` is same as `file_offset` used for `AP::FS().lseek`. The content appearing inside this file match with dump of microSD card taken before doing this experiment (`dd if=/dev/mmcblk0p1 of=dump_file status=progress`) .

Later we also see:
```
ftp list /APM/TERRAIN    
STABILIZE> Listing /APM/TERRAIN     
   N01E000.DAT  1292288    
   N26E000.DAT  856064      
Total size 2098.00 kByte 
```
This is because mavproxy sends TERRAIN_DATA (134). This data gets written to the end of file as expected.

**Additional Comments**  
When the above operation tries to `lseek` it calls `f_lseek` ([ardupilot/modules/ChibiOS/ext/fatfs/source/ff.c](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ChibiOS/blob/1ec9f168b2e64a043470a87225b405e79d187354/ext/fatfs/source/ff.c#L4423)). There are hints of file size being zero (`fp->obj.objsize` is 0) and [if condition](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ChibiOS/blob/1ec9f168b2e64a043470a87225b405e79d187354/ext/fatfs/source/ff.c#L4504)
```cpp
		if (ofs > fp->obj.objsize && (FF_FS_READONLY || !(fp->flag & FA_WRITE))) {	/* In read-only mode, clip offset with the file size */
			ofs = fp->obj.objsize;
		}
```
to restrict offset (`ofs`) to `fp->obj.objsize`. But this never happens in above situation, possibly due to `FF_FS_READONLY` not being True.

**Version**  
ArduCopter V4.4.0 (502702df)

**Platform**  
[ ] All
[ ] AntennaTracker
[x] Copter -> **with microSD card (FATFS)**
[ ] Plane
[ ] Rover
[ ] Submarine

**Airframe type**  
Not applicable.

**Hardware type**  
Board: omnibusF4
With microSD card (FATFS)

**Logs**  
Already inline above.

author: tridge
body: yes, we use sparse files deliberately in AP_Terrain, and we use a header in the file that indicates which blocks are valid to use. We deliberately don't fill in the unused blocks

author: sahilsihag
body:
I might be mistaken, but I am referring to a different situation altogether. What I would like to convey:
- With a `TERRAIN_CHECK` message, IO thread can be forced to read a file from disk which does not even exist (case [`DiskIoWaitRead`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/502702df62572519b56971fe9fed5b2883640879/libraries/AP_Terrain/TerrainIO.cpp#L370))
- Even then, the firmware tries to lseek file descriptor (fd) to offset specified in TERRAIN_CHECK message.
- When this offsetted fd is closed, a file appears in file system (here: `N01E000.DAT`) which exposes bytes directly from the device hardware as a file system entry.

ChibiOS allows restricting file's lseek offset to its size [here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ChibiOS/blob/1ec9f168b2e64a043470a87225b405e79d187354/ext/fatfs/source/ff.c#L4504) but ArduPilot does not make use of this condition.

As a result: microSD card can be physically filled with only a few malicious/wrong TERRAIN_CHECKs and expose files which were deleted but not wiped at device block level.

author: tridge
body:
> As a result: microSD card can be physically filled with only a few malicious/wrong TERRAIN_CHECKs and expose files which were deleted but not wiped at device block level.

If someone malicious controls the contents of the sdcard then the vehicle is completely compromised. That is not an interesting case to consider.
For the non-malicious case the blocks would have to have both a correct CRC, have correct lat/lon, correct spacing, correct version and have the right bitmap bits filled in. So essentially it would need to be valid terrain data.
I'm struggling to see what the real risk is here. The reason we quite deliberately use sparse files like this is the IO cost of pre-filling these files would be huge. The filesystem is slow, so we rely on the signatures in the read blocks to ensure we are getting valid data.
It total we check 14 bytes of data on a block before using it. The chances those 14 bytes are randomly correct is vanishingly small.

author: shancock884
body:
This may be a bit more than checking the validity of the incoming LOG_REQUEST_LIST packet.... I can think of 3 cases, which I believe trigger this behaviour:
1/ Incoming packet has start > end - this is clearly invalid, so maybe it is appropriate to ignore it.
2/ Incoming packet has start = end = 0 - this could be seen invalid, as maybe end should always >= 1, but actually could be seen as a 'nice' way to request the number of logs without getting the whole list.
3/ Incoming packet requests a valid interval, which just happens to be empty. i.e. start=10, end=15, when there are <10 logs available.

In the 3rd case, I believe the correct response is a LOG_ENTRY packet with id=0, numLogs correctly set, and lastLog=0.
In the 2nd case, I think it would be nice to also do the same as 3rd case, to give a easy means to get the total number of logs.
In the 1st case, I could go either way - maybe I'd lean towards doing the same as other cases (to avoid sending back nothing, and to avoid risk/effort for an unlikely case by keeping code changes more constrained).

0x14 Link statistics
Payload:
● uint8_t Uplink RSSI Ant. 1 ( dBm * -1 )

● uint8_t Uplink Package success rate / Link quality ( % )

mW, 1000 mW, 2000mW )
● uint8_t Downlink RSSI ( dBm * -1 )
● uint8_t Downlink package success rate / Link quality ( % )
● int8_t Downlink SNR ( db )
Uplink is the connection from the ground to the UAV and downlink the opposite direction.

author: Ryanf55
title: AP_DDS: Add UDP support for ChibiOS using the LWIP stack
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

You can only connect real hardware to a companion computer over serial, which is slow.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Allow using the new network stack to connect to the companion computer over network, which is much faster


**Platform**
[ x] All

**More info**

Here's the interface that we already met for the UDP in AP_DDS: 
https://github.com/eProsima/Micro-XRCE-DDS-Client/blob/master/include/uxr/client/profile/transport/custom/custom_transport.h

It was implemented here:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/5bd5aa87a728ebae468e3c3247467d8971a5d6fa/libraries/AP_DDS/AP_DDS_UDP.cpp#L12

As far as I can tell, the ArduPilot DDS over UDP is implemented as a UDP Client on Port 2019. No multicast is used right now. 
We currently hard code the address to 127.0.0.1 , so it only works in SITL. This is the address for the server address for the DDS agent on the companion computer. It needs to be exposed through a parameter. 
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/5bd5aa87a728ebae468e3c3247467d8971a5d6fa/libraries/AP_DDS/AP_DDS_Client.h#L140

The port is already has a  parameter:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/5bd5aa87a728ebae468e3c3247467d8971a5d6fa/libraries/AP_DDS/AP_DDS_Client.cpp#L63

author: dxs94
title: Change the way horizon line is drawned on OSD when inverted to conform with aviation standards
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When flying inverted (ie after a 180° roll), the artificial horizon pitch indication on the osd is reversed compared to any full size aviation ADI.
To reproduce: fly inverted (half roll). Push on the elevator stick so that airplane is now in a climb with the nose above horizon. Observe that the osd artificial horizon bar moves DOWN in your goggles whereas it should move UP.

**Current (bad) behavior**
Below: link to video of arduplane behaviour. When inverted, the OSD horizon line moves **opposite** to real horizon line.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jwwi2szEIdQ

—————————————————-

**The correct behavior**
Below: from Yaapu telemetry script on a TX16S, **correct** representation of horizon line. When flying inverted, the OSD horizon line follows real horizon line.

![IMG_0971](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/88461305/d1068cd3-ff5e-4859-a570-7e8d153d070b)

![IMG_0972](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/88461305/1f8b6f03-b2e3-4b03-b910-2e1bafd8ea09)

—————————————————-

**The solution: how OSD should like in Arduplane**
Taking into accound b/w character based OSD limitations, having something like this (below) in the OSD would be appropriate. This is an example of a half roll. The aircraft reference (say « the nose ») of the aircraft is still fixed. The horizon line is drawn differently to follow what a pilot inside the aircraft would see, this is what Ardupilot OSD should depict to conform with aviation standards.
![Half roll](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/88461305/8d1d8527-18c9-4861-81f3-5bb4c9fd6e81)
while always keeping the horizon line in view even at extreme pitch angles so that the pilot always knows it's attitude.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This could be optionnal (current behaviour / new one) based on user preference but I can't think an any situation where the way horizon line is currently drawn is better (except for taking less real estate on screen being made only with " - " characters).

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[x] Copter
[x] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
An artificial horizon has to present the pilot a virtual horizon line from the pilot’s perspective. That and a sky/ground reference to show which side of the line is earth and which is sky. The whole point is that to level off the aircraft the pilot flies to the ADI horizon line no matter if the plane is upright or inverted. Which is impossible if the ADI is just showing « is the aircraft nose above horizon or not ? » as Ardupilot depicts (on top of not having a sky/ground reference).

author: IamPete1
title: Plane: TECS update and usage race condition resulting in NaN
body:
It is possible to try and run TECS having never told it the airspeed. In the worst case this can result in it trying to use 0 and getting a constraining NaN internal error (I have a log of this).

The a 50Hz loop checks if it should run TECS here:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/ad19321d8974d2906607fed2142cd96a5368c6a5/ArduPlane/ArduPlane.cpp#L207

That if that returns false so TECS is not run.

 Now we change modes and check again here in a different loop run at 10Hz rate:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/ad19321d8974d2906607fed2142cd96a5368c6a5/ArduPlane/ArduPlane.cpp#L554

Now because we changed modes in between we have not run `TECS_controller.update_50hz()` recently (or at all) so when we call `TECS_controller.update_pitch_throttle` it has a out of date speed.

The way this causes the internal error is if the user has set `INITIAL_MODE` to a mode that does not run TECS so its never run, and the airspeed is never set to a value `update_50hz()` constraint is to be at least 3m/s. But is TECS has never run its still 0. That 0 propagates from `_TAS_state` to the `gainInv` here:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/ad19321d8974d2906607fed2142cd96a5368c6a5/libraries/AP_TECS/AP_TECS.cpp#L984

Which is then used here resulting in a NaN:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/ad19321d8974d2906607fed2142cd96a5368c6a5/libraries/AP_TECS/AP_TECS.cpp#L1027

That is then constrained here:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/ad19321d8974d2906607fed2142cd96a5368c6a5/libraries/AP_TECS/AP_TECS.cpp#L1035

And we get the internal error. The `TECS` log shows the 0 value of `_TAS_state` in the `sp` field:

![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/33176108/4fc74f0a-1dc9-4eba-97ff-bfe75e5f8f85)

The next time we come through that has been constrained up to that minimum 3 m/s value. 

It would be quite easy to paper over the internal error with a extra constrain, but that does not fix the fundamental issue of using stale data. The only way to fix that is to fix the race condition between the running and updating of TECS. It looks like the only reason were not running the `TECS_controller.update_50hz()` on every loop is to provoke a reset, the fix would be to run it all the time and add new hooks to trigger the reset.

author: magicrub
title: ESC_TELEM_MAX_ESCS <=3 never sends MSG_ESC_TELEMETRY_1_TO_4
body:
ESC_Telemetry will not send MAVLink MSG_ESC_TELEMETRY_1_TO_4 if ESC_TELEM_MAX_ESCS (PWM/SERVO) count is <=3

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/dc8455411adb90308eff08b47d3db7c4faf7be1e/libraries/AP_ESC_Telem/AP_ESC_Telem.cpp#L312C50-L312C50

```
const uint8_t num_idx = ESC_TELEM_MAX_ESCS/4;
    for (uint8_t idx = 0; idx < num_idx; idx++) {
        const uint8_t i = (next_idx + idx) % num_idx;
        ...
```

There's actually two problems caused by `num_idx == (ESC_TELEM_MAX_ESCS/4) == 0`:
1. the for loop will loop 0 times (will never send anything)
2. `foo % num_idx` throws a compiler warning/error about preforming mod 0 which is a divide-by-zero (but unreachable).

I made PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/24771 to fix the divide-by-zero but @andyp1per noticed the will-never-send bug so I closed it in favor of a more complete solution.

author: luweiagi
title: Copter: is this a bug in AC_WPNav::advance_wp_target_along_track at old version?
body:
@lthall 
Hi, I sometimes still read the old version code, and make a contrast with the newest version.
When I see the function of AC_WPNav::advance_wp_target_along_track() in the old code version,
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/25f1a4a4e1e5ccc10c744ff4b6028e27079aabe1/libraries/AC_WPNav/AC_WPNav.cpp#L446
```
        // increase intermediate target point's velocity if not yet at the leash limit
        if(dt > 0 && !reached_leash_limit) {
            _limited_speed_xy_cms += 2.0f * _track_accel * dt;
        }
```
I am confused that why there is a number 2?
because the formular is: 
v_t = v_0 + a * dt
NOT
v_t = v_0 + 2 * a * dt
So, why there is a number 2?
I guess you multiply 2 for the reason of making _track_accel bigger? But if for this reason, why not directly increase _track_accel  itself?

author: lthall
body:
Oh wow. That is going back in time :)

This factor of two is because the aircraft moves on a leash or rubber band defined by the stopping distance. We moved by moving the target point out in front of the aircraft so at any time we could stop moving that point and the aircraft could stop as it reached that point using the maximum acceleration.

When starting from stationary we need to move the point off out in front of the aircraft. However, because the aircraft moves slower than that point we need to use 2 x the acceleration to get the aircraft to move off at 1 x the acceleration.

author: rmackay9
title: RemoteID: include RemoteId support by default (or use Custom Build server?)
body:
It would be convenient for some users to be able to easily download/install a firmware that includes [RemoteID support](https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-remoteid.html).  It could either be included in the standard firmware or perhaps it could be added to the [custom build server](https://custom.ardupilot.org/).

Part of the reason that AP does not currently include the feature by default is that it would only be used by a small subset of AP users but also because the FAA requirements include a "temper resistance" clause which means there are additional steps required to produce a compliant firmware ([see video here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Az8v4Kx4hS0)).

This request comes from [this discussion](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/offical-copter-release-with-remote-id-support/105543).

author: TodWulff
body: As a recreational user (non-Part 107), and in the interests of timely regulatory compliance, I welcome the ability to optionally include RemoteID/ODID options in the custom-build server, and possibly in the standard firmware downloads for common FCs.  Not being an OEM/Builder/Reseller, instantiating the infrastructure to perform custom FW generation organically for the FC and the RID modules is a daunting proposition.  Just tossing in my vote in favor of this enhancement.  Thanks for the opportunity to comment.

title: Will not recognize u-Blox GNSS UBX-M9140 SPG 4.04 ROM Based Devices correctly
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

Code only identifies FLASH based "EXT CORE" SPG 4.xx firmwares, most current step of IC has SPG 4.04 in ROM.
The firmware is near identical save a couple of bytes, and subsequent signing hash, so otherwise commands

author: rmackay9
title: Copter: auto mode yaw may point to old heading after condition-yaw completes
body:
Copter may momentarily point to an old heading after a condition-yaw command completes if the vehicle is not moving.

Below is a mission that demonstrates the issue.
![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/1498098/83b46667-2b97-47c1-a71c-cc465514a846)

In the image above the vehicle has just completed the condition-yaw command (pointing to 180deg/South) and is waiting at Waypoint 4 for 3 seconds.  Once this delay is complete, the vehicle will momentarily point to about 270 deg (North-West) before correctly pointing at waypoint 5 (East).

The reason is that the default yaw behaviour is to point at the next waypoint (see WP_YAW_BEHAVIOR=2).  The target yaw comes from AC_PositionControl which only updates the heading once the vehicle is moving at greater than 5% of _vel_max_xy_cms ([see code here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AC_AttitudeControl/AC_PosControl.cpp#L1215)).  This means that the target has not been updated since the vehicle came to a halt .. and when it came to a halt, the target yaw was North-West.

The solution may be to change AC_PosControl::get_yaw_cd() so that it returns a boolean indicating whether it has a good target or not.  The caller could then skip updating the attitude controller's target.

author: rmackay9
body: The fix has been merged to master now and will be released in 4.5.2.

title: AP_MISSION: MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE Unsupported
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

_This issue is related to https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/24691_
I am attempting to increase compatibility for MAVSDK with ArduPilot. MAVSDK uses the following code when creating a mission sequence object to create the commands necessary in the sequence to control the gimbal: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/e7657c2d87917df739186981f34f98a14c898893/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L459-L480

The acquire_gimbal_items_v2 method sends a MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE mission command when the boolean that represents if the GC has control over the gimbal is false
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/e7657c2d87917df739186981f34f98a14c898893/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L1288-L1312

I identified that MAVSDK sending the MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE message is what is causing the MAV_MISSION_TYPE_UNSUPPORRTED message to be sent to the GC.

It appears that while ArduPilot does keep track of which sys/comp id controls a gimbal via a struct here https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/e14afa6f2bf5050cf736a7ded1ee41d2457d88ab/libraries/AP_Mount/AP_Mount_Backend.h#L272-L275
It does not use this struct in any way when actually controlling the gimbal.

Is it good practice to add MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE as a supported command in AP_MISSION but have it do nothing, at least until proper gimbal control is implemented?
I am mindful of PR https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/23737
This is something I have already implemented in my fork. I can submit a PR when I do further testing.

author: mikedkelly
title: Plane: Allow nudging of horizon level via transmitter when in non-altitude-hold modes
body:
The docs describe FBWA, Training, and Stability flight modes as effective ways to maiden new models and for beginners to learn to control an aircraft before transitioning to manual mode. However, if the horizon level calibration is incorrect, the pilot has no way to "trim" the model in flight. He is left with holding a corrective demand throughout the model's flight in order to maintain a level attitude. This is very distracting and undesirable during a maiden or as a beginner pilot. Aborting the flight and recalibrating level attitude on the ground is not only cumbersome, but without the use of precise tools, will rarely result in an accurate pitch trim for the model.

Since the use of transmitter trim causes adverse effects in these flight modes, I propose something like a new tuning parameter in transmitter based tuning where a slider or pot on the transmitter could be set to nudge either AHRS_TRIM_Y or TRIM_PITCH_CD (and the equivalent roll settings). The reset and save functionality of transmitter based tuning should apply as well. This allows the pilot to correct their setup while continuing to fly as well as make additional adjustments resulting from throttle changes if the mode's attitude hold is not adequate in this regard. 

I've considered methods of iteratively correcting the mechanical linkages as documented, as well as simply using other modes such as FBWB and Acro mode, but it still comes back to having a properly calibrated level setting, and currently that can only be adjusted on the ground. While making changes to the level calibration in the air can have adverse consequences if not used correctly, I feel the risk is no greater than setting it incorrectly on the ground and taking flight.

While primarily useful for LOS fixed wing flying, I can also see this as a useful enhancement to any model type.

author: IamPete1
body:
We do have a "save trim" RC option on copter, it just sets the current attitude to be 0. We could implement it on plane I suppose.

However I don't think the "make it easier for beginners" argument is really a valid one. We should now say that they need to setup this extra channel as well as there flight modes and control inputs? And that they should then twiddle the new channel as there flying for the first time? Much better to just have clear instructions on how to get the trim correct in the first place.

author: mikedkelly
body: I think that would be a good solution. It allows you to use the transmitter trims in flight, which is the procedure pilots are used to, but gives you a layer of safety by only making the adjustment to the level calibration once you have landed. I was always under the impression that you should never adjust transmitter trim in a stabilized mode, but if this works I am all for it.

author: peterbarker
body:
> I think that would be a good solution. It allows you to use the transmitter trims in flight, which is the procedure pilots are used to, but gives you a layer of safety by only making the adjustment to the level calibration once you have landed. I was always under the impression that you should never adjust transmitter trim in a stabilized mode, but if this works I am all for it.

We can't work backwards from RC trims to level calibrations - there's no way to map that.

@IamPete1 's "get the trim right in the first place" is probably the best advice.

Having said that, we could potentially make Copter's "RC Channel tuning" available on all vehicles.  This would allow you to directly modify the AHRS trim parameters on the transmitter - either on pots or via some *very* fancy stuff using the trim tabs and custom mixing.

author: mikedkelly
body: The copter solution is a step in the right direction, but it doesn't really solve the underlying problem. Aerodynamically, an aircraft with positive pitch stability will change its level pitch trim with every change in thrust. So in pilot-controlled modes like FBWA, Training, and Stabilize, we need to be able to adjust trim on the transmitter during flight as we change throttle settings without it causing adverse effects to the autopilot. I think you answered @IamPete1 's advice though with your statement above it - you can't "get the trim right in the first place" if there is no way to set the correct level calibration based on a trim value - manually or otherwise. You can't just look at an aircraft on the ground and be able to know intuitively or measure what the trim setting should be.

author: LupusTheCanine
body:
There are parameters to adjust pitch trim vs throttle in FBWA. I personally set it so the plane at minimum throttle glides near minimum airspeed, at cruise throttle flies level and above starts to climb (saddly setting the parameter for flying level decreases maximum commanded climb angle at full throttle).

You don't need perfect pitch trim for the first flights as they are relatively short and likely you will be swinging the stick anyways 😁 (AUTOTUNE). Setting decent trim for min and trim throttle requires one reasonably short flight so it shouldn't be an issue.

author: mikedkelly
body: That is a good point. I guess level calibration is more of a gyro angle vs. pitch trim being a climb rate. Perhaps as IamPete1 said above, a good instruction doc is the best solution. Something like: manually trim your plane to level in FWBA at your desired cruise throttle, then use the logs to get the angle of attack during level flight. Use some formula f(x) to convert that to the level calibration angle and set that parameter. Then reset your trims back to 0 and fly again. Decide on how you want the plane to behave with changes to throttle and adjust the pitch trim vs. throttle parameter. I am just spoiled with modern programmable transmitters that let you create multi-point mix curves that you can dynamically modify in-flight with a pot on your transmitter.

author: rsaxvc
title: Cortex-M4 loop alignment
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'd like to suggest a potential small optimization for Cortex-M3 and M4, possibly M7.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
This ticket tracks the testing and tuning of different loop alignment options for ArduPilot and CMSIS. I'd like feedback on proposed loop tuning.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative would be to keep it as-is, which results in no additional loop padding(wasted space).

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[X] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
On several M4 devices, I've run into a per-iteration penalty cycle for loops that start with a 32-bit instruction that is only 16-bit aligned. I've noticed a few places this occurs in CMSIS in ArduPilot, and wanted to suggest considering tuning the -falign-loops=4 parameter, which would result in adding a narrow NOP(1 loop entry overhead) just before each unaligned loop(even those starting with a narrow instruction). Here's an example from CMSIS:

```
08138138 <arm_mult_f32>:
 8138138:       ea5f 0c93       movs.w  ip, r3, lsr #2
 813813c:       b4f0            push    {r4, r5, r6, r7}
 813813e:       d033            beq.n   81381a8 <arm_mult_f32+0x70>
 8138140:       f100 0610       add.w   r6, r0, #16
 8138144:       f101 0510       add.w   r5, r1, #16
 8138148:       f102 0410       add.w   r4, r2, #16
 813814c:       4667            mov     r7, ip
//loop to process 4 samples per iteration
 813814e:       ed15 7a04       vldr    s14, [r5, #-16] //This loop starts with a 16-bit aligned 32-bit wide instruction, which requires two 32-bit instruction fetches
 8138152:       3f01            subs    r7, #1
 8138154:       ed56 7a04       vldr    s15, [r6, #-16]
 8138158:       f105 0510       add.w   r5, r5, #16
 813815c:       f106 0610       add.w   r6, r6, #16
 8138160:       f104 0410       add.w   r4, r4, #16
 8138164:       ee67 7a87       vmul.f32        s15, s15, s14
 8138168:       ed44 7a08       vstr    s15, [r4, #-32] ; 0xffffffe0
 813816c:       ed15 7a07       vldr    s14, [r5, #-28] ; 0xffffffe4
 8138170:       ed56 7a07       vldr    s15, [r6, #-28] ; 0xffffffe4
 8138174:       ee67 7a87       vmul.f32        s15, s15, s14
 8138178:       ed44 7a07       vstr    s15, [r4, #-28] ; 0xffffffe4
 813817c:       ed15 7a06       vldr    s14, [r5, #-24] ; 0xffffffe8
 8138180:       ed56 7a06       vldr    s15, [r6, #-24] ; 0xffffffe8
 8138184:       ee67 7a87       vmul.f32        s15, s15, s14
 8138188:       ed44 7a06       vstr    s15, [r4, #-24] ; 0xffffffe8
 813818c:       ed56 7a05       vldr    s15, [r6, #-20] ; 0xffffffec
 8138190:       ed15 7a05       vldr    s14, [r5, #-20] ; 0xffffffec
 8138194:       ee67 7a87       vmul.f32        s15, s15, s14
 8138198:       ed44 7a05       vstr    s15, [r4, #-20] ; 0xffffffec
 813819c:       d1d7            bne.n   813814e <arm_mult_f32+0x16> //Branch target is aligned on 2
 813819e:       ea4f 140c       mov.w   r4, ip, lsl #4
 ...rest of function handles remaining 0-3 samples, and has been omitted...
```

I suspect M7 has a 64-bit or wider fetch interface, so this would may impact it when a 32-bit instruction stradles two instruction fetches. And Cortex-M7 has a branch predictor, so may not suffer from this as often as the M4.

author: magicrub
body: Have you tried compiling with that option? How does it effect code-size?

author: tridge
body: @rsaxvc definately worth trying, do you need help benchmarking this?

author: rsaxvc
rsaxvc
body:
I built a few boards to look at the differences in codespace vs instructions. In short, I don't think this is worth looking into for the main ArduPilot codebase. Each -falign=4 build added:

* KakuteH7: +16-24 bytes.
* Pixhawk1: +8-16 bytes.
* speedybeef4v3: 0-8bytes.

Usually this impacts the following functions(which vary per build):
* NavEKF2::UpdateFilter()  -moves epilogue nop.n from end of function to just before loop-start to align loop. +0B
* NavEKF2::requestYawReset() -adds nop.n to loop-start, pads epilogue with nop.n, +4B.
* ChibiOS::RCOutput::_set_neopixel_rgb_data(...) - same as requestYawReset()
* ChibiOS::RCOutput::_set_profiled_rgb_data(...) - same as requestYawReset()
* ChibiOS::RCOutput::fill_DMA_buffer_serial_led(...) - same as requestYawReset()

I don't think this may not be worth the effort of profiling for the bulk of ArduPilot, because UpdateFilter() seems like the only thing possibly useful for tuning, but that loop is large enough that the penalty cycle would always be a small part.

I'll probably pick this up for the CMSIS stuff when I get back to building that from source.

author: rmackay9
title: AP_DroneCAN: if sensor doesn't respond to get/set param request, AP will never send get/set again
body:
If a DroneCAN sensor does not respond to a get or set parameter request, AP will never again send a get or set parameter request to the device.  I.e. there's no timeout.

This has been reproduced on a Xacti camera gimbal which can fail to respond to a request to get/set a parameter if it is received too soon after another command.

FYI @bugobliterator

author: Ryanf55
title: Provide VSCode launch and debug tasks for developers to build and debug SITL
body:
## Feature request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Due to ArduPilot's highly custom simulation bringup (sim_vehicle.py), and lack of use of CMake or other common build tool, it's difficult to use VSCode's GUI support for configuring, building, testing, and debugging. 

Developers are maintaining [their own custom configs](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot_vscode_devenv/issues/1#issuecomment-1214816404), but these aren't shared.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Merge one of the dev's `launch.json` and `tasks.json` files that works on `master`, and then allow others to start contributing. When working, this provides the ability to use a keyboard shortcut to configure, build, run `sim_vehicle.py`, attach `gdb`, and inspect the code at a breakpoint WITHOUT using `gdb's` CLI. This can be faster and easier, but it still allows console-commands for gdb.

Here is a hard-coded launch and task showing a breakpoint being triggered in SITL. 
![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/25047695/24a5ccee-ab2d-41f8-972c-0431a778db29)


**Describe alternatives you've considered**

https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot_vscode_devenv/issues/1

See the following branches:
```
bugobliterator/pr-vscode-tasks
khancyr/pr-vscode-tasks
TunaLobster/pr/vscode-rec-extensions
```

And the current wiki: https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/debugging-with-gdb-using-vscode.html?highlight=vscode

Which has this flaw of needing to pick the process:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65723608/vs-code-debugging-is-it-possible-to-supply-process-id-pgrep-x-myprog-for

And, GDB console needs `exec` prefixed all the time:
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-cpptools/issues/106

And, ideally when you launch sim_vehicle from command line, you could add a `--vscode-debug` option that would launch the vscode debugger inside the current VSCode session
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/10979

Some discussion in discord can be found here: https://discord.com/channels/674039678562861068/674039678982422579/1137475852838387913

```
        {
            "name": "Copter",
            "type": "cppdbg",
            "request": "attach",
            "program": "${workspaceFolder}/build/sitl/bin/arducopter",
            "processId": "${command:pickProcess}",
            "MIMode": "gdb",
            "setupCommands": [
                {
                    "description": "Enable pretty-printing for gdb",
                    "text": "-enable-pretty-printing",
                    "ignoreFailures": true
                }
            ]
        },
```

**Platform**
[x ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[  ] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

author: bnsgeyer
title: Cyclic Swashplate support for Coax Copter
body:
There have been several users attempting to use Ardupilot to control coaxial helicopters that have fixed collective pitch rotors but have cyclic swashplate control.  The tradheli code does not handle fixed collective pitch, variable speed main rotors.  The multirotor Coax copter frame is better suited for this helicopter type but it cannot handle the unique swashplate types.  

Since @IamPete1 has recently cleaned up the swashplate library to be more self contained, it seems reasonable to use this library in the Coax copter to provide users the ability to control these helis.

Here is a link to a thread where users are requesting support for this special helicopter type
https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/new-co-axial-heli/60067/35
https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/coaxcopter-coaxial-is-not-working-on-heli-firmware-4-3-7/102270

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Users trying to setup a coaxial helicopter with fixed collective pitch cannot use Coax copter because it doesn't support swashplates

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Incorporate the swashplate library into coax copter to enable users to use this frame type to control this special helicopter type. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This special helicopter type could be made into a frame in the trad heli code but it doesn't seem logical as this helicopter type uses variable speed fixed collective pitch to control the thrust. It would probably be more difficult to implement into trad heli 

**Platform**
[  ] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[X] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

**Additional context**
_Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here._

author: rmackay9
title: AutoTest: add test of GSF emergency yaw reset
body:
While reviewing a log from a vehicle with a bad yaw at takeoff (see issue https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/20532) we noticed that AutoTest does not test the GSF emergency yaw reset.  It really should because it is an important safety feature.

The test could be something like:

- param set COMPASS_ORIENT 4 (yaw 180)
- param set COMPASS_USE2 0
- param set COMPASS_USE3 0
- GUIDED
- arm throttle
- takeoff 20
- wait for text message, "EKF3 IMUx emergency yaw reset"
- check that the vehicle has not flow more than 20m

FYI @peterbarker

The error is resolved in newer compiler versions. We make compiler a version a hard requirement for ChibiOS builds, but not SITL. I guess we might need to add a minimum version check for SITL too.

Default compiler works for me on Ubuntu 22 but not 18. It might be worth a fix... looks like it would take a little effort, its not just a one liner. @rmackay9 any thoughts?

If we do fix we should at least add this compiler to CI. We did recently back out some python version requirements so as not to break those on Ubuntu 18.

Edit2:
We could bodge it up by turning off the viewpro mount backend for SITL on older compilers. We could generate the define from sim vehicle.

title: EKF failsafe untriggered on high errors, resulting in a crash #9
body:
### Issue details

Reporting one of the discovered instance of an ArduCopter SITL execution , where the Extended Kalman Filter does not trigger fail safe landing, despite significant errors in Copter's mission resulting from compromised accelerometer values. EKF undergoes multiple lane and core switches, drone crashes before completing assigned mission.

Significant deviation in Y velocity in the mission. (Other controllers have errors too, this is an sample to show the impact, logs are attached to aid in deeper analysis)
![Zvel_error](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/48596558/b8ecd871-b2c2-4ec8-8f22-b3b26b2511e7)

### Version
ArduCopter V4.5.0-dev 

### Platform
[X] Copter
[X] Ardupilot SITL simulation

### Logs
Attached is the telemetry logs of the mission,BIN file for further log analysis and the mission used in this execution.

[logs.zip](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/files/12209650/logs.zip)

Mission plan used:

[mission.txt](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/files/12209648/07-22-06-49-49.txt)

### Context
As part of my research in contributing towards making Ardupilot more resilient to sensor injection attacks , I have modified AP to inject malicious yet realistic(can be generated in the real world) accelerometer values and run different missions. Some executions (such as the one described in this report , successfully crashes the drone without triggering the EKF3's failsafe emergency landing, which could lead to physically damaging the drone instead of minimizing the damage in a real attack scenario)

author: joshanne
title: IMU Data Loss in Copter 4.3.7 Stable (mRoControlZeroH7)
body:
## Bug report

**Issue details**

**Version**
Copter-4.3.7
Copter-4.4 beta3 (sha: 3c4abe469a47965eb76788d148a88045c0697344)

**Platform**
[?] All
[  ] AntennaTracker
[x] Copter
[  ] Plane
[  ] Rover
[  ] Submarine

Note: This seems likely to affect all platforms that do not contain the proposed fix commit.

**Hardware Configuration**
* mRoControlZeroH7 (Copter-4.3.7 - latest stable release)
* mRo SAM GPS + IST8308 Mag (Full Size) M10037 (See: https://store.mrobotics.io/product-p/m10037a.htm)

**Description**

We are experiencing data loss for the IMUs when the Flight Controller is configured with External GPS/Compass module. When the module is not present, there is no data loss in the IMUs.

We can replicate (and validate the proposed solution) with the following parameter set.

```
EK3_IMU_MASK  7
LOG_REPLAY 1
```

1. Enable `LOG_DISARMED`
2. Reboot
3. Generate ~1min log data
4. Disable `LOG_DISARMED`
5. Reboot
6. Download log and check with `graph sum(RISI[0].DADT,1) sum(RISI[1].DADT,2) sum(RISI[2].DADT,3) IMU[0].TimeUS/1E6`

Looking at the log, we observe a time slip in the recorded data.

![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/12959316/2fc1f223-8203-429d-aced-0c36f78c26e9)

**Solution**

It appears for this flight controller the I2C DMA is interfering with the IMUs, resulting in data loss.

Cherry-picking these upstream commits (on top of Copter-4.3.7) addresses the issue seen. https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/23568/commits

With these changes, we can see all three IMUs are being read without data loss, and the accumulated time rises at the same gradient as elapsed time.

![image](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/12959316/071e4cef-abf7-4052-961d-ad5ac578667f)

Two log files are attached in this zip. They contain:
1. The issue present, on Copter-4.3.7 stable (_log-copter-4.3.7-issue-present.bin_)
2. The issue resolved, Copter-4.3.7 with cherry-picked commit (log-copter-4.3.7-fixed-with-cherrypick-commits)

[log-copter-4.3.7.zip](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/files/12190867/log-copter-4.3.7.zip)

author: rmackay9
title: AP-4.5.0-dev: dual CAN support broken
body:
Latest (aka "master", aka "4.5.0-dev") cannot support two separate CAN interfaces when using DroneCAN (and perhaps other versions of CAN as well).

The issue can be replicated by connected a DroneCAN GPS to the CAN2 port of a CubeOrange (or probably any other autopilot) and then set:

- CAN_D1_PROTOCOL = 1 (DroneCAN)
- CAN_P1_DRIVER = 1 (First Driver)
- CAN_D2_PROTOCOL = 1 (DroneCAN)
- CAN_P2_DRIVER = 2 (Second Driver)

The GPS, compass and notify LEDs will not work.  Next set the parameter below so that there is only one CAN bus (with two ports)

- CAN_P2_DRIVER = 1 (First Driver)

.. and the GPS will start working.

If these tests are repeated on 4.4.0 (or earlier) the GPS works in both cases.

Reporting one of the discovered instance of an ArduCopter SITL execution , where the Extended Kalman Filter does not trigger fail safe landing, despite significant errors in Copter's mission resulting from compromised gyroscope values. 

Significant deviation in Yaw in the mission. (Other controllers have errors too, this is an sample to show the impact, logs are attached to aid in deeper analysis)
![yaw_error](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/48596558/1bd9203f-9859-4ad3-ae09-fe11122d7b8d)

Also the position errors towards the end of the mission:
![position_errors](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/assets/48596558/5f685dd6-40f0-4d84-8eaf-ad6a081c66a1)



### Version
ArduCopter V4.5.0-dev 

### Platform
[X] Copter
[X] Ardupilot SITL simulation

### Logs
Attached is the telemetry logs of the mission,BIN file for further log analysis and the mission used in this execution.
[logs.zip](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/files/12156754/logs.zip)


Mission plan used:

[07-20-10-06-48.txt](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/files/12156748/07-20-10-06-48.txt)


### Context
As part of my research in contributing towards making Ardupilot more resilient to sensor injection attacks , I have modified AP to inject malicious yet realistic(can be generated in the real world) gyroscope values and run different missions. Some executions (such as the one described in this report , successfully crashes the drone without triggering the EKF3's failsafe emergency landing, which could lead to physically damaging the drone instead of minimizing the damage in a real attack scenario)
